title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄序
嘉靖戊子秋八月浙江鄉試
給事中臣粲郎中臣鑰寔奉
命主之臣粲竊惟浙江古揚州之
境而今之首藩也粤自我
皇祖起南服定金陵遂下浙東西
諸郡方
國家草創日不暇給而崇禮樂
考文章搢紳先生出入風議
訢訢如也其間二三耆碩參
侍帷幄者大抵皆自浙起以
博學贍辭潤色鴻業於是
皇明之號令典法炳焉與三代同
風而浙之文遂先天下粲不
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄序

嘉靖戊子秋八月，浙江鄉試，給事中臣粲、郎中臣鑰寔奉命主之。臣粲竊惟浙江，古揚州之境，而今之首藩也。粤自我皇祖起南服，定金陵，遂下浙東西諸郡。方國家草創，日不暇給，而崇禮樂，考文章，搢紳先生出入風議，訢訢如也。其間二三耆碩參侍帷幄者，大抵皆自浙起，以博學贍辭潤色鴻業。於是皇明之號令典法，炳焉與三代同風，而浙之文遂先天下。粲不
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn in the wuzi year of Jiajing [1528], your servants Can, Supervising Secretary, and Yue, Bureau Director, received the imperial command to preside over the Zhejiang Provincial Examination. Your servant Can humbly considers that Zhejiang lay within the territory of ancient Yangzhou and is now foremost among the provinces. When our imperial ancestor rose in the southern regions and secured Jinling, he proceeded to conquer the prefectures of eastern and western Zhejiang. While the state was newly founded, with each day scarcely sufficient for its pressing affairs, he nevertheless exalted rites and music and examined literary compositions. The gentlemen of the official class came and went, offering counsel and deliberating in a spirit of cheerful harmony. Among them, the few venerable scholars who attended him in his inner councils had almost all risen from Zhejiang. With their extensive learning and rich literary expression, they lent lustre to his grand undertaking. Thus the proclamations, statutes, and laws of our imperial Ming shone with the same spirit as those of the Three Dynasties, and Zhejiang’s literary accomplishment came to lead all under Heaven. I, Can, …

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
佞嘗好觀
國朝故事而知其槩矣乃今承
乏考校始盡得其賢士者之
文而縱觀焉有取之無窮而
讀之不厭者信乎其為盛也
於是知
皇祖之澤遠矣雖然文者道之華
===
而行之飾也昔者孔子稱周
之盛曰郁郁乎文哉他日論
禮樂則慨然思從先進又曰
我於辭命則不能也非謂夫
文之有本哉由周以下言文
者必曰秦漢秦漢尚矣近世
以文取士宜莫盛於唐時則
punctuated:
佞嘗好觀國朝故事，而知其槩矣。乃今承乏考校，始盡得其賢士者之文而縱觀焉。有取之無窮而讀之不厭者，信乎其為盛也！於是知皇祖之澤遠矣。
雖然，文者道之華，而行之飾也。昔者孔子稱周之盛曰：「郁郁乎文哉！」他日論禮樂，則慨然思從先進，又曰：「我於辭命則不能也。」非謂夫文之有本哉？由周以下，言文者必曰秦漢。秦漢尚矣，近世以文取士，宜莫盛於唐，時則
translation_en:
…I, unworthy as I am, have long delighted in examining the precedents of our dynasty and have thus come to understand their general outline. Now, having been called upon for want of someone better to serve as an examiner, I have for the first time obtained the writings of all its worthy scholars and read them at leisure. There is inexhaustible material to draw upon, and one never tires of reading them. Truly, this is a flourishing age of letters! From this I recognize how far-reaching is the beneficence of our imperial forefather.
Nevertheless, literary accomplishment is the flowering of the Way and the adornment of conduct. In former times, Confucius praised the flourishing culture of Zhou, saying: “How splendid is its refinement!” Yet on another occasion, discussing ritual and music, he earnestly wished to follow the men of earlier times. He also said: “As for diplomatic language, I am not capable of it.” Was he not saying that literary accomplishment must have a foundation? After Zhou, anyone discussing literature invariably speaks of Qin and Han. But Qin and Han are remote antiquity. In more recent times, the selection of men for office through literary accomplishment surely flourished most under the Tang. At that time…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有若陸贄者司考校而韓愈
輩出焉天下至于今稱之然
愈嘗自言其當時程試之文
以爲讀之使人忸怩而已耳
其信然乎抑有激而云爾也
夫唐之文初亦失之靡矣自
愈出然後一振之以復于古
===
彼所謂豪傑之士者非邪而
其始也微贄孰能知而取之
我
國家稽古立法以經術造士百
六十年治敎煕洽文亦日趨
于盛學士大夫操筆伸紙類
能達其所欲言者顧藻飾有
punctuated:
有若陸贄者司考校，而韓愈輩出焉，天下至于今稱之。然愈嘗自言其當時程試之文，以爲讀之使人忸怩而已耳。其信然乎？抑有激而云爾也？夫唐之文，初亦失之靡矣。自愈出，然後一振之以復于古。彼所謂豪傑之士者非邪？而其始也，微贄，孰能知而取之？
我國家稽古立法，以經術造士，百六十年，治敎煕洽，文亦日趨于盛。學士大夫操筆伸紙，類能達其所欲言者，顧藻飾有
translation_en:
…there were men such as Lu Zhi who presided over the examinations, and Han Yu and others emerged through them. To this day, all under Heaven praise this. Yet Han Yu once said of his own examination compositions of that time that reading them merely made one feel embarrassed. Was this really so? Or was he provoked into saying it? Writing in the Tang initially erred toward excessive ornamentation. Only after Han Yu emerged was it reinvigorated and restored to the ancient models. Was he not what is called a man of outstanding talent? Yet at the outset, without Lu Zhi, who could have recognized and selected him?
Our dynasty has studied antiquity to establish its institutions and has cultivated scholars through classical learning. For 160 years, government and moral instruction have flourished in harmony, and writing too has grown ever more flourishing. Scholars and officials, taking up their brushes and spreading out their paper, can generally express what they wish to say. Yet in ornamental embellishment there is…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
餘而朴茂忠實之意視前輩
若少衰焉當是時其亦有豪
傑者出而振之而司考校者
亦能知而取之乎
聖天子方篤意教化屢詔所司選
師儒嚴條約將責士以有本
之學而非直曰文云者故屬
===
者之舉雖有司存而特
簡近臣涖之意嚮所在昭然可識
士於是時有弗自奮也者非
夫也况若浙之嘗以文先天
下者哉將必有異才焉如愈
者卓然出其間乎得若人以
稱塞
punctuated:
餘，而朴茂忠實之意，視前輩若少衰焉。當是時，其亦有豪傑者出而振之，而司考校者亦能知而取之乎？
聖天子方篤意教化，屢詔所司選師儒、嚴條約，將責士以有本之學，而非直曰文云者。故屬者之舉，雖有司存，而特簡近臣涖之，意嚮所在，昭然可識。士於是時有弗自奮也者，非夫也，况若浙之嘗以文先天下者哉！將必有異才焉，如愈者卓然出其間乎？得若人以稱塞
translation_en:
…in abundance, yet their spirit of unadorned richness, loyalty, and sincerity seems somewhat diminished in comparison with their predecessors. At such a time, will outstanding men emerge to revive it, and will those charged with examining candidates be able to recognize and select them?
The sagely Son of Heaven is now deeply committed to moral instruction. He has repeatedly commanded the responsible officials to select learned teachers and tighten regulations, intending to require of scholars learning with a firm foundation, rather than mere literary accomplishment. Thus, for the recent examination, although the regular officials were in place, he specially selected close attendants to oversee it. The direction of his intentions is plainly discernible. A scholar who fails to exert himself at such a time is no true man—how much more so in Zhejiang, which once led all under Heaven in literary achievement! Surely there will be exceptional talents, men like Yu, who stand out conspicuously among them? To obtain such men and thereby worthily fulfill…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
明詔則司考校者之責任亦無負
矣而愧無贄之明弗能識也
抑所謂公無私者或庶幾焉
爾矣是舉也同考試則學正
孫鰲凌雲教諭鄭子充徐逵
宋大本唐佐吳畀陳岳林汝
永毛鳳監臨則巡按監察御
===
史張問行申飭藩臬百務具
舉提調則左布政使潘旦右
布政使劉節監試則按察使
桑溥副使傅鑰遴士以試則
提學副使萬潮協贊于外則
監察御史王化工部主事郭
秉聰南京戶部主事王銳參
punctuated:
明詔，則司考校者之責任亦無負矣。而愧無贄之明，弗能識也。抑所謂公無私者，或庶幾焉爾矣。
是舉也，同考試則學正孫鰲、凌雲，教諭鄭子充、徐逵、宋大本、唐佐、吳畀、陳岳、林汝永、毛鳳。監臨則巡按監察御史張問行，申飭藩臬，百務具舉。提調則左布政使潘旦、右布政使劉節。監試則按察使桑溥、副使傅鑰。遴士以試則提學副使萬潮。協贊于外則監察御史王化、工部主事郭秉聰、南京戶部主事王銳、參
translation_en:
…the enlightened imperial edict, then those charged with examining and assessing the candidates will also have discharged their responsibility. Yet I am ashamed that I lack Zhi’s discernment and cannot recognize such men. As for what is called being impartial and free of private interests, perhaps I may come close to that, and that alone.
For this examination, Sun Ao and Ling Yun, School Directors, served as Associate Examiners. Zheng Zichong, Xu Kui, Song Daben, Tang Zuo, Wu Bi, Chen Yue, Lin Ruyong, and Mao Feng, Instructors, also served as Associate Examiners. Zhang Wenxing, Regional Inspector and Investigating Censor, served as Supervising Official; he issued injunctions to the provincial administration and surveillance authorities, and all the necessary business was carried out. Pan Dan, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Liu Jie, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner, served as Proctors. Sang Pu, Surveillance Commissioner, and Fu Yue, Surveillance Vice Commissioner, supervised the examination. Wan Chao, Surveillance Vice Commissioner serving as Education Intendant, selected the scholars to sit the examination. Those providing assistance outside the examination compound were Wang Hua, Investigating Censor; Guo Bingcong, Secretary in the Ministry of Works; Wang Rui, Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; and the Administration Vice Commissioner …

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
政胡纘宗葉䙾朱裳叅議萬
廷彩龐浩副使党以平何鰲
汪金僉事孫元巴思明梁世
驃江良材都指揮僉事張浩
李節士就試者二千八百有
奇預選者九十人刻其文之
優者二十一篇合諸執事姓
名為錄以
獻粲序之
從仕郎工科給事中陸粲謹
序
punctuated:
政胡纘宗、葉䙾、朱裳，叅議萬廷彩、龐浩，副使党以平、何鰲、汪金，僉事孫元、巴思明、梁世驃、江良材，都指揮僉事張浩、李節。士就試者二千八百有奇，預選者九十人。刻其文之優者二十一篇，合諸執事姓名為錄，以獻。粲序之。
從仕郎、工科給事中陸粲謹序。
translation_en:
…Administration Vice Commissioners Hu Zuanzong, Ye Shi 葉䙾 [?], and Zhu Shang; Administration Assistant Commissioners Wan Tingcai and Pang Hao; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Dang Yiping, He Ao, and Wang Jin; Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Sun Yuan, Ba Siming, Liang Shibiao, and Jiang Liangcai; and Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Zhang Hao and Li Jie.
More than 2,800 scholars sat the examination, and ninety were selected. Twenty-one outstanding pieces of their writing were engraved for printing and compiled together with the names of the officials involved into a record for presentation to the throne. I, Can, have written its preface.
Respectfully prefaced by Lu Can, Attendant Gentleman and Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Works.

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖七年浙江鄉試
監臨官
巡按浙江監察御史張問行〔子書直隸內黃縣人辛巳進士〕
提調官
浙江等處承宣布政使司左布政使潘旦〔希周直隸婺源縣人乙丑進士〕
浙江等處承宣布政使司右布政使劉節〔介夫江西大庾縣人乙丑進士〕
監試官
浙江等處提刑按察司按察使桑溥〔汝公山東濮州人甲戌進士〕
浙江等處提刑按察司副使傅鑰〔希準遼東廣寧左衛人辛未進士〕
===

從仕郎工科給事中陸粲〔浚明直隸長洲縣人丙戌進士〕
承德郎兵部武庫清吏司署郎中事主事華鑰〔德啟直隸無錫縣人癸未進士〕
同考試官
河南開封府歸德州儒學學正孫鰲〔用寧雲南晉寧州籍直隸通州人壬午貢士〕
湖廣荆州府荆門州儒學學正凌雲〔應賢福建閩縣人丙子貢士〕
湖廣黃州府黃陂縣儒學教諭鄭守充〔道充福建莆田縣人壬午貢士〕
山東兖州府曹州曹縣儒學教諭徐逵〔九達江西金谿縣人丙子貢士〕
山東濟南府章丘縣儒學教諭宋大本〔秉中直隸新城縣人己卯貢士〕
punctuated:
嘉靖七年浙江鄉試

監臨官
巡按浙江監察御史張問行〔子書，直隸內黃縣人，辛巳進士〕。

提調官
浙江等處承宣布政使司左布政使潘旦〔希周，直隸婺源縣人，乙丑進士〕。
浙江等處承宣布政使司右布政使劉節〔介夫，江西大庾縣人，乙丑進士〕。

浙江等處提刑按察司按察使桑溥〔汝公，山東濮州人，甲戌進士〕。
浙江等處提刑按察司副使傅鑰〔希準，遼東廣寧左衛人，辛未進士〕。

從仕郎工科給事中陸粲〔浚明，直隸長洲縣人，丙戌進士〕。
承德郎兵部武庫清吏司署郎中事主事華鑰〔德啟，直隸無錫縣人，癸未進士〕。

同考試官
河南開封府歸德州儒學學正孫鰲〔用寧，雲南晉寧州籍，直隸通州人，壬午貢士〕。
湖廣荆州府荆門州儒學學正凌雲〔應賢，福建閩縣人，丙子貢士〕。
湖廣黃州府黃陂縣儒學教諭鄭守充〔道充，福建莆田縣人，壬午貢士〕。
山東兖州府曹州曹縣儒學教諭徐逵〔九達，江西金谿縣人，丙子貢士〕。

translation_en:
Zhejiang Provincial Examination, Seventh Year of Jiajing (1528)

Supervising Official
Zhang Wenxing, Regional Inspector of Zhejiang and Investigating Censor, courtesy name Zishu, was from Neihuang County, Zhili. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the xinsi year.

Proctors
Pan Dan, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Zhejiang, courtesy name Xizhou, was from Wuyuan County, Zhili. He became a metropolitan graduate in the yichou year.
Liu Jie, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Zhejiang, courtesy name Jiefu, was from Dayu County, Jiangxi. He became a metropolitan graduate in the yichou year.

Examination Inspectors
Sang Pu, Surveillance Commissioner of Zhejiang, courtesy name Rugong, was from Pu Subprefecture, Shandong. He became a metropolitan graduate in the jiaxu year.
Fu Yue, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Zhejiang, courtesy name Xizhun, was from Guangning Left Guard, Liaodong. He became a metropolitan graduate in the xinwei year.

Examiners
Lu Can, Gentleman for Attending Affairs and Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Works, courtesy name Junming, was from Changzhou County, Zhili. He became a metropolitan graduate in the bingxu year.
Hua Yue, Gentleman for Recognized Virtue and Secretary acting as Director of the Bureau of Armories in the Ministry of War, courtesy name Deqi, was from Wuxi County, Zhili. He became a metropolitan graduate in the guiwei year.

Associate Examiners
Sun Ao, Instructor at the Confucian School of Guide Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, had the courtesy name Yongning. Registered in Jinning Subprefecture, Yunnan, and originally from Tongzhou, Zhili, he became a tribute scholar (gongshi) in the renwu year.
Ling Yun, Instructor at the Confucian School of Jingmen Subprefecture, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, courtesy name Yingxian, was from Min County, Fujian. He became a tribute scholar in the bingzi year.
Zheng Shouchong, Instructor at the Confucian School of Huangpi County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, courtesy name Daochong, was from Putian County, Fujian. He became a tribute scholar in the renwu year.
Xu Kui, Instructor at the Confucian School of Cao County, Cao Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, courtesy name Jiuda, was from Jinxi County, Jiangxi. He became a tribute scholar in the bingzi year.
Song Daben, Instructor at the Confucian School of Zhangqiu County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, courtesy name Bingzhong, was from Xincheng County, Zhili. He became a tribute scholar in the jimao year.

text:

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
禮云禮云玉帛云乎哉樂云樂云鍾鼓云
乎哉
唯天下至誠為能經綸天下之大經立天
下之大本知天地之化育夫焉有所倚
肫肫其仁淵淵其淵浩浩其天
夫道一而已矣成覸謂齊景公曰彼丈夫
也我丈夫也吾何畏彼哉顏淵曰舜何
===
人也予何人也有為者亦若是公明儀
曰文王我師也周公豈欺我哉
易
先王以建萬國親諸侯
觀其所聚而天地萬物之情可見矣
是故君子所居而安者易之序也所樂而
玩者爻之辭也是故君子居則觀其象
而玩其辭動則觀其變而玩其占是以
自天祐之吉无不利
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

禮云禮云，玉帛云乎哉？樂云樂云，鍾鼓云乎哉？

唯天下至誠，為能經綸天下之大經，立天下之大本，知天地之化育，夫焉有所倚？肫肫其仁，淵淵其淵，浩浩其天。

夫道一而已矣。成覸謂齊景公曰：「彼丈夫也，我丈夫也，吾何畏彼哉？」顏淵曰：「舜何人也？予何人也？有為者亦若是。」公明儀曰：「文王我師也，周公豈欺我哉？」

易

先王以建萬國，親諸侯。

觀其所聚，而天地萬物之情可見矣。

是故君子所居而安者，易之序也；所樂而玩者，爻之辭也。是故君子居則觀其象而玩其辭，動則觀其變而玩其占，是以自天祐之，吉无不利。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“Ritual, ritual!” Does this mean merely jade and silk? “Music, music!” Does this mean merely bells and drums?

Only one possessed of the utmost sincerity under Heaven can order the great guiding principles of the world, establish its great foundation, and understand the transforming and nourishing operations of Heaven and Earth. On what, then, would he depend? How earnest his benevolence, how profound his depth, how vast his Heaven!

The Way is one, and that is all. Cheng Jian said to Duke Jing of Qi: “He is a man, and I am a man. Why should I fear him?” Yan Yuan said: “What sort of person was Shun? What sort of person am I? Anyone who strives can become like him.” Gongming Yi said: “King Wen is my teacher. Could the Duke of Zhou have deceived me?”

Book of Changes

The former kings accordingly established the myriad states and cultivated close relations with the feudal lords.

By observing what things gather together, one can discern the true circumstances of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things.

Thus, what the gentleman abides in and finds security in is the ordering of the Changes; what he delights in and ponders is the wording of the lines. Therefore, when at rest, the gentleman observes its images and ponders its statements; when acting, he observes its changes and ponders its prognostications. Hence, “Heaven itself aids him: good fortune, with nothing unfavorable.”

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
復則不妄矣故受之以无妄
書
人心惟危道心惟微惟精惟一允執厥中
朝夕納誨以輔台德
王省惟歲卿士惟月師尹惟日
受王嘉師監于茲祥刑
詩
葛之覃兮施于中谷維葉莫莫是刈是濩
爲絺爲綌服之無斁
===
宜爾室家樂爾妻帑是究是圖亶其然乎
追琢其章金玉其相勉勉我王綱紀四方
紹庭上下陟降厥家休矣皇考以保明其
身
春秋
公會齊侯于防隱公九年
楚子蔡侯次于厥貉文公十年公會宋公
陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯晉趙盾癸酉
同盟于新城文公十有四年
punctuated:
復則不妄矣，故受之以无妄。

書
人心惟危，道心惟微，惟精惟一，允執厥中。
朝夕納誨，以輔台德。
王省惟歲，卿士惟月，師尹惟日。
受王嘉師，監于茲祥刑。

詩
葛之覃兮，施于中谷，維葉莫莫。是刈是濩，爲絺爲綌，服之無斁。
宜爾室家，樂爾妻帑。是究是圖，亶其然乎？
追琢其章，金玉其相。勉勉我王，綱紀四方。
紹庭上下，陟降厥家。休矣皇考，以保明其身。

春秋
公會齊侯于防。隱公九年。
楚子、蔡侯次于厥貉。文公十年。公會宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯、晉趙盾，癸酉，同盟于新城。文公十有四年。
translation_en:
With return, there is no recklessness; therefore it is followed by Without Recklessness (Wuwang).

Book of Documents
The human mind is precarious; the mind of the Way is subtle. Be discerning and single-minded, and sincerely hold fast to the mean.
Morning and evening, offer admonitions to assist my virtue.
The king’s scrutiny concerns the year; that of the ministers, the month; that of the officials, the day.
You who have charge of the king’s good people, take these beneficent punishments as your guide.

Book of Odes
The kudzu vines spread into the valley’s midst, their leaves luxuriant. They are cut and boiled, made into fine and coarse cloth, worn without weariness.
Bring harmony to your household and joy to your wife and children. Examine this and consider it: is it truly so?
Its ornament is engraved and carved; its substance is gold and jade. Diligently our king orders the four quarters.
He continued his ancestors’ ways in the court, above and below, ascending and descending within his house. Glorious was his august deceased father, who thereby preserved and made illustrious his person.

Spring and Autumn Annals
The duke met the Marquis of Qi at Fang. Ninth year of Duke Yin.
The Viscount of Chu and the Marquis of Cai encamped at Juehe. Tenth year of Duke Wen.
The duke met the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, and Zhao Dun of Jin. On the guiyou day, they jointly entered into a covenant at Xincheng. Fourteenth year of Duke Wen.

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
齊人伐我北鄙僖公二十有六年楚公子
貞帥師伐鄭襄公八年
晉人執宋仲幾于京師定公元年
禮記
故人情者聖王之田也脩禮以耕之陳義
以種之講學以耨之本仁以聚之播樂
以安之故禮也者義之實也協諸義而
協則禮雖先王未之有可以義起也義
者藝之分仁之節也協於藝講於仁得
===
之者强仁者義之本也順之體也得之
者尊
禁於未發之謂豫當其可之謂時
樂則安安則久久則天天則神
博施備物可謂不匱矣
第貳場
論
治天下者審所上
詔誥表內科一道
punctuated:
齊人伐我北鄙，僖公二十有六年。楚公子貞帥師伐鄭，襄公八年。
晉人執宋仲幾于京師，定公元年。

禮記
故人情者，聖王之田也。脩禮以耕之，陳義以種之，講學以耨之，本仁以聚之，播樂以安之。故禮也者，義之實也。協諸義而協，則禮雖先王未之有，可以義起也。義者，藝之分，仁之節也。協於藝，講於仁，得之者强。仁者，義之本也，順之體也，得之者尊。
禁於未發之謂豫，當其可之謂時。
樂則安，安則久，久則天，天則神。
博施備物，可謂不匱矣。

第貳場
論
治天下者審所上。
詔誥表內科一道。
translation_en:
The men of Qi attacked our northern borderlands. Twenty-sixth year of Duke Xi.
Prince Zhen of Chu led an army to attack Zheng. Eighth year of Duke Xiang.
The men of Jin seized Zhongji of Song at the royal capital. First year of Duke Ding.

Record of Rites (Liji)
Thus human feelings are the field of the sage kings. They cultivate ritual to plough it, set forth righteousness to sow it, expound learning to weed it, take benevolence as the foundation for gathering its harvest, and spread music to bring it peace. Thus ritual is the concrete realization of righteousness. If a practice is tested against righteousness and accords with it, then even if the former kings had no such rite, it may be instituted on the basis of righteousness. Righteousness determines the distinctions within the arts and regulates benevolence. Those who accord with the arts and thoroughly examine benevolence, attaining righteousness, are strong. Benevolence is the root of righteousness and the embodiment of accord; those who attain it are honored.
To prevent something before it arises is called anticipation; to act at the appropriate moment is called timeliness.
Joy brings repose; repose brings endurance; endurance brings accord with Heaven; accord with Heaven brings spiritual efficacy.
To bestow generously and provide all things may be called inexhaustible.

Second Session
Discourse
Those who govern all under Heaven must carefully consider what they esteem.
One topic from among edicts, proclamations, and memorials [the word 科 in the transcription is doubtful: ?].

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
擬漢令郡國舉孝廉詔元光元年
擬唐以孫伏伽為治書侍御史誥武德元
年
擬宋開天章閣引輔臣入對參知政事范
仲淹謝表慶曆三年
判語五條
上言大臣德政
檢踏災傷田糧
禁止師巫邪術
===
關防內使出入
失時不修隄防
第參塲
策五道
問古之有國家者必封建宗親以藩王室
我
太祖高皇帝肇創大業廣樹
親藩布列天下磐石之宗萬世永賴既又親
作
punctuated:
擬漢令郡國舉孝廉詔，元光元年。
擬唐以孫伏伽為治書侍御史誥，武德元年。
擬宋開天章閣引輔臣入對，參知政事范仲淹謝表，慶曆三年。

判語五條：
上言大臣德政。
檢踏災傷田糧。
禁止師巫邪術。
關防內使出入。
失時不修隄防。

第參塲
策五道
問：古之有國家者，必封建宗親以藩王室。我太祖高皇帝肇創大業，廣樹親藩，布列天下，磐石之宗，萬世永賴。既又親作
translation_en:
Compose a draft Han edict ordering the commanderies and kingdoms to recommend men distinguished for filial devotion and integrity (xiaolian). First year of Yuanguang (134 BCE).
Compose a draft Tang appointment proclamation making Sun Fujia Vice Censor-in-chief. First year of Wude (618).
Compose a draft memorial of thanks by Fan Zhongyan, Vice Grand Councilor, on the Song emperor’s opening the Tianzhang Pavilion and summoning his chief ministers to an audience. Third year of Qingli (1043).

Five legal judgments:
Reporting to the throne on the virtuous administration of high ministers.
Inspecting disaster damage to farmland and assessing the associated grain taxes.
Prohibiting the heterodox arts of ritual masters and spirit mediums.
Regulating the entry and exit of palace eunuchs.
Failing to repair dikes in a timely manner.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions
Question: Those who ruled states in antiquity invariably enfeoffed their imperial kinsmen to serve as bulwarks of the royal house. Our founding emperor, Taizu Gao, established the great imperial enterprise and created numerous princely fiefs for his kinsmen throughout the realm. This rock-solid imperial clan would provide enduring support for ten thousand generations. Subsequently, he also personally composed…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
祖訓以貽
東宫及
諸王使世守焉數傳之後本支益昌敦睦之
風内外隆洽所以恪遵
訓典者至矣自今觀之猶竊有未安於心者夫
歲禄時賜禮秩有定矣然支庶日蕃而
勢將不贍何以處之而使無戚戚具爾
之心樂善好禮賢名有聞矣然稍踰檢
制者亦未嘗無也何以道之而使有卓
===
爾不羣之行抑又有異焉者親賢並用
故事也今連姻
帝胄則仕者不得通籍京朝内外均勞常法
也今備位藩僚則終身無遷轉之望果
皇祖之訓則然乎抑别有據乎是皆關繫政體
之大者願一言之將轉
聞焉以為
當宁法
祖睦親之助
punctuated: 《祖訓》以貽東宫及諸王，使世守焉。數傳之後，本支益昌，敦睦之風内外隆洽，所以恪遵訓典者至矣。自今觀之，猶竊有未安於心者。夫歲禄時賜，禮秩有定矣，然支庶日蕃，而勢將不贍，何以處之而使無戚戚具爾之心？樂善好禮，賢名有聞矣，然稍踰檢制者亦未嘗無也，何以道之而使有卓爾不羣之行？抑又有異焉者：親賢並用，故事也，今連姻帝胄，則仕者不得通籍京朝；内外均勞，常法也，今備位藩僚，則終身無遷轉之望。果皇祖之訓則然乎？抑别有據乎？是皆關繫政體之大者，願一言之，將轉聞焉，以為當宁法祖睦親之助。
translation_en:
…the Ancestral Injunctions (Zuxun), to be bequeathed to the Crown Prince and the princes, so that they might observe them generation after generation. After several generations, the main line and collateral branches have flourished ever more abundantly, and a spirit of familial harmony has prevailed both within and beyond the court. Their reverent observance of these ancestral precepts has been exemplary. Yet, considering matters as they stand today, I venture to harbor certain misgivings.

Annual stipends, occasional grants, and ceremonial privileges are fixed. Yet the collateral branches grow daily more numerous, and resources will inevitably become insufficient. How can this be managed so that these close kinsmen have no cause for anxiety? They delight in goodness and cherish ritual propriety, and their reputations for worthiness are widely known. Nevertheless, there have also been some who overstep the restraints and regulations. How can they be guided toward conduct that is outstanding and exceptional?

There are, moreover, other anomalies. Employing both imperial relatives and worthy men is an established precedent; yet today, when someone becomes related by marriage to the imperial house, those holding office are barred from enrollment among officials of the capital and court. Sharing service burdens equally between metropolitan and provincial officials is the regular rule; yet today, those serving as officials in princely establishments have no prospect of transfer or promotion throughout their lives. Is this truly what the imperial ancestor’s injunctions prescribe, or is there some other basis for it?

These are all major matters concerning the ordering of government. Please address them all. Your views will be transmitted to the throne to assist the reigning sovereign in following his ancestor’s example and maintaining harmony with his imperial kin.

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
問廉耻者士人之美節風俗者天下之大
事也古昔人知自重行已有耻而習以
相安此豈一朝一夕之故哉秦漢而下
士多隨世以就功名守義者少尚通者
多其間明君賢輔間嘗崇獎高潔以激
厲一時如不拜諫議遇以故人不受右
相待爲賓友固辭諫官特加待制安於
靜退乞賜甄擢私書不至京師召復御
史問訊不及政府薦充舘職若此者可
===
歷數其人歟我
國家所以造士道民者率由禮義廉耻而又
風勸養厲于其間宜乎道德可一風俗
可同也夫何習俗尚未盡美而士風亦
未盡淳恬退者固多冒進者猶或間有
其故何歟恭遇
皇上聖資高明動稽堯舜力欲挽回隆古之盛
茲固首務也歷考前聞或謂退讓不可
以刑罰使或謂莫若倡清議于天下或
punctuated: 問：廉耻者，士人之美節；風俗者，天下之大事也。古昔人知自重，行已有耻，而習以相安，此豈一朝一夕之故哉？秦漢而下，士多隨世以就功名，守義者少，尚通者多。其間明君賢輔，間嘗崇獎高潔，以激厲一時。如不拜諫議，遇以故人；不受右相，待爲賓友；固辭諫官，特加待制；安於靜退，乞賜甄擢；私書不至京師，召復御史；問訊不及政府，薦充舘職。若此者，可歷數其人歟？我國家所以造士道民者，率由禮義廉耻，而又風勸養厲于其間，宜乎道德可一，風俗可同也。夫何習俗尚未盡美，而士風亦未盡淳？恬退者固多，冒進者猶或間有，其故何歟？恭遇皇上聖資高明，動稽堯舜，力欲挽回隆古之盛，茲固首務也。歷考前聞，或謂退讓不可以刑罰使，或謂莫若倡清議于天下，或
translation_en:
Question: Integrity and a sense of shame are admirable virtues in scholars; customs are a matter of great consequence for all under Heaven. In antiquity, people knew to respect themselves and had a sense of shame in their conduct, becoming accustomed to living harmoniously together. Could this have come about in a single morning or evening? From the Qin and Han onward, scholars mostly accommodated themselves to their times in pursuit of achievement and renown. Few upheld righteousness; many prized advancement. During those times, enlightened rulers and worthy ministers occasionally honored and rewarded men of lofty integrity to inspire their contemporaries. Thus, one who declined appointment as Remonstrance Counselor was treated as an old friend; one who refused to become Chief Councilor of the Right was treated as a guest and friend; one who firmly declined a remonstrance post was specially granted the title of Edict Attendant; one who was content with quiet retirement was the subject of a request that he be selected for promotion; one whose private letters never reached the capital was summoned back as a censor; and one who sent no inquiries or greetings to the chief councilors was recommended for a library post. Can you enumerate the men who exemplify such conduct?

The means by which our dynasty cultivates scholars and guides the people follow ritual propriety, righteousness, integrity, and a sense of shame, while also encouraging, nurturing, and inspiring them. It should therefore be possible to unify moral standards and bring customs into accord. Why, then, are customary practices still not wholly admirable, and the ethos of scholars still not wholly sincere? Although many are content to remain quietly withdrawn, some still seek advancement presumptuously. What is the reason for this?

We reverently enjoy the reign of His Majesty, whose sagely endowments are lofty and enlightened, who takes Yao and Shun as his models in every action, and who strives to restore the flourishing condition of high antiquity. This is assuredly a foremost task. Examining earlier teachings in turn, some say that modest withdrawal and deference cannot be compelled through punishments; others say that nothing is better than promoting principled public judgment throughout the realm; others …

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
謂崇靜退以率之或謂妙求人物參錯
立朝之數說者施之于今何者為當抑
别有其本乎願相與一論之
問孔門學者以德行言語政事文學並稱
而獨稱顏子為好學曰不遷怒不貳過
夷考之其過與怒無聞焉顏子嘗曰夫
子博我以文約我以禮亦不見其所謂
文也然則顏子所好果何學歟自是千
有餘年獨宋儒有曰學顏子之所學曰
===
===
顏子示不違如愚之學於後世曰顏子
之學與今之學異觀其道之所傳有天
資出人造養深遠者有探索本原洞見
道體者有默坐澄心體認天理者而皆
不涉於言語文字之間豈即所謂顏子
之學歟厥後朱子繼出乃取聖賢之遺
言遺旨發明精蘊自有經傳以來著述
之盛一人而已其書一出天下家傳而
人誦之學者曉然趨道之至正誠所謂
punctuated:
謂崇靜退以率之，或謂妙求人物，參錯立朝。之數說者，施之于今，何者為當？抑别有其本乎？願相與一論之。

問：孔門學者，以德行、言語、政事、文學並稱，而獨稱顏子為好學，曰：「不遷怒，不貳過。」夷考之，其過與怒無聞焉。顏子嘗曰：「夫子博我以文，約我以禮。」亦不見其所謂文也。然則顏子所好，果何學歟？自是千有餘年，獨宋儒有曰：「學顏子之所學。」曰：「顏子示不違如愚之學於後世。」曰：「顏子之學與今之學異。」觀其道之所傳，有天資出人、造養深遠者，有探索本原、洞見道體者，有默坐澄心、體認天理者，而皆不涉於言語文字之間，豈即所謂顏子之學歟？厥後朱子繼出，乃取聖賢之遺言遺旨，發明精蘊。自有經傳以來，著述之盛，一人而已。其書一出，天下家傳而人誦之，學者曉然趨道之至正，誠所謂
translation_en:
…say that quiet withdrawal should be honored to set an example for them; others advocate discerning searches for worthy men and appointing them in varied combinations at court. Of these several proposals, which would be appropriate to apply today? Or is there some other underlying basis? Let us discuss this together.

Question: Among those who studied in Confucius’s school, moral conduct, speech, government service, and literary learning were all recognized, yet Yan Zi alone was singled out as loving learning. Confucius said of him: “He did not transfer his anger to others, nor repeat a fault.” Yet on careful examination, we hear nothing of his faults or anger. Yan Zi once said: “The Master broadens me through cultural learning and restrains me through ritual.” Yet here, too, we do not see what this cultural learning actually comprised. What learning, then, did Yan Zi truly love? More than a thousand years later, it was only among the Song Confucians that we find such statements as: “Learn what Yan Zi learned”; “Yan Zi showed later generations a way of learning in which he offered no contradiction and seemed foolish”; and “Yan Zi’s learning differed from the learning of today.” Looking at those to whom this Way was transmitted, some possessed exceptional natural gifts and attained profound self-cultivation; some investigated the roots and origins and clearly apprehended the substance of the Way; some sat silently, clearing their minds and apprehending heavenly principle. None of these practices involved speech or writing. Could this be what is meant by Yan Zi’s learning?

Subsequently Zhu Zi emerged. He took the words and underlying meanings bequeathed by the sages and worthies and elucidated their subtle depths. Since the existence of the Classics and their commentaries, he alone had attained such abundance in writing. Once his books appeared, households throughout the realm passed them on and people recited them. Students clearly understood how to approach the utmost correctness of the Way. Truly, he may be called…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有大造於萬世者也當時乃有陸子靜
者議其專道問學而不尊德性朱子又
謂子靜之學不自知其日入于禪儒先
已有定論無庸贅矣然顔子不以言語
政事文章爲學而朱子似以著述爲教
同乎戾乎且今之讀其書者多取之以
資論說爲文章而不知所以反之約其
弊胡爲乎然也夫學貴知要而必有所
從入也諸生試舉所嘗用力者告我
===
問禹貢揚州之田下下今嘉湖與蘇松諸
郡皆其境也計其財賦所入幾當天下
之半夫以今視昔地非加廣而取之之
多如此民何以堪之古者什一之法後
世弗可行矣獨不能稍從節省以寬吾
民與今天下財力大抵殫盡而此諸郡
其尤也其間積弊之病民者蓋不可縷
數當事者亦嘗爲之深憂而卒未有所
處也夫官逋日積而長鄉賦者靡不破
punctuated:
有大造於萬世者也。當時乃有陸子靜者，議其專道問學而不尊德性。朱子又謂子靜之學，不自知其日入于禪。儒先已有定論，無庸贅矣。然顔子不以言語、政事、文章爲學，而朱子似以著述爲教，同乎？戾乎？且今之讀其書者，多取之以資論說、爲文章，而不知所以反之約，其弊胡爲乎然也？夫學貴知要，而必有所從入也。諸生試舉所嘗用力者告我。

問：《禹貢》揚州之田下下，今嘉湖與蘇松諸郡皆其境也。計其財賦所入，幾當天下之半。夫以今視昔，地非加廣，而取之之多如此，民何以堪之？古者什一之法，後世弗可行矣，獨不能稍從節省以寬吾民與？今天下財力大抵殫盡，而此諸郡其尤也。其間積弊之病民者，蓋不可縷數。當事者亦嘗爲之深憂，而卒未有所處也。夫官逋日積，而長鄉賦者靡不破
translation_en:
…one who has rendered an immense service to all generations. At that time, however, Lu Zijing criticized him for concentrating exclusively on inquiry and learning without honoring the moral nature. Master Zhu, in turn, said that Zijing’s learning was drifting daily into Chan Buddhism without his realizing it. Earlier Confucian scholars have already reached a settled judgment on this, and further discussion is unnecessary. Yet Master Yan did not take speech, government affairs, or literary composition as the substance of learning, while Master Zhu seems to have taught through his writings. Are their approaches consistent or opposed? Moreover, those who read his books today mostly draw on them to furnish arguments and compose essays, without knowing how to return from this breadth of learning to what is essential. Why has this failing arisen? In learning, grasping the essentials is precious, but one must have a point of entry. You candidates should tell me about the matters on which you have actually exerted yourselves.

Question: In the Tribute of Yu (Yu gong), the fields of Yangzhou are ranked lowest of the low. The present prefectures of Jiaxing, Huzhou, Suzhou, and Songjiang all lie within its territory. Their fiscal revenues amount to nearly half those of the empire. Comparing the present with the past, the territory has not grown larger, yet so much is extracted from it: how can the people bear this? The ancient system of taxing one-tenth cannot be implemented in later ages; but can we not at least make some economies to ease the burden on our people? Today the financial resources of the empire are largely exhausted, and these prefectures are especially afflicted. The accumulated abuses that harm their people are too numerous to enumerate. Those responsible have also felt deep concern over them, yet ultimately have taken no measures to address them. Tax arrears owed to the government accumulate daily, and those who oversee rural tax collection all suffer ruin…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
家何以捄之徵斂無經而輸納之費動
至數倍何以省之徭役有常期矣而輕
重失均何以平之田賦有定額矣而詭
射之弊至不可勝窮何以釐之民多轉
徙而荒蕪未闢又遺其税以為公私之
累何以處之水利有專官而旱潦不免
於涸溢何以拯之當是時欲求經常簡
易之法可以弭斯患者非豪傑之士誰
與議此故願諸君之極言之也
===
問記稱問國之富數馬以對馬之所繫亦
重矣考之周禮大司馬之屬有校人以
掌王六馬有廋人以掌十二閑又有趣
馬巫馬馬質牧師圉師圉人之類夫一
事而設官之多如此無乃失之冗與至
其取之民者自丘甸以上積而數之至
於一同之地出戎馬百乘亦不為不多
矣不識當時國有征役何以能弗擾而
事集與抑其法亦可用於今日否與今
punctuated:
家，何以捄之？徵斂無經，而輸納之費動至數倍，何以省之？徭役有常期矣，而輕重失均，何以平之？田賦有定額矣，而詭射之弊至不可勝窮，何以釐之？民多轉徙，而荒蕪未闢，又遺其税以為公私之累，何以處之？水利有專官，而旱潦不免於涸溢，何以拯之？當是時，欲求經常簡易之法，可以弭斯患者，非豪傑之士，誰與議此？故願諸君之極言之也。

問：記稱：「問國之富，數馬以對。」馬之所繫亦重矣。考之《周禮》，大司馬之屬有校人，以掌王六馬；有廋人，以掌十二閑；又有趣馬、巫馬、馬質、牧師、圉師、圉人之類。夫一事而設官之多如此，無乃失之冗與？至其取之民者，自丘甸以上，積而數之，至於一同之地，出戎馬百乘，亦不為不多矣。不識當時國有征役，何以能弗擾而事集與？抑其法亦可用於今日否與？今
translation_en:
…their households ruined: how can this be remedied? Levies follow no regular rules, and the costs of delivering payments often reach several times the amount due: how can these be reduced? Labor service has its prescribed periods, yet its burdens are unevenly distributed: how can these be equalized? Land taxes have fixed quotas, yet fraudulent devices for evading them are virtually inexhaustible: how can these be rectified? Many people have migrated, leaving waste land unreclaimed and taxes outstanding as a burden on both government and private households: how should this be handled? There are officials specifically responsible for water conservancy, yet droughts and excessive rains still bring dried-up waterways and overflowing waters: how can relief be provided? At such a time, we seek regular, simple, and practicable methods capable of ending these afflictions. With whom could we deliberate on this, if not men of outstanding ability? We therefore hope that you gentlemen will express your views fully.

Question: The Record of Rites states: “When asked about a state's wealth, one replies by counting its horses.” The matters that depend on horses are indeed weighty. Examining the Rites of Zhou, we find among the subordinates of the Minister of War a Director of Horse Management, responsible for the king's six categories of horses; stable keepers, responsible for the twelve stables; and also such officers as horse trainers, horse healers, horse appraisers, pasture masters, supervisors of grooms, and grooms. With so many offices established for a single undertaking, was this not excessively redundant? As for the contributions exacted from the people, if one adds them up from the territorial units of qiu and dian upward, an area of one tong supplied warhorses for a hundred chariots—a quantity by no means small. We wonder: when the state undertook military expeditions in those days, how could it accomplish the task without disturbing the people? And could those methods also be applied today? Now…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
國馬所出內則計丁以牧之民間外則用茶
以易之蕃夷是法也亦嘗襲前代之舊
與夫飼牧之民日困而孳畜不聞其蕃
息差發之制不行而招易所得未必皆
良也馬政之弊至今日極矣茲欲舉二
者之法一振起之使上不病國下不妨
民而馬皆足用若何而可諸生其必有
以處此矣
punctuated: 國馬所出，內則計丁以牧之民間，外則用茶以易之蕃夷。是法也，亦嘗襲前代之舊與？夫飼牧之民日困，而孳畜不聞其蕃息；差發之制不行，而招易所得未必皆良也。馬政之弊至今日極矣！茲欲舉二者之法，一振起之，使上不病國，下不妨民，而馬皆足用，若何而可？諸生其必有以處此矣。
translation_en: …As for the sources of horses for the state, within the realm, horse-rearing is assigned among the common people according to the number of adult males; beyond it, tea is exchanged for horses among the non-Chinese peoples of the frontier. Were these methods also inherited from earlier dynasties? The people who feed and rear horses grow poorer by the day, yet we hear of no increase in the breeding stock. The system of requisitions is not implemented, and the horses obtained by encouraging trade are not necessarily all of good quality. The failings of horse administration have now reached their extreme! If we wish to take up these two methods and thoroughly revitalize them, so that neither the state above is burdened nor the people below are hindered in their livelihoods, and horses are fully adequate for use, how can this be accomplished? You candidates must surely have a way to address this.

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
禮云禮云玉帛云乎哉樂云樂云鐘鼓云
乎哉
周如底
同考試官教諭唐批聖人語意含蓄深遠非
達禮樂者未易識是作默會成文詞理俱到其達
者乎
同考試官教諭林批題本正大作者頓尚華
===
藻而於夫子當時本旨亦頗反失之是篇明白典雅
詞若近簡而讀之自有一倡三嘆之妙殆有意於
變浮靡之習者與
考試官署郎中華批詞明潔而意具足當是
作者
考試官給事中陸批簡明可取
聖人論禮樂不專於末以見其本之有在也甚
矣禮樂之有本也玉帛鍾鼓特其末耳曾足以
盡之乎且夫禮樂之在天下不可一日無顧人
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

「禮云禮云，玉帛云乎哉？樂云樂云，鐘鼓云乎哉？」

周如底

同考試官教諭唐批：聖人語意含蓄深遠，非達禮樂者未易識。是作默會成文，詞理俱到，其達者乎！

同考試官教諭林批：題本正大，作者頓尚華藻，而於夫子當時本旨亦頗反失之。是篇明白典雅，詞若近簡，而讀之自有一倡三嘆之妙，殆有意於變浮靡之習者與！

考試官署郎中華批：詞明潔而意具足，當是作者。

考試官給事中陸批：簡明可取。

聖人論禮樂，不專於末，以見其本之有在也。甚矣，禮樂之有本也！玉帛鍾鼓，特其末耳，曾足以盡之乎？且夫禮樂之在天下，不可一日無，顧人
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“Ritual, ritual—is it merely jade and silk? Music, music—is it merely bells and drums?”

Zhou Rudi 周如底

Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: The Sage’s words convey an implicit meaning of great depth and reach; anyone who does not comprehend ritual and music will find it difficult to discern. This essay gives written form to a tacit understanding, attaining excellence in both expression and reasoning. Surely its author is one who comprehends them!

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: The topic is fundamentally upright and substantial. Writers have come to prize ornate diction [?], yet in doing so often lose sight of the Master’s original intent when he spoke. This essay is lucid, classically elegant, and refined. Its language may seem almost plain, but reading it brings the subtle pleasure of one voice singing out and three voices responding. Perhaps the author deliberately seeks to reform the prevailing habit of superficial extravagance!

Comment by Examiner Hua, Acting Director: The language is clear and clean, and the meaning fully expressed. Surely this is an accomplished writer.

Comment by Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary: Concise and clear; worthy of selection.

In discussing ritual and music, the Sage did not dwell exclusively on their outward details, thereby revealing that their foundation lies elsewhere. How profound is the foundation of ritual and music! Jade and silk, bells and drums, are merely their outward details. Could these possibly encompass them fully? Moreover, the world cannot go a single day without ritual and music; yet people …

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有終身由之而不知者矣自夫斯人之相際也
而有禮以節之禮云禮云孰不曰玉帛而已乎
夫禮行於文飾玉帛固不可無也然方其物之
未將必有所以為之先者彼圭璧之錯陳玄黃
之稠疊皆其具耳禮果專在是乎蓋禮非文飾
之謂也有無體之禮矣自夫斯人之相與也而
有樂以洽之樂云樂云孰不曰鍾鼓而已乎夫
樂寓於聲音鍾鼓固不可無也然方其聲之未
著必有所以為之主者彼節奏之抑揚音律之
===
高下特其文耳樂果專在是乎蓋樂非聲音之
謂也有無聲之樂矣要之玉帛不足以言禮敬
而將之斯禮之成也鍾鼓不足以言樂和而發
之斯樂之成也從事於禮樂者惡可遺其本而
惟末之是務哉聖人言此所以警當世者切矣
抑斯言卽易所謂道器之說耳禮樂之原出於
天地而其道則具於人心玉帛鍾鼓皆器也器
由道而立道以器而彰二者相須以成而先後
本末之間則自有等矣夫子所云雖一時有警
punctuated:
有終身由之而不知者矣。自夫斯人之相際也，而有禮以節之。禮云禮云，孰不曰玉帛而已乎？夫禮行於文飾，玉帛固不可無也。然方其物之未將，必有所以為之先者。彼圭璧之錯陳、玄黃之稠疊，皆其具耳。禮果專在是乎？蓋禮非文飾之謂也，有無體之禮矣。自夫斯人之相與也，而有樂以洽之。樂云樂云，孰不曰鍾鼓而已乎？夫樂寓於聲音，鍾鼓固不可無也。然方其聲之未著，必有所以為之主者。彼節奏之抑揚、音律之高下，特其文耳。樂果專在是乎？蓋樂非聲音之謂也，有無聲之樂矣。要之，玉帛不足以言禮，敬而將之，斯禮之成也；鍾鼓不足以言樂，和而發之，斯樂之成也。從事於禮樂者，惡可遺其本而惟末之是務哉？聖人言此，所以警當世者切矣。
抑斯言卽《易》所謂道器之說耳。禮樂之原出於天地，而其道則具於人心。玉帛鍾鼓皆器也。器由道而立，道以器而彰。二者相須以成，而先後本末之間，則自有等矣。夫子所云，雖一時有警
translation_en:
…there are those who follow them throughout their lives without understanding them. When people interact, ritual regulates their relations. “Ritual, ritual”—who does not say that it is merely jade and silk? Ritual is carried out through ornamented forms, and jade and silk certainly cannot be dispensed with. Yet before these objects are presented, there must be something that precedes them. The tablets and disks of jade arrayed together, and the dark and yellow silks piled in layers, are merely its implements. Does ritual really consist exclusively in these? Ritual does not mean ornamented forms: there is ritual without physical form.
When people associate, music brings them into harmony. “Music, music”—who does not say that it is merely bells and drums? Music resides in sound, and bells and drums certainly cannot be dispensed with. Yet before their sounds become audible, there must be something that governs them. The rise and fall of rhythms and the high and low pitches are merely its outward expression. Does music really consist exclusively in these? Music does not mean sound: there is music without sound.
In sum, jade and silk are insufficient to explain ritual. Present them with reverence, and ritual is fulfilled. Bells and drums are insufficient to explain music. Sound them in harmony, and music is fulfilled. How can those engaged in ritual and music abandon their root and attend solely to their outward manifestations? The sage’s words here offer an earnest admonition to his age.
Indeed, these words express precisely the teaching about the Way and concrete things found in the Book of Changes. Ritual and music originate in Heaven and Earth, while their Way is fully present in the human heart. Jade, silk, bells, and drums are all concrete things. Concrete things are established through the Way, and the Way is made manifest through concrete things. The two depend upon one another for their fulfillment; yet there is an inherent ordering between what comes first and what follows, between root and outward manifestation. Although what the Master said was an admonition prompted by the circumstances of his time…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之言而聖人制作之本意宜不外此故欲知禮
樂之情者必先明於道器之說而後可
唯天下至誠為能經綸天下之大經立天
下之大本知天地之化育夫焉有所倚
肫肫其仁淵淵其淵浩浩其天
姜良翰
同考試官教諭徐批至誠功用自然之妙舉
者類能言之然體認不精支離可厭是義詞理俱
到非平日用心於內者不能作
===
同考試官教諭鄭批一破卓有定見講中以
誠字發明精蘊讀之令人豁然
同考試官學正孫批題本難作諸卷非泛則
畧惟此篇體認親切而氣象舂容即文可以知人矣
考試官署郎中華批說理精密
考試官給事中陸批自是理趣文字
中庸極言至誠之道必贊其道之至也夫道之
所以為至者一誠而已中庸極言以贊之聖人
之道之極致豈復有餘蘊哉且均是人也而有
punctuated:
之言，而聖人制作之本意宜不外此。故欲知禮樂之情者，必先明於道器之說而後可。

唯天下至誠，為能經綸天下之大經，立天下之大本，知天地之化育。夫焉有所倚？肫肫其仁，淵淵其淵，浩浩其天。
姜良翰

同考試官教諭徐批：至誠功用自然之妙，舉者類能言之，然體認不精，支離可厭。是義詞理俱到，非平日用心於內者不能作。

同考試官教諭鄭批：一破卓有定見，講中以誠字發明精蘊，讀之令人豁然。

同考試官學正孫批：題本難作，諸卷非泛則畧，惟此篇體認親切，而氣象舂容，即文可以知人矣。

考試官署郎中華批：說理精密。

考試官給事中陸批：自是理趣文字。

中庸極言至誠之道，必贊其道之至也。夫道之所以為至者，一誠而已。中庸極言以贊之，聖人之道之極致，豈復有餘蘊哉？且均是人也，而有
translation_en:
…words of admonition, yet the original intent behind the sage’s institutions surely goes no further than this. Thus, anyone wishing to understand the true nature of rites and music must first understand the relationship between the Way and concrete implements.

“Only one possessed of utmost sincerity under Heaven can order the great guiding relationships of the world, establish its great foundation, and understand the transforming and nourishing activities of Heaven and Earth. On what, then, could he depend? How earnest his benevolence, how deep his profundity, how vast his Heaven!”
Jiang Lianghan

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: “Candidates can generally speak of the wondrous spontaneity of utmost sincerity’s efficacy. Yet their understanding is imprecise, and their fragmented explanations are tiresome. This essay succeeds in both expression and reasoning; only someone who habitually devotes himself to inward cultivation could have written it.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “The opening interpretation immediately displays a remarkably firm understanding. In the exposition, the word ‘sincerity’ brings out the profound subtleties; reading it gives one a sudden sense of illumination.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Sun, School Instructor: “The topic is inherently difficult to write on. The other essays are either vague or cursory. This essay alone shows an intimate grasp of the subject and a spacious, unhurried bearing [?]. From the writing itself one can know the man.”

Comment by Examiner Hua, Acting Bureau Director: “The exposition of principle is precise and meticulous.”

Comment by Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary: “This is indeed writing imbued with the savor of principle.”

The Doctrine of the Mean speaks exhaustively of the Way of utmost sincerity, surely to extol that Way’s perfection. What makes the Way perfect is sincerity alone. When the Doctrine of the Mean speaks exhaustively in its praise, could any profundity of the supreme perfection of the sage’s Way remain unexpressed? Moreover, all are equally human, yet there are…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
所謂至誠者焉渾乎賦予之眞而天德無不實
湛乎純一之體而天下莫能加是故天下有大
經焉人倫是也則隨其分而比其類各盡夫當
然之實所謂惟聖盡倫而天下後世之法於是
乎在矣天下有大本焉人性是也則得於天者
全於己無一毫私偽之雜所謂惟聖盡性而千
變萬化之道皆此焉出矣且化育著于兩間至
神妙也則斯理之中涵一天命之於穆而於所
謂發見流行之實與之默契而弗違焉凡若此
===
者蓋其無妄盡天下之理極誠一天下之動不
假於思勉而亦無事乎心力夫豈有所倚著于
物而後能哉是以自其盡倫者言之五品之間
藹然至恩之篤純乎其純而情意之懇到是即
仁而已矣而無或間焉者也自其盡性者言之
一中之立允為衆理之源淵乎其淵而靜深之
無際是即淵而已矣而無或二焉者也自其知
化者言之神明不測一太極本然之妙而浩浩
乎其廣大是即所謂天焉又非特如之而已也
punctuated: 所謂至誠者焉，渾乎賦予之眞，而天德無不實；湛乎純一之體，而天下莫能加。是故天下有大經焉，人倫是也，則隨其分而比其類，各盡夫當然之實，所謂惟聖盡倫，而天下後世之法於是乎在矣。天下有大本焉，人性是也，則得於天者全於己，無一毫私偽之雜，所謂惟聖盡性，而千變萬化之道皆此焉出矣。且化育著于兩間，至神妙也，則斯理之中涵一天命之於穆，而於所謂發見流行之實，與之默契而弗違焉。凡若此者，蓋其無妄盡天下之理，極誠一天下之動，不假於思勉，而亦無事乎心力，夫豈有所倚著于物而後能哉？是以自其盡倫者言之，五品之間，藹然至恩之篤，純乎其純，而情意之懇到，是即仁而已矣，而無或間焉者也。自其盡性者言之，一中之立，允為衆理之源，淵乎其淵，而靜深之無際，是即淵而已矣，而無或二焉者也。自其知化者言之，神明不測，一太極本然之妙，而浩浩乎其廣大，是即所謂天焉，又非特如之而已也。
translation_en:
…there are those spoken of as possessing utmost sincerity. Wholly preserving the genuineness bestowed upon them, they possess Heaven’s virtue with nothing unreal in it; profoundly grounded in a pure and undivided constitution, they are unsurpassed by anyone under Heaven. Thus, there are great constant norms under Heaven: these are the human relationships. In accordance with the respective roles and corresponding categories of these relationships, they fully realize what each rightly requires. This is what is meant by saying that only the sage fully fulfills the human relationships; herein lies the standard for all under Heaven and for later generations. There is a great foundation under Heaven: this is human nature. What they receive from Heaven is preserved whole within themselves, without the slightest admixture of selfishness or falsity. This is what is meant by saying that only the sage fully realizes human nature; from this proceed the principles of all the myriad changes and transformations.

Moreover, the transforming and nourishing processes manifest between Heaven and Earth are supremely wondrous. Within this principle they encompass the profound mystery of Heaven’s mandate; with what is called its actual manifestation and circulation, they accord silently and never diverge. All this is because, free from falsity, they fully realize the principles of all under Heaven, and through perfect sincerity unify all its movements. They need not resort to deliberation or effort, nor expend their mental powers. How could they attain this only by relying upon external things?

Thus, speaking of their fulfillment of human relationships, among the five relationships there flourishes the deepest benevolence, pure in its purity, with feelings and intentions utterly earnest. This is simply humaneness, admitting of no interruption. Speaking of their full realization of human nature, the establishment of the single central equilibrium is truly the source of all principles. Deep in its depth, boundless in its still profundity, this is simply depth, admitting of no division. Speaking of their knowledge of transformation, their unfathomable spiritual intelligence is wholly the inherent wonder of the Supreme Ultimate (taiji), vast in its immensity. This is what is called Heaven itself, and does more than merely resemble it.

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
上下一致徹性命之精微道器相安妙身心之
神化而天下至誠之功用斯其至矣借曰有所
倚而能之固不若是其至也吁其斯以為天道
歟大抵人之一心萬善咸備盛德大業皆由此
出至誠之道亦惟有是心而已是心也人病弗
求耳擴而充之人皆可以為堯舜復而執之君
子之所以不可及也要其所入亦自下學為己
立心之始求之故曰惟慎獨可以行王道
夫道一而已矣成覸謂齊景公曰彼丈夫
===
也我丈夫也吾何畏彼哉顏淵曰舜何
人也予何人也有為者亦若是公明儀
曰文王我師也周公豈欺我哉
謝紘
同考試官教諭陳批能發孟子道性善之旨
而氣昌辭達殆究心於性學而有得者
考試官署郎中華批峻整可誦
考試官給事中陸批得孟子語意
大賢論道無二致而引言以明之所以發性善
punctuated:
上下一致，徹性命之精微；道器相安，妙身心之神化，而天下至誠之功用斯其至矣。借曰有所倚而能之，固不若是其至也。吁！其斯以為天道歟？大抵人之一心，萬善咸備，盛德大業皆由此出。至誠之道，亦惟有是心而已。是心也，人病弗求耳。擴而充之，人皆可以為堯舜；復而執之，君子之所以不可及也。要其所入，亦自下學為己、立心之始求之。故曰：「惟慎獨可以行王道。」
夫道一而已矣。成覸謂齊景公曰：「彼丈夫也，我丈夫也，吾何畏彼哉？」顏淵曰：「舜何人也？予何人也？有為者亦若是。」公明儀曰：「文王我師也，周公豈欺我哉？」
謝紘
同考試官教諭陳批：「能發孟子道性善之旨，而氣昌辭達，殆究心於性學而有得者。」
考試官署郎中華批：「峻整可誦。」
考試官給事中陸批：「得孟子語意。」
大賢論道無二致，而引言以明之，所以發性善
translation_en:
…Above and below form a single unity, penetrating the subtleties of human nature and destiny; the Way and its concrete manifestations accord with one another, bringing the wondrous transformation of body and mind to perfection. Here the efficacy of utmost sincerity under Heaven reaches its culmination. Supposing that one could accomplish this only by relying on something else, it certainly would not attain such perfection. Ah! Is this what constitutes the Way of Heaven? Within the single human heart, all goodness is fully present; abundant virtue and great achievements alike issue from it. The way of utmost sincerity likewise consists simply in possessing this heart. The trouble is only that people fail to seek it. By extending and fully developing it, everyone can become a Yao or a Shun; by recovering and holding fast to it, the gentleman becomes beyond others’ reach. To seek the point of entry, one must look to the beginnings of learning in everyday matters for one’s own moral cultivation and establishing one’s resolve. Thus it is said: “Only through vigilance when alone can one practice the kingly Way.”
“The Way is one, and that is all. Cheng Jian said to Duke Jing of Qi: ‘He is a man, and I too am a man. Why should I fear him?’ Yan Yuan said: ‘What kind of person was Shun? What kind of person am I? Anyone who strives can become like him.’ Gongming Yi said: ‘King Wen is my teacher. How could the Duke of Zhou have deceived me?’”
Xie Hong
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “He brings out the purport of Mengzi’s teaching on the goodness of human nature. His spirit is vigorous and his expression fluent; he appears to have devoted himself to the study of human nature and gained insight into it.”
Comment by Examiner Hua, Acting Director: “Elevated and well ordered; worthy of recitation.”
Comment by Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary: “He grasps the meaning of Mengzi’s words.”
The great worthy’s discussion of the Way admits no divergent principles, and he quotes these sayings to illuminate it, thereby bringing out the goodness of human nature…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之旨備矣夫人性之善未始不一也不然何以
見聖賢之必可學哉宜孟子以是釋世子之疑
也其意若曰道之原出於天而其體存乎性性
之所在道之所在也是故時有古今而天之賦
於物者未始不均人有聖愚而我之得於天者
未嘗不一蓋性善之外無他道而論性之外無
他說矣然非特吾有是言也古人有是言也觀
諸成覸之謂齊景公則曰聖賢與我均之爲丈
夫也在彼不過能盡其性耳我能自勉則亦聖
===
===
賢而已何足畏哉顏淵之言則曰舜之於予均
是人也在舜不過能充其性耳人能有爲則亦
如舜而已何所愧哉若公明儀則又以爲彼文
王優入於聖域而周公稱其爲我師是蓋以人
性無不同故聖人有可學驗之以理而理所必
有言雖大而非誇也度之於力而力有可能事
雖難而非異也周公豈欺我者哉夫三人不同
而其言一也三人之言不同而性善之旨一也
所謂道無二致者如此世子亦惟篤信力行以
punctuated: 之旨備矣。夫人性之善，未始不一也。不然，何以見聖賢之必可學哉？宜孟子以是釋世子之疑也。其意若曰：道之原出於天，而其體存乎性；性之所在，道之所在也。是故時有古今，而天之賦於物者未始不均；人有聖愚，而我之得於天者未嘗不一。蓋性善之外無他道，而論性之外無他說矣。然非特吾有是言也，古人有是言也。觀諸成覸之謂齊景公，則曰：「聖賢與我，均之爲丈夫也。在彼不過能盡其性耳，我能自勉，則亦聖賢而已，何足畏哉？」顏淵之言則曰：「舜之於予，均是人也。在舜不過能充其性耳，人能有爲，則亦如舜而已，何所愧哉？」若公明儀，則又以爲彼文王優入於聖域，而周公稱其爲我師，是蓋以人性無不同，故聖人有可學。驗之以理，而理所必有，言雖大而非誇也；度之於力，而力有可能，事雖難而非異也。周公豈欺我者哉？夫三人不同，而其言一也；三人之言不同，而性善之旨一也。所謂道無二致者如此。世子亦惟篤信力行，以
translation_en:
…the meaning is fully set forth. The goodness of human nature has always been the same in everyone. Otherwise, how could we know that becoming a sage or worthy through learning is necessarily possible? It was fitting that Mengzi used this to resolve the heir apparent’s doubts. His meaning was as follows: the Way originates in Heaven, and its substance resides in human nature. Wherever human nature resides, there too resides the Way. Thus, although times differ between antiquity and the present, what Heaven bestows upon beings has always been equally imparted; although people differ as sages and fools, what we receive from Heaven has always been the same. Beyond the goodness of human nature there is no other Way, and beyond discussing human nature there is no other teaching. Yet I am not alone in saying this: the ancients said it too.

Consider what Cheng Jian said to Duke Jing of Qi: “Sages and worthies and I are equally men. They have simply succeeded in fully realizing their nature. If I exert myself, I too shall be a sage or worthy. Why should I stand in awe of them?” Yan Yuan said: “Shun and I are equally human. Shun simply succeeded in fully developing his nature. Anyone who makes the effort can likewise become like Shun. What cause is there for shame?” As for Gongming Yi, he held that King Wen had attained the realm of sagehood with ease, and that the Duke of Zhou called him ‘my teacher.’ This was surely because human nature is the same in everyone, so becoming a sage through learning is possible. Tested against principle, this is something that principle necessarily admits: although the claim is great, it is no exaggeration. Measured against human capacity, it is something within our power: although the undertaking is difficult, it is nothing extraordinary. Could the Duke of Zhou have deceived me?

These three men were different, but their message was one. Their words differed, but their meaning concerning the goodness of human nature was one. This is what it means to say that the Way admits of no divergence. The heir apparent need only hold firm in his belief and exert himself in practice, so as to…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
師聖賢而已尚何他說之可求乎抑孟子性善
之云豈獨爲世子告哉實以示天下後世也自
道學不明而儒者之言性往往失之君子以爲
欲知性之本善求諸心而已方其寂然不動之
中善且未形而惡有所謂惡又惡有所謂善惡
混與三品者哉夫心與性亦有異乎曰非異也
語有之曰心之神明是謂性
易
是故君子所居而安者易之序也所樂而
===
玩者爻之辭也是故君子居則觀其象
而玩其辭動則觀其變而玩其占是以
自天祐之吉无不利
俞介
同考試官教諭毛批詞理明瑩機軸自別場
中如此作者絕少
同考試官教諭吳批題本明白正大作者紛
紜令人厭觀認理精切措詞渾雅無踰此篇而一
結尤有發明其深於易者乎
punctuated:
師聖賢而已，尚何他說之可求乎？抑孟子性善之云，豈獨爲世子告哉？實以示天下後世也。自道學不明，而儒者之言性往往失之。君子以爲欲知性之本善，求諸心而已。方其寂然不動之中，善且未形，而惡有所謂惡？又惡有所謂善惡混與三品者哉？夫心與性亦有異乎？曰：非異也。語有之曰：「心之神明，是謂性。」

易

是故君子所居而安者，易之序也；所樂而玩者，爻之辭也。是故君子居則觀其象而玩其辭，動則觀其變而玩其占。是以自天祐之，吉无不利。

俞介

同考試官教諭毛批：詞理明瑩，機軸自別，場中如此作者絕少。

同考試官教諭吳批：題本明白正大，作者紛紜，令人厭觀。認理精切，措詞渾雅，無踰此篇，而一結尤有發明。其深於易者乎？
translation_en:
…take the sages and worthies as teachers, and nothing more. What other doctrine need he seek? Moreover, were Mengzi’s words on the goodness of human nature addressed solely to the heir apparent? They were in fact intended to instruct all under Heaven and later generations. Since the learning of the Way became obscured, scholars discussing human nature have often gone astray. The gentleman holds that to understand the original goodness of human nature, one need only seek it in the mind. While the mind is still and unmoving, even goodness has not yet taken manifest form: how could there be what is called evil? And how could there be what is called a mixture of good and evil, or the three grades of human nature? Are the mind and human nature, then, different? The answer is: they are not. As the saying goes, “The mind’s spiritual intelligence is what is called human nature.”

Book of Changes

“Thus, what the gentleman dwells in and finds peace in is the sequence of the Changes; what he delights in and ponders is the wording of its lines. Thus, when at rest, the gentleman observes its images and ponders its statements; when acting, he observes its changes and ponders its prognostications. Therefore, Heaven itself aids him: good fortune, with nothing unfavorable.”

Yu Jie 俞介

Comment by Associate Examiner Mao, Instructor: The language and reasoning are lucid and luminous, and the composition has a distinctive organizing conception. Very few candidates in this examination write like this.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: The topic itself is clear, upright, and substantial, yet writers treat it in such confused profusion that reading them becomes tiresome. In its precise grasp of principle and its rounded, elegant diction, no essay surpasses this one. Its conclusion is especially illuminating. Surely its author has a profound understanding of the Changes!

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭宋批所居而安說多不一是
義順題平寫自覺明備子之所養可知矣
考試官署郎中華批善體貼
考試官給事中陸批是善言易者
大傳即君子得易之妙著君子學易之益甚矣
君子之有得乎易也然非動靜兼致其學亦孰
從而得之哉且易旣作於聖人則象變辭占之
已具而天下之理盡之矣非君子不能學也何
則君子以言以動順適乎隨時變易之天而無
===
所困所居何其安也蓋易有事理當然之序昭
著於卦爻而君子為能得之時有萬變一陰陽
消息之流通也事或殊途一剛柔盈虛之運用
也泰然從容於自足孰非易之序乎心領神會
沉潛於得意忘言之表而不可逺所樂何其深
也蓋易有吉凶悔吝之辭發揮於諸爻而君子
為能玩之精蘊之所發有以研其旨趣也隱顯
之所之有以極其幾微也悠然涵泳于不厭孰
非爻之辭乎是蓋隨在有得乎易矣然非學何
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭宋批：所居而安，說多不一，是義順題平寫，自覺明備，子之所養可知矣。
考試官署郎中華批：善體貼。
考試官給事中陸批：是善言易者。
大傳即君子得易之妙，著君子學易之益。甚矣，君子之有得乎易也！然非動靜兼致其學，亦孰從而得之哉？且易旣作於聖人，則象變辭占之已具，而天下之理盡之矣，非君子不能學也。何則？君子以言以動，順適乎隨時變易之天，而無所困，所居何其安也！蓋易有事理當然之序，昭著於卦爻，而君子為能得之。時有萬變，一陰陽消息之流通也；事或殊途，一剛柔盈虛之運用也。泰然從容於自足，孰非易之序乎？心領神會，沉潛於得意忘言之表，而不可逺，所樂何其深也！蓋易有吉凶悔吝之辭，發揮於諸爻，而君子為能玩之。精蘊之所發，有以研其旨趣也；隱顯之所之，有以極其幾微也。悠然涵泳于不厭，孰非爻之辭乎？是蓋隨在有得乎易矣，然非學何
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Song, Instructor, comments: “There are many differing explanations of ‘that in which he abides and finds peace.’ This essay follows the topic and sets it out straightforwardly, achieving clarity and completeness. From this one can discern what you have cultivated within yourself.”
Examiner Hua, Acting Director, comments: “It enters admirably into the meaning.”
Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary, comments: “Here is someone who speaks well of the Book of Changes.”
The Great Commentary draws upon the subtlety of the gentleman’s understanding of the Book of Changes to reveal the benefits of his studying it. Profound indeed is what the gentleman gains from the Changes! Yet unless he fully pursues its study in both activity and stillness, how could he attain this understanding? Since the Changes was composed by the sages, its images, transformations, statements, and prognostications are all complete, and the principles of all under Heaven are fully encompassed within it. Only the gentleman can study it. Why is this? In speech and action, the gentleman accords with Heaven as it changes with the times, encountering no impediment. How secure he is in that wherein he abides! For the Changes contains the proper order of affairs and their principles, clearly displayed in its hexagrams and lines, and the gentleman is able to grasp it. Though circumstances undergo myriad changes, these are all the circulating ebb and flow of yin and yang; though affairs may follow different courses, these are all the operation of firmness and yielding, fullness and emptiness. Calm and composed in his own sufficiency, what does he encounter that is not the order of the Changes? He apprehends it in his heart and understands it in spirit, immersing himself in a realm beyond words, where meaning is grasped and words forgotten; he cannot distance himself from it. How profound is his delight! For the Changes contains statements concerning good fortune, misfortune, regret, and humiliation, elaborated in its various lines, and the gentleman is able to ponder them. Where their subtle import emerges, he has the means to investigate their purport; where the hidden and manifest tend, he has the means to fathom their subtlest workings. At ease, he immerses himself in them without tiring: what does he encounter that is not the statements of the lines? Thus he gains understanding of the Changes wherever he finds himself. Yet without study, how …

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
以致之也哉是以君子時乎靜焉尚象以觀其
形容而尤玩味乎所繫之辭先事而說諸心也
時乎動焉尚變以觀其變化而尤精審乎所值
之占臨事而研諸慮也靜知所學則靜與天俱
動知所學則動與吉會若或相之在在有資深
逢原之益矣何所往而不利哉若或祐之隨處
有引伸觸類之妙矣何所適而不宜哉夫君子
學易之事如此其資於易者深矣人亦何憚而
不學乎大抵學易之道不外乎安分窮理二者
===
而已君子所樂而玩玩其理也所居而安安其
分也安分則窮理愈精窮理則安分愈固此君
子終身之心學也若不進於此而徒牽滯于辭
變象占之間則亦藝焉而已其諸異乎君子之
學歟
復則不妄矣故受之以无妄
翁溥
同考試官教諭毛批此題似易實難場中多
為所窘是篇平平寫出若不經意且明白冲淡必
punctuated:
以致之也哉？是以君子時乎靜焉，尚象以觀其形容，而尤玩味乎所繫之辭，先事而說諸心也；時乎動焉，尚變以觀其變化，而尤精審乎所值之占，臨事而研諸慮也。靜知所學，則靜與天俱；動知所學，則動與吉會。若或相之，在在有資深逢原之益矣，何所往而不利哉？若或祐之，隨處有引伸觸類之妙矣，何所適而不宜哉？夫君子學易之事如此，其資於易者深矣，人亦何憚而不學乎？大抵學易之道，不外乎安分、窮理二者而已。君子所樂而玩，玩其理也；所居而安，安其分也。安分則窮理愈精，窮理則安分愈固，此君子終身之心學也。若不進於此，而徒牽滯于辭、變、象、占之間，則亦藝焉而已，其諸異乎君子之學歟？
「復則不妄矣，故受之以无妄。」
翁溥
同考試官教諭毛批：此題似易實難，場中多為所窘。是篇平平寫出，若不經意，且明白冲淡，必
translation_en:
…how could one attain this? Thus, when the gentleman is at rest, he esteems the images in order to observe their forms, and especially savors the statements attached to them, finding delight in his heart before events arise. When he acts, he esteems the changes in order to observe their transformations, and especially scrutinizes the prognostication he encounters, examining it in his deliberations as he faces events. If he knows what to study in stillness, then in stillness he is at one with Heaven; if he knows what to study in action, then in action he meets with good fortune. As though someone were assisting him, everywhere he gains the benefit of drawing deeply upon his resources and finding their source. Wherever he goes, how could he fail to benefit? As though someone were protecting him, everywhere he finds the subtle efficacy of extending his understanding and comprehending analogous cases. Wherever he turns, how could anything be inappropriate? Such is the gentleman’s study of the Changes, and profound indeed is the sustenance he draws from it. Why, then, should anyone shrink from studying it? In general, the way of studying the Changes consists simply of two things: resting content in one’s allotted place and investigating principle exhaustively. What the gentleman delights in and contemplates is its principle; what he occupies and rests content in is his allotted place. The more content he is in his allotted place, the more refined his investigation of principle becomes; the more thoroughly he investigates principle, the more firmly he rests content in his allotted place. This is the gentleman’s lifelong learning of the mind. If one does not advance to this, but merely becomes entangled among statements, changes, images, and prognostications, then it is only a technical skill. Would this not differ from the gentleman’s learning?
“Once there is Return, there is no falsity; therefore it is followed by Without Falsity.”
Weng Pu 翁溥

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
深於理學者故錄
同考試官教諭吳批說理文字至此亦精矣
高薦何忝
同考試官教諭宋批心學之妙極難形容是
篇酌量不苟舂容有條愈讀而愈有味
考試官署郎中華批易義當如是作
考試官給事中陸批說復與无妄處明白
觀實理所以得于心知无妄所以次于復夫人
心有主則實亦復其理而已矣序卦之義以之
===
宜聖人發明以示人也歟且理在人心本無不
實自夫物欲交蔽理斯失焉而妄即乘之矣謂
之曰復則善端著于介然之頃有以收其放而
存其良天理於是乎復全也全體呈于本心之
明有以啓其端而致其養天真於是乎復反也
夫理欲相為消長而誠偽不容並立天理既還
則復者漸以實而私欲自爾其潜消將馴致于
至誠無息之域矣而尚何妄之存哉天真内涵
則實者漸以充而德性自爾其完固將日進于
punctuated:
深於理學者，故錄。
同考試官教諭吳批：說理文字至此，亦精矣。高薦何忝！
同考試官教諭宋批：心學之妙，極難形容。是篇酌量不苟，舂容有條，愈讀而愈有味。
考試官署郎中華批：易義當如是作。
考試官給事中陸批：說復與无妄處明白。
觀實理所以得于心，知无妄所以次于復。夫人心有主則實，亦復其理而已矣。序卦之義，以之宜聖人發明以示人也歟？且理在人心，本無不實。自夫物欲交蔽，理斯失焉，而妄即乘之矣。謂之曰復，則善端著于介然之頃，有以收其放而存其良，天理於是乎復全也；全體呈于本心之明，有以啓其端而致其養，天真於是乎復反也。夫理欲相為消長，而誠偽不容並立。天理既還，則復者漸以實，而私欲自爾其潜消，將馴致于至誠無息之域矣，而尚何妄之存哉？天真内涵，則實者漸以充，而德性自爾其完固，將日進于
translation_en:
…someone deeply versed in the learning of principle; hence its inclusion.

Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: “Writing that expounds principle has here attained refinement indeed. What shame could there be in recommending it highly!”

Associate Examiner Song, Instructor, comments: “The subtleties of the learning of the mind are exceedingly difficult to describe. This essay is carefully considered, without carelessness, and its ample, unhurried expression is orderly. The more one reads it, the more savor it offers.”

Examiner Hua, Acting Director, comments: “Essays on the meaning of the Book of Changes should be written like this.”

Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary, comments: “The passages explaining Return and Freedom from Falsehood are clear.”

By observing how genuine principle is apprehended in the mind, one understands why Freedom from Falsehood (Wuwang) follows Return (Fu). When the human mind has a governing center, it becomes genuine: this is simply the restoration of its principle. As for the meaning of the Sequence of the Hexagrams, was it therefore fitting that the sage elucidate it to instruct others [?]?

Now principle within the human mind is originally wholly genuine. Once material desires obscure it on every side, principle is lost, and falsehood immediately takes advantage of this. What is called Return means that the beginnings of goodness become manifest in a fleeting instant, enabling one to gather in what has strayed and preserve one's goodness; heavenly principle thus becomes whole again. Its entirety appears in the illumination of the original mind, enabling one to awaken its beginnings and fully nurture it; one's innate genuineness thus returns.

Principle and desire wax and wane in relation to one another, while sincerity and falsity cannot coexist. Once heavenly principle has returned, what has been restored gradually becomes genuine, and selfish desires naturally fade away unnoticed. One will gradually reach the realm of utmost sincerity without cessation. How, then, could any falsehood remain? When innate genuineness is contained within, what is genuine gradually becomes abundant, and one's moral nature naturally becomes complete and firm. One will advance daily toward…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
純一無偽之地矣而亦何妄之有哉夫人心之
機如此是以聖人之序卦也於復之後必以无
妄次之蓋復有復善之義而无妄有實理自然
之義一先後之相承而斷乎其不可易一次第
之相因而確乎其不容紊存乎易者猶夫存乎
人者也聖人序卦之意夫豈苟焉者哉大抵理
之在人心者未嘗息而君子之學莫有先于復
者復則不妄至于无妄則誠矣誠則止矣復者
賢人之事无妄則聖人之道也若理雖粗復而
===
有未純己雖粗克而有未盡皆非君子自止之
地也故雖以顏子之不遠復幾于聖矣而夫子
猶曰未見其止也學易者審諸
書
人心惟危道心惟微惟精惟一允執厥中
錢應揚
同考試官教諭唐批帝王授受心法最所難
言此作認理明白詞亦鬯達錄之
同考試官教諭林批體認精切詞理明瑩是
punctuated:
純一無偽之地矣，而亦何妄之有哉？夫人心之機如此，是以聖人之序卦也，於復之後必以无妄次之。蓋復有復善之義，而无妄有實理自然之義。一先後之相承，而斷乎其不可易；一次第之相因，而確乎其不容紊。存乎易者，猶夫存乎人者也。聖人序卦之意，夫豈苟焉者哉？大抵理之在人心者未嘗息，而君子之學莫有先于復者。復則不妄，至于无妄則誠矣，誠則止矣。復者賢人之事，无妄則聖人之道也。若理雖粗復而有未純，己雖粗克而有未盡，皆非君子自止之地也。故雖以顏子之不遠復，幾于聖矣，而夫子猶曰：「未見其止也。」學易者審諸。
書
人心惟危，道心惟微，惟精惟一，允執厥中。
錢應揚
同考試官教諭唐批：「帝王授受心法，最所難言。此作認理明白，詞亦鬯達，錄之。」
同考試官教諭林批：「體認精切，詞理明瑩，是
translation_en:
…the state of pure unity without falsity; what delusion could remain? Such is the subtle working of the human mind. Thus, when the sage arranged the hexagrams, he invariably placed Wuwang (Without Delusion) after Fu (Return). Fu signifies returning to goodness, while Wuwang signifies the spontaneous operation of true principle. Their succession is decidedly unalterable; their sequential dependence is assuredly not to be disturbed. What is found in the Changes is just like what is found in human beings. Could the sage’s intention in ordering the hexagrams have been arbitrary? In general, principle never ceases to operate within the human mind, and in the gentleman’s learning nothing takes precedence over returning. Returning dispels delusion; reaching the state of no delusion brings sincerity, and sincerity brings one to the point of rest. Returning is the undertaking of the worthy; being without delusion is the Way of the sage. If principle has been roughly restored but is not yet pure, or the self has been roughly overcome but not yet completely, neither condition is a point at which the gentleman may stop. Thus, although Master Yan’s returning before straying far brought him close to sagehood, the Master still said: “I have never seen him stop.” Let those who study the Changes examine this carefully.

Documents
“The human mind is precarious; the mind of the Way is subtle. Be discerning and single-minded; truly hold fast to the mean.”

Qian Yingyang

Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: “The teaching concerning the mind transmitted from one emperor or king to another is among the most difficult subjects to discuss. This composition apprehends principle clearly, and its language is also fluent and expressive. Accepted for inclusion.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Its understanding is precise and penetrating, and its language and reasoning are clear and lucid. This is…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
善言心學者
考試官署郎中華批講危微精一處似有得
者
考試官給事中陸批文有典則
觀聖君治法之傳一心學之要也蓋天下無心
外之治也卽一心而察以守之則執中之要在
是矣帝舜命禹攝位而傳以治之之法如此且
治道不外乎中執中必本於心心一也自其發
於形氣者謂之人心人心雖未入於邪惡而牽
===
引之機已動易私而難公也何危如之自其發
於義理者謂之道心道心雖根於天性而發見
之端始萌難明而易昧也何微如之二者雜於
方寸之間而無以治之則危者愈危微者愈微
矣必也自其一念之所從起者而察之極其精
使凡感於外而動於中者不雜於形氣之私也
旣精矣必也因吾之所已明者而守之極其固
使凡萌於中而漸以著者一純乎義理之正也
夫然則人心已收孰非道心道心所擴孰非中
punctuated:
善言心學者。
考試官署郎中華批：講危微精一處，似有得者。
考試官給事中陸批：文有典則。
觀聖君治法之傳，一心學之要也。蓋天下無心外之治也，卽一心而察以守之，則執中之要在是矣。帝舜命禹攝位，而傳以治之之法如此。且治道不外乎中，執中必本於心。心一也，自其發於形氣者謂之人心。人心雖未入於邪惡，而牽引之機已動，易私而難公也，何危如之！自其發於義理者謂之道心。道心雖根於天性，而發見之端始萌，難明而易昧也，何微如之！二者雜於方寸之間，而無以治之，則危者愈危，微者愈微矣。必也自其一念之所從起者而察之，極其精，使凡感於外而動於中者，不雜於形氣之私也。旣精矣，必也因吾之所已明者而守之，極其固，使凡萌於中而漸以著者，一純乎義理之正也。夫然，則人心已收，孰非道心？道心所擴，孰非中
translation_en:
…one who speaks well of the learning of the mind.

Examiner Hua, Acting Director, comments: “His discussion of peril, subtlety, discrimination, and singleness seems to show genuine understanding.”

Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary, comments: “The composition follows established models and rules.”

Looking at the sage rulers’ transmission of the methods of government, we see that it consists entirely in the essentials of learning concerning the mind. For there is no government of the world apart from the mind. By examining and preserving this single mind, one finds the essentials of holding fast to the mean. Such was the method of government that Emperor Shun transmitted when he commanded Yu to assume the throne provisionally. Moreover, the Way of government does not extend beyond the mean, and holding fast to the mean must be rooted in the mind. The mind is one. Insofar as it issues from bodily form and vital energies, it is called the human mind. Although the human mind has not yet fallen into perversity and evil, the impulse that draws it astray has already stirred: it readily becomes selfish and finds impartiality difficult. What could be more perilous? Insofar as it issues from moral principle, it is called the mind of the Way. Although the mind of the Way is rooted in our Heaven-endowed nature, the first signs of its manifestation are only beginning to emerge: it is difficult to discern and easily obscured. What could be more subtle? These two mingle within the heart. Without a means of governing them, the perilous becomes still more perilous, and the subtle still more subtle.

One must examine each thought at its very source, exercising the utmost discrimination, so that whatever responds to external stimuli and stirs within is unmixed with the selfishness arising from bodily form and vital energies. Having achieved such discrimination, one must then hold with the utmost firmness to what one has already understood, so that whatever sprouts within and gradually becomes manifest conforms wholly and purely to the rectitude of moral principle. When this is so, once the human mind has been brought under control, what in it is not the mind of the Way? Wherever the mind of the Way extends, what is not the mean…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
道由一心之動靜以至萬變之酬酢而自無過
不及之差自一身之云爲以至萬幾之裁决而
皆至當不易之理謂之允執厥中蓋信乎其能
執中而天下之治皆從此出矣舜之命禹何其
言約而義盡也哉抑是道也乃舜所親受於堯
者唐虞之治所以精純粹美而非後世所能及
端在於此自秦漢以下心學不傳而千載不得
蒙至治之澤良以人君不知用力於此耳欲學
堯舜者其可以他求哉然學之之要一言以蔽
===
之曰敬而已
王省惟歲卿士惟月師尹惟日
周如底
同考試官教諭唐批題本正大作者爲五氣
五事休咎得失等語所困往往纏繞可厭詞不費
而意足獨見此篇
同考試官教諭林批措詞命意自是精確箕
子告武王之旨正如此
考試官署郎中華批冲淡中有餘味
punctuated:
道。由一心之動靜，以至萬變之酬酢，而自無過不及之差；自一身之云爲，以至萬幾之裁决，而皆至當不易之理。謂之允執厥中，蓋信乎其能執中，而天下之治皆從此出矣。舜之命禹，何其言約而義盡也哉！抑是道也，乃舜所親受於堯者。唐虞之治，所以精純粹美而非後世所能及，端在於此。自秦漢以下，心學不傳，而千載不得蒙至治之澤，良以人君不知用力於此耳。欲學堯舜者，其可以他求哉？然學之之要，一言以蔽之，曰敬而已。

王省惟歲，卿士惟月，師尹惟日。
周如底。

同考試官教諭唐批：題本正大，作者爲五氣、五事、休咎、得失等語所困，往往纏繞可厭。詞不費而意足，獨見此篇。

同考試官教諭林批：措詞命意，自是精確。箕子告武王之旨，正如此。

考試官署郎中華批：冲淡中有餘味。
translation_en:
…the Way of the Mean. From the activity and stillness of the single mind to its responses to countless changes, there will naturally be no error of excess or deficiency; from the words and deeds of one person to decisions on the myriad affairs of government, all will accord with principles that are perfectly appropriate and unalterable. This is called “truly holding fast to the Mean”: one can indeed hold fast to the Mean, and the ordering of all under Heaven proceeds from this. How concise were Shun’s words in charging Yu, yet how fully they expressed their meaning! Moreover, this Way was what Shun personally received from Yao. It was precisely this that made the governance of Tang and Yu so refined, pure, and excellent that later ages could not equal it. From the Qin and Han onward, the learning of the mind was no longer transmitted, and for a thousand years people could not enjoy the blessings of perfect governance. This was simply because rulers did not know to devote their efforts to this. Can those who wish to emulate Yao and Shun seek elsewhere? Yet the essential point of learning from them can be summed up in a single word: reverence.

“The king examines the year; the high ministers, the month; the various officials, the day.”
By Zhou Rudi 周如底.

Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: The topic itself is upright and substantial. Writers become hampered by such terms as the five climatic influences, the five activities, favorable and unfavorable signs, and successes and failures; their writing often becomes tiresomely entangled. Only in this essay have I seen fullness of meaning without wasted words.

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: The wording and conception are indeed precise. This is exactly the purport of Jizi’s instruction to King Wu.

Comment by Examiner Hua, Acting Bureau Director: Beneath its tranquil simplicity lies a lingering savor.

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官給事中陸批整潔
君子敘庶徵之當省者一視其分之尊卑而已
夫庶徵之休咎因天以驗於人者也然則君臣
之分不同而其所省能弗異乎箕子衍庶徵之
疇以告武王及此謂夫天人相與之際亦甚可
畏矣彼王統卿士而卿士統乎師尹猶夫歲之
統月而月之統日也故五事有得失而庶徵之
休咎應之其所當省者則各有等焉莫尊於王
而所省則其係於一歲之利害者也蓋王者統
===
御萬國而綱紀四方凡歲功之虧全在君德之
修否自當容心於其大者矣王省不於歲而何
其次則有卿士焉輔佐之任攸歸而調燮之功
有賴然其位稍卑而所統者則有限矣故順天
行以考其職業者獨於一月之利害所係耳是
雖未擬於王者而亦非無所當省也所謂卿士
惟月者以此其次則有師尹焉分理之務既衆
而奉順之責惟均然其職愈降而所及者益無
幾矣故因時變以驗其修爲者獨於一日之利
punctuated:
考試官給事中陸批：整潔。

君子敘庶徵之當省者，一視其分之尊卑而已。夫庶徵之休咎，因天以驗於人者也。然則君臣之分不同，而其所省能弗異乎？箕子衍庶徵之疇以告武王，及此，謂夫天人相與之際，亦甚可畏矣。彼王統卿士，而卿士統乎師尹，猶夫歲之統月，而月之統日也。故五事有得失，而庶徵之休咎應之，其所當省者則各有等焉。莫尊於王，而所省則其係於一歲之利害者也。蓋王者統御萬國而綱紀四方，凡歲功之虧全，在君德之修否，自當容心於其大者矣。王省不於歲而何？其次則有卿士焉，輔佐之任攸歸，而調燮之功有賴。然其位稍卑，而所統者則有限矣。故順天行以考其職業者，獨於一月之利害所係耳。是雖未擬於王者，而亦非無所當省也。所謂卿士惟月者以此。其次則有師尹焉，分理之務既衆，而奉順之責惟均。然其職愈降，而所及者益無幾矣。故因時變以驗其修爲者，獨於一日之利
translation_en:
Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary, comments: “Orderly and polished.”

In setting forth which of the various signs ought to be examined, the gentleman considers solely the relative dignity of each person’s station. The favorable and unfavorable signs provide a means of assessing human conduct through Heaven. Since the stations of ruler and ministers differ, how could what they examine fail to differ? When Jizi expounded the category of the various signs to King Wu, he reached this point and declared that the interaction between Heaven and humanity is indeed deeply to be feared. The king presides over the high ministers, and the high ministers preside over the heads of offices, just as the year encompasses the months and the months encompass the days. Thus, successes and failures in the five activities elicit corresponding favorable and unfavorable signs, and what each ought to examine is differentiated by rank. None stands higher than the king, and what he examines concerns the benefits and harms of an entire year. For the king rules the myriad states and orders the four quarters. Whether the year’s achievements are deficient or complete depends upon whether the ruler cultivates his virtue; naturally, he ought to direct his attention to matters of the greatest scope. If the king does not examine the year, what should he examine?

Next come the high ministers. They bear responsibility for assisting the ruler, and the work of harmonizing the forces of nature depends upon them. Yet their station is somewhat lower, and their jurisdiction has limits. Thus, in following Heaven’s course to assess the performance of their duties, they attend only to what bears upon the benefits and harms of a single month. Although they do not stand on a level with the king, they nevertheless have things they ought to examine. This is the meaning of the saying, “The high ministers attend to the month.”

Next come the heads of offices. Their separate administrative duties are numerous, and they share equally the responsibility to obey and carry out commands. Yet their offices are still lower, and the reach of their authority is more limited still. Thus, in using changes in the seasons to assess their conduct, they attend only to what bears upon the benefits of a single day…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
害所係耳是雖未同於卿士而亦自有所當省
也所謂師尹惟日者以此其尊者省之大而要
非曰略也其卑者省之小而詳非曰繁也即人
事之當為以準天時之序有自然而不容紊者
矣抑所謂省之云者夫豈必徧求於歲日月之
間哉亦視其有所關係者云爾然大小之分雖
殊而警懼之心則一孰謂王者於月日之徵畧
而不問卿士師尹於歲之徵避而不省耶有國
家者必上下交修以免夫咎徵之反然後協於
===
箕子衍疇之旨
詩
追琢其章金玉其相勉勉我王綱紀四方
姜良翰
同考試官教諭徐批是題最難措詞晩得此
卷殆不可以塲屋文字目之
同考試官教諭鄭批於追琢金玉處盡去陳
言綱紀只就勉勉上見而文王當時維持世道之
心溢於言表真得詩人詠歌聖德之意
punctuated:
害所係耳。是雖未同於卿士，而亦自有所當省也。所謂「師尹惟日」者以此。其尊者省之大而要，非曰略也；其卑者省之小而詳，非曰繁也。即人事之當為，以準天時之序，有自然而不容紊者矣。抑所謂省之云者，夫豈必徧求於歲日月之間哉？亦視其有所關係者云爾。然大小之分雖殊，而警懼之心則一。孰謂王者於月日之徵畧而不問，卿士師尹於歲之徵避而不省耶？有國家者，必上下交修，以免夫咎徵之反，然後協於箕子衍疇之旨。

詩
追琢其章，金玉其相。勉勉我王，綱紀四方。
姜良翰

同考試官教諭徐批：「是題最難措詞，晩得此卷，殆不可以塲屋文字目之。」

同考試官教諭鄭批：「於追琢金玉處，盡去陳言；綱紀只就勉勉上見，而文王當時維持世道之心溢於言表，真得詩人詠歌聖德之意。」
translation_en:
…the harm at stake. Although these officials are not on the same level as the high ministers, they too have matters they ought to examine. This is what is meant by “The departmental chiefs attend to the day.” Those of higher rank examine matters that are broad and essential; this does not mean that they are cursory. Those of lower rank examine matters that are small and detailed; this does not mean that they are needlessly elaborate. Aligning the proper conduct of human affairs with the ordered succession of Heaven’s seasons entails a natural order that must not be disturbed. Yet does this talk of examination necessarily mean searching exhaustively through years, days, and months? It means simply attending to what bears upon one’s responsibilities. Although the scope of their duties differs, their spirit of vigilance and apprehension is the same. Who would say that the king neglects the signs manifested in months and days without inquiring into them, or that the high ministers and departmental chiefs evade the signs manifested in the year without examining them? Those who govern a state must ensure that superiors and subordinates alike cultivate their conduct, so as to avert the answering manifestations of baleful signs. Only then will they accord with the purpose of Jizi’s exposition of the categories of the Great Plan.

Book of Odes
“Carved and polished are his patterns; gold and jade are his bearing. Ever striving is our king, giving order to the four quarters.”
Jiang Lianghan

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: “This topic is exceptionally difficult to put into words. I came upon this script late in the reading; it can hardly be regarded as merely an examination composition.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “In treating ‘carved and polished’ and ‘gold and jade,’ he entirely dispenses with stock expressions. He brings out ‘giving order’ solely through ‘ever striving,’ while King Wen’s concern at that time for sustaining the moral order of the world shines through beyond the words themselves. He has truly grasped the poet’s intention in singing the praises of sagely virtue.”

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同考試官學正孫批士子既以勉勉講德而
於綱紀又以政治言之殊戾傳意此篇詞不繁而
意已獨至宜錄之以式來學
考試官署郎中華批得旨
考試官給事中陸批醇雅
詩人興聖德之純繫人心之至夫惟德可以繫
天下之心也聖人之德純而不已則所以綱紀
四方者不已至耶此亦以詠歌文王之德也且
百工之事攻金曰追攻玉曰琢文非追琢猶夫
===
===
文耳而非美之至也惟追之琢之以致其飾焉
則雕刻之功既極而天下之文無以尚之矣質
非金玉猶夫質耳而非美之至也惟以金以玉
而為之地焉則純瑩得之天成而天下之質不
足言矣夫物且然況我周王之德乎我周王以
視民如傷之心持遹求厥寧之志一誠貫徹於
終始而勤勞之匪懈一敬緝熙於無息而日昃
之不遑雖未嘗有所勉也而人見之若勉勉不
已者焉勉勉如此則蘊之而為天德徵之而為
punctuated:
同考試官學正孫批：士子既以勉勉講德，而於綱紀又以政治言之，殊戾傳意。此篇詞不繁而意已獨至，宜錄之以式來學。
考試官署郎中華批：得旨。
考試官給事中陸批：醇雅。
詩人興聖德之純，繫人心之至。夫惟德可以繫天下之心也。聖人之德純而不已，則所以綱紀四方者不已至耶？此亦以詠歌文王之德也。且百工之事，攻金曰追，攻玉曰琢。文非追琢，猶夫文耳，而非美之至也。惟追之琢之，以致其飾焉，則雕刻之功既極，而天下之文無以尚之矣。質非金玉，猶夫質耳，而非美之至也。惟以金以玉而為之地焉，則純瑩得之天成，而天下之質不足言矣。夫物且然，況我周王之德乎？我周王以視民如傷之心，持遹求厥寧之志，一誠貫徹於終始，而勤勞之匪懈；一敬緝熙於無息，而日昃之不遑。雖未嘗有所勉也，而人見之若勉勉不已者焉。勉勉如此，則蘊之而為天德，徵之而為
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Sun, an Instructor, comments: Candidates explain “unceasing diligence” in terms of virtue, yet then discuss “ordering and regulating” in terms of political administration, thus seriously departing from the commentary’s meaning. This essay is concise in expression but uniquely profound in meaning. It should be recorded as a model for future students.
Examiner Hua, Acting Director, comments: It grasps the essential meaning.
Examiner Lu, a Supervising Secretary, comments: Pure and elegant.
Through evocative imagery, the poet conveys the purity of sagely virtue and its consummate power to bind people’s hearts. Only virtue can bind the hearts of all under Heaven. When the sage’s virtue is pure and unceasing, is not the means by which he orders and regulates the four quarters already consummate? This, too, serves to sing the praises of King Wen’s virtue. Now, among the crafts, working metal is called chasing, and working jade is called carving. Without chasing and carving, ornament remains merely ornament and does not attain the utmost beauty. Only when it is chased and carved to perfect its embellishment does the engraver’s work reach its utmost, so that no ornament in the world can surpass it. If the underlying substance is not metal or jade, it remains merely substance and does not attain the utmost beauty. Only when metal and jade form its foundation does it possess a purity and lustre bestowed by nature, beside which other substances in the world are scarcely worth mentioning.
If this is so even of objects, how much more must it be so of the virtue of our king of Zhou? Our king of Zhou, with a heart that regarded the people as though they were injured, maintained his resolve to seek their tranquillity. A single sincerity ran through his conduct from beginning to end, and he never slackened in his labours; a single reverence shone ever brighter without cease, and even as the sun declined he had no leisure. Though he never had to force himself, people saw him as one who exerted himself diligently without end. With diligence such as this, what he harboured within constituted Heaven’s virtue, and what he manifested outwardly constituted…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
王道天下雖大也精神志向與吾而相攝由人
心觀之祇自覺其有所屬焉而莫知其然也億
兆雖衆也心神意氣與吾而相關由斯民觀之
祇日見其有所統焉而莫知為之者也謂之曰
綱紀四方信乎文王之德繫於人心而歸附趨
向之勢自有所不容已矣抑禹思天下有溺者
由己溺之也稷思天下有飢者由己飢之也文
王當殷道之衰天下之憔悴於虐政也甚矣勉
勉之心固有不容自已者故位不在文王而天
===
人叩人心在焉蓋一念憂勤王業勃然興矣雖然
文王豈有心於是哉為人臣止於敬是亦勉勉
之心也
紹庭上下陟降厥家休矣皇考以保明其
身
符驗
同考試官教諭徐 批 成王繼述之志實在於
道而延訪羣臣其意甚至此篇寫出句句親切直
是作者
punctuated:
