王道。天下雖大也，精神志向與吾而相攝；由人心觀之，祇自覺其有所屬焉，而莫知其然也。億兆雖衆也，心神意氣與吾而相關；由斯民觀之，祇日見其有所統焉，而莫知為之者也。謂之曰「綱紀四方」，信乎文王之德繫於人心，而歸附趨向之勢自有所不容已矣。抑禹思天下有溺者，由己溺之也；稷思天下有飢者，由己飢之也。文王當殷道之衰，天下之憔悴於虐政也甚矣。勉勉之心固有不容自已者，故位不在文王，而天人叩人心在焉。蓋一念憂勤，王業勃然興矣。雖然，文王豈有心於是哉？為人臣止於敬，是亦勉勉之心也。
紹庭上下，陟降厥家。休矣皇考，以保明其身。
符驗
同考試官教諭徐批：成王繼述之志，實在於道，而延訪羣臣，其意甚至。此篇寫出，句句親切，直是作者。
translation_en:
…the kingly Way. Vast though the realm is, its spirit and aspirations are bound together with mine. Seen from the people’s hearts, they simply feel that they have somewhere to belong, without knowing why. Numerous though the multitudes are, their hearts, spirits, intentions, and energies are linked with mine. Seen from these people’s perspective, each day they perceive that they are united under a common authority, without knowing who brings this about. This is called “ordering and guiding the four quarters.” Truly, King Wen’s virtue held the people’s hearts, and their impulse to submit and turn toward him could not be restrained.
Moreover, Yu thought that if anyone in the realm drowned, it was as though he himself had drowned that person; Ji thought that if anyone in the realm went hungry, it was as though he himself had caused that person’s hunger. King Wen lived during the decline of the Yin dynasty’s Way, when the realm suffered grievously under oppressive government. His unremitting concern was indeed something he could not restrain. Thus, although the throne did not belong to King Wen, Heaven and the people’s hearts were with him [落?; the transcription 天人叩人心 is doubtful]. With a single thought of anxious diligence, the kingly enterprise arose vigorously. Yet did King Wen deliberately seek this? As a minister, he rested in reverence: this, too, was the expression of his unremitting heart.
“Continue the courtly service above and below, ascending and descending within his house. Glorious is the august deceased father, thereby preserving and illuminating his person.”
Fu Yan 符驗
Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: King Cheng’s resolve to carry forward his predecessor’s work truly lay in the Way, and his purpose in inviting and consulting his assembled ministers was most earnest. This essay brings that out, every sentence closely capturing its meaning. Here indeed is an accomplished writer.

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭鄭批繼體守成不外乎敬而
成王之學多得于此是作文勢沛然而結意尤爲
明備
同考試官學正孫批文字典雅僅見此篇務
實之學也
考試官署郎中華批平實可取
考試官給事中陸批詞到意足
欲法乎先王之所爲以承乎先王之所底周王
訪其臣然也夫先王之道隨在而有著也於此
===
法之亦焉往而不得其底哉成王延訪群臣之
意如此蓋以先王之治本於道先王之道見於
行吾於多難則未堪而求道則未合必何如而
可乎誠以皇考常莅之以出治者廷也一上一
下正百官者以此御萬幾者以此亦於此而繼
之乎以仰希其成憲之所在謨訓功烈識其大
也禮樂文章識其小也紹之弗得弗措焉皇考
常居之以正始者家也一陟一降端本者以此
善則者以此亦於此而繼之乎以近守其懿範
punctuated:
同考試官教諭鄭批：繼體守成，不外乎敬，而成王之學多得于此。是作，文勢沛然，而結意尤爲明備。
同考試官學正孫批：文字典雅，僅見此篇，務實之學也。
考試官署郎中華批：平實可取。
考試官給事中陸批：詞到意足。
欲法乎先王之所爲，以承乎先王之所底，周王訪其臣然也。夫先王之道，隨在而有著也，於此法之，亦焉往而不得其底哉？成王延訪群臣之意如此。蓋以先王之治本於道，先王之道見於行。吾於多難則未堪，而求道則未合，必何如而可乎？誠以皇考常莅之以出治者，廷也。一上一下，正百官者以此，御萬幾者以此，亦於此而繼之乎？以仰希其成憲之所在，謨訓功烈，識其大也；禮樂文章，識其小也。紹之，弗得弗措焉。皇考常居之以正始者，家也。一陟一降，端本者以此，善則者以此，亦於此而繼之乎？以近守其懿範
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Zheng, an Instructor, comments: “Succeeding to the throne and preserving inherited achievements depend upon reverence alone, and much of King Cheng’s learning lay in this. This composition has abundant momentum, and its concluding argument is particularly clear and comprehensive.”
Associate Examiner Sun, an Instructor, comments: “For classical elegance of expression, this essay alone stands out. Its learning attends to practical substance.”
Examiner Hua, Acting Director, comments: “Straightforward and substantial; worthy of acceptance.”
Examiner Lu, a Supervising Secretary, comments: “The expression is apt and the meaning fully conveyed.”
Desiring to emulate what the former king had done, and thereby carry forward what the former king had achieved: such was the purpose of the king of Zhou in consulting his ministers. The former king’s Way manifests itself wherever one looks. If one takes it as a model here, wherever one goes, how could one fail to attain what he attained? Such was King Cheng’s intention in summoning and consulting his assembled ministers.
For the former king’s governance was rooted in the Way, and his Way was made manifest in his actions. “I have not yet proved equal to the many difficulties, and in seeking the Way I have not yet accorded with it. What must I do to succeed? The place where my august late father regularly presided to conduct government was the court. In every movement, ascending or descending, it was here that he set the hundred officials right, and here that he managed the myriad affairs of state. Should I not carry on his work here too? Thus I would look up to the established standards he left: in his counsels, instructions, and meritorious achievements, I would discern their greater aspects; in rites, music, and cultural forms, I would discern their lesser aspects. I would continue his work and not desist until I had attained it.
“The place where my august late father regularly dwelt to rectify the beginnings of order was his household. In every movement, ascending or descending, it was here that he set the root right, and here that he made his example good. Should I not carry on his work here too? Thus I would closely uphold his exemplary conduct…”

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之所貽几席觴豆求其志也定省起居述其事
也紹之弗能弗措焉將見循前人之迹或可以
得前人之休拱穆清而正位凝命法之所在即
休之所在也庶幾賴之以保吾之所未安優游
者或以享而泮奐者或可期九重無震驚之虞
亦吾克艱之一助耳不然身且不保成業可得
而守乎亶聰明而垂憲貽謀法之所存即休之
所存也庶幾賴之以啓吾之所未明不聰者或
以擴而緝熈者或可至萬幾無叢脞之患亦吾
===
造哲之一資耳不然則身且不明盛治可得而
致乎夫成王纘緒之圖如此其切此所以道無
不合而克光前烈也歟大抵守成之君未有不
得其祖宗之法而可以善其治者也成王繼序
不忘乎心猶訪于臣而不自是於是羣臣進以
敬之之戒而事天事親之道備矣噫君臣一心
創守一道此所以就文武之業崇大化之本歟
春秋
楚子蔡侯次于厥貉〔文公十年〕公會宋公
punctuated:
之所貽。几席觴豆，求其志也；定省起居，述其事也。紹之弗能弗措焉。將見循前人之迹，或可以得前人之休。拱穆清而正位凝命，法之所在，即休之所在也。庶幾賴之以保吾之所未安，優游者或以享，而泮奐者或可期，九重無震驚之虞，亦吾克艱之一助耳。不然，身且不保，成業可得而守乎？亶聰明而垂憲貽謀，法之所存，即休之所存也。庶幾賴之以啓吾之所未明，不聰者或以擴，而緝熈者或可至，萬幾無叢脞之患，亦吾造哲之一資耳。不然，則身且不明，盛治可得而致乎？夫成王纘緒之圖如此其切，此所以道無不合而克光前烈也歟！大抵守成之君，未有不得其祖宗之法而可以善其治者也。成王繼序，不忘乎心，猶訪于臣而不自是，於是羣臣進以敬之之戒，而事天事親之道備矣。噫！君臣一心，創守一道，此所以就文武之業、崇大化之本歟！

春秋

楚子、蔡侯次于厥貉〔文公十年〕。公會宋公、
translation_en:
…what he has bequeathed. Through his tables and mats, wine cups and vessels, I seek his intentions; through attending him morning and evening and caring for his daily needs, I carry on his practices. Until I can continue them successfully, I shall not desist. We shall then see that, by following our predecessor’s footsteps, we may obtain our predecessor’s blessings. With hands folded in the tranquil purity of the court, I shall occupy the rightful position and secure the mandate. Where his models are found, there too are his blessings. Perhaps I may rely on them to secure what is not yet secure for me: ease may be enjoyed, and expansive contentment may be hoped for. Within the ninefold palace gates there will be no fear of alarm. This, too, is one aid in my overcoming difficulties. Otherwise, if I cannot even preserve myself, how can I maintain the enterprise already established?

Truly intelligent and discerning, he handed down standards and bequeathed plans. Where his models endure, there too his blessings endure. Perhaps I may rely on them to illuminate what I do not yet understand: my deficient understanding may be broadened, and continuing illumination may be attained. The myriad affairs of government will suffer no confusion over petty details. This, too, is one resource for my attaining wisdom. Otherwise, if I myself lack understanding, how can flourishing government be achieved?

Such was the urgency of King Cheng’s resolve to continue his predecessors’ undertaking. Was this not why he accorded with the Way in every respect and could bring glory to their achievements? Generally speaking, no ruler preserving an inherited achievement has ever governed well without grasping the models of his ancestors. King Cheng succeeded to the throne and kept this constantly in mind, yet still consulted his ministers rather than assuming himself right. His assembled ministers thereupon offered the admonition to be reverent, and the way of serving Heaven and serving one’s parents was made complete. Ah! Ruler and ministers were of one mind; founding an enterprise and preserving it followed one Way. Was this not how they brought the enterprise of Kings Wen and Wu to fulfillment and strengthened the foundation of great moral transformation?

Spring and Autumn Annals

The Viscount of Chu and the Marquis of Cai encamped at Juehe. 〔Tenth year of Duke Wen〕 The duke met with the Duke of Song …

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯晉趙盾癸酉
同盟于新城文公十有四年
謝紘
同考試官教諭陳批聖人予奪晉楚之意無
非以謹君臣之義耳此作能發之而辭義嚴正自
是關繫世教文字未可以場屋之士目之
考試官署郎中華批謹嚴有法
考試官給事中陸批得傳意
夷惡逞而與國從春秋以大義奪之伯信講而
===
諸侯協春秋以大義予之夫君臣之義春秋之
所謹也得不于晉楚之行事而予奪以見意哉
且楚之行事猶夫晉耳而春秋每奪之者何吾
觀其筆削於厥貉之舉而知之盖楚以蠻夷而
竊王號其冒犯名義之罪大矣今焉穆也將逞志
於北方因按兵而脅宋是舉也藏禍心以憑諸
夏也而陳鄭與宋從之盖迫於禍難弗獲已耳
若蔡無他虞乃輕為服役得非樂於異類之從
耶窓四夷雖大不過曰子王法所在夫誰敢不
punctuated:
陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯、晉趙盾，癸酉，同盟于新城。文公十有四年。
謝紘。
同考試官教諭陳批：聖人予奪晉楚之意，無非以謹君臣之義耳。此作能發之，而辭義嚴正，自是關繫世教文字，未可以場屋之士目之。
考試官署郎中華批：謹嚴有法。
考試官給事中陸批：得傳意。
夷惡逞而與國從，《春秋》以大義奪之；伯信講而諸侯協，《春秋》以大義予之。夫君臣之義，《春秋》之所謹也，得不于晉楚之行事而予奪以見意哉？且楚之行事猶夫晉耳，而《春秋》每奪之者何？吾觀其筆削於厥貉之舉而知之。盖楚以蠻夷而竊王號，其冒犯名義之罪大矣。今焉穆也將逞志於北方，因按兵而脅宋。是舉也，藏禍心以憑諸夏也，而陳、鄭與宋從之，盖迫於禍難，弗獲已耳。若蔡無他虞，乃輕為服役，得非樂於異類之從耶？窓四夷雖大，不過曰子。王法所在，夫誰敢不
translation_en:
…the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, and Zhao Dun of Jin. On the guiyou day, they entered into a joint covenant at Xincheng. Fourteenth year of Duke Wen.
Xie Hong.
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: The Sage’s intention in approving or condemning Jin and Chu is entirely to uphold strictly the proper relationship between ruler and minister. This composition brings that intention out, and its language and reasoning are rigorous and upright. It is certainly a piece of writing that bears upon moral instruction in the world; its author cannot be regarded merely as a candidate in the examination hall.
Comment by Examiner Hua, Acting Director: Careful and rigorous, with sound method.
Comment by Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary: Grasps the meaning of the Commentary.
When barbarian wickedness asserted itself and allied states followed, the Spring and Autumn Annals condemned them according to the great principles of right. When a hegemon cultivated good faith and the regional lords acted in concert, the Spring and Autumn Annals approved them according to those same principles. The proper relationship between ruler and minister is what the Spring and Autumn Annals guards strictly. Could it fail to express its intent through approval and condemnation of the actions of Jin and Chu?
Moreover, Chu’s actions were much like Jin’s. Why, then, does the Spring and Autumn Annals repeatedly condemn Chu? By examining its choices of inclusion and omission in recording the undertaking at Juehe, I understand why. Chu, a barbarian state, usurped the title of king: its offense in violating rightful titles and obligations was grave indeed. Now Mu intended to impose his will upon the north, using the stationing of troops to intimidate Song. In this undertaking, he harbored malicious designs to overawe the states of the central realm. Chen and Zheng, together with Song, followed him because, pressed by impending calamity, they had no alternative. Cai, however, faced no other danger, yet readily submitted to his service. Was this not taking pleasure in following those of an alien kind?
[?] However great the peoples of the four barbarian regions might be, their rulers were entitled to be called no more than viscounts. Where royal law applies, who would dare fail to …

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
嚴楚也實亂之而蔡人則甘心爲之羽翼是僭
王之惡楚爲首而蔡亦其從也苟自此而或逞
其志使禍及宗周君臣之義其與存者幾何春
秋以尊周爲本者不能無懼乎此故削三國而
書蔡侯以罪之奪從楚之蔡所以奪僭王之楚
也若晉之行事猶夫楚耳而春秋每予之者何
吾觀其致意於新城之盟而知之蓋晉自文襄
已主夏盟其著仗義之略久矣今焉趙盾倡爲
外楚之謀因講服貳之信是盟也抑強夷以安
===
周室也而陳鄭與宋在焉蓋出於同欲非強之
矣雖蔡不預盟而决於從楚亦何害于衆志之
同耶噫周德雖衰天命未改王室之憂其誰能
弗恤晉也實念之而諸侯則恊心爲之股肱是
尊王之舉晉爲主而諸國其輔也苟繼此而益
堅其從使威伸強楚君臣之義不尚亦有賴哉
春秋以大義率人者不能不謹乎此故特書同
盟以善之予從晉之諸侯所以予尊王之晉也
其進退抑揚皆非苟然者夫豈有所私於其間
punctuated:
嚴？楚也實亂之，而蔡人則甘心爲之羽翼，是僭王之惡，楚爲首而蔡亦其從也。苟自此而或逞其志，使禍及宗周，君臣之義其與存者幾何？春秋以尊周爲本者，不能無懼乎此。故削三國而書蔡侯以罪之，奪從楚之蔡，所以奪僭王之楚也。
若晉之行事猶夫楚耳，而春秋每予之者何？吾觀其致意於新城之盟而知之。蓋晉自文襄已主夏盟，其著仗義之略久矣。今焉趙盾倡爲外楚之謀，因講服貳之信，是盟也，抑強夷以安周室也。而陳鄭與宋在焉，蓋出於同欲，非強之矣。雖蔡不預盟，而决於從楚，亦何害于衆志之同耶？噫！周德雖衰，天命未改，王室之憂，其誰能弗恤？晉也實念之，而諸侯則恊心爲之股肱，是尊王之舉，晉爲主而諸國其輔也。苟繼此而益堅其從，使威伸強楚，君臣之義不尚亦有賴哉？春秋以大義率人者，不能不謹乎此。故特書同盟以善之，予從晉之諸侯，所以予尊王之晉也。其進退抑揚皆非苟然者，夫豈有所私於其間？
translation_en:
…hold it in awe? It was Chu that truly disrupted this order, while the people of Cai willingly served as its wings. Thus, in the wrongdoing of usurping the royal title, Chu was the leader and Cai its accomplice. If Chu should thereafter attain its ambitions and bring disaster upon the ancestral Zhou realm, how much of the proper relationship between ruler and minister would remain? The Spring and Autumn Annals, which takes honoring Zhou as its foundation, could not but view this with apprehension. It therefore omits the three states and records the Lord of Cai, thereby condemning him. Its censure of Cai for following Chu is a means of censuring Chu for usurping the royal title.
If Jin’s conduct was much like Chu’s, why does the Spring and Autumn Annals repeatedly approve of it? I understand this from observing the significance it assigns to the covenant at Xincheng. Since the days of Dukes Wen and Xiang, Jin had presided over the covenants of the states of Xia, and had long made manifest its policy of upholding righteousness. Now Zhao Dun advocated a plan to exclude Chu and accordingly sought pledges of good faith to secure the allegiance of the wavering. This covenant restrained the powerful barbarians in order to bring peace to the house of Zhou. Chen, Zheng, and Song participated because they shared this desire, not because they were compelled. Although Cai did not participate in the covenant and was resolved to follow Chu, how could that impair the unity of purpose among the others? Alas! Though Zhou’s virtue had declined, Heaven’s mandate had not changed. Who could fail to care about the troubles of the royal house? Jin truly kept them in mind, and the feudal lords united in serving as its arms and legs. Thus, in this undertaking to honor the king, Jin took the lead and the other states assisted it. If thereafter they grew still firmer in their allegiance, extending their authority over powerful Chu, would not the proper relationship between ruler and minister still find support in this? The Spring and Autumn Annals, which guides people through the great principles of righteousness, could not but treat this with care. It therefore specifically records that they “joined together in covenant,” thereby commending them. Its approval of the feudal lords who followed Jin is a means of approving Jin for honoring the king. Its advancements and demotions, censures and commendations, are never arbitrary. How could there be any partiality in them?

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
抑當是時動天下屬諸侯有大感焉列國若
尚聞知而盟好是講悖矣又況主之者晉卿而
其君不預也春秋何善乎是而與之夫中國不
振旅而蠻夷入伐是盟也猶有憂思防患之意
焉且其事關於君臣夷夏之際春秋有不得不
予之者矣嗚呼其衰世之意耶
齊人伐我北鄙〔僖公二十有六年〕楚公子
貞帥師伐鄭〔襄公八年〕
羅洪
===
同考試官教諭陳批斐然之文竒氣溢發而
敘事且極詳備錄此以警世之學春秋而忽傳註
者
考試官署郎中華批詳贍
考試官給事中陸批不失題旨
稱王命以卻敵賢臣修辭之功背伯信以從夷
大夫失職之罪此展禽之卻齊所以能安其國
而子駟之從楚卒於不免其身也觀春秋所書
而得失見矣嘗夫莒衞請平而我僖因背齊以
punctuated:
抑當是時，動天下、屬諸侯，有大感焉。列國若尚聞知，而盟好是講，悖矣！又況主之者晉卿，而其君不預也，春秋何善乎是而與之？夫中國不振旅，而蠻夷入伐，是盟也，猶有憂思防患之意焉。且其事關於君臣夷夏之際，春秋有不得不予之者矣。嗚呼，其衰世之意耶！
齊人伐我北鄙〔僖公二十有六年〕。楚公子貞帥師伐鄭〔襄公八年〕。
羅洪
同考試官教諭陳批：斐然之文，竒氣溢發，而敘事且極詳備。錄此以警世之學春秋而忽傳註者。
考試官署郎中華批：詳贍。
考試官給事中陸批：不失題旨。
稱王命以卻敵，賢臣修辭之功；背伯信以從夷，大夫失職之罪。此展禽之卻齊所以能安其國，而子駟之從楚卒於不免其身也。觀春秋所書，而得失見矣。嘗夫莒衞請平，而我僖因背齊以
translation_en:
Yet at that time there was a great disturbance [?] that stirred all under Heaven and brought the feudal lords together. If the various states had still heard and understood this, yet concerned themselves with friendly covenants, that was perverse! Moreover, the man presiding was a minister of Jin, while his ruler took no part. What did the Spring and Autumn Annals approve in this, that it should commend it? Since the central states did not mobilize their armies, while the barbarians invaded, this covenant at least showed concern for danger and an intention to forestall calamity. Furthermore, the affair touched upon the distinctions between ruler and minister, and between the barbarians and the Chinese states: the Spring and Autumn Annals could not but give it some approval. Alas, does this express its outlook in an age of decline?
“The men of Qi attacked our northern border region.” 〔Twenty-sixth year of Duke Xi.〕 “Zhen, a prince of Chu, led an army to attack Zheng.” 〔Eighth year of Duke Xiang.〕
Luo Hong
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “An accomplished composition, overflowing with extraordinary vigor; its narration of events is also exceptionally full and detailed. We record it to admonish those in our day who study the Spring and Autumn Annals but neglect its commentaries and annotations.”
Comment by Examiner Hua, Acting Director: “Detailed and ample.”
Comment by Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary: “Keeps to the purport of the topic.”
Invoking the king’s command to repel an enemy is an achievement of a worthy minister’s skill in framing his words; betraying faith with the hegemon to follow the barbarians is the culpable dereliction of a grand master. This is why Zhan Qin, in repelling Qi, was able to secure his state, whereas Zisi, in following Chu, ultimately could not save himself. By examining what the Spring and Autumn Annals records, we can see their successes and failures. Now [?], Ju and Wei requested peace, and our Duke Xi consequently turned his back on Qi in order to …

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
從之一盟于洮再盟于向而齊人逞忿之兵至
矣爲魯者苟如臧孫之謀不以義服而徒以賂
免其何恥如之幸而柳下惠有辭以應敵而展
喜且將犒師之禮於是乎稱先王之命以對之
不曰股肱周室之盟載書猶在則曰糾合諸侯
之舉舊職未忘果爾其言未終而齊師遂退當
是之時室如縣罄野無青草魯幾無以爲國微
惠也誰安之從容應對以抑強暴之鋒偃息笑
談而紓危亡之禍辭之有益蓋如此傳曰不有
===
君子其能國乎斯之謂矣後此仲尼相魯秉禮
而化強齊以惠方之殆庶幾哉當夫晉楚爭鄭
而鄭人復侵蔡以怒之既敗其兵又獲其將而
楚人問罪之師至矣爲鄭者能如子展之謀堅
守老楚而杖信待晉其誰曰不可夫何公孫騑
決謀以向楚而諸卿共執牛耳之盟於是乎背
五會之信以從之晉君方明不能事也而親我
無成楚師將歸弗能待也而鄙我是欲果爾爲
盟未久而晉師又至自是之後犧牲玉帛待於
punctuated:
從之，一盟于洮，再盟于向，而齊人逞忿之兵至矣。爲魯者，苟如臧孫之謀，不以義服，而徒以賂免，其何恥如之！幸而柳下惠有辭以應敵，而展喜且將犒師之禮，於是乎稱先王之命以對之。不曰股肱周室之盟，載書猶在，則曰糾合諸侯之舉，舊職未忘。果爾，其言未終，而齊師遂退。當是之時，室如縣罄，野無青草，魯幾無以爲國。微惠也，誰安之？從容應對，以抑強暴之鋒；偃息笑談，而紓危亡之禍。辭之有益，蓋如此。傳曰：「不有君子，其能國乎？」斯之謂矣。後此仲尼相魯，秉禮而化強齊，以惠方之，殆庶幾哉！
當夫晉楚爭鄭，而鄭人復侵蔡以怒之，既敗其兵，又獲其將，而楚人問罪之師至矣。爲鄭者，能如子展之謀，堅守老楚，而杖信待晉，其誰曰不可？夫何公孫騑決謀以向楚，而諸卿共執牛耳之盟，於是乎背五會之信以從之！晉君方明，不能事也，而親我無成；楚師將歸，弗能待也，而鄙我是欲。果爾，爲盟未久，而晉師又至。自是之後，犧牲玉帛待於
translation_en:
…follow them, making one covenant at Tao and another at Xiang; then the army of Qi arrived to vent its anger. Had those governing Lu followed Zangsun’s plan, seeking escape merely through bribes instead of winning the enemy over through righteousness, what greater disgrace could there have been! Fortunately, Liu Xiahui furnished words with which to answer the enemy, and Zhan Xi undertook the ceremonial presentation of provisions to its army. He therefore invoked the former kings’ command in answering them. He spoke both of the covenant to serve as the arms and legs of the royal house of Zhou, whose written text still survived, and of the undertaking to unite the regional lords, an ancient duty not yet forgotten. Indeed, before he had finished speaking, the army of Qi withdrew. At that time, houses were as empty as suspended chime stones, and there was no green grass in the fields: Lu could scarcely sustain itself as a state. Without Liu Xiahui, who could have secured its peace? Through composed replies he blunted the assault of a powerful aggressor; with ease and smiling conversation he relieved the danger of destruction. Such was the benefit of persuasive speech. The Commentary says: “Without gentlemen, could a state be maintained?” This is what it means. Later, Zhongni served as minister in Lu and, upholding ritual propriety, transformed the conduct of powerful Qi. Measured against him, Liu Xiahui surely came close!
When Jin and Chu were contending for Zheng, the people of Zheng again invaded Cai, thereby provoking Chu. They defeated Cai’s troops and captured its commander, and Chu’s army arrived to punish them. Had those governing Zheng followed Zizhan’s plan, holding firm until Chu’s forces were exhausted and relying on their pledged faith while awaiting Jin, who could have said this was wrong? Why, then, did Gongsun Fei decide to turn toward Chu, with the ministers jointly entering a covenant sealed by holding a bull’s ear, thus betraying the pledges of five meetings in order to follow Chu? The ruler of Jin was then enlightened, yet they could not serve him, and his efforts to draw Zheng close came to nothing [?]; Chu’s army was about to withdraw, yet they could not wait, although Chu wished to make Zheng its border dependency. Indeed, not long after the covenant was made, Jin’s army arrived once more. From then onward, sacrificial animals, jade, and silk were kept ready at …

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
二竟鄭幾不免於亡則騑也實爲之忍陪貳之
辱而甘心市井之行忘政本之重而終遺社稷
之憂謀之不臧孰甚焉詩曰誰生厲階至今爲
梗斯之謂矣後此子産相鄭馳詞以當晉楚以
騑視之不有愧哉蓋未幾有西宫之難騑與二
卿死焉君子謂斯人之宜及此久矣春秋削其
大夫所以示當官失職者之戒也抑又有可深
慨者夫以展季之賢魯國賴之以安而終不見
用雖臧孫之竊位蔽賢而魯僖亦不能無責矣
===
若公孫騑之謀所謂一言喪邦者顧其盟與否
皆二三臣主之而君不與知焉此何爲者哉然
則春秋所書不惟人臣謀國任事之鑒亦人君
聽言用人之法也
禮記
故人情者聖王之田也脩禮以耕之陳義
以種之講學以耨之本仁以聚之播樂
以安之故禮也者義之實也協諸義而
協則禮雖先王未之有可以義起也義
punctuated:
二竟，鄭幾不免於亡，則騑也實爲之。忍陪貳之辱，而甘心市井之行；忘政本之重，而終遺社稷之憂。謀之不臧，孰甚焉？詩曰：「誰生厲階？至今爲梗。」斯之謂矣。後此子産相鄭，馳詞以當晉楚，以騑視之，不有愧哉？蓋未幾有西宫之難，騑與二卿死焉。君子謂斯人之宜及此久矣。春秋削其大夫，所以示當官失職者之戒也。抑又有可深慨者：夫以展季之賢，魯國賴之以安，而終不見用，雖臧孫之竊位蔽賢，而魯僖亦不能無責矣。若公孫騑之謀，所謂一言喪邦者，顧其盟與否，皆二三臣主之，而君不與知焉，此何爲者哉？然則春秋所書，不惟人臣謀國任事之鑒，亦人君聽言用人之法也。
禮記
故人情者，聖王之田也。脩禮以耕之，陳義以種之，講學以耨之，本仁以聚之，播樂以安之。故禮也者，義之實也。協諸義而協，則禮雖先王未之有，可以義起也。義
translation_en:
…at the two borders, and Zheng came close to destruction: it was Fei who truly brought this about. He endured the humiliation of serving two masters and willingly adopted the conduct of the marketplace; he forgot the importance of the foundations of government and ultimately left the state in peril. What counsel could have been worse? The Book of Odes says: “Who first created these steps to calamity, which remain an obstruction to this day?” This is precisely what it means. Later, Zichan served as chief minister of Zheng and deployed his words to hold his own against Jin and Chu. Measured against him, would Fei not be ashamed? Indeed, before long the troubles at the Western Palace occurred, and Fei died there along with two other ministers. The gentleman judges that this man had long deserved to meet such an end. The Spring and Autumn Annals omits his designation as a grand master, thereby warning those who hold office but fail in their duties.
There is, moreover, something else deeply to lament. Worthy as Zhan Ji was, and although the state of Lu depended on him for its security, he was never given employment. Although Zangsun usurped his position and concealed a worthy man's abilities, Duke Xi of Lu cannot escape responsibility either. As for Gongsun Fei's counsel, it was what is called “a single utterance that destroys a state.” Yet whether or not to enter the covenant was decided entirely by a few ministers, without their ruler having any part in the matter. What sort of conduct was this? Thus, what the Spring and Autumn Annals records is not only a mirror for ministers who deliberate on affairs of state and undertake responsibilities, but also a model for rulers in listening to advice and employing men.
Book of Rites
Thus, human feelings are the field of the sage kings. They cultivate ritual to plough it, set forth righteousness to sow it, expound learning to weed it, take benevolence as the foundation for gathering its harvest, and spread music to bring it peace. Thus ritual is the concrete embodiment of righteousness. If a rite is measured against righteousness and accords with it, then even if the former kings had no such rite, it may be instituted on the basis of righteousness. Righteousness…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
者藝之分仁之節也協於藝講於仁得
之者強仁者義之本也順之體也得之
者尊
徐建
同考試官學正凌批聖王治情以禮義仁爲
急而講學播樂非從事於三者之外此作識見真
到詞意貫通以下爲廣明相須之義尤根本註疏
成說以發集說所未備其殆究心經學者高薦允
宜
===
考試官署郎中華批亦可與言禮矣
考試官給事中陸批縝密
記者叙聖王脩道以治情必深明其道有相須
之義也夫聖王治情之道亦多矣序不可紊而
義實相須此所以盡善而無弊歟記禮運者若
曰農人耕種耨穫以治田聖王脩道以治人情
是人情乃聖王之田也而治之何如夫禮者人
情之防範可以濯舊習正持循也則品節于開
導之初猶農夫舉趾于載耕之候然特習其事
punctuated:
者，藝之分、仁之節也。協於藝，講於仁，得之者強。仁者，義之本也，順之體也，得之者尊。
徐建
同考試官學正凌批：聖王治情，以禮義仁爲急，而講學播樂，非從事於三者之外。此作識見真到，詞意貫通。以下爲廣明相須之義，尤根本註疏成說，以發集說所未備。其殆究心經學者，高薦允宜。
考試官署郎中華批：亦可與言禮矣。
考試官給事中陸批：縝密。
記者叙聖王脩道以治情，必深明其道有相須之義也。夫聖王治情之道亦多矣，序不可紊，而義實相須，此所以盡善而無弊歟？記禮運者若曰：農人耕種耨穫以治田，聖王脩道以治人情，是人情乃聖王之田也。而治之何如？夫禮者，人情之防範，可以濯舊習、正持循也。則品節于開導之初，猶農夫舉趾于載耕之候，然特習其事
translation_en:
…is the differentiation of the arts and the articulation of benevolence. It accords with the arts and is elucidated through benevolence; those who attain it are strong. Benevolence is the root of righteousness and the embodiment of accordance; those who attain it are honored.
Xu Jian
Associate Examiner Ling, School Instructor, comments: In governing human feelings, the sage kings gave priority to ritual, righteousness, and benevolence. Expounding learning and disseminating music were not activities outside these three. This composition displays truly penetrating understanding, and its language and ideas are coherent throughout. The ensuing discussion broadly elucidates their mutual dependence. In particular, it grounds itself in the established interpretations of the commentaries and subcommentaries to develop what the Collected Explanations leaves incomplete. Its author is surely someone who has devoted himself to studying the Classics. A high recommendation is entirely fitting.
Examiner Hua, Acting Bureau Director, comments: Here is someone with whom one may indeed discuss ritual.
Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary, comments: Meticulous and closely reasoned.
In describing how the sage kings cultivated the Way to govern human feelings, the recorder must explain thoroughly how its elements depend upon one another. The sage kings indeed had many ways of governing human feelings. Their sequence must not be confused, yet in principle they depend upon one another. Is this not why they achieved complete excellence without harmful consequences? The author of the “Operation of Ritual” chapter seems to say: Farmers cultivate their fields by plowing, sowing, weeding, and harvesting; the sage kings cultivate the Way to govern human feelings. Thus human feelings are the sage kings’ fields. How, then, are they to be cultivated? Ritual provides safeguards and standards for human feelings: it can cleanse old habits and rectify observance and conduct. Accordingly, regulating and ordering them at the outset of instruction is like a farmer setting his feet to work when the time for plowing arrives. Yet this is merely practicing the activities…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
耳義者事之宜也必陳義以示其裁制之方使
善端滋長如播種而有生夫種之斯耨之矣於
此有非義之義不能擇而去之也則講學以明
之去非存是而義於是乎精焉然特明諸心耳
仁者心之德也必本仁以要其合一之歸使心
德渾全如旣耨而有穫夫穫之斯得之矣於此
而強仁利仁未遽至於安之也則播樂以養之
詠歌舞蹈而仁於是乎熟焉夫治情之道如此
然亦未始不相須也以禮言之視權度之推移
===
而經制由之以定非義之實乎若有事合於義
而在所當爲則禮雖未有固可以義而創爲之
制矣禮之義如此其廣也不觀諸義乎義也者
爲藝之分限而協合其事宜爲仁之品節而量
度其隆殺且得義者強足以有執也義之義如
此其博也又不觀諸仁乎仁也者以全德則爲
禮義之本以大用則爲百順之質且得仁者尊
足以長人也夫禮義仁之相須如此學也者明
此者也樂也者安此者也盡始終條理之功而
punctuated:
耳。義者，事之宜也，必陳義以示其裁制之方，使善端滋長，如播種而有生。夫種之斯耨之矣，於此有非義之義，不能擇而去之也，則講學以明之，去非存是，而義於是乎精焉。然特明諸心耳。仁者，心之德也，必本仁以要其合一之歸，使心德渾全，如旣耨而有穫。夫穫之斯得之矣，於此而強仁、利仁，未遽至於安之也，則播樂以養之，詠歌舞蹈，而仁於是乎熟焉。
夫治情之道如此，然亦未始不相須也。以禮言之，視權度之推移，而經制由之以定，非義之實乎？若有事合於義，而在所當爲，則禮雖未有，固可以義而創爲之制矣。禮之義如此其廣也。不觀諸義乎？義也者，爲藝之分限而協合其事宜，爲仁之品節而量度其隆殺，且得義者強足以有執也。義之義如此其博也。又不觀諸仁乎？仁也者，以全德則爲禮義之本，以大用則爲百順之質，且得仁者尊足以長人也。夫禮義仁之相須如此，學也者明此者也，樂也者安此者也，盡始終條理之功而
translation_en:
…only. Righteousness is what is appropriate to affairs. One must expound righteousness to show how to judge and regulate them, allowing the beginnings of goodness to grow, just as sowing seeds brings forth life. Once one has sown, one must weed. If, at this point, there is purported righteousness that is not truly righteous, and one cannot distinguish and remove it, one must pursue learning to clarify it. By removing what is wrong and preserving what is right, righteousness becomes refined. Yet this is only to understand it in the mind. Benevolence is the virtue of the mind. One must take benevolence as the foundation and seek the ultimate unity of these practices, making the mind’s virtue whole and complete, just as weeding leads to a harvest. Once one has harvested, one has obtained the crop. If, at this point, one practices benevolence through effort or for its benefits, without yet being at ease in it, one must perform music to nurture it. Through singing and dancing, benevolence then ripens.
Such is the way of governing the feelings, yet its elements have always depended upon one another. To speak of ritual: established institutions are determined by attending to changes in the weighing and measuring of circumstances—is this not the substance of righteousness? If an undertaking accords with righteousness and ought to be carried out, then even where ritual provides no precedent, one may certainly create regulations for it on the basis of righteousness. So broad is the meaning of ritual. Should we not examine righteousness? Righteousness sets the bounds of the arts, bringing their practice into accord with what is appropriate; it gives measured articulation to benevolence, gauging where its expression should be fuller or more restrained. Moreover, one who attains righteousness possesses sufficient firmness to hold fast. So extensive is the meaning of righteousness. Should we not also examine benevolence? As complete virtue, benevolence is the root of ritual and righteousness; in its great functioning, it is the substance of all forms of accord. Moreover, one who attains benevolence possesses sufficient dignity to lead others. Such is the mutual dependence of ritual, righteousness, and benevolence. Learning makes these clear; music brings one to rest at ease in them. By fully accomplishing the work of ordering them coherently from beginning to end, and…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有曲暢旁通之妙則情無不治而禮制行矣其
斯以為君人之大柄歟大抵禮者一定不易而
人情則曲折萬殊制禮本以治情也故必酌諸
義之權度藝之分量仁之支節以觀其會通然
後可以言禮雖三代因革與天地不磨者惟此
義之實耳若體信達順則仁之用塞乎兩間也
噫禮一也脩之則情其性矣廢之則性其情矣
是故先王慎其所以治情者
樂則安安則久久則天天則神
===
許來學
同考試官學正凌批樂音和平中正故致此
以治心而感化之妙如此此作妙會是意而天神
久安四字句句親切非有得於樂而窮神知化者
不能
考試官署郎中華批此樂化章中精粹語而
學者苦於無註子獨發揮明白且神字處與人異
是之取爾
考試官給事中陸批語和而莊
punctuated:
有曲暢旁通之妙，則情無不治而禮制行矣。其斯以為君人之大柄歟？大抵禮者一定不易，而人情則曲折萬殊。制禮本以治情也，故必酌諸義之權度、藝之分量、仁之支節，以觀其會通，然後可以言禮。雖三代因革，與天地不磨者，惟此義之實耳。若體信達順，則仁之用塞乎兩間也。噫！禮一也，脩之則情其性矣，廢之則性其情矣。是故先王慎其所以治情者。
樂則安，安則久，久則天，天則神。
許來學。
同考試官學正凌批：樂音和平中正，故致此以治心，而感化之妙如此。此作妙會是意，而天、神、久、安四字，句句親切。非有得於樂而窮神知化者不能。
考試官署郎中華批：此樂化章中精粹語，而學者苦於無註。子獨發揮明白，且神字處與人異，是之取爾。
考試官給事中陸批：語和而莊。
translation_en:
…and attain the subtle ability to develop every detail fully and extend understanding to related matters, then all feelings will be regulated and the institutions of ritual will prevail. Is this not the great instrument by which a ruler governs his people? In general, ritual is fixed and unchanging, while human feelings have countless twists and variations. Ritual was instituted precisely to regulate feelings. Thus one must weigh the standards of righteousness, the proper measures of the arts, and the articulations of benevolence, examining how they converge and interconnect, before one can speak of ritual. Despite the continuities and changes of the Three Dynasties, what endures undiminished alongside Heaven and Earth is simply the substance of this righteousness. As for embodying trustworthiness and realizing harmony, these are the workings of benevolence filling the space between Heaven and Earth. Ah! Ritual is one and the same: cultivate it, and feelings express one's nature; abandon it, and feelings are made into one's nature. Thus the former kings were careful about the means by which they regulated feelings.
“Music brings ease; ease brings endurance; endurance brings naturalness; naturalness brings spiritual efficacy.”
Xu Laixue 許來學.
Comment by Associate Examiner Ling, Instructor: “Musical tones are harmonious, balanced, centered, and correct. Hence, when these qualities are brought to bear upon the cultivation of the mind, their power to influence and transform is as marvelous as this. This essay subtly grasps that meaning, and every sentence closely addresses the four terms ‘naturalness,’ ‘spiritual efficacy,’ ‘endurance,’ and ‘ease.’ Only someone who has gained insight into music, fathomed spiritual efficacy, and understood transformation could achieve this.”
Comment by Examiner Hua, Acting Director: “These are words of the utmost refinement from the chapter ‘Transformation through Music,’ yet students struggle because they lack commentary. You alone have expounded them clearly; moreover, your treatment of ‘spiritual efficacy’ differs from that of others. It is for this that I select your essay.”
Comment by Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary: “The language is harmonious yet dignified.”

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
善豫於中而馴致其妙此樂之治心然也甚矣
樂之入人深也旣豫於中則有所得矣而安久
天神之妙有不馴致者哉且君子所貴乎樂者
無他正以治其心耳誠於和平中正之音以致
則易直子諒之心以生其不有所樂乎蓋善端
萌動悅意自爾其流通有義理以養其心也道
腴深味至趣悠然其自適有和粹以平其性也
夫心每患於不安為其未能樂也旣樂矣則豈
弟之美優柔厭飫而外物無以撓其真性分之
===
懿涵泳從容而非僻無以奪其守一何如其安
乎夫心每難於持久為其未能安也旣安矣則
心與理一確乎貞固不以始終而或違德惟日
新卓乎堅定不以先後而或間又何如其久乎
持之以久不但已也充養渾化而朕兆不萌于
見聞存主純熟而機緘不涉於形迹即吾心固
有之天而得乎渾然自成之妙矣非天而何旣
至于天不徒然也無聲無臭而淵乎幾微之黙
運無方無體而関乎流動之不拘即吾心神明
punctuated: 善豫於中，而馴致其妙，此樂之治心然也。甚矣，樂之入人深也！旣豫於中，則有所得矣，而安、久、天、神之妙，有不馴致者哉？且君子所貴乎樂者，無他，正以治其心耳。誠於和平中正之音以致，則易直子諒之心以生，其不有所樂乎？蓋善端萌動，悅意自爾，其流通有義理以養其心也；道腴深味，至趣悠然，其自適有和粹以平其性也。夫心每患於不安，為其未能樂也。旣樂矣，則豈弟之美，優柔厭飫，而外物無以撓其真；性分之懿，涵泳從容，而非僻無以奪其守。一何如其安乎！夫心每難於持久，為其未能安也。旣安矣，則心與理一，確乎貞固，不以始終而或違；德惟日新，卓乎堅定，不以先後而或間。又何如其久乎！持之以久，不但已也。充養渾化，而朕兆不萌于見聞；存主純熟，而機緘不涉於形迹。即吾心固有之天，而得乎渾然自成之妙矣，非天而何？旣至于天，不徒然也。無聲無臭，而淵乎幾微之黙運；無方無體，而関乎流動之不拘。即吾心神明
translation_en:
…goodness and joy within, and gradually attaining their wondrous effects: this is what music accomplishes in ordering the heart. How deeply music enters into people! Once there is joy within, something has been gained. Could the wondrous states of repose, enduring constancy, Heaven, and spiritual efficacy fail to follow gradually? Moreover, what the gentleman values in music is nothing other than its capacity to order his heart. If he sincerely brings this about through peaceful, harmonious, balanced, and correct sounds, a heart of ease, uprightness, kindness, and trustworthiness arises. Would he not then find joy? As the beginnings of goodness stir, delight naturally follows; in their free circulation, moral principles nourish his heart. As he deeply savors the richness of the Way, its highest delights unfold at leisure; in this contentment, harmony and purity bring his nature into balance.

The heart often suffers from a lack of repose because it has not yet attained joy. Once it has attained joy, it gently and fully absorbs the beauty of an affable disposition, so that external things cannot disturb its authenticity. It leisurely immerses itself in the excellence of its inherent nature, so that perversity and deviation cannot wrest away what it holds fast. How profound its repose! The heart often finds enduring constancy difficult because it has not yet attained repose. Once it has attained repose, the heart and principle become one, firmly upright and steadfast, without deviation from beginning to end. Virtue is renewed daily, outstandingly firm and settled, without interruption from earlier to later. How enduring its constancy!

Nor does the matter end with maintaining this constancy. Through full nourishment and thorough transformation, no incipient signs emerge within sight or hearing; through thoroughly matured preservation and inner mastery, the workings leave no visible traces. In the Heaven inherent in my own heart, I attain the marvel of what spontaneously completes itself as an undivided whole. What could this be but Heaven? Having reached Heaven, this is no empty attainment. Soundless and odorless, it is profound in the silent operation of its subtlest workings; without fixed direction or form, it opens onto [?] an unrestrained flow. Within the spiritual luminosity of my own heart…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之奧而入于變化莫測之中矣非神而何夫曰
樂曰安曰久人道之所由至也曰天曰神天德
之所由達也一致樂以治心而其妙如此君子
之於樂也而可斯須去身哉抑此論君子治心
之學至爲精切雖禮順樂和表裏交養而養於
中者實爲之主故以禮治身不過嚴威而止樂
之治心則至于天且神即子思之致中孟子之
大化也要之聖人作樂之本端在于此故曰致
禮樂之道舉而措之天下無難矣
===
第貳塲
論
治天下者審所上
顧四科
同考試官教諭毛 批 筆勢滔滔波瀾千里而
自有曲折往復之妙學者得之文體當爲一變
同考試官教諭吳 批 此題作者類以陳言綴
緝成文是篇立意迥別而詞足以發之故錄
同考試官教諭宋 批 文氣秀發□□□□□
punctuated:
之奧，而入于變化莫測之中矣，非神而何？夫曰樂、曰安、曰久，人道之所由至也；曰天、曰神，天德之所由達也。一致樂以治心，而其妙如此，君子之於樂也，而可斯須去身哉？抑此論君子治心之學，至爲精切。雖禮順樂和，表裏交養，而養於中者實爲之主。故以禮治身，不過嚴威而止；樂之治心，則至于天且神，即子思之致中、孟子之大化也。要之，聖人作樂之本端在于此，故曰：「致禮樂之道，舉而措之天下，無難矣。」
第貳塲
論
治天下者審所上
顧四科
同考試官教諭毛批：筆勢滔滔，波瀾千里，而自有曲折往復之妙。學者得之，文體當爲一變。
同考試官教諭吳批：此題作者，類以陳言綴緝成文。是篇立意迥別，而詞足以發之，故錄。
同考試官教諭宋批：文氣秀發，□□□□□。
translation_en:
…the profundity of our own mind’s spiritual intelligence, entering into transformations beyond all fathoming. What could this be but the spiritual? Joy, repose, and endurance are stages through which the human Way reaches fulfillment; Heaven and the spiritual are the attainments through which heavenly virtue finds expression. Simply bringing music to its fullest realization to govern the mind produces such subtle wonders: could the gentleman allow music to leave his person even for a moment? Moreover, this discussion of the gentleman’s discipline of governing the mind is supremely precise and pertinent. Although ritual brings order and music brings harmony, nurturing the outer and inner together, it is inward cultivation that truly takes the lead. Thus, governing the person through ritual goes no further than solemn dignity; governing the mind through music reaches Heaven and even the spiritual. This is precisely Zisi’s realization of equilibrium and Mencius’s greatness and transformative power. In essence, herein lies the fundamental purpose for which the sages created music. Hence the saying: “Bring the Way of ritual and music to its fullest realization, and there will be no difficulty in applying it throughout the world.”
Second Session
Discourse
“Those Who Govern All under Heaven Must Examine What They Esteem”
By Gu Sike 顧四科
Associate Examiner Mao, School Instructor, comments: “The momentum of the writing surges onward, its waves rolling a thousand li, yet it possesses its own subtle art of turns and returns. If students grasp this, their literary style should undergo a transformation.”
Associate Examiner Wu, School Instructor, comments: “Those who write on this topic generally stitch together familiar sayings to make an essay. This piece is altogether distinctive in conception, and its language adequately expresses that conception. It has therefore been selected for inclusion.”
Associate Examiner Song, School Instructor, comments: “The vitality of the prose blossoms with elegance; [five illegible characters].”

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官署郎中華批清美圓健機軸自別
考試官給事中陸批脫去近時浮靡之習是
亦能審所上者
君子所以先天下者亦惟有定志而已天
下之俗未始不自夫在上者為之也是故
必有所上焉以先之者然而古之為治者
其術亦甚不同也有先之以禮者矣有先
之以刑者矣是二者其志不同故所上不
同而俗之美惡因之此無他存乎審不審
之間而已故夫治天下者莫先於定其志
志定則所上無不審而天下之治幾矣甞
觀賈誼之論治有所謂審取舍者而匡衡
告元帝亦曰治天下者審所上彼衡之言
亦誼之遺說與夫二子者以為刑罰之不
如禮誼法令之不如教化而思以是易天
下也其意亦美矣雖然天下之治則莫先
於人主之有定志而二子者之論未之及
也刑罰之不如禮誼也法令之不如教化
punctuated:
考試官署郎中華批：清美圓健，機軸自別。
考試官給事中陸批：脫去近時浮靡之習，是亦能審所上者。
君子所以先天下者，亦惟有定志而已。天下之俗，未始不自夫在上者為之也。是故必有所上焉以先之者。然而古之為治者，其術亦甚不同也。有先之以禮者矣，有先之以刑者矣。是二者，其志不同，故所上不同，而俗之美惡因之。此無他，存乎審不審之間而已。故夫治天下者，莫先於定其志。志定則所上無不審，而天下之治幾矣。甞觀賈誼之論治，有所謂審取舍者，而匡衡告元帝亦曰：「治天下者審所上。」彼衡之言，亦誼之遺說與？夫二子者，以為刑罰之不如禮誼，法令之不如教化，而思以是易天下也，其意亦美矣。雖然，天下之治，則莫先於人主之有定志，而二子者之論未之及也。刑罰之不如禮誼也，法令之不如教化
translation_en:
Examiner Hua, Acting Bureau Director, comments: “Pure and elegant, rounded and vigorous; its conception and structure are distinctive.”
Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary, comments: “It casts off the recent habit of superficial extravagance. This writer, too, is capable of carefully judging what to esteem.”
What enables the gentleman to lead all under Heaven is simply firmness of purpose. The customs of the realm have invariably been shaped by those above. Thus those who lead must esteem something by which to guide others. Yet the methods of those who governed in antiquity differed greatly. Some led through ritual propriety; others led through punishments. Their purposes differed, and so did what they esteemed; the goodness or badness of customs followed accordingly. The reason is nothing other than whether or not they judged carefully. Hence, for one who governs all under Heaven, nothing takes precedence over fixing his purpose. Once his purpose is fixed, everything he esteems will have been carefully judged, and good government throughout the realm will be close at hand.
I have read Jia Yi’s discussion of government, in which he speaks of carefully judging what to adopt and what to reject. Kuang Heng likewise told Emperor Yuan: “One who governs all under Heaven carefully judges what he esteems.” Was Heng’s statement also a teaching inherited from Yi? These two men held that punishments were inferior to ritual propriety and righteousness, and laws and ordinances inferior to moral instruction and transformation. They hoped thereby to change the realm, and their intention was admirable. Nevertheless, in governing all under Heaven, nothing takes precedence over the ruler’s having a fixed purpose, and the arguments of these two men did not reach this point. That punishments are inferior to ritual propriety and righteousness, and laws and ordinances inferior to moral instruction and transformation…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
也世主亦知之矣然不能勉於此而顧安
於彼者何也彼其志不先定則見之弗明
而行之有弗力故也是故其道非難知而
難擇非難擇而難守能擇能守可以言審
所上矣而非有定志者其孰知之今夫法
之所用易見而禮之所爲難知也人主之
能無惑焉者鮮矣苟擬議之間稍有不當
將有不勝其弊者故必辨之明而斷之決
曉然見其若黑白之相去也而後從之夫
===
是之謂能擇天下固有知所上者也勉於
一時而不能持之終身其心初向於道而
異說入焉則有盡棄其所爲以從之者此
尤君子之所愼焉而不敢忽也執此之政
堅如金石持此之令信如四時吾之所上
在是則舉天下無以加之夫是之謂能守
能擇而後得所審能守而後所審者不易
所審者不易夫然後推而行之則敎化之
流由內及外動之而和綏之而安民日遷
punctuated: 也，世主亦知之矣。然不能勉於此而顧安於彼者，何也？彼其志不先定，則見之弗明，而行之有弗力故也。是故其道非難知而難擇，非難擇而難守。能擇能守，可以言審所上矣，而非有定志者，其孰知之？今夫法之所用易見，而禮之所爲難知也，人主之能無惑焉者鮮矣。苟擬議之間稍有不當，將有不勝其弊者，故必辨之明而斷之決，曉然見其若黑白之相去也，而後從之，夫是之謂能擇。天下固有知所上者也，勉於一時而不能持之終身，其心初向於道，而異說入焉，則有盡棄其所爲以從之者，此尤君子之所愼焉而不敢忽也。執此之政，堅如金石；持此之令，信如四時。吾之所上在是，則舉天下無以加之，夫是之謂能守。能擇而後得所審，能守而後所審者不易。所審者不易，夫然後推而行之，則敎化之流，由內及外，動之而和，綏之而安，民日遷
translation_en: …The rulers of the age also know this. Yet why do they fail to exert themselves in pursuing the latter and instead rest content with the former? Because their resolve is not first settled, they do not see clearly and lack vigor in carrying it out. Thus, regarding this way, the difficulty lies less in knowing it than in choosing it, and less in choosing it than in holding to it. Those who can both choose and hold to it may be said to judge carefully what they exalt. Yet who without settled resolve could understand this? Now, the effects of applying laws are readily seen, whereas what ritual accomplishes is difficult to discern. Few rulers can remain free of confusion about this. If their deliberations go even slightly astray, the resulting harm may prove overwhelming. They must therefore distinguish clearly and decide firmly, seeing the difference as plainly as that between black and white, and only then follow their choice. This is what is meant by being able to choose. There are certainly people in the world who know what to exalt, yet exert themselves only for a time and cannot sustain it throughout their lives. Their hearts initially turn toward the Way, but when divergent teachings enter, some abandon everything they have been doing to follow them. This is precisely what the gentleman guards against most carefully and dares not neglect. In administering such government, be as firm as metal and stone; in maintaining its ordinances, be as dependable as the four seasons. If this is what I exalt, nothing in all the world can surpass it. This is what is meant by being able to hold fast. Only through the ability to choose does one arrive at a considered judgment; only through the ability to hold fast does that judgment remain unchanged. Once that judgment remains unchanged, one can extend it and put it into practice. Then the influence of moral instruction flows from within to without: moved by it, the people become harmonious; soothed by it, they become secure; day by day, the people advance…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
善遠罪而不自知也而其俗有弗廓然大
變者乎古之能審所上者其知之矣堯舜
禹都俞唯諾而四方為之風動文王之治
岐也躬行于國中而兎罝漢廣之俗莫不
化之何修而得此哉彼其為政也本於身
行於家自夫起居飲食之間而達之天下
行之數十世而禮教不衰其積之有本而
施之有漸如此者有定志故也彼以是為
不足法而以刑驅其民者秦是也是以棄
===
禮義捐廉恥而其俗日壞傳二世而禍亂
隨之嗟乎世主之欲審所上者亦舉三代
與秦之事觀之矣故曰取舍之極定於內
而安危之萌應於外其弗信乎吾觀夫西
漢之俗則亦有甚敝者盖自文景武宣之
間則然而何有於孝元之衰世顧嘗考其
一時賢人君子之論議亦多懇懇於禮樂
教化而莫粹於董子正心之論此雖賈誼
未之及而陋儒若匡衡何足以知之然今
punctuated: 善、遠罪而不自知也，而其俗有弗廓然大變者乎？古之能審所上者，其知之矣。堯舜禹都俞唯諾，而四方為之風動；文王之治岐也，躬行于國中，而《兎罝》《漢廣》之俗莫不化之。何修而得此哉？彼其為政也，本於身，行於家，自夫起居飲食之間而達之天下，行之數十世而禮教不衰。其積之有本而施之有漸如此者，有定志故也。彼以是為不足法而以刑驅其民者，秦是也。是以棄禮義，捐廉恥，而其俗日壞，傳二世而禍亂隨之。嗟乎！世主之欲審所上者，亦舉三代與秦之事觀之矣。故曰：「取舍之極定於內，而安危之萌應於外。」其弗信乎？吾觀夫西漢之俗，則亦有甚敝者，盖自文景武宣之間則然，而何有於孝元之衰世？顧嘗考其一時賢人君子之論議，亦多懇懇於禮樂教化，而莫粹於董子正心之論。此雖賈誼未之及，而陋儒若匡衡何足以知之？然今
translation_en: …toward goodness and away from wrongdoing without themselves realizing it. Could their customs then fail to undergo a thorough transformation? The ancients who could carefully discern what to esteem surely understood this. Yao, Shun, and Yu exchanged exclamations of counsel and assent, and the four quarters stirred in response as though moved by the wind. When King Wen governed Qi, he personally put his principles into practice within his domain, and the customs depicted in “The Rabbit Net” (Tu ju) and “The Broad Han River” (Han guang) were all transformed by his influence. What did they cultivate to achieve this? Their government was rooted in their own persons and practiced within their households; from the daily affairs of rising, resting, eating, and drinking, they extended it throughout the realm. It continued for scores of generations without any decline in ritual instruction. That their accumulated efforts had such firm roots and their implementation proceeded so gradually was because their resolve was fixed. As for those who deemed this unworthy of emulation and drove their people by punishments, Qin was such a case. Thus it abandoned ritual propriety and righteousness, cast aside integrity and shame, and its customs deteriorated daily. Once rule passed to the second generation, calamity and disorder followed. Alas! Rulers who wish to discern carefully what to esteem need only consider the affairs of the Three Dynasties and Qin. Thus it is said: “The ultimate standard of acceptance and rejection is fixed within, and the beginnings of security and peril respond without.” Is this not trustworthy? When I examine the customs of the Western Han, I find that they too suffered grievous corruption. This was already so during the reigns of Emperors Wen, Jing, Wu, and Xuan; how much more so in the declining age of Emperor Xiaoyuan! Yet when I examine the discussions of the worthy and exemplary men of that time, many were earnest in advocating rites, music, and moral instruction. None, however, was more refined than Master Dong’s argument for rectifying the heart. Even Jia Yi did not attain this understanding; how could a shallow scholar such as Kuang Heng have understood it? Yet today…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之言治則舍是而曰有定志也者何哉夫
未有不定其志而能正其心者吾之言固
董子意也學者不足以知此而謂有二焉者
是未足與言審所上也
同前
姜良翰
同考試官教諭徐批士子類用匡衡語而重
疊排比之是卷筆老意新而步驟衝逸眞妙於文
哉
===
同考試官教諭鄭批場中作論語者固多率
掇拾腐說誇多鬪靡此卷獨能會題意於言外理
到而句亦工也
同考試官學正孫批此作波瀾疊壓而源委
不紊讀之惟恐其盡是宜錄出
考試官署郎中華批詞氣充贍而亦不失程
文之矩度
考試官給事中陸批有議論有操縱他作鮮
及
punctuated:
之言治，則舍是而曰有定志也者，何哉？夫未有不定其志而能正其心者，吾之言固董子意也。學者不足以知此，而謂有二焉者，是未足與言審所上也。

同前。
姜良翰。

同考試官教諭徐批：士子類用匡衡語而重疊排比之，是卷筆老意新，而步驟衝逸，眞妙於文哉！

同考試官教諭鄭批：場中作《論語》者固多，率掇拾腐說，誇多鬪靡。此卷獨能會題意於言外，理到而句亦工也。

同考試官學正孫批：此作波瀾疊壓而源委不紊，讀之惟恐其盡，是宜錄出。

考試官署郎中華批：詞氣充贍，而亦不失程文之矩度。

考試官給事中陸批：有議論，有操縱，他作鮮及。
translation_en:
…when discussing governance, why abandon this and speak instead of fixing one’s resolve? No one has ever been able to rectify his mind without first fixing his resolve. What I have said is indeed Master Dong’s meaning. Scholars who fail to understand this and claim that these are two separate things are not yet fit to discuss discerning what one esteems.

Same as the preceding topic.
Jiang Lianghan 姜良翰.

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: Candidates generally use Kuang Heng’s words, repeating and arranging them in parallel constructions. This paper displays a seasoned hand and fresh ideas, while its movement is vigorous and unrestrained. Truly a marvel of composition!

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: There are certainly many in the examination hall writing on the Analects, but most merely gather stale explanations, flaunting their abundance and competing in ornament. This paper alone grasps the topic’s meaning beyond its explicit wording. Its reasoning is sound, and its sentences are skillfully crafted.

Comment by Associate Examiner Sun, School Director: The waves of this composition surge one upon another, yet its sources and development remain orderly. Reading it, one fears only that it will end. It deserves to be transcribed for inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Hua, Acting Bureau Director: Its diction and rhetorical force are ample and rich, yet it also conforms to the standards of a model answer.

Comment by Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary: It has substantive argument and assured command of the composition. Few other works can match it.

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
聖人有先天下之見而後可以善其道於
不窮夫聖人之道以治民也民之趨于治
也恒不于其所治而于其治之所先何謂
治之所先上者下之先也近者遠之先也
聖人有見焉於是預爲之所裁度於一心
推移於世變逆覩於斯民之所欲趨而鼓
之以爲風漸之以爲化使相率而趨之不
自知其由也夫然後惟吾之所欲爲而無
不如意匡衡曰治天下者審所上此之謂
===
也夫有一代之興必有一代之尚尚也者
一人作之百人和之一日行之百年從之
其始也翕然而趨其既也恬然而習其成
也帖然而安尚而至於成則雖聖人不能
以自挽挽之而天下不從是故聖人必審
之於先而不敢以自易嘗觀古者聖人之
作易也於泰則曰无平不陂无往不復於
否則曰其亡其亡繫于苞桑而於賁則曰
觀乎人文以化成天下聖人豈故深思而
punctuated:
聖人有先天下之見，而後可以善其道於不窮。夫聖人之道，以治民也。民之趨于治也，恒不于其所治，而于其治之所先。何謂治之所先？上者，下之先也；近者，遠之先也。聖人有見焉，於是預爲之所，裁度於一心，推移於世變，逆覩於斯民之所欲趨，而鼓之以爲風，漸之以爲化，使相率而趨之，不自知其由也。夫然後，惟吾之所欲爲，而無不如意。匡衡曰：「治天下者審所上。」此之謂也。

夫有一代之興，必有一代之尚。尚也者，一人作之，百人和之；一日行之，百年從之。其始也，翕然而趨；其既也，恬然而習；其成也，帖然而安。尚而至於成，則雖聖人不能以自挽；挽之而天下不從。是故聖人必審之於先，而不敢以自易。嘗觀古者聖人之作易也，於泰則曰：「无平不陂，无往不復。」於否則曰：「其亡其亡，繫于苞桑。」而於賁則曰：「觀乎人文，以化成天下。」聖人豈故深思而
translation_en:
Only when the sage possesses foresight that precedes the understanding of all under Heaven can he ensure that his Way continues to work well without end. The sage’s Way serves to govern the people. Yet the people’s movement toward good order depends ordinarily not on what he directly governs, but on what takes precedence in his governance. What does this mean? Those above set the lead for those below; those nearby set the lead for those far away. Understanding this, the sage makes provision beforehand. He weighs and judges within his own mind, adapting to changes in the world. He foresees the direction in which the people wish to move, then inspires them to establish customs and gradually imbues them with transforming influence. He causes them to follow one another in that direction without themselves knowing why. Only then does everything he wishes to undertake accord with his intentions. Kuang Heng said: “One who governs all under Heaven must carefully examine what he esteems.” This is what he meant.

Whenever a dynasty rises, it necessarily has something distinctive that it esteems. What is esteemed is initiated by one person and echoed by a hundred; put into practice for a single day, it is followed for a hundred years. At first, people move toward it in concert; thereafter, they become accustomed to it without concern; once it is fully established, they rest contentedly in it. When what is esteemed has become fully established, even a sage cannot reverse it by himself. If he tries to reverse it, all under Heaven will refuse to follow. Therefore the sage must examine it carefully beforehand and dare not treat it lightly. I have observed how the sages of antiquity composed the Book of Changes. In the hexagram Tai, Peace, it says: “No level ground fails to slope; no departure fails to return.” In Pi, Obstruction, it says: “‘It may perish! It may perish!’ Bind it to a clump of mulberry trees.” And in Bi, Adornment, it says: “Observe the patterned forms of human culture, thereby transforming all under Heaven and bringing it to completion.” Could the sage have deliberately pondered so deeply and …

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
過慮之直以天下之治不可以法病道道
固萬世無弊而紛紜膠轕以變更乎天下
者皆法也觀其變神其幾其預待乎天下
後世者審矣故夏之尚忠也忠弊而商救
之以質質弊而周則以文救之皆通於道
而不離於法善其道於不窮者也雖然後
世之徒法也久矣清靜而黃老之刻核而
申韓之執一實以御百虛而權謀功利之
玆數者恒足以奔走天下之人而聖人則
===
育於仁陶於禮成於義而終不肯以彼易
此彼以厲吾恬以和彼以速吾安以鈍計
功程效而吾則疎宜乎後世之君深信彼
之有成而不吾尚也夫吾之治一道也非
徒法也彼雖不吾信而吾將見彼之日窮
矣此非神於幾達於變者孰能察識於心
術之微而審之也哉審之無異術也是其
所是必其非天下之公是也非其所非必
其非天下之公非也非非而是是者求之
punctuated: 過慮之，直以天下之治不可以法病道。道固萬世無弊，而紛紜膠轕以變更乎天下者，皆法也。觀其變，神其幾，其預待乎天下後世者審矣。故夏之尚忠也，忠弊而商救之以質；質弊而周則以文救之。皆通於道而不離於法，善其道於不窮者也。雖然，後世之徒法也久矣。清靜而黃老之，刻核而申韓之，執一實以御百虛而權謀功利之。玆數者，恒足以奔走天下之人，而聖人則育於仁，陶於禮，成於義，而終不肯以彼易此。彼以厲，吾恬以和；彼以速，吾安以鈍。計功程效，而吾則疎。宜乎後世之君深信彼之有成，而不吾尚也。夫吾之治，一道也，非徒法也。彼雖不吾信，而吾將見彼之日窮矣。此非神於幾、達於變者，孰能察識於心術之微而審之也哉？審之無異術也：是其所是，必其非天下之公是也；非其所非，必其非天下之公非也。非非而是是者，求之
translation_en:
…and worry excessively about it? It was simply because, in governing the realm, methods must not be allowed to impair the Way. The Way itself remains free of defects through ten thousand generations; what becomes tangled and contentious and brings alterations to the realm consists entirely of methods. By observing changes and discerning their incipient signs with spiritual insight, the sages carefully prepared for the realm and for later generations. Thus, the Xia prized loyalty; when loyalty developed abuses, the Shang remedied them through simplicity. When simplicity developed abuses, the Zhou remedied them through cultural refinement. All comprehended the Way without departing from methods, keeping their Way sound and inexhaustible.

Nevertheless, later generations have long relied on methods alone. Seeking purity and stillness, they follow Huang-Lao; seeking exacting scrutiny, they follow Shen Buhai and Han Fei; grasping one substantial principle to control a hundred empty possibilities [?], they pursue stratagems, achievement, and profit. These approaches invariably suffice to set the people of the realm rushing about in their service. The sages, however, nurture through benevolence, mold through ritual propriety, and bring to completion through righteousness, never consenting to exchange these for those other approaches. They employ severity; we remain tranquil through harmony. They employ speed; we rest content with slowness. When achievements are reckoned and results measured, we appear wanting. It is understandable that rulers of later generations firmly believe those approaches will succeed and do not esteem ours.

Our government rests entirely upon the Way, not merely upon methods. Though they do not trust us, we shall see their approaches grow more exhausted by the day. Unless one possesses spiritual insight into incipient signs and comprehends change, who could perceive and understand the subtleties of the workings of the mind and judge them carefully? There is no special technique for such judgment: when they approve what they approve, it is surely not what all under Heaven impartially approve; when they condemn what they condemn, it is surely not what all under Heaven impartially condemn. To condemn what is wrong and approve what is right, one seeks it…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
吾心之公也求之道也而非徒法也吾計
已定吾術已明諒其非而去之原其是而
從之由是見微於泰以防天下之過也由
是起教於否以約天下之趨也由是觀變
於賁以成天下之文也明物采設典則天
下之化成而民情樂彼之清靜無為者吾
弗尚之矣慎感孚妙鼓舞天下之風清而
習俗淳彼之綜核名實者吾弗尚之矣不
識不知與天下相安於仁義禮樂之歸彼
===
之執實以御虛如權謀術數之類皆吾所
見棄者也吾又何求然則吾之所尚者皆
道也而非徒法也苟不此之審而與天下
日逐逐于教令刑罰之末則雖強焉以必
之而天下不從是何也不從其所治而從
其治之所先也且刑者仁之薄也令者禮
之衰也教者義之竭也秪見其民日殘而
俗日壞矣雖日教而求其治不可得也古
之聖人未嘗一日不審所尚以為天下先
punctuated: 吾心之公也，求之道也，而非徒法也。吾計已定，吾術已明，諒其非而去之，原其是而從之。由是見微於泰，以防天下之過也；由是起教於否，以約天下之趨也；由是觀變於賁，以成天下之文也。明物采，設典則，天下之化成而民情樂，彼之清靜無為者，吾弗尚之矣。慎感孚，妙鼓舞，天下之風清而習俗淳，彼之綜核名實者，吾弗尚之矣。不識不知，與天下相安於仁義禮樂之歸，彼之執實以御虛，如權謀術數之類，皆吾所見棄者也。吾又何求？然則吾之所尚者皆道也，而非徒法也。苟不此之審，而與天下日逐逐于教令刑罰之末，則雖強焉以必之，而天下不從。是何也？不從其所治，而從其治之所先也。且刑者，仁之薄也；令者，禮之衰也；教者，義之竭也。秪見其民日殘而俗日壞矣，雖日教而求其治，不可得也。古之聖人未嘗一日不審所尚，以為天下先。
translation_en:
…in the impartiality of my own heart; I seek it in the Way, rather than merely in methods. My plans are settled, and my methods are clear. I ascertain what is wrong and discard it; I examine the grounds of what is right and follow it. Thus I discern the subtle signs within Peace (Tai), to guard against the errors of all under Heaven; thus I initiate instruction amid Stagnation (Pi), to restrain the tendencies of all under Heaven; thus I observe change within Adornment (Bi), to bring the cultural refinement of all under Heaven to completion. By making clear the distinctions expressed through objects and their ornamentation and establishing institutions and standards, transformation throughout the realm is accomplished and the people are content. I therefore do not esteem that doctrine of quietude and nonaction. By attending carefully to the sincerity that moves people and inspiring them with subtle skill, the moral atmosphere of the realm becomes pure and its customs wholesome. I therefore do not esteem that practice of comprehensively checking names against actual performance. Without conscious knowledge or contrivance, I dwell at peace with all under Heaven in our common adherence to benevolence, righteousness, rites, and music. Those practices of grasping the substantial to control the insubstantial—such things as political stratagems and manipulative techniques—are all things I reject. What more should I seek? Thus, everything I esteem belongs to the Way, rather than merely to methods.

If one fails to examine this carefully, and instead busies oneself and all under Heaven day after day with the peripheral matters of instruction, commands, punishments, and penalties, then, even if one uses force to compel compliance, the people will not follow. Why is this? They follow not what the ruler seeks to regulate, but what he puts first in governing. Moreover, punishment is benevolence grown thin; commands are ritual propriety in decline; instruction is righteousness exhausted. One will only see the people increasingly afflicted and their customs increasingly corrupted. Even if one instructs them daily in pursuit of good order, it cannot be attained. The sages of antiquity never let a single day pass without carefully examining what they esteemed, so as to set an example for all under Heaven.

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
特以漢承乎秦而先王之良法美意幾盡
非惟不知所審且文帝過於仁而近于黃
老武帝過於義而近于權謀宣帝尚嚴刻
而近于刑名歷孝元而天下之弊極矣此
固識治體者所深憂也匡衡乃以斯言進
雖其言未發致審之要而亦深可取也已
善乎程子之言曰三代之治後世决可復
不以三代為治者終苟道也嗚呼夷考于
漢之諸君其不安於苟道也者幾希
===
表
擬宋開天章閣引輔臣入對參知政事范
仲淹謝表慶曆三年
費滂
同考試官教諭徐批表語駢儷已非古意而
近代舉業復襲浮詞以益之趨愈下矣此篇剷華
就實親切簡當得士如此豈獨重其文乎
同考試官教諭鄭批宋范質憚太祖英武每
事具劄子進呈遂廢命坐面論之禮仁宗開閣引
punctuated:
特以漢承乎秦，而先王之良法美意幾盡，非惟不知所審，且文帝過於仁而近于黃老，武帝過於義而近于權謀，宣帝尚嚴刻而近于刑名，歷孝元而天下之弊極矣。此固識治體者所深憂也。匡衡乃以斯言進，雖其言未發致審之要，而亦深可取也已。善乎程子之言曰：「三代之治，後世决可復；不以三代為治者，終苟道也。」嗚呼！夷考于漢之諸君，其不安於苟道也者幾希！

表

擬宋開天章閣引輔臣入對，參知政事范仲淹謝表。慶曆三年。

費滂

同考試官教諭徐批：表語駢儷，已非古意，而近代舉業復襲浮詞以益之，趨愈下矣。此篇剷華就實，親切簡當。得士如此，豈獨重其文乎？

同考試官教諭鄭批：宋范質憚太祖英武，每事具劄子進呈，遂廢命坐面論之禮。仁宗開閣引
translation_en:
…Yet because the Han succeeded the Qin, the excellent institutions and good intentions of the former kings had almost entirely disappeared. Not only did the rulers fail to understand what required careful scrutiny: Emperor Wen also carried benevolence to excess and approached the teachings of Huang-Lao; Emperor Wu carried righteousness to excess and approached expedient manipulation; and Emperor Xuan prized severity and approached the doctrines of punishments and names. By the reign of Emperor Xiaoyuan, the empire’s maladies had reached their extreme. This was indeed a source of deep concern to anyone who understood the essentials of government. Kuang Heng therefore presented these words to the throne. Although his words did not reveal the essentials of thorough scrutiny, they nevertheless had much to commend them. How excellent were Master Cheng’s words: “The government of the Three Dynasties can certainly be restored in later ages. Those who do not take the Three Dynasties as their model for government ultimately follow a course of mere expediency.” Alas! On dispassionately examining the Han rulers, how few were not content with mere expediency!

Memorial

A memorial of thanks composed in the voice of Fan Zhongyan, Vice Grand Councilor, on the occasion when the Song emperor opened the Tianzhang Pavilion and summoned his chief ministers for an audience. Third year of Qingli [1043].

Fei Pang

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: The parallel phrasing used in memorials already departs from the spirit of antiquity. Recent examination writing compounds this by borrowing empty expressions, so that its tendency is ever further downward. This piece strips away ornament and attends to substance; it is pertinent, concise, and apt. When we obtain a scholar such as this, can it be merely his writing that we value?

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: Fan Zhi of the Song stood in awe of Emperor Taizu’s martial prowess and submitted a written memorandum on every matter. Thus the ceremonial practice of inviting ministers to sit and discuss affairs face to face fell into disuse. Emperor Renzong opened the pavilion and summoned…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
對此致治之本也是作莊整得體讀之使人興起
同考試官學正孫批辭氣恭謹寫出希文忠
愛至情宜錄以
獻
考試官署郎中華批典重不浮寓意懇切
考試官給事中陸批得宋人告君之意
慶曆三年某月某日伏蒙
開天章閣引輔臣入對者伏以
道隆交際鴻猷益懋于泰來義重彌綸
===
清問式勤於晉接當
萬幾之少暇誠千載之一時表著聳觀搢紳
動色臣〔仲淹〕誠歡誠忭稽首頓首竊惟元
首得股肱而弘化宰輔贊天子以經邦二
典都俞濬開心學曰言厲翼典慎面從一
家人父子之相親敦左右臣鄰之大義但
道隨時降而分與堂高坐論風衰恩覃造
膝疇咨日懈獻匪格心補過漢庭願毋違
于紫闥論思唐閣制旋廢乎正牙尋常僅
punctuated:
對，此致治之本也。是作莊整得體，讀之使人興起。

同考試官學正孫批：辭氣恭謹，寫出希文忠愛至情，宜錄以獻。

考試官署郎中華批：典重不浮，寓意懇切。

考試官給事中陸批：得宋人告君之意。

慶曆三年某月某日，伏蒙開天章閣引輔臣入對者。伏以，道隆交際，鴻猷益懋于泰來；義重彌綸，清問式勤於晉接。當萬幾之少暇，誠千載之一時。表著聳觀，搢紳動色。臣〔仲淹〕誠歡誠忭，稽首頓首。竊惟元首得股肱而弘化，宰輔贊天子以經邦。二典都俞，濬開心學；曰言厲翼，典慎面從。一家人父子之相親，敦左右臣鄰之大義。但道隨時降，而分與堂高。坐論風衰，恩覃造膝；疇咨日懈，獻匪格心。補過漢庭，願毋違于紫闥；論思唐閣，制旋廢乎正牙。尋常僅
translation_en:
…to an audience: this is the foundation of achieving good government. This composition is dignified, orderly, and appropriate to its genre; reading it inspires the reader.

Comment by Associate Examiner Sun, School Instructor: Its language and tone are respectful and circumspect, expressing the deepest feelings of loyalty and devotion of Xiwen [Fan Zhongyan]. It deserves to be copied out and presented to the throne.

Comment by Examiner Hua, Acting Bureau Director: Classical and weighty, without superficiality; its meaning is earnest and heartfelt.

Comment by Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary: It captures the spirit in which men of the Song addressed their sovereign.

On a certain day of a certain month in the third year of Qingli [1043], we humbly received the favor of Your Majesty’s opening the Tianzhang Pavilion and summoning the chief ministers to an audience. We humbly consider that when the Way flourishes through intercourse between ruler and ministers, the grand design advances still further with the advent of harmonious prosperity; when due importance is attached to the duty of ordering all affairs, enlightened inquiries are diligently pursued as ministers are received. Amid a brief respite from the myriad affairs of government, this is truly an occasion encountered once in a thousand years. Its manifest splendor astonishes all who behold it; the assembled officials are visibly moved. Your servant〔Zhongyan〕is filled with joy and delight, bowing his head to the ground and repeatedly kowtowing.

I humbly reflect that the head requires its limbs to extend its transforming influence, and chief ministers assist the Son of Heaven in governing the realm. In the Two Canons, the exchanges of counsel and assent opened profound approaches to the learning of the mind; the words concerning speech and diligent assistance set forth caution against merely outward compliance [?]. With the mutual affection of father and son within a single household, ruler and ministers strengthen the great obligations binding the sovereign to those serving at his side. Yet the Way declined with the passage of time, while distinctions of rank grew as lofty as the ruler’s hall. The practice of sitting together to discuss affairs waned, and approaching close to the sovereign became a special favor; consultation grew daily more perfunctory, and counsel offered no longer rectified the sovereign’s heart [?]. At the Han court, ministers seeking to remedy faults wished never to depart from the palace gates; in the Tang pavilions, the institution of deliberation and counsel was soon abolished at the regular court audience [?]. On ordinary occasions, there was scarcely more than…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
止趨班臨御多從畸日延英五刻便殿無
時或假借而強從或背議而少直徒沿故
事遹侈彌文茲蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
聖功天監
神道民懷言路一開攬機權而獨運仁聲四
訖歛智勇以無爲謂
三聖經綸久布昭回之象而百年禮樂當調未
解之弦不有盡言曷裨至理弘開
秘閣廣佇論思尚手攜面命之風求苦口沃
心之助蓋禮意極其周至而
寵渥無復有加者也臣仲淹夙夜先憂致身
是願再三陳列多口茲憎方甘盡瘁於邊
防忽荷
深知于巷遇適當通變宜民之際可無補偏
救敝之陳言出心聲情因義激內外本末
其凡一十餘條興革後先冀采萬分之一
孤切惓惓自許敢謂鑿鑿可行伏願
punctuated:
止趨班，臨御多從畸日；延英五刻，便殿無時。或假借而強從，或背議而少直，徒沿故事，遹侈彌文。茲蓋伏遇：
〇〇〇〇
聖功天監，神道民懷。言路一開，攬機權而獨運；仁聲四訖，歛智勇以無爲。謂三聖經綸，久布昭回之象；而百年禮樂，當調未解之弦。不有盡言，曷裨至理？弘開秘閣，廣佇論思，尚手攜面命之風，求苦口沃心之助。蓋禮意極其周至，而寵渥無復有加者也。
臣仲淹夙夜先憂，致身是願；再三陳列，多口茲憎。方甘盡瘁於邊防，忽荷深知于巷遇。適當通變宜民之際，可無補偏救敝之陳？言出心聲，情因義激。內外本末，其凡一十餘條；興革後先，冀采萬分之一。孤切惓惓自許，敢謂鑿鑿可行？伏願
translation_en:
… amounted only to hastening to their places in the court ranks; imperial audiences generally occurred on alternate days. Audiences in the Yanying Hall lasted five quarter-hours, while those in the side hall had no fixed time. Sometimes indulgence led to reluctant assent; sometimes criticism behind others’ backs left little frankness. They merely followed established precedents, increasingly multiplying empty formalities.
〇〇〇〇
Now, however, we have reverently encountered Your Majesty, whose sagely achievements Heaven observes and whose spiritual way the people cherish. Once the channels of counsel were opened, you gathered the powers of decision into your own hands and exercised them independently. Your renown for benevolence reaches everywhere; you restrain cleverness and martial prowess, governing through nonaction. You consider that the ordering work of the three sage sovereigns has long displayed the radiance of their heavenly pattern, yet the rites and music of a hundred years require the tuning of strings not yet loosened. Without fully outspoken counsel, how could perfect government be aided? You have opened wide the Palace Library and broadly awaited deliberation and reflection, honoring the practice of taking ministers by the hand and instructing them face to face, seeking the aid of bitter counsel that refreshes the heart. Your courteous consideration has thus reached the utmost fullness, and your gracious favor could admit of no addition.
Your servant Zhongyan worries before others, morning and night, wishing only to devote himself to service. Repeatedly setting forth my views, I have incurred resentment for speaking too much. Just as I was content to exhaust my strength in frontier defense, I unexpectedly received your profound understanding in an encounter in a lane [?]. At this very moment, when institutions must be adapted to changing circumstances for the people’s benefit, could I fail to offer proposals for correcting imbalances and remedying abuses? My words give voice to my heart; my feelings are stirred by duty. Covering affairs within and without, fundamentals and particulars, they comprise more than ten articles. Concerning what to establish or abolish, and what should come first or later, I hope that even one ten-thousandth may be adopted. I venture to claim only an earnest and unflagging devotion, standing alone; dare I assert that my proposals are assuredly practicable? I humbly pray that …

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
舍己從人廣好問好察之智
任賢去倖秉勿貳勿疑之公同朝儆戒於無
虞羣類尊親于有截臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叁塲
===
策
第一問
周如厎
同考試官教諭唐批
皇祖垂訓之意詳審精密仁至義盡莫有加者此作能鋪敘揄揚且
所處亦皆有見一以法
祖睦親為主是可為
當宁獻矣
同考試官教諭林批
punctuated:
舍己從人，廣好問好察之智；任賢去倖，秉勿貳勿疑之公。同朝儆戒於無虞，羣類尊親于有截。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叁塲
策
第一問
周如厎
同考試官教諭唐批：
皇祖垂訓之意，詳審精密，仁至義盡，莫有加者。此作能鋪敘揄揚，且所處亦皆有見，一以法祖睦親為主，是可為當宁獻矣。
同考試官教諭林批：
translation_en:
…set aside your own views and follow those of others, broadening the wisdom that delights in questioning and careful scrutiny; employ the worthy and dismiss favorites, maintaining the impartiality that neither wavers nor doubts. May those at court together remain vigilant when there is no cause for alarm, and may all ranks honor and cherish one another in orderly harmony. Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Majesty, cannot contain his intense emotion and trembling awe. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my thanks and make them known to Your Majesty.
Third Session
Policy Essay
First Question
Zhou Rudi 周如厎
Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor:
The intent of the Imperial Ancestor in bequeathing his instructions was considered and precise in every detail, consummate in benevolence and complete in righteousness; nothing could surpass it. This essay expounds and celebrates that intent, and its proposed measures all show discernment. Throughout, it takes emulating the ancestor and fostering harmony among imperial kinsmen as its guiding principles. It is worthy of presentation to the reigning emperor.
Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor:

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
聖祖貽謀盡善具在
祖訓誠
聖子
神孫所當世守也此策鋪張偉麗區畫詳審殆有識之士錄之豈特
以其文哉
考試官署郎中華批此策關係
國家大務自非通達治體能仰窺我
聖祖立訓之心者不能言也得此亦可以轉
聞于
===
上矣
考試官給事中陸批
朝廷體
聖祖之心以待
宗室者至矣其有未安正在隨宜處之耳子所言大抵有見余復
欲建白以通融之可謂卓識有言責者為子興感
矣
帝王之治天下本於仁義而行之必自近
始故親親之道恩以懷之而法以御之恩
punctuated:
聖祖貽謀盡善，具在《祖訓》，誠聖子神孫所當世守也。此策鋪張偉麗，區畫詳審，殆有識之士。錄之，豈特以其文哉？

考試官署郎中華批：此策關係國家大務，自非通達治體、能仰窺我聖祖立訓之心者，不能言也。得此，亦可以轉聞于上矣。

考試官給事中陸批：朝廷體聖祖之心以待宗室者至矣，其有未安，正在隨宜處之耳。子所言，大抵有見。余復欲建白以通融之，可謂卓識！有言責者為子興感矣。

帝王之治天下，本於仁義，而行之必自近始。故親親之道，恩以懷之，而法以御之。恩
translation_en:
The sagely ancestor’s plans bequeathed to posterity are perfect in every respect and are fully set out in the Ancestral Instructions. These are indeed what his sagely sons and divine grandsons ought to preserve generation after generation. This policy essay is magnificent in its exposition and detailed and judicious in its arrangements. Its author is surely a man of discernment. Could its selection have been merely for its literary qualities?

Comment by Examiner Hua, Acting Director: This policy essay concerns great affairs of state. Only someone who thoroughly understands the principles of governance and can reverently discern our sagely ancestor’s intentions in establishing his instructions could speak thus. Having obtained this essay, we may also forward it for His Majesty’s attention.

Comment by Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary: The court has gone to the utmost in embodying the sagely ancestor’s intentions in its treatment of the imperial clan. Whatever remains unsettled simply requires handling as circumstances demand. What you say is, on the whole, perceptive. I further wish to submit proposals to make these arrangements more adaptable. This may be called outstanding discernment! Those charged with the responsibility to speak out are moved by your words.

The rule of emperors and kings over all under Heaven is founded on benevolence and righteousness, and putting these into practice must begin with those nearest to them. Thus, the way of cherishing one’s kin is to win their hearts through favor and regulate them through law. Favor…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
施而濟以法則其恩不流於褻仁之至也
法立而先以恩則其法不傷於刻義之盡
也我
皇祖所以垂訓萬世之意惟此而在
今日繼述之道亦惟此而已請敢陳之嘗觀
古之有天下者必建宗親以藩王室然或
懷之以恩恩勝則流於褻故寵祿踰制者
啓奢僭之端或御之以法法勝則傷於刻
故防檢過密者致殫微之患其能盡善而
===
無弊者鮮矣肆我
皇祖創業之初深惟根本之慮擇良日王諸子
宰臣授冊宗伯授詔次第畢封而藩屏海
內者二十有四王既又親作
祖訓以授之歷六年七謄藁而始成所以貽燕
翼之謀至深遠也雖金匱石室之藏不可
窺見然其條章已出示臣民而見於學士
大夫之所敘述者亦詳矣其間如禮儀之
節法律之守職制之等兵衞之法營繕之
punctuated:
施而濟以法，則其恩不流於褻，仁之至也；法立而先以恩，則其法不傷於刻，義之盡也。我皇祖所以垂訓萬世之意，惟此而在；今日繼述之道，亦惟此而已。請敢陳之。
嘗觀古之有天下者，必建宗親以藩王室。然或懷之以恩，恩勝則流於褻，故寵祿踰制者啓奢僭之端；或御之以法，法勝則傷於刻，故防檢過密者致殫微之患。其能盡善而無弊者鮮矣。
肆我皇祖創業之初，深惟根本之慮，擇良日王諸子，宰臣授冊，宗伯授詔，次第畢封，而藩屏海內者二十有四王。既又親作《祖訓》以授之，歷六年，七謄藁而始成，所以貽燕翼之謀至深遠也。雖金匱石室之藏不可窺見，然其條章已出示臣民，而見於學士大夫之所敘述者亦詳矣。其間如禮儀之節、法律之守、職制之等、兵衞之法、營繕之
translation_en:
…when benevolence is bestowed and tempered with law, it does not lapse into undue familiarity: this is humanity at its highest. When law is established but benevolence comes first, it does not become injuriously harsh: this is righteousness fully realized. Herein lies our Imperial Ancestor’s intention in bequeathing instruction to ten thousand generations; the way to carry on his work today likewise consists in this alone. Allow me respectfully to set it forth.
I have observed that those who possessed All under Heaven in antiquity invariably enfeoffed their imperial kinsmen to serve as bulwarks of the royal house. Yet some cherished them with benevolence, and when benevolence prevailed excessively, it lapsed into undue familiarity. Thus, favor and emoluments exceeding the prescribed limits opened the way to extravagance and usurpation of prerogatives. Others controlled them through law, and when law prevailed excessively, it became injuriously harsh. Thus, excessively stringent restraints brought the danger of depletion and decline [?]. Few could achieve complete excellence without harmful consequences.
Accordingly, at the founding of his enterprise, our Imperial Ancestor thought deeply about safeguarding its foundations. He chose an auspicious day to invest his sons as princes. The chief minister presented the patents of investiture, and the Minister of Rites presented the edicts. The enfeoffments were completed in succession, producing twenty-four princes who served as bulwarks throughout the realm. He then personally composed the Ancestral Instructions (Zuxun) and bestowed them upon the princes. Only after six years and seven transcriptions of the draft was it completed. His planning to bequeath security and support to his descendants was profoundly far-reaching. Although what is preserved in golden coffers and stone chambers cannot be inspected, its articles have already been made known to officials and the people, and the accounts of them by scholars and officials are also detailed. Among them are provisions concerning ceremonial observances, adherence to laws, gradations in the system of offices, rules for military guards, and construction and repair…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
式供用之度宏綱大體粲然具列條貫品
式纖悉不遺維持保愛之意無所不至而
節制防範之道亦未嘗不行乎其間恩法
並施仁義兼得真足以傳之萬世而無弊
矣百六十年
聖子
神孫守爲家法
朝廷隆敦敘之恩
諸藩膺忠謹之福自三代以還未有若是之
===
盛也執事乃以爲猶有所未安者殆弗然
乎藉令有之而愚以爲
皇祖之訓典具在
聖孝之繼述方隆舉而行之亦甚易爾夫祿賜
不贍誠有可慮者愚以爲莫若訓之以儉
必也示撙節之方以去其靡習且於歲時
之給無所稽滯而屬之疎者則間施不時
之恩如古所謂以脤膰親兄弟之國者可
也或者患其不繼則曰是何不繼也
punctuated:
式、供用之度，宏綱大體，粲然具列；條貫品式，纖悉不遺。維持保愛之意，無所不至，而節制防範之道，亦未嘗不行乎其間。恩法並施，仁義兼得，真足以傳之萬世而無弊矣。百六十年，聖子神孫守爲家法，朝廷隆敦敘之恩，諸藩膺忠謹之福，自三代以還，未有若是之盛也。執事乃以爲猶有所未安者，殆弗然乎？藉令有之，而愚以爲皇祖之訓典具在，聖孝之繼述方隆，舉而行之，亦甚易爾。
夫祿賜不贍，誠有可慮者。愚以爲莫若訓之以儉，必也示撙節之方，以去其靡習，且於歲時之給，無所稽滯；而屬之疎者，則間施不時之恩，如古所謂以脤膰親兄弟之國者，可也。或者患其不繼，則曰：「是何不繼也？」
translation_en:
…standards for construction and limits on supplies and expenditure: the broad principles and essential framework are all clearly set out, while the detailed regulations and prescribed forms omit nothing, however minute. The intent to sustain, protect, and cherish is expressed in every possible way, yet measures of restraint and precaution also operate throughout. Favor and law are applied together, and both benevolence and righteousness are achieved. Truly, these provisions could be handed down for ten thousand generations without ill effect. For a hundred and sixty years, sagely sons and divine grandsons have observed them as the rules of the imperial house. The court has bestowed abundant favor in strengthening the ordered bonds of kinship, and the princely houses have enjoyed the blessings of loyalty and circumspection. Since the Three Dynasties, there has never been such flourishing. Yet you, sir, consider that there are still grounds for unease. Surely this is not so? Even supposing there are, in my humble view the Imperial Progenitor’s authoritative instructions remain fully available, and our sagely sovereign’s filial continuation of his predecessor’s work is now flourishing. Taking up those instructions and putting them into practice would be very easy indeed.
As for insufficient stipends and grants, this is indeed a matter deserving concern. In my humble view, nothing would be better than instructing the princes in frugality. They must be shown ways of economizing so as to eliminate their extravagant habits, and their regular annual and seasonal allowances must suffer no delay. Those more distantly related should occasionally receive extraordinary favors, following the ancient practice of using raw and cooked sacrificial meats to maintain close relations with the states of brother rulers. This would be appropriate. Should anyone worry that such provision could not be sustained, I would reply: “Why could it not be sustained?”

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
國家之冗費多矣盍推其餘以厚同姓乎若
然庶可使無戚戚具爾之心如曹植所議
矣檢制稍踰亦不能無者愚以為莫若示
之以禮必也重輔翼之任以謹其法守且
使誘惑之徒無由親昵而年之幼者則別
為訓迪之法如古所謂庶子之正於公族
者可也或者病其難行則曰是何難行也
宗室之賢能多矣盍擇其人以為之倡乎若
然庶可使有卓爾不羣之行如班固所稱
===
矣有文武才能依常調選用此
祖訓所以待
天族者不聞幷廢其姻戚也不然當時淑媛
之選大抵出於勳閥至有一家數人者獨
不慮其有他乎逆未形之患而棄有用之
才似非所以勸親親也導王以義者必以
禮相待此
祖訓所以處藩僚者不聞禁絕其遷轉也不然
當時侍從之臣大抵起於
punctuated:
國家之冗費多矣，盍推其餘以厚同姓乎？若然，庶可使無戚戚具爾之心，如曹植所議矣。檢制稍踰，亦不能無者。愚以為莫若示之以禮，必也重輔翼之任，以謹其法守，且使誘惑之徒無由親昵；而年之幼者，則別為訓迪之法，如古所謂庶子之正於公族者可也。或者病其難行，則曰：是何難行也？宗室之賢能多矣，盍擇其人以為之倡乎？若然，庶可使有卓爾不羣之行，如班固所稱矣。
有文武才能，依常調選用，此祖訓所以待天族者，不聞幷廢其姻戚也。不然，當時淑媛之選，大抵出於勳閥，至有一家數人者，獨不慮其有他乎？逆未形之患，而棄有用之才，似非所以勸親親也。導王以義者，必以禮相待，此祖訓所以處藩僚者，不聞禁絕其遷轉也。不然，當時侍從之臣，大抵起於
translation_en:
…The state has many superfluous expenditures. Why not redirect the surplus to provide generously for those of the imperial surname? If so, perhaps they could be spared the anxious feelings concerning kinship discussed by Cao Zhi. Some slight breaches of restraint and regulation are also inevitable. In my humble view, nothing would be better than guiding them through ritual propriety. Above all, weight must be given to the responsibility of those who assist and guide them, so that established rules are scrupulously observed; and those who would lead them astray must have no opportunity to become their intimates. For the young, separate methods of instruction should be devised, following the ancient example of the shuzi officials who set the ducal clan in order. Some may object that this would be difficult to carry out. I reply: what is difficult about it? There are many worthy and capable members of the imperial clan. Why not choose suitable men from among them to take the lead? If so, perhaps they could develop the outstanding conduct praised by Ban Gu.
Those possessing civil or military ability are to be selected for service through the regular procedures: this is how the Ancestral Injunctions provide for the imperial clan. I have not heard that its relatives by marriage were also to be excluded from service. Otherwise, since the women selected as imperial consorts at that time generally came from families distinguished by meritorious service, sometimes with several from a single family, was there no concern that something untoward might arise? To anticipate troubles that have not yet taken shape and discard useful talent hardly seems a way to encourage affection for one’s kin. Those who guide a prince in righteousness must be treated with ritual propriety: this is how the Ancestral Injunctions provide for officials serving in princely establishments. I have not heard that their promotion and transfer were prohibited. Otherwise, the officials attending upon the emperor at that time generally rose from …

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
藩府至有位登三事者豈可謂其無人乎居
輔導之任而同廢錮之流似非所以厚本
支也若是者在
祖訓無之而
本朝禮制諸書則草莽之臣未能徧考是雖
不敢斷然以為無所據而推
皇祖垂訓之意則竊有知其不然者意者一時
有所懲創而其後遂因襲之乎
聖天子方率
===
祖攸行以親九族有能建白及此下
廷臣集議或有以通融之者一以廣因心之
孝一以開進賢之途顧不為盛舉哉雖然
事關
宗室人所難言惟在上者以至公為心主議
者以體國為重念舊章之當復而不惟近
事之拘然後可望其必行耳大抵親親之
道雖貴於恩與法之並行然與其使法勝
恩也寧使恩勝法故曰仁可過也義不可
punctuated:
藩府，至有位登三事者，豈可謂其無人乎？居輔導之任，而同廢錮之流，似非所以厚本支也。若是者，在祖訓無之，而本朝禮制諸書，則草莽之臣未能徧考。是雖不敢斷然以為無所據，而推皇祖垂訓之意，則竊有知其不然者。意者一時有所懲創，而其後遂因襲之乎？
聖天子方率祖攸行，以親九族。有能建白及此，下廷臣集議，或有以通融之者，一以廣因心之孝，一以開進賢之途，顧不為盛舉哉？雖然，事關宗室，人所難言。惟在上者以至公為心，主議者以體國為重，念舊章之當復，而不惟近事之拘，然後可望其必行耳。大抵親親之道，雖貴於恩與法之並行，然與其使法勝恩也，寧使恩勝法。故曰：「仁可過也，義不可
translation_en:
…princely establishments, some even rising to the rank of the Three Dukes. How can one say that these establishments lacked capable men? To hold responsibility for assisting and guiding a prince, yet be treated like those dismissed and permanently barred from office, hardly seems a way to strengthen the imperial lineage, root and branches alike. Such provisions do not appear in the Ancestral Injunctions. As for this dynasty’s various books of ritual regulations, however, your servant, a man outside official service, has been unable to examine them all. Although I dare not categorically assert that these practices lack any basis, when I consider the imperial ancestor’s intention in bequeathing his instructions, I venture to see grounds for believing that he intended otherwise. Perhaps some incident once prompted restrictive measures, which later generations simply continued to follow?
The sage Son of Heaven is now following the path of his ancestor to foster affection among the nine degrees of kinship.
