If someone could submit a proposal on this matter and have it referred to the court officials for collective deliberation, a means of accommodating these restrictions might be found. This would both extend his innate filial devotion and open a path for advancing worthy men. Would it not be a splendid undertaking? Nevertheless, this matter concerns the imperial clan, and people find it difficult to speak about. Only if those above take complete impartiality to heart, and those directing deliberations give priority to the interests of the state—recognizing that the old regulations should be restored rather than remaining bound solely by recent precedents—can we hope that it will assuredly be put into effect. In general, although the proper treatment of kin requires that benevolence and law operate together, it is better to let benevolence prevail over law than to let law prevail over benevolence. Thus it is said: “Benevolence may be carried to excess, but righteousness must not…”

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
過也愚也願以斯言爲
今日法
祖睦親之助
第二問
姜良翰
同考試官教諭徐批士習之係於教化固也
子言養之者有本而道之者有幾誠探本之論
同考試官教諭鄭批才氣渾厚立論不迂必
佳士也
===
同考試官學正孫批議論敷暢典實而末以
昭德照臨于上爲言其知風化之機者矣嗟乎志
定所謂見善明用心剛者子非其人乎
考試官署郎中華批國家以養士爲先而士
以不自失爲貴此策得之
考試官給事中陸批議論正大而文體莊重
可以觀所養矣
甚矣士習之有與於世道也貴乎充所養
以端其守而審所尚以道其趨夫義者士
punctuated:
過也。愚也願以斯言爲今日法祖睦親之助。

第二問
姜良翰

同考試官教諭徐批：士習之係於教化，固也。子言養之者有本，而道之者有幾，誠探本之論。

同考試官教諭鄭批：才氣渾厚，立論不迂，必佳士也。

同考試官學正孫批：議論敷暢典實，而末以昭德照臨于上爲言，其知風化之機者矣。嗟乎！志定，所謂見善明、用心剛者，子非其人乎？

考試官署郎中華批：國家以養士爲先，而士以不自失爲貴，此策得之。

考試官給事中陸批：議論正大，而文體莊重，可以觀所養矣。

甚矣，士習之有與於世道也！貴乎充所養以端其守，而審所尚以道其趨。夫義者，士
translation_en:
…be carried too far. In my humble judgment, I hope these words may help the present government emulate the ancestors and foster harmony among imperial kinsmen.

Second Policy Question
Jiang Lianghan

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: That the habits of scholars depend upon moral instruction is certainly true. You say that nurturing them has a foundation, and guiding them has its crucial points. This is indeed an argument that probes the root.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: His talent and spirit are substantial and vigorous, and his argument is not impractical. He must be an excellent scholar.

Comment by Associate Examiner Sun, Instructor: The argument unfolds fluently and is grounded in the classics and solid learning. He concludes by speaking of manifesting virtue and shining upon those below from above: he understands the key to moral transformation. Ah, with resolve settled [?], are you not one of those described as “clear in discerning goodness and firm in purpose”?

Comment by Examiner Hua, Acting Director: The state gives priority to nurturing scholars, while scholars prize preserving their own integrity. This policy essay grasps that principle.

Comment by Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary: The argument is upright and broad in scope, and the style dignified. From this one can discern his cultivation.

Profound indeed is the influence of scholars’ habits upon the moral condition of the age! What matters is to bring their cultivation to fullness so as to make their adherence upright, and to scrutinize what is honored so as to guide their aspirations. Now righteousness is what scholars …

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之守也表位以旌義明王之所尚也孔子
曰不患無位患所以立下焉者夫亦守吾
義而已矣又曰舉善而教不能則勸上焉
者夫亦提衡旌別而已矣蓋朝廷有教化
然後士人有廉恥士人有廉恥然後天下
有風俗事固有始而治必有機也嘗聞治
世所貴乎位者三一曰貴道二曰貴禮三
曰貴志貴道者師而不臣就而不召也貴
禮者三揖而進一辭而退也貴志者不事
===
王侯高尚其事也所順乎位者三一曰道
順二曰職順三曰心順道順者樂乎其義
也職順者循乎其資也心順者安乎其分
也後世所貴乎位者一而所輕乎位者五
一曰貴貴貴貴者以貴高人也以貴相高
則競生競生則逆逆則何貴之有是故高
下失序則位輕班級不固則位輕遷轉煩
瀆則位輕黜陟不明則位輕責任弗久則
位輕夫位也者天位也天下之所寶也輕
punctuated: 之守也。表位以旌義，明王之所尚也。孔子曰：「不患無位，患所以立。」下焉者，夫亦守吾義而已矣。又曰：「舉善而教不能，則勸。」上焉者，夫亦提衡旌別而已矣。蓋朝廷有教化，然後士人有廉恥；士人有廉恥，然後天下有風俗。事固有始，而治必有機也。嘗聞治世所貴乎位者三：一曰貴道，二曰貴禮，三曰貴志。貴道者，師而不臣，就而不召也。貴禮者，三揖而進，一辭而退也。貴志者，不事王侯，高尚其事也。所順乎位者三：一曰道順，二曰職順，三曰心順。道順者，樂乎其義也；職順者，循乎其資也；心順者，安乎其分也。後世所貴乎位者一，而所輕乎位者五。一曰貴貴。貴貴者，以貴高人也。以貴相高，則競生；競生則逆，逆則何貴之有？是故高下失序則位輕，班級不固則位輕，遷轉煩瀆則位輕，黜陟不明則位輕，責任弗久則位輕。夫位也者，天位也，天下之所寶也。輕…
translation_en:
…what a scholar holds fast to. To confer distinction through office in order to honor righteousness is what an enlightened king esteems. Confucius said: “Do not worry about having no position; worry about what qualifies you to occupy one.” Those below need only hold fast to their righteousness. He also said: “Promote the good and teach those who lack ability, and they will be encouraged.” Those above need only weigh men fairly and distinguish their worth. Only when the court provides moral instruction do scholars possess integrity and a sense of shame; only when scholars possess integrity and a sense of shame do proper customs prevail throughout the realm. Affairs indeed have their beginnings, and good government necessarily has its pivotal point.

I have heard that in a well-governed age, three things are esteemed in relation to office: first, the Way; second, ritual propriety; third, resolve. Esteeming the Way means treating a worthy man as a teacher rather than a subject, and going to him rather than summoning him. Esteeming ritual propriety means advancing after three bows and withdrawing after a single refusal. Esteeming resolve means refusing to serve kings and lords and holding one’s own pursuits in high esteem.

There are three forms of accord in relation to office: first, accord with the Way; second, accord in one’s duties; third, accord in one’s heart. Accord with the Way means delighting in what is right; accord in one’s duties means proceeding in keeping with one’s qualifications; accord in one’s heart means resting content with one’s allotted station.

In later ages, there is one thing esteemed in relation to office, but five things that diminish its standing. The one is esteem for high rank itself. To esteem high rank itself is to use it to place oneself above others. When people use rank to vie for superiority, contention arises; contention produces disorder, and amid disorder, what esteem can remain? Thus, when higher and lower lose their proper order, office is devalued; when ranks and grades are unstable, office is devalued; when transfers and promotions are excessive and troublesome, office is devalued; when dismissals and advancements are not judicious, office is devalued; and when men are not entrusted with responsibilities for long, office is devalued. Office is a station conferred by Heaven, something treasured by all under Heaven. If it is devalued…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
則喪吾寶矣孰謂聖人握天之寶以貴天
下而可容競進於其間哉要之治世之所
由貴者以養而後世之所由輕者以競何
謂養有土者設爵祿車服禮樂于朝以待
天下之賢賢者脩仁義忠信孝悌於家以
需一時之用下能副其待則待者愈厚上
知厚乎下則下愈不自輕故能履三順以
享三貴也是之謂充所養以端其守後世
反是爵人者必俟于求無爵者不自進則
===
無由以得嗚呼求之則予不自進則不得
此士之所以必於求進而競逆所由生也
雖然良心不異乎古今而豪傑不移於習
染未嘗厚士不可謂下無其人未嘗自重
不可謂上無其人不觀東京節義之所由
植乎一嚴光不仕而光武高之耳不觀布
衣有貴於宰相之榮乎一李泌尚志而肅
宗成之耳司馬池固辭諫官仁宗則命為
待制矣韓維不就廷試文彥博則薦乞甄
punctuated:
則喪吾寶矣。孰謂聖人握天之寶以貴天下，而可容競進於其間哉？要之，治世之所由貴者以養，而後世之所由輕者以競。何謂養？有土者設爵祿車服禮樂于朝，以待天下之賢；賢者脩仁義忠信孝悌於家，以需一時之用。下能副其待，則待者愈厚；上知厚乎下，則下愈不自輕，故能履三順以享三貴也。是之謂充所養以端其守。後世反是，爵人者必俟于求，無爵者不自進則無由以得。嗚呼！求之則予，不自進則不得，此士之所以必於求進，而競逆所由生也。
雖然，良心不異乎古今，而豪傑不移於習染。未嘗厚士，不可謂下無其人；未嘗自重，不可謂上無其人。不觀東京節義之所由植乎？一嚴光不仕，而光武高之耳。不觀布衣有貴於宰相之榮乎？一李泌尚志，而肅宗成之耳。司馬池固辭諫官，仁宗則命為待制矣；韓維不就廷試，文彥博則薦乞甄
translation_en:
…then we lose our treasure. Who could say that the sage holds Heaven’s treasure to confer honor upon all under Heaven, yet may permit competitive advancement to intrude? In essence, in a well-governed age, office is esteemed because men are nurtured; in later ages, it is held lightly because men compete for it. What is meant by nurturing? Those who rule a territory establish ranks, emoluments, carriages, robes, rites, and music at court in readiness for the worthy men of the realm. Worthy men cultivate benevolence, righteousness, loyalty, trustworthiness, filial piety, and fraternal respect at home, awaiting a time when their service is needed. When those below can fulfill the expectations of those awaiting them, they receive still more generous treatment. When those above know to treat those below generously, those below become still less inclined to demean themselves. Thus they can observe the three forms of accord and enjoy the three forms of honor. This is called fully developing what one cultivates so as to keep one’s commitments upright. Later ages reverse this: those who confer rank invariably wait for it to be solicited, while those without rank have no means of obtaining it unless they put themselves forward. Alas! If rank is granted upon request, and cannot be obtained without putting oneself forward, this necessarily drives scholars to seek advancement and gives rise to competition and disorder.
Nevertheless, the innate moral sense does not differ between antiquity and the present, and men of exceptional character are not swayed by prevailing habits. If one has never treated scholars generously, one cannot say that there are no worthy men below; if one has never respected oneself, one cannot say that there are no worthy men above. Have you not considered how integrity and righteousness took root in the Eastern Han? It was simply that Yan Guang declined to serve, and Emperor Guangwu esteemed him for it. Have you not considered how a commoner could possess a dignity surpassing the glory of a chief minister? It was simply that Li Mi held his aspirations high, and Emperor Suzong enabled him to fulfill them. When Sima Chi firmly declined appointment as a remonstrance official, Emperor Renzong appointed him Academician-in-waiting. When Han Wei did not present himself for the Palace Examination, Wen Yanbo recommended him and requested that he be selected…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
擢矣唐介復爲御史非以其私書不至京
師乎劉安世得充舘職非以其書問不及
政府乎凡若此者皆表揚高潔三代以後
所僅見也是之謂審所尚以道其趨雖然
世之所尚隨時而異要在審其宜耳故庾
峻有曰退讓不可以刑罰使莫若聽朝士
時時從志山林往往間出游酢則曰欲人
人自好而相高以名節莫若朝廷之上倡
清議於天下李綱又曰欲息奔競莫若崇
===
靜退以率之靜退之士内有養見善明用
心剛者也以類立朝必有可觀之三說者
言雖不同其欲崇好尚以道之則一也劉
光祖見士無廉靜言於朝曰其患在於不
封殖人材朝堂初無長養幸妙求人物朝
野共屬者參錯立朝國勢自壯是說也深
有得乎養士之意然亦有其本也我
國家之造士歛才也經術以陶之學校以羣
之科第以羅之資格以劑之殿最以澄之
punctuated:
擢矣。唐介復爲御史，非以其私書不至京師乎？劉安世得充舘職，非以其書問不及政府乎？凡若此者，皆表揚高潔，三代以後所僅見也。是之謂審所尚以道其趨。雖然，世之所尚隨時而異，要在審其宜耳。故庾峻有曰：「退讓不可以刑罰使，莫若聽朝士時時從志山林，往往間出。」游酢則曰：「欲人人自好而相高以名節，莫若朝廷之上倡清議於天下。」李綱又曰：「欲息奔競，莫若崇靜退以率之。靜退之士，内有養、見善明、用心剛者也。以類立朝，必有可觀之。」三說者，言雖不同，其欲崇好尚以道之則一也。劉光祖見士無廉靜，言於朝曰：「其患在於不封殖人材。朝堂初無長養，幸妙求人物，朝野共屬者參錯立朝，國勢自壯。」是說也，深有得乎養士之意，然亦有其本也。
我國家之造士歛才也，經術以陶之，學校以羣之，科第以羅之，資格以劑之，殿最以澄之。
translation_en:
…and promoted. Was Tang Jie restored as Investigating Censor not because his private letters never reached the capital? Was Liu Anshi appointed to an academy post not because his letters and inquiries never reached the chief councillors? All such cases honored lofty integrity—something rarely seen since the Three Dynasties. This is what is meant by carefully determining what to esteem in order to guide scholars’ aspirations. Nevertheless, what the world esteems changes with the times; the essential thing is to judge what is appropriate.
Thus Yu Jun said: “Modesty and deference cannot be imposed through punishments. Nothing is better than allowing court officials from time to time to follow their inclination to retire among the mountains and forests, occasionally emerging to serve.” You Zuo said: “If one wishes everyone to cherish his own integrity and vie with others in reputation and principle, nothing is better than for the imperial court to champion upright public judgment throughout the realm.” Li Gang also said: “To end competitive scrambling for advancement, nothing is better than honoring quiet withdrawal as an example. Men who quietly withdraw possess inner cultivation, discern goodness clearly, and remain firm in their resolve. If men of this kind serve together at court, there will surely be something worthy of admiration.” Although these three statements differ in wording, they share the same desire to elevate worthy aspirations and thereby guide scholars.
Seeing that scholars lacked integrity and restraint, Liu Guangzu said at court: “The trouble lies in the failure to foster talent. The court has provided no nurturing from the outset. If it might carefully seek out worthy men [?], and those to whom court and country alike look with hope were interspersed in its ranks, the strength of the state would naturally increase.” This statement grasps profoundly the intention behind nurturing scholars. Yet this, too, has its foundation.
In forming scholars and gathering talent, our dynasty molds them through classical learning, brings them together in schools, draws them in through examination degrees, regulates their advancement through eligibility and seniority, and sifts them through assessments of inferior and superior performance…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
禮義廉恥長之育之德行道藝優之游之
所以充乎其養者純以備也右循良重正
直表內脩奬恬退拔幽滯所以道其所尚
者亷以潔也故自立國以來人才獨盛習
尚可觀而非漢唐宋所能及者正在此耳
執事乃慮士風尚未醇而冒進者或有欲
挽之以追隆古誠不可以他求也竊謂道
德之心勝則功名之念薄恬退之風盛則
急躁之圖沮衆正之門開則驟遷之途塞
===
誠能朝野名才間出其人凛凛自好名節
相高則靜退者無淹抑而奔競者自無所
容矣靜退者無淹抑則所謂妙求碩望崇
立朝端者在是學術政理有宗廟堂滋長
養之風人材自是封植而奔競者自知所
化矣然於此有本焉必有至公至明之心
照臨于上而所以養之道之者一務乎實
而不事乎虛文率之以漸持之以久則立
敎也有本運化也有機重輕之柄反乎上
punctuated:
禮義廉恥長之育之，德行道藝優之游之，所以充乎其養者純以備也。右循良，重正直，表內脩，奬恬退，拔幽滯，所以道其所尚者亷以潔也。故自立國以來，人才獨盛，習尚可觀，而非漢唐宋所能及者，正在此耳。執事乃慮士風尚未醇，而冒進者或有，欲挽之以追隆古，誠不可以他求也。竊謂道德之心勝，則功名之念薄；恬退之風盛，則急躁之圖沮；衆正之門開，則驟遷之途塞。
誠能朝野名才間出，其人凛凛自好，名節相高，則靜退者無淹抑，而奔競者自無所容矣。靜退者無淹抑，則所謂妙求碩望、崇立朝端者在是。學術政理有宗，廟堂滋長養之風，人材自是封植，而奔競者自知所化矣。然於此有本焉：必有至公至明之心照臨于上，而所以養之道之者，一務乎實，而不事乎虛文。率之以漸，持之以久，則立敎也有本，運化也有機，重輕之柄反乎上。
translation_en:
…It nurtures and raises them through ritual propriety, righteousness, integrity, and a sense of shame, and allows them to develop at ease in virtuous conduct, the Way, and the arts. The means by which it provides for their cultivation are thus pure and comprehensive. It favors conscientious and upright officials, esteems integrity, honors inward cultivation, rewards quiet restraint, and advances those left in obscurity. The means by which it guides their aspirations are thus incorrupt and unsullied. This is precisely why, since the founding of our dynasty, men of talent have flourished as never before and prevailing habits have been admirable, beyond anything the Han, Tang, or Song could achieve. You, honored examiners, are nevertheless concerned that the ethos of scholars is not yet pure and that some still seek advancement presumptuously. If you wish to reverse this tendency and emulate high antiquity, truly the remedy must be sought here alone. I humbly submit that when devotion to the Way and virtue prevails, thoughts of achievement and fame diminish; when quiet restraint flourishes, schemes for impatient advancement are checked; and when the gate is opened to upright men, the path to precipitous promotion is closed.
If men of recognized talent could indeed emerge from time to time both at court and outside it, maintaining their integrity with stern resolve and vying with one another in honorable reputation and moral principle, then the quietly retiring would no longer languish neglected, while those who scramble for advancement would naturally find no place. Once the quietly retiring are no longer held back, what is meant by carefully seeking men of great standing and placing them in high positions at court would be realized. Learning and government would have exemplary standards to follow, and the court would foster a spirit of nurturing talent. Talented men would thereby be cultivated, while those who scramble for advancement would themselves understand how to reform. Yet this, too, has a foundation: a mind of utmost impartiality and discernment must preside above, and all means of nurturing and guiding men must attend exclusively to substance, without pursuing empty forms. Lead them gradually and persevere over time: then the establishment of moral instruction will have a foundation, the work of transformation will have its operative means, and the power to determine what is esteemed or slighted will return to those above…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
三順之道成于下上下交相責而先王治
隆俗美之盛可立而俟矣
第三問
許來學
同考試官學正凌批聖賢之所以爲學博約
二字盡之矣此策以求諸內爲說學有根據而不
知反約一節最切今時學者之弊且文字不事馳
騁而步驟自與人殊是用錄之
考試官署郎中華批此策正欲觀學者之趨
===
向與其所得之淺深子能於心學之要敷析詳明
確有定識將來造就予日望之
考試官給事中陸批朱子之道師範當世非
末學可得妄議者然學如子靜要有所自得吾豈
敢遽以爲非哉他日願從子而極論之
學之道無他求諸內而已矣求諸內無他
要其所歸而已矣天下之理必先求諸心
知所往而後力行以要其至未有不知而
能行者也其行之未至與幾至而畫者皆
punctuated:
三順之道成于下，上下交相責，而先王治隆俗美之盛可立而俟矣。

第三問
許來學

同考試官學正凌批：聖賢之所以爲學，博約二字盡之矣。此策以求諸內爲說，學有根據，而不知反約一節，最切今時學者之弊。且文字不事馳騁，而步驟自與人殊，是用錄之。

考試官署郎中華批：此策正欲觀學者之趨向與其所得之淺深。子能於心學之要敷析詳明，確有定識，將來造就，予日望之。

考試官給事中陸批：朱子之道，師範當世，非末學可得妄議者。然學如子靜，要有所自得，吾豈敢遽以爲非哉？他日願從子而極論之。

學之道無他，求諸內而已矣。求諸內無他，要其所歸而已矣。天下之理，必先求諸心，知所往而後力行以要其至，未有不知而能行者也。其行之未至與幾至而畫者，皆
translation_en:
…the way of the three forms of compliance [?] is realized below. When those above and below hold one another accountable, the flourishing government and admirable customs of the former kings can soon be expected.

Third Question
Xu Laixue 許來學

Comment by Associate Examiner Ling 凌, School Instructor: The learning of the sages and worthies is fully encompassed by two words: breadth and concentration. This policy essay takes seeking within oneself as its thesis. Its learning has a foundation, and the passage on failing to return to concentration addresses most pointedly the shortcomings of scholars today. Moreover, its prose does not indulge in rhetorical display, yet its progression naturally distinguishes it from others. For these reasons it has been selected for inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Hua 華, Acting Bureau Director: This policy question was intended precisely to reveal the direction of scholars’ learning and the depth of their attainments. You have expounded and analyzed the essentials of the learning of the mind in detail and with clarity, demonstrating firmly grounded understanding. I look forward daily to your future accomplishments.

Comment by Examiner Lu 陸, Supervising Secretary: Master Zhu’s Way serves as a model for the present age; it is not something that those of limited learning may presumptuously criticize. Yet if one studies as Zijing did, seeking to attain understanding for oneself, how could I dare hastily to pronounce it wrong? On another day I would gladly join you in discussing this to the fullest.

The way of learning is nothing other than seeking within oneself. Seeking within oneself is nothing other than grasping its ultimate end. The principles of all things under Heaven must first be sought in the mind. Only after knowing where to go can one exert oneself in practice to reach that destination. There has never been anyone who could act without knowing. Those whose practice falls short, and those who nearly arrive but stop short, all…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
知之未至也夫道若大路然吾心譬諸日
之明而光之照也日以明爲體以光爲用
吾心以虛靈爲體神明爲用也亦弗蔽之
而已矣弗蔽則虛虛則明矣吾心管攝乎
衆理也虛明則純靜純靜則動以天矣聖
人之學端不外此故孔門獨顏子以好學
稱而其學所從入亦曰博文約禮而已夫
文與禮者非他也性分之內天理燦然隨
處發見各有條理昭而析之謂之文執而
===
安之謂之禮顯諸文藏諸禮而天下之學
盡之矣顏子則明睿所照觸處洞然博約
之功無所不至而皆用於人所不見之地
有不可得而名言者其於禮也非禮也非
禮之禮也悉精擇而禁止之過不再萌怒
隨物釋以視以聽以言以動無適而非天
理之周流祗見其服膺勿失也不遠復也
不改其樂也而言語政事文章不與焉自
得之學莫有深于顏子者子思之學問思
punctuated: 知之未至也。夫道若大路然，吾心譬諸日之明而光之照也。日以明爲體，以光爲用；吾心以虛靈爲體，神明爲用也，亦弗蔽之而已矣。弗蔽則虛，虛則明矣。吾心管攝乎衆理也，虛明則純靜，純靜則動以天矣。聖人之學端不外此。故孔門獨顏子以好學稱，而其學所從入，亦曰博文約禮而已。夫文與禮者非他也，性分之內，天理燦然，隨處發見，各有條理。昭而析之謂之文，執而安之謂之禮。顯諸文，藏諸禮，而天下之學盡之矣。顏子則明睿所照，觸處洞然，博約之功無所不至，而皆用於人所不見之地，有不可得而名言者。其於禮也，非禮也，非禮之禮也，悉精擇而禁止之。過不再萌，怒隨物釋，以視，以聽，以言，以動，無適而非天理之周流。祗見其服膺勿失也，不遠復也，不改其樂也，而言語、政事、文章不與焉。自得之學，莫有深于顏子者。子思之學問思
translation_en:
…their understanding has not yet reached its fullest extent. The Way is like a broad road, and our mind is comparable to the sun’s brightness and the illumination of its rays. The sun has brightness as its substance and radiance as its function; our mind has empty, numinous awareness as its substance and spiritual intelligence as its function. We need only keep it unobscured. Unobscured, it is empty; empty, it is clear. Our mind governs and encompasses the manifold principles. Empty and clear, it becomes wholly still; wholly still, it acts in accordance with Heaven. The learning of the sages lies entirely within this.

Thus, among Confucius’s disciples, Yan Zi alone was praised as devoted to learning. The means by which he entered into learning were simply to broaden his knowledge through cultural learning and to restrain himself through ritual propriety. Cultural learning and ritual propriety are nothing extraneous: within our allotted nature, Heaven’s principle shines forth, manifesting everywhere, each manifestation having its own orderly pattern. To illuminate and distinguish these patterns is called cultural learning; to hold to them and rest securely in them is called ritual propriety. Manifest in cultural learning and stored within ritual propriety, they encompass all the learning under Heaven.

Wherever Yan Zi’s clear intelligence shone, everything he encountered became thoroughly transparent. His efforts to broaden his learning and restrain himself reached everywhere, yet all were applied where others could not see, with something that could not be named or expressed in words. As for ritual propriety, what contravened ritual propriety, and ritual that was not truly ritual [?], he discriminated minutely and prohibited and checked it. His faults did not arise a second time, and his anger dissolved as the occasion passed. In looking, listening, speaking, and acting, there was nowhere that Heaven’s principle did not flow all around. We see only that he held it close to his heart without losing it, returned before straying far, and never altered his joy. Eloquence, government affairs, and literary composition had no part in this. In learning attained for oneself, none went deeper than Yan Zi. Zisi’s study, inquiry, and reflection…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
辨而要之於篤行孟子之博學詳說而要
之於反約皆是物也自秦而下聖學失傳
漢人索于訓詁唐人牽于詞章枝葉茂而
本根離矣有宋周程三子者出始知聖道
有在而顏氏為真傳也濂溪清明高遠超
然獨得明道思索妙造以靜為學伊川潛
神靜閱教人以敬而千載不傳之緒於是
乎續傳之龜山則天資出人造養深遠德
器蚤成吾道有託矣再傳之豫章則探索
===
本原洞見道體潛心力行任重詣極矣又
傳之延平則默坐澄心體認天理驗一中
於未發會覺處於靜極矣一脉相承深造
自得踐履多於發用涵養多於講說孔顏
之道不自此而一著乎然當時學者論格
致每遺精微論中庸或淫於老佛至謂大
本既立則不必讀書可以逕造聖域羨曹
周程之至而不知其所從入也於是朱子
出焉啓之以致知本之以居敬而反躬以
punctuated: 辨，而要之於篤行；孟子之博學詳說，而要之於反約，皆是物也。自秦而下，聖學失傳，漢人索于訓詁，唐人牽于詞章，枝葉茂而本根離矣。有宋周程三子者出，始知聖道有在，而顏氏為真傳也。濂溪清明高遠，超然獨得；明道思索妙造，以靜為學；伊川潛神靜閱，教人以敬，而千載不傳之緒於是乎續。傳之龜山，則天資出人，造養深遠，德器蚤成，吾道有託矣。再傳之豫章，則探索本原，洞見道體，潛心力行，任重詣極矣。又傳之延平，則默坐澄心，體認天理，驗一中於未發，會覺處於靜極矣。一脉相承，深造自得，踐履多於發用，涵養多於講說，孔顏之道不自此而一著乎？然當時學者論格致，每遺精微；論中庸，或淫於老佛，至謂大本既立，則不必讀書，可以逕造聖域。羨曹周程之至，而不知其所從入也。於是朱子出焉，啓之以致知，本之以居敬，而反躬以
translation_en:
…discrimination, bringing it all to fulfillment in earnest practice; Mengzi’s broad learning and detailed exposition, brought back to essential simplicity: these were all this same thing. From the Qin onward, the learning of the sages ceased to be transmitted. Han scholars sought it in textual glosses, while Tang scholars were drawn into literary composition. Branches and leaves flourished, but they had become detached from their roots.

Only when the three masters Zhou and the two Chengs emerged in the Song did people begin to recognize where the Way of the sages resided and that Yan Hui had truly transmitted it. Lianxi was lucid and pure, lofty and far-reaching, attaining an understanding uniquely his own, beyond the ordinary. Mingdao reached subtle understanding through reflection and inquiry, making stillness the basis of learning. Yichuan concentrated his spirit and contemplated in stillness, teaching others through reverent attentiveness. Thus the thread whose transmission had been broken for a thousand years was resumed.

It was transmitted to Guishan, whose natural endowments surpassed others, whose attainment and cultivation were profound and far-reaching, and whose virtue and capacity matured early: our Way now had someone to whom it could be entrusted. It was transmitted in turn to Yuzhang, who investigated its ultimate source, perceived the substance of the Way with penetrating clarity, and devoted himself to vigorous practice, bearing a weighty responsibility and reaching the highest attainment. It was then transmitted to Yanping, who sat silently to clarify his mind and personally apprehend heavenly principle, verifying the single equilibrium before the feelings had arisen and comprehending the point of awareness in utmost stillness.

This single lineage was handed down in succession. Its masters advanced deeply and attained understanding for themselves, emphasizing personal practice more than outward application, and inward cultivation more than lectures and exposition. Was it not through this that the Way of Kongzi and Yan Hui became manifest in its unity? Yet scholars of that time, when discussing the investigation of things and the extension of knowledge, often neglected the subtlest aspects; when discussing the Doctrine of the Mean, some strayed into the teachings of Laozi and Buddhism. They went so far as to say that once the great foundation was established, reading books was unnecessary, and one could proceed directly into the realm of sagehood. They admired [?] the supreme attainments of Zhou and the Chengs without knowing the path by which they had entered.

Then Master Zhu emerged. He opened the way for them through the extension of knowledge, grounded them in maintaining reverent attentiveness, and had them turn back upon themselves in order to…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
踐其實其為教也必始諸下學而著述獨
盛于前古極吾心之大用折百氏之異同
所謂集大成者是矣夫濂洛獨啓心傳於
詞章口耳盛行之餘而朱子乃救流弊於
馳心空渺之始一則予欲無言之旨一則
刪述垂憲之意也嗚呼朱子之用心若此
其慮後世也遠矣愚獨怪夫今之學者滯
章句以溺其心而無或進于道也豈朱子
之為是教也將徒博而已乎夫亦擴我聰
===
明之實耳今之學者或涉獵章句或綴緝
詞章佔畢而言性命道德之不離于口肆
筆而書習為竒僻甚至不能以句則曰學
云學云而不知身心性情為何物由朱子
觀之其異于俗學也者幾希豈顏子之所
謂博乎無惑乎其不知約也夫學之為道
未有不知要而能博者亦未有不博而能
逕約者故曰耳目之官不思而蔽於物心
之官則思思則得之博必資於耳目而耳
punctuated: 踐其實。其為教也，必始諸下學，而著述獨盛于前古，極吾心之大用，折百氏之異同，所謂集大成者是矣。夫濂洛獨啓心傳於詞章口耳盛行之餘，而朱子乃救流弊於馳心空渺之始，一則「予欲無言」之旨，一則刪述垂憲之意也。嗚呼！朱子之用心若此，其慮後世也遠矣。愚獨怪夫今之學者，滯章句以溺其心，而無或進于道也。豈朱子之為是教也，將徒博而已乎？夫亦擴我聰明之實耳。今之學者，或涉獵章句，或綴緝詞章，佔畢而言，性命道德之不離于口；肆筆而書，習為竒僻，甚至不能以句，則曰「學云學云」，而不知身心性情為何物。由朱子觀之，其異于俗學也者幾希。豈顏子之所謂博乎？無惑乎其不知約也！夫學之為道，未有不知要而能博者，亦未有不博而能逕約者。故曰：「耳目之官不思，而蔽於物；心之官則思，思則得之。」博必資於耳目，而耳
translation_en:
…put its substance into practice. His teaching necessarily began with elementary learning, while his writings surpassed those of earlier ages in their abundance. He fully developed the great operations of our minds and adjudicated the agreements and differences among the various schools. This is what is meant by bringing all achievements together into a great synthesis. The masters of Lian and Luo uniquely opened up the transmission of the mind after literary composition and learning confined to the lips and ears had become prevalent; Master Zhu then remedied the ensuing abuses as minds began to stray into empty vagueness. The former approach embodied the purport of “I wish to be without words”; the latter, the intention of editing and transmitting the classics to leave enduring standards. Ah! Such was Master Zhu’s concern, and so far-reaching was his solicitude for later generations!

I, in my ignorance, find it strange that scholars today become mired in textual explication, submerging their minds in it, without making any progress toward the Way. Could Master Zhu have established this teaching merely for the sake of extensive learning? Its purpose was surely to enlarge the substance of our perceptiveness and understanding. Scholars today either browse through textual explications or piece together literary compositions. They speak by reciting texts, with human nature, destiny, the Way, and virtue constantly on their lips; when they wield their brushes, they habitually strive for the strange and obscure, sometimes failing even to form a sentence. Yet they keep saying “learning, learning,” without knowing what the person and mind, human nature and feelings actually are. Viewed from Master Zhu’s standpoint, their difference from vulgar learning is negligible. Is this what Master Yan meant by breadth of learning? No wonder they do not understand how to bring it to its essentials!

In the pursuit of learning, no one has ever attained breadth without knowing what is essential, nor has anyone proceeded directly to the essentials without breadth of learning. Thus it is said: “The organs of hearing and sight do not think and are obscured by external things; the organ of the mind thinks, and through thought it attains understanding.” Breadth of learning must draw upon the ears and eyes, yet the ears…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
目則役于心心固萬理咸具也其所謂蔽
者有二查滓以渾淆於有生之初邪偽以
汙壞於既長之後不知省察慎獨而溺心
章句譬諸目瞖交蔽坐于寶藏之中不自
知其所有也其必讀書以破愚以格物窮
理使吾心之蔽光明四達萬理呈見而不
可勝用夫然後謂之博耳程子曰聖賢千
言萬語欲人將已放之心約之使反復入
身來朱子亦以居敬窮理互相發為讀書
===
之要夫亦求博于吾心之智則今之學者
之弊亦庶乎其可救矣或者乃曰盍亦以
子靜之學救之乎夫子靜專尊德性而先
立乎其大者自是高明獨得之學有子靜
之資斯可矣惟恐不善學者後致知而先
行事將必至廢書而不讀則識見不充蘊
蓄不大無復經綸大經焉而理學之功用
狹矣夫子靜之學一也善學者則進于高
明不善學者則馳于空渺存乎人之自識
punctuated:
目則役于心，心固萬理咸具也。其所謂蔽者有二：查滓以渾淆於有生之初，邪偽以汙壞於既長之後。不知省察慎獨，而溺心章句，譬諸目瞖交蔽，坐于寶藏之中，不自知其所有也。其必讀書以破愚，以格物窮理，使吾心之蔽光明四達，萬理呈見，而不可勝用，夫然後謂之博耳。程子曰：「聖賢千言萬語，欲人將已放之心約之，使反復入身來。」朱子亦以居敬窮理互相發為讀書之要。夫亦求博于吾心之智，則今之學者之弊，亦庶乎其可救矣。

或者乃曰：「盍亦以子靜之學救之乎？」夫子靜專尊德性，而先立乎其大者，自是高明獨得之學，有子靜之資斯可矣。惟恐不善學者後致知而先行事，將必至廢書而不讀，則識見不充，蘊蓄不大，無復經綸大經焉，而理學之功用狹矣。夫子靜之學一也，善學者則進于高明，不善學者則馳于空渺，存乎人之自識
translation_en:
…the eyes, however, serve the mind, and the mind inherently possesses all principles. There are two kinds of what we call obscuration: dregs that cloud it at the beginning of life, and perversity and falsity that defile it after one has grown. To immerse one's mind in textual passages and phrases without knowing how to examine oneself and remain vigilant when alone is like having one's eyes covered with cataracts: one sits amid a treasury without knowing what one possesses. One must read books to dispel ignorance, investigating things and probing principles, so that the obscuration of one's mind [is removed?] and its light reaches in all directions, with all principles manifest and inexhaustible in their application. Only then may this be called breadth of learning. Master Cheng said: “The thousands upon thousands of words spoken by sages and worthies seek to have people gather in their minds, which have strayed, and bring them back within themselves.” Master Zhu likewise regarded maintaining reverent attentiveness and probing principles, each advancing the other, as the essentials of reading. If we too seek breadth through the knowing capacity of our own minds, then perhaps the failings of today's students can be remedied.

Someone then asks: “Why not remedy them through Zijing's teaching?” Zijing devoted himself to honoring the moral nature and first establishing its greater part. This is certainly a lofty and lucid teaching attained through his own insight; it is practicable for those endowed as Zijing was. My only fear is that those who do not learn well will put extending knowledge after undertaking action, eventually abandoning books altogether. Their understanding will then be insufficient and their accumulated learning scant; they will no longer be able to order the great guiding relationships, and the practical efficacy of the learning of principle will be narrowed. Zijing's teaching is one and the same: those who learn it well advance toward loftiness and lucidity, while those who learn it poorly race toward emptiness and vagueness. It depends on each person's own discernment…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而非所以示人也教人者亦曰讀書窮理
求博于吾心之智而反之約也約之維何
仁人心也顏子自視聽言動以至不違亦
約諸仁耳約而未至于仁仁而或在或亡
不足以言約也其博也以智而其約也以
仁何往而非心學哉愚故曰求諸内而已
矣要其所歸而已矣
第四問
俞介
===
同考試官教諭毛 批 識見高遠憂國憂民之
念溢於言表經世之學也
同考試官教諭吳 批 推原東南之患起於賦
重最爲有見而末三弊之說尤甚警切所謂豪傑
之士非耶
同考試官教諭宋 批 東南之地財賦所仰給
關係匪細是策于致弊之由補弊之法歷歷條答
無遺非平日究心于時務者談不及此讀之令人
起敬
punctuated:
而非所以示人也。教人者亦曰：讀書窮理，求博于吾心之智，而反之約也。約之維何？仁，人心也。顏子自視聽言動，以至不違，亦約諸仁耳。約而未至于仁，仁而或在或亡，不足以言約也。其博也以智，而其約也以仁，何往而非心學哉？愚故曰：求諸内而已矣，要其所歸而已矣。

第四問
俞介

同考試官教諭毛批：識見高遠，憂國憂民之念溢於言表，經世之學也。

同考試官教諭吳批：推原東南之患，起於賦重，最爲有見，而末三弊之說尤甚警切。所謂豪傑之士非耶？

同考試官教諭宋批：東南之地，財賦所仰給，關係匪細。是策于致弊之由、補弊之法，歷歷條答無遺。非平日究心于時務者，談不及此。讀之令人起敬。
translation_en:
…and is not a means of instructing others. Those who teach others likewise say: read books and investigate principles, seek breadth in the understanding of one’s own mind, and return from this to the essential. What is this essential? Benevolence is the human mind. From his seeing, hearing, speaking, and acting to his never departing from benevolence, Master Yan likewise brought everything back to benevolence alone. If this concentration on the essential has not attained benevolence, or if benevolence is present at times and absent at others, it cannot be called concentration on the essential. Breadth is achieved through wisdom, and concentration on the essential through benevolence: where, then, is this not the learning of the mind? Thus I humbly say: seek it within, and that is all; grasp its ultimate destination, and that is all.

Fourth Policy Question
Yu Jie

Comment by Associate Examiner Mao, Instructor: His insight is lofty and far-reaching. Concern for the country and its people overflows his words. This is learning directed toward ordering the world.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: He traces the troubles of the southeast to their source in heavy taxation—a most perceptive judgment. His discussion of the three abuses at the end is especially arresting and pointed. Is he not what is called a man of outstanding ability?

Comment by Associate Examiner Song, Instructor: The southeast supplies the wealth and tax revenues on which the state depends; its importance is no small matter. This policy essay answers point by point, clearly and exhaustively, concerning both the causes of abuses and the methods of remedying them. Someone who had not regularly devoted himself to studying current affairs could not discuss them at this level. Reading it inspires respect.

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官署郎中華批東南利病夫人能言之
未有善處如是者所謂識時務者子其人耶
考試官給事中陸批議論切中時弊而規畫
皆有定見當路者得是說而推行之吳浙之民其
有廖乎
古所謂豪傑之士必其能通於世務者也
執事之意蓋以是望諸生而愚也豈其人
哉雖然天下之事非愚所知而東南之利
病則習聞之矣執事之問及之愚其容默
===
乎夫東南之地自晉宋以來蓋已日趨於
富庶非復往時厥田下下之舊已若今嘉
湖與蘇松諸郡民力勤而物產盛則財賦
因之加多固也然嘗考前代賦額皆莫有
重於今者雖
國初猶不至是也蓋自永樂以後漕運既遠
且凡雜征汎賦一切取給于其中而加耗
日重至于今日極矣洪武開創之初軍國
之用甚廣然猶屢下蠲租之
punctuated:
考試官署郎中華批：東南利病，夫人能言之，未有善處如是者。所謂識時務者，子其人耶？

考試官給事中陸批：議論切中時弊，而規畫皆有定見。當路者得是說而推行之，吳浙之民其有廖乎？

古所謂豪傑之士，必其能通於世務者也。執事之意，蓋以是望諸生，而愚也豈其人哉？雖然，天下之事非愚所知，而東南之利病則習聞之矣。執事之問及之，愚其容默乎？夫東南之地，自晉宋以來，蓋已日趨於富庶，非復往時厥田下下之舊已。若今嘉湖與蘇松諸郡，民力勤而物產盛，則財賦因之加多，固也。然嘗考前代賦額，皆莫有重於今者，雖國初猶不至是也。蓋自永樂以後，漕運既遠，且凡雜征汎賦，一切取給于其中，而加耗日重，至于今日極矣。洪武開創之初，軍國之用甚廣，然猶屢下蠲租之
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Hua, Acting Bureau Director: Anyone can discuss the advantages and ills of the southeast, but none has proposed such effective ways of addressing them. Are you the very person meant by the expression “one who understands the affairs of the times”?

Comment by Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary: The argument precisely addresses the ills of the times, and the proposed measures all rest on firm judgments. If those in authority obtain these proposals and implement them, might the people of Wu and Zhejiang find relief [?]?

Those whom the ancients called outstanding men must have been men thoroughly versed in worldly affairs. Your intention, honored examiner, is surely to hold this expectation of us students; but how could someone as unworthy as I be such a man? Nevertheless, although the affairs of the realm are beyond my knowledge, I have often heard about the advantages and ills of the southeast. Since your question touches upon them, how could I remain silent?

Since the Jin and Song dynasties, the southeast has steadily grown wealthier and more populous. It is no longer as it was in former times, when “its fields were of the lowest grade.” In such prefectures as Jiaxing, Huzhou, Suzhou, and Songjiang today, the people work diligently and produce is abundant, so it is natural that tax revenues should increase accordingly. Yet I have examined the tax quotas of earlier dynasties, and none was heavier than those of today. Even at the beginning of our dynasty, they had not reached this level. Since the Yongle reign, not only has grain tribute had to be transported over great distances, but all miscellaneous levies and sundry taxes have also been drawn from this region. Surcharges for wastage have grown heavier by the day, reaching their utmost extent today. At the founding of the dynasty in the early Hongwu reign, military and state expenditures were enormous, yet repeated orders were still issued for the remission of land taxes …

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
詔宣德間亦嘗降
旨減蘇郡賦額至七十餘萬石當其時民未甚
病也矧疲弊如今而可無以寬之哉夫賦
額一定誠有未可輕議者彼舊逋之積能
捐以予民如洪武之
詔額外之入能稍為節省如宣德之
旨奚獨不可乎雖然
聖天子賢公卿在上苟有意於養民而本末之
政兼舉其父也雖一定之賦亦安知其終
===
不可減哉蓋今日為東南之患者固難縷
數而其原皆起於賦重苟於此有以處之
則其他如執事所憂者固可以漸而去也
夫昔之民長鄉賦者督其賦之入而已今
則厨傳饋遺百需萃焉重以貪吏侵牟豪
強逋負歲運則利歸於姦民交兌則力屈
於悍卒誠舉是數者悉去之且使長民者
無徒以威虐加之而有體悉愛護之意則
亦庶幾其有瘳乎輸納之費在於懲有司
punctuated:
詔。宣德間亦嘗降旨，減蘇郡賦額至七十餘萬石。當其時，民未甚病也。矧疲弊如今，而可無以寬之哉？夫賦額一定，誠有未可輕議者。彼舊逋之積，能捐以予民，如洪武之詔；額外之入，能稍為節省，如宣德之旨，奚獨不可乎？雖然，聖天子、賢公卿在上，苟有意於養民，而本末之政兼舉其父也，雖一定之賦，亦安知其終不可減哉？蓋今日為東南之患者，固難縷數，而其原皆起於賦重。苟於此有以處之，則其他如執事所憂者，固可以漸而去也。
夫昔之民長鄉賦者，督其賦之入而已。今則厨傳饋遺，百需萃焉，重以貪吏侵牟、豪強逋負。歲運則利歸於姦民，交兌則力屈於悍卒。誠舉是數者悉去之，且使長民者無徒以威虐加之，而有體悉愛護之意，則亦庶幾其有瘳乎？輸納之費，在於懲有司
translation_en:
…edicts. During the Xuande reign, an imperial command also reduced the tax quota of Suzhou Prefecture to more than 700,000 shi of grain. At that time, the people were not yet suffering severely. How much more exhausted and impoverished they are today—can there be no means of easing their burdens? Once a tax quota has been fixed, there are indeed reasons why it cannot lightly be reconsidered. Yet why should it be impossible to cancel accumulated arrears for the people's benefit, as in the Hongwu emperor's edict, or to reduce somewhat the collections beyond the quota, as in the Xuande emperor's command? Nevertheless, with a sagely Son of Heaven and worthy high ministers above, if they intend to nurture the people and undertake measures addressing both fundamentals and particulars—the text here reads “their father” [?]—how can we know that even a fixed tax quota may not ultimately be reduced? The troubles afflicting the southeast today are indeed too numerous to enumerate, but their source lies entirely in heavy taxation. If this can be dealt with, the other troubles that concern you can certainly be eliminated gradually.
Formerly, commoners who headed local tax collection [?] merely supervised the payment of taxes. Today, provisioning official travelers, presenting gifts, and a hundred other demands converge upon them, compounded by the exactions of corrupt clerks and the unpaid taxes of powerful local families. In the annual grain transport, the profits go to unscrupulous people; when grain is handed over, their strength is exhausted in dealing with overbearing soldiers. If all these abuses were truly eliminated, and those who govern the people were made to treat them with understanding and care, instead of merely imposing intimidation and cruelty, might the people not have some prospect of recovery? Reducing the costs of delivering and paying taxes depends upon restraining the responsible officials…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之苛刻絕胥吏之旁緣而事涉
中禁又能不以宫府有所異同俾外廷得制
其出入則或可省矣徭役之制舉十年之
力而盡於一時既非所堪而九等之數奸
人又得上下其手必也計里而受役論丁
以出庸舉周文襄之舊法而復之乎田賦
之則自巧歷者所不能筭而以喻愚氓難
矣今欲計其所入之數而均之於田使較
若畫一足以杜詭射之弊而豪貴不便自
===
非主計之臣誠心經理無爲身謀而
廟堂之上剛斷不惑未易行也民多轉徙而荒
蕪未闢賦役不均之所致耳而其間亦不
能無所欺蔽固有冒其名而享膏腴之利
有其實而蒙督責之擾者今必先覈其真
僞然後盡蠲舊逋與之更始而於願耕之
民厚加優恤庶乎有開墾之漸而釋公私
之累矣水利之不修則主其事者憚於任
怨而弗躬親之耳誠得果敢有爲者任之
punctuated: 之苛刻，絕胥吏之旁緣，而事涉中禁，又能不以宫府有所異同，俾外廷得制其出入，則或可省矣。徭役之制，舉十年之力而盡於一時，既非所堪，而九等之數，奸人又得上下其手。必也計里而受役，論丁以出庸，舉周文襄之舊法而復之乎？田賦之則，自巧歷者所不能筭，而以喻愚氓，難矣。今欲計其所入之數而均之於田，使較若畫一，足以杜詭射之弊，而豪貴不便。自非主計之臣誠心經理，無爲身謀，而廟堂之上剛斷不惑，未易行也。民多轉徙而荒蕪未闢，賦役不均之所致耳。而其間亦不能無所欺蔽，固有冒其名而享膏腴之利、有其實而蒙督責之擾者。今必先覈其真僞，然後盡蠲舊逋，與之更始，而於願耕之民厚加優恤，庶乎有開墾之漸，而釋公私之累矣。水利之不修，則主其事者憚於任怨而弗躬親之耳。誠得果敢有爲者任之，
translation_en:
…the harsh exactions of the responsible officials, and cutting off the opportunities for clerks to profit on the side. Where matters involve the inner palace, if palace and government offices can be treated alike, and the outer court allowed to regulate receipts and expenditures, these costs might be reduced. Under the corvée system, ten years’ worth of labor is exhausted at a single stroke—already more than people can bear—and unscrupulous men can also manipulate the nine assessment grades. Surely we must assign service according to the village units and assess payments in lieu of labor according to the adult males, restoring the old regulations of Zhou Wenxiang?

The land-tax rates are such that even skilled calculators cannot reckon them; explaining them to unlettered commoners is therefore difficult. The present aim is to calculate the amount of revenue required and distribute it evenly over the land, making the assessments clear and uniform enough to prevent fraudulent tax evasion. Yet this would disadvantage the powerful and eminent. Unless the officials responsible for revenue administer the matter sincerely, without scheming for their own benefit, and those at court act with firm and unwavering resolve, it will not be easy to carry out.

That so many people move away and so much waste land remains unreclaimed results simply from the unequal distribution of taxes and labor service. Yet there must also be deception and concealment involved: some falsely claim the designation while enjoying the profits of fertile land, whereas others actually bear the circumstances and suffer the harassment of demands for payment [?]. We must first ascertain what is true and what is false, then remit all old arrears and allow the people a fresh start. Those willing to cultivate should receive generous concessions and assistance. In this way reclamation may gradually begin, relieving burdens on both government and people.

The neglect of water-control works results simply from those in charge fearing the resentment they would incur and failing to attend to the work personally. If truly resolute and capable men could be found and entrusted with it…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
按圖籍以尋源委之迹懲豪猾以復陂堰
之利嚴脩築以固隄防之設時疏濬以續
已成之功且無與水爭尺寸而多爲之委
以瀦瀉之又何旱潦涸溢之足患哉夫是
數者皆方今迫切之憂有志者所欲亟圖
而終莫能遂則有故矣吏之不肖者監司
容養而不問曰惜其出於科目也愛其善
於承迎也是故吏得以肆于民上而無忌
此一弊也昔之主計大臣任之久者至二
===
十餘年而郡縣親民之吏亦七八年五六
年而後遷也今也歲歲易之彼雖賢者亦
不暇行其志矣此一弊也在上者求治甚
切也然吏之奉行者取具文移而無實是
以
詔書每下詞意懇惻士民欣欣而姦胥老吏已
相與竊笑之彼知其文雖美而其實終無
所成耳此一弊也使此三弊而不去則雖
有良法莫爲之經理求民之息肩終不可
punctuated:
按圖籍以尋源委之迹，懲豪猾以復陂堰之利，嚴脩築以固隄防之設，時疏濬以續已成之功，且無與水爭尺寸，而多爲之委以瀦瀉之，又何旱潦涸溢之足患哉？夫是數者，皆方今迫切之憂，有志者所欲亟圖而終莫能遂，則有故矣。
吏之不肖者，監司容養而不問，曰：「惜其出於科目也，愛其善於承迎也。」是故吏得以肆于民上而無忌，此一弊也。昔之主計大臣，任之久者至二十餘年，而郡縣親民之吏亦七八年、五六年而後遷也。今也歲歲易之，彼雖賢者，亦不暇行其志矣，此一弊也。在上者求治甚切也，然吏之奉行者取具文移而無實，是以詔書每下，詞意懇惻，士民欣欣，而姦胥老吏已相與竊笑之。彼知其文雖美，而其實終無所成耳，此一弊也。使此三弊而不去，則雖有良法，莫爲之經理，求民之息肩終不可
translation_en:
…consult maps and registers to trace the watercourses from their sources to their outlets; punish powerful wrongdoers to restore the benefits of reservoirs and weirs; rigorously undertake construction and repairs to strengthen dikes and embankments; and dredge periodically to sustain what has already been accomplished. Moreover, rather than contesting every inch of land with the water, provide ample outlets for its storage and discharge. What cause would there then be to fear drought and waterlogging, drying up and overflowing? These several matters are all urgent concerns of the present day. That men of resolve wish to address them promptly yet ultimately cannot accomplish their aims has its reasons.
Surveillance commissioners tolerate and protect unworthy officials without calling them to account, saying, “We cherish them because they emerged through the examinations; we favor them because they are adept at accommodating and flattering their superiors.” Thus officials can act wantonly over the people without restraint. This is one abuse. In former times, high ministers responsible for fiscal administration served, in the longest cases, for more than twenty years; even prefectural and county officials who dealt directly with the people served seven or eight years, or five or six, before being transferred. Now they are replaced every year. Even worthy men have no time to carry out their aspirations. This is another abuse. Those above are most earnest in seeking good government, but the officials charged with implementing their wishes merely produce the requisite official correspondence, without substantive action. Thus whenever an imperial edict is issued, its language and intent earnest and compassionate, scholars and commoners rejoice, while unscrupulous clerks and seasoned functionaries are already secretly laughing together at it. They know that, however fine its wording, nothing will ultimately be accomplished in practice. This is another abuse. If these three abuses are not eliminated, then even if good laws exist, no one will administer them, and securing relief from the people’s burdens will ultimately be impossible…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
得矣夫當積蠹大壞之餘而欲求經常簡
易之說不先從其要者圖之雖一日百變
法豈有益哉執事苟不以愚言為迂妄而
有取焉豈惟東南雖推之天下可也
第五問
謝紘
同考試官教諭陳批馬政國之大事固儒者
所當究心也士子所對殊為疎略晚得此策條答
敷暢考據詳明而議論鑿鑿讀之令人忘倦吾知
===
斯人行且空冀北之羣矣
考試官署郎中華批此策救弊窮源而得其
處之之要他日有位亦何施而不可
考試官給事中陸批馬政策詳贍且以東南
之士而能具知西北之利害亦難得矣
馬政之不善未有甚於今日者也在民有
無窮之害而於國無纖毫之益當是時雖
吾
祖宗之舊法有不能盡行者矣乃欲議及於周
punctuated:
得矣。夫當積蠹大壞之餘，而欲求經常簡易之說，不先從其要者圖之，雖一日百變法，豈有益哉？執事苟不以愚言為迂妄而有取焉，豈惟東南，雖推之天下可也。
第五問
謝紘
同考試官教諭陳批：馬政，國之大事，固儒者所當究心也。士子所對殊為疎略，晚得此策，條答敷暢，考據詳明，而議論鑿鑿，讀之令人忘倦。吾知斯人行且空冀北之羣矣。
考試官署郎中華批：此策救弊窮源，而得其處之之要。他日有位，亦何施而不可？
考試官給事中陸批：馬政策詳贍，且以東南之士而能具知西北之利害，亦難得矣。
馬政之不善，未有甚於今日者也。在民有無窮之害，而於國無纖毫之益。當是時，雖吾祖宗之舊法，有不能盡行者矣。乃欲議及於周
translation_en:
…be attained. Amid the devastation left by accumulated abuses, if one seeks arrangements that are enduring, simple, and practicable without first addressing the essentials, what benefit could there be even in changing the laws a hundred times a day? If you, sir, do not dismiss my humble words as impractical and reckless, but find something worth adopting in them, they could be applied not merely in the southeast but throughout the realm.
Fifth Question
Xie Hong
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: Horse administration is a great affair of state, and certainly deserves careful study by Confucian scholars. The candidates’ answers were particularly sketchy. Late in the process I came upon this policy essay: its answers to the individual points are fully and fluently developed, its supporting evidence detailed and clear, and its arguments firmly grounded. Reading it makes one forget fatigue. I know that this man will soon leave the herds of northern Ji empty—that is, outshine all his peers.
Comment by Examiner Hua, Acting Bureau Director: This policy essay traces abuses to their sources in seeking remedies and grasps the essentials of dealing with them. When its author holds office in the future, what undertaking could be beyond him?
Comment by Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary: This policy essay on horse administration is detailed and substantial. Moreover, for a scholar from the southeast to possess such comprehensive knowledge of the advantages and disadvantages of conditions in the northwest is a rare accomplishment.
Never has horse administration been worse than it is today. It brings endless harm to the people and not the slightest benefit to the state. At such a time, even some of the old regulations of our dynastic ancestors cannot be fully implemented. Yet to wish to extend the discussion to the Zhou …

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
官之政難矣哉雖然有治人無治法法之
立也不能保其無弊變而通之亦存乎人
焉爾矣甞讀周禮而知周公留意於馬政
之切也掌邦政者以司馬名之蓋示戎事
之莫急於此而其屬則有校人掌王六馬
有廋人掌十二閑趣馬齊其節巫馬治其
疾馬質平其賈牧師掌其地圉師主其教
圉人供其役設官多而立法詳若是聖人
之所重者亦可識矣至其取之於民則以
===
六千四百井之地而出馬百乗積而數之
誠若不可勝計而視後世則已省矣矧自
其井牧之法行而上下之間聯絡通貫國
有大事不待徵發之勞而無弗具集事已
兵休則渙然復故而已亦何病於擾哉由
周而來言馬政者凡幾變矣牧之官者典
守怠而侵牟起則病於國牧之民者亡失
多而輸納困則妨於民而
本朝實兼受其弊在今日則耗散窘迫之勢
punctuated: 官之政，難矣哉！雖然，有治人，無治法。法之立也，不能保其無弊；變而通之，亦存乎人焉爾矣。甞讀《周禮》，而知周公留意於馬政之切也。掌邦政者以司馬名之，蓋示戎事之莫急於此。而其屬則有校人掌王六馬，有廋人掌十二閑，趣馬齊其節，巫馬治其疾，馬質平其賈，牧師掌其地，圉師主其教，圉人供其役。設官多而立法詳若是，聖人之所重者亦可識矣。至其取之於民，則以六千四百井之地而出馬百乗。積而數之，誠若不可勝計，而視後世則已省矣。矧自其井牧之法行，而上下之間聯絡通貫，國有大事，不待徵發之勞而無弗具集；事已兵休，則渙然復故而已，亦何病於擾哉！由周而來，言馬政者凡幾變矣。牧之官者，典守怠而侵牟起，則病於國；牧之民者，亡失多而輸納困，則妨於民。而本朝實兼受其弊，在今日則耗散窘迫之勢
translation_en:
…the administration of the Offices of Zhou—how difficult that would be! Nevertheless, there are men who bring about good government, but no laws that do so of themselves. When laws are established, one cannot guarantee that they will remain free of abuses; adapting them to changing circumstances likewise depends upon people alone. I have read the Rites of Zhou and thereby learned how earnestly the Duke of Zhou attended to horse administration. The official responsible for governing the realm was named Minister of War (sima, literally “Director of Horses”), evidently to show that nothing in military affairs was more urgent than this. Among his subordinates, the Director of Horses managed the king’s six classes of horses; the Stable Master managed the twelve stables; the Horse Overseer regulated their routines; the Horse Shaman treated their illnesses; the Horse Appraiser determined fair prices for them; the Pasture Master managed their grazing grounds; the Chief Groom directed their training; and the Grooms performed the necessary labor. With so many offices established and such detailed regulations laid down, one can discern the importance the sage attached to this matter.

As for what was required of the people, land comprising 6,400 well-field units supplied horses for one hundred chariots. Added together, the total might indeed seem beyond counting, yet it was already modest compared with later ages. Moreover, once the system of well-fields and pasturage was in operation, higher and lower levels were linked in a continuous whole. When the state faced a great undertaking, everything was assembled without the trouble of issuing levies. Once the undertaking ended and the troops stood down, all simply dispersed and returned to their former condition. What suffering could there have been from disruption?

Since the Zhou, how many changes horse administration has undergone! When horses were raised by the authorities, those charged with their custody grew negligent and embezzlement arose, harming the state. When they were raised by the people, deaths and losses were numerous and delivery obligations burdensome, harming the people. Our own dynasty has in fact suffered both sets of abuses. Today, the depletion and dispersal of resources and the pressure of straitened circumstances…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
極矣誠宜亟處而不容巳者以民牧之法
言之則宋熈寧保馬之舊也然牧必計丁
不問其願否不貫其他役則其害視宋益
甚矣矧孳生有供給之繁倒失有陪納之
費其所養且多羸劣無益戎行河洛齊魯
兩畿之民日困而
國家曾未得其利也為今之計亦惟優恤貧
弱蠲其積逋令民當出馬者輸直有差而
不復歲課其駒之入至於畿內之寄養孳
生者則官自牧之而不以煩民可矣近時
丘文莊公常論此欲即里社為廐舎寓官
牧於民養是或一說然愚恐其如昔人社
倉之制終貽擾民之害此或未易行耳以
招易之法言之亦宋熈寧茶馬之遺也然
名曰差發如田之有賦如身之有庸則國
體視彼為尊矣自金牌之制廢而私易行
給蕃之茶偽而官市沮故所得大抵駑下
徒費豢養洮河西寧三衛之卒苦之而邊
punctuated:
極矣，誠宜亟處而不容巳者。以民牧之法言之，則宋熈寧保馬之舊也。然牧必計丁，不問其願否，不貫其他役，則其害視宋益甚矣。矧孳生有供給之繁，倒失有陪納之費，其所養且多羸劣，無益戎行。河洛、齊魯、兩畿之民日困，而國家曾未得其利也。為今之計，亦惟優恤貧弱，蠲其積逋，令民當出馬者輸直有差，而不復歲課其駒之入。至於畿內之寄養孳生者，則官自牧之，而不以煩民可矣。近時丘文莊公常論此，欲即里社為廐舎，寓官牧於民養，是或一說。然愚恐其如昔人社倉之制，終貽擾民之害，此或未易行耳。

以招易之法言之，亦宋熈寧茶馬之遺也。然名曰差發，如田之有賦，如身之有庸，則國體視彼為尊矣。自金牌之制廢而私易行，給蕃之茶偽而官市沮，故所得大抵駑下，徒費豢養。洮、河、西寧三衛之卒苦之，而邊
translation_en:
…has reached an extreme: this truly demands urgent action and admits of no delay. As for the system of having commoners rear horses, it follows the precedent of the horse-guarantee system of the Song dynasty’s Xining era. Yet horse-rearing obligations are assessed by the number of adult males, without asking whether they are willing and without taking their other service obligations into account [?]; its harm is therefore even greater than under the Song. Moreover, breeding entails burdensome provisioning, while deaths and losses entail the expense of compensation. The horses raised are also mostly weak and inferior, of no use to the army. The people of Heluo, Qilu, and the two metropolitan regions grow poorer by the day, yet the state has obtained no benefit.

The only course now is to give generous relief to the poor and vulnerable, remit their accumulated arrears, and require those liable to supply horses to pay their monetary value at graded rates, no longer exacting an annual quota of foals. As for horses entrusted to households within the metropolitan region for rearing and breeding, officials should rear them themselves, without burdening the people. Recently, Lord Qiu Wenzhuang discussed this, proposing to establish stables in local communities and incorporate official horse-rearing into household husbandry. This is one possible proposal. Yet I fear that, like the community granary system of earlier times, it would ultimately leave a legacy of burdens upon the people. It may therefore be difficult to implement.

As for the system of procuring horses through exchange, it too is a survival of the tea-for-horses system of the Song dynasty’s Xining era. Yet it is designated a requisition, like the tax on land or the service obligation upon a person; thus the dignity of the state is better upheld than under the Song arrangement. Since the gold-token system was abolished and private trading spread, the tea supplied to the non-Han peoples has been adulterated and official trading obstructed. Consequently, the horses obtained are mostly inferior stock, merely wasting the expense of feeding them. The soldiers of the three guards of Tao, He, and Xining suffer from this, while the frontier…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
方非全賴其用也為今之計亦惟嚴設屯
戍以遏私販令茶之輸官者每箆皆精而
仍復往年招商之舊至於諸邊之奏乞開
中者則弗徇其請而專以易馬可矣近時
李文正公嘗論此欲增馬直以啖羣胡捐
微利以收奇駿是誠良策然愚則以為我
聖祖差發之設實寓制戎之機此所當先復耳
抑馬政有可議者惟牧於官為善而執事
之間未之及也今欲振而起之則有二說
===
焉得其地也得其人也夫燕薊之地馬之
所生而秦隴涇渭之間有唐人監牧之迹
今草塲侵沒馬曠土多汙萊矣能覈實以
歸官則芻牧奚患乎無資廐寺之官牧政
所寄而撫諭巡察之職又督率作興之機
今選用滅裂而更代者不常矣能精擇而
久任則綱紀何患乎不舉如是則可以復
祖宗之政而侵據有罰倒失有罰尅減盜易者
有罰凡可以為馬之害無不去也可以行
punctuated:
方非全賴其用也。為今之計，亦惟嚴設屯戍以遏私販，令茶之輸官者每箆皆精，而仍復往年招商之舊。至於諸邊之奏乞開中者，則弗徇其請，而專以易馬可矣。近時李文正公嘗論此，欲增馬直以啖羣胡，捐微利以收奇駿，是誠良策。然愚則以為我聖祖差發之設，實寓制戎之機，此所當先復耳。
抑馬政有可議者，惟牧於官為善，而執事之間未之及也。今欲振而起之，則有二說焉：得其地也，得其人也。夫燕薊之地，馬之所生，而秦隴涇渭之間，有唐人監牧之迹。今草塲侵沒，馬曠土多汙萊矣。能覈實以歸官，則芻牧奚患乎無資？廐寺之官，牧政所寄，而撫諭巡察之職，又督率作興之機。今選用滅裂，而更代者不常矣。能精擇而久任，則綱紀何患乎不舉？如是，則可以復祖宗之政，而侵據有罰，倒失有罰，尅減盜易者有罰，凡可以為馬之害，無不去也；可以行
translation_en:
…the frontier does not depend entirely on their service. For present purposes, we need only establish firm garrisons to curb private trading, ensure that every basket [?] of tea delivered to the authorities is of fine quality, and restore the former practice of recruiting merchants. As for memorials from the various frontier regions requesting the opening of merchant provisioning exchanges, their requests should not be granted; the tea should be reserved exclusively for obtaining horses. Recently, Lord Li Wenzheng discussed this matter, proposing to raise the price paid for horses to entice the various Hu peoples, sacrificing a small profit to obtain exceptional steeds. This is indeed a sound policy. Yet I consider that our sagely founder’s establishment of the requisition system actually embodied a means of controlling the Rong peoples. This is what should first be restored.
There is, moreover, another aspect of horse administration worth discussing: official management of horse breeding is best, yet you gentlemen have not addressed it. If we now wish to revive it, two things are required: obtaining the land and obtaining the right men. The lands of Yan and Ji are places where horses are bred, while in the regions of Qin and Long, and between the Jing and Wei rivers, traces remain of the Tang horse-breeding directorates. Today the pastures have been encroached upon and appropriated, and the horse lands [?] have largely become waste and scrub. If their extent can be verified and they can be restored to official possession, why fear a shortage of resources for fodder and grazing? Responsibility for horse breeding rests with the officials of the Court of the Imperial Stud, while the duties of those charged with pacification, instruction, and inspection also provide the means to supervise and stimulate this work. Today appointments are made carelessly, and replacements occur at irregular intervals. If men can be carefully chosen and kept long in office, why fear that proper discipline will not be maintained? In this way, the policies of our imperial ancestors can be restored: encroachment and unlawful occupation will be punished; deaths and losses of horses will be punished; embezzlement, theft, and illicit substitution will be punished. Everything that could harm the horses will be eliminated, and it will be possible to put into practice…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
周官之政而攻駒有法講馭有法游牝去
特者有法凡可以為馬之利者無不興也
亦何必襲宋人之弊法以重困吾民哉雖
然得其地易得其人難是二者之輕重亦
可知也故曰存乎人焉爾矣
punctuated: 周官之政，而攻駒有法，講馭有法，游牝去特者有法，凡可以為馬之利者，無不興也。亦何必襲宋人之弊法，以重困吾民哉？雖然，得其地易，得其人難，是二者之輕重亦可知也。故曰：存乎人焉爾矣。
translation_en: …the policies of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), with proper methods for gelding colts, practicing driving, and pasturing mares apart from stallions: every measure beneficial to horses would be put into effect. Why, then, must we follow the defective methods of the Song and thereby further burden our people? Nevertheless, obtaining suitable land is easy; obtaining suitable men is difficult. The relative importance of these two can thus be understood. Hence I say: it rests upon the men, and that is all.

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄後序
我
高皇帝立國之明年即建學弘化
又明年
詔開科取士俾士各專一經以効
用諸所科條盡刷漢唐以來
苟簡之規而敺之古將以成
===
全才也是以百六十年于玆
涵育既久人文鬯達昌大衍
溢之才相望于海內顧各省
校文專限學職而議其不便
者亦久矣恭遇
皇上釐敝更化百度咸貞時惟戊
子鄉試爰稽故事分
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄後序

我高皇帝立國之明年，即建學弘化。又明年，詔開科取士，俾士各專一經以効用。諸所科條，盡刷漢唐以來苟簡之規，而敺之古，將以成全才也。是以百六十年于玆，涵育既久，人文鬯達，昌大衍溢之才相望于海內。顧各省校文專限學職，而議其不便者亦久矣。恭遇皇上釐敝更化，百度咸貞。時惟戊子鄉試，爰稽故事，分
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

In the year after founding the dynasty, our Emperor Gao established schools to extend moral transformation. In the following year, he decreed that examinations be held to recruit scholars, requiring each scholar to specialize in one Classic in order to render service. The regulations he laid down swept away all the perfunctory practices inherited from the Han and Tang onward and directed scholars toward antiquity, with the aim of producing men of fully developed abilities. Thus, over the 160 years down to the present, sustained cultivation has brought literary culture into full flourishing, and men of abundant, expansive talent have appeared in succession throughout the realm. Yet the evaluation of examination essays in each province was restricted exclusively to educational officials, and the disadvantages of this arrangement have long been debated.

We have reverently witnessed His Majesty remedy abuses and renew governance, setting all institutions in proper order. At the time of the Provincial Examination of the wuzi year [1528], precedents were accordingly consulted, and separate …

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
遣廷臣爲各省考試官錄士之
文率尚平實爾雅思得醇篤
眞材以資化理乃六月丁卯
上方精白載嘗以承休慶而臣粲
臣鑰寔受
命典試浙中深以譾劣弗稱是𢞁
至則合諸事事者鎖院試之
===
三而防檢經理加密矣因得
一省多士之文而熟觀之淵
乎理之奧也浩乎政之藏也
蔚乎氣之光也文運道化風
行海流顧玆藩亦極盛也已
竊嘗論之理精矣貴得也政
達矣貴純也文盛矣貴不窮
punctuated:
遣廷臣爲各省考試官，錄士之文率尚平實爾雅，思得醇篤眞材，以資化理。乃六月丁卯，上方精白載嘗，以承休慶，而臣粲、臣鑰寔受命典試浙中，深以譾劣弗稱是𢞁。至則合諸事事者，鎖院試之三，而防檢經理加密矣。因得一省多士之文而熟觀之，淵乎理之奧也，浩乎政之藏也，蔚乎氣之光也！文運道化，風行海流，顧玆藩亦極盛也已。

竊嘗論之：理精矣，貴得也；政達矣，貴純也；文盛矣，貴不窮
translation_en:
…court officials were dispatched to serve as Examiners in the various provinces. In selecting candidates’ writings, they generally favored plainness, substance, and cultivated correctness, seeking genuine talent of integrity and steadfastness to aid moral transformation and good government. On the dingmao day of the sixth month, His Majesty was then, with utmost purity of purpose, performing the seasonal ancestral offering [?] to receive auspicious blessings. Your servants Can and Yue duly received the command to preside over the examination in Zhejiang, deeply apprehensive that our shallow abilities made us unequal to the charge. Upon arrival, we assembled all those responsible for the work, secluded ourselves within the examination compound, and examined the candidates in three sessions, making precautions, inspections, and administrative arrangements still more rigorous. We thus obtained the writings of the many scholars of the province and studied them closely. How profound their exploration of principle’s subtleties! How vast their store of knowledge of government! How splendid the radiance of their vital spirit! Literary flourishing and the transforming influence of the Way spread like the wind and flowed like the sea: this province, indeed, had reached a height of prosperity.

I have ventured to reflect on this: when understanding of principle is refined, what matters is truly grasping it; when knowledge of government is comprehensive, what matters is its purity; when literary culture flourishes, what matters is that it remain inexhaustible…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
也天下之盛而乆乆而不窮
者鮮矣聖人垂衣裳而天下
治焉其實有得而用無窮也
夫自渾淪初闢凡幾開明而
後道法始備道法既立凡幾
述作而後六經始成六經也
者天地聖人之精蘊也學者
===
舍是無以學治者舍是無以
治而顧使之專守其一以器
天下之才賢何哉於乎易以
神變書以彌化詩以長善春
秋以精義禮以密而樂以宣
其入不同其歸一也天下之
業專則精精則得得則乆乆
punctuated: 也。天下之盛而乆，乆而不窮者鮮矣。聖人垂衣裳而天下治焉，其實有得而用無窮也。夫自渾淪初闢，凡幾開明而後道法始備；道法既立，凡幾述作而後六經始成。六經也者，天地聖人之精蘊也。學者舍是無以學，治者舍是無以治，而顧使之專守其一，以器天下之才賢，何哉？於乎！易以神變，書以彌化，詩以長善，春秋以精義，禮以密而樂以宣，其入不同，其歸一也。天下之業，專則精，精則得，得則乆，乆
translation_en:
…Indeed, few things in the world flourish and endure, enduring without exhaustion. The sage lets his robes hang down, and the world is well governed: this is because he has truly attained understanding, and its application is inexhaustible. From the first opening of primordial chaos, how many stages of enlightenment passed before the Way and its methods became complete? Once the Way and its methods were established, how many acts of transmitting and composing passed before the Six Classics took shape? The Six Classics contain the essential subtleties of Heaven, Earth, and the sages. Without them, students have no means to learn, and rulers have no means to govern. Yet students are made to concentrate exclusively on just one of them, as the means of shaping the talented and worthy throughout the realm. Why is this?
Ah! The Book of Changes enables wondrous transformation; the Book of Documents extends moral transformation everywhere; the Book of Odes nurtures goodness; the Spring and Autumn Annals refines the understanding of rightness; the Book of Rites brings meticulous order, while the Book of Music gives expansive expression. Their points of entry differ, but their ultimate destination is one. In the undertakings of the world, concentration leads to mastery, mastery to attainment, and attainment to endurance; endurance…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
則通通則一不專則不信不
達而無所於得百物匱而六
學窮矣故示之以弗兼寔引
而深之以俟其通耳若或施
之有政而弗果於用畏且遷
焉弗周于用窒且跆焉則六
經一筌蹄耳矣而亦何貴於
===
專哉我
皇祖首詔作成之意殆不若是也
夫豈獨作成之意有在我
皇上今日
側席之懷亦夫人所可測而知
也諸士子獲登玆選幾於專
以精矣博以達矣其將守之
punctuated: 則通，通則一。不專則不信不達，而無所於得，百物匱而六學窮矣。故示之以弗兼，寔引而深之，以俟其通耳。若或施之有政，而弗果於用，畏且遷焉；弗周于用，窒且跆焉，則六經一筌蹄耳矣，而亦何貴於專哉？我皇祖首詔作成之意，殆不若是也。夫豈獨作成之意有在？我皇上今日側席之懷，亦夫人所可測而知也。諸士子獲登玆選，幾於專以精矣，博以達矣，其將守之
translation_en: …then understanding becomes comprehensive; comprehensive understanding leads to unity. Without specialization, one achieves neither conviction nor understanding and gains nothing: the myriad undertakings languish, and the six disciplines are exhausted. Thus, instructing students not to study them all at once is actually a means of guiding them deeper, awaiting their comprehensive understanding. If, however, when applying their learning in government, they fail to act decisively, becoming timid and wavering, or fail to apply it comprehensively, becoming obstructed and faltering [?], then the Six Classics are merely fish traps and rabbit snares. What, then, is so valuable about specialization? Surely this was not our imperial ancestor’s intention in his first edict to nurture and perfect talent. Nor is that intention to nurture talent the only consideration: anyone can discern our present Emperor’s eagerness to welcome worthy men, as though leaving a place beside him on his seat. You scholars who have gained selection in this examination have perhaps attained refinement through specialization and understanding through broad learning. Will you hold fast to this …

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
終身而弗畏弗遷矣乎其將
局於一藝而弗利弗安矣乎
今之登茲選者固他日致用
之地也敢於試事告竣因以
諗之
承德郎兵部武庫清吏司署
郎中事主事華鑰謹序
punctuated:
終身而弗畏弗遷矣乎？其將局於一藝而弗利弗安矣乎？今之登茲選者，固他日致用之地也。敢於試事告竣，因以諗之。
承德郎、兵部武庫清吏司署郎中事主事華鑰謹序。
translation_en:
…throughout their lives, without fear or wavering? Or will they confine themselves to a single field of learning, finding neither advantage nor ease? Selection in the present examination is surely the foundation for putting their abilities to use in the future. As the examination proceedings conclude, I venture to offer these words of counsel.
Preface respectfully composed by Hua Yue, Gentleman for Receiving Virtue and Secretary serving as Acting Director of the Bureau of the Arsenal in the Ministry of War.

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭鄭批繼體守成不外乎敬而
成王之學多得于此是作文勢沛然而結意尤爲
明備
同考試官學正孫批文字典雅僅見此篇務
實之學也
考試官署郎中華批平實可取
考試官給事中陸批詞到意足
欲法乎先王之所爲以承乎先王之所底周王
訪其臣然也夫先王之道隨在而有着也於此
===
法之亦焉往而不得其底哉成王延訪群臣之
意如此蓋以先王之治本於道先王之道見於
行吾於多難則未堪而求道則未合必何如而
可乎誠以皇考常蒞之以出治者廷也一上一
下正百官者以此御萬幾者以此亦於此而繼
之于以仰希其成憲之所在謨訓功烈識其大
也禮樂文章識其小也紹之弗得弗措焉皇考
常居之以正始者家也一陟一降端本者以此
善則者以此亦於此而繼之于以近守其懿範
punctuated:
同考試官教諭鄭批：繼體守成，不外乎敬，而成王之學多得于此。是作文勢沛然，而結意尤爲明備。

同考試官學正孫批：文字典雅，僅見此篇，務實之學也。

考試官署郎中華批：平實可取。

考試官給事中陸批：詞到意足。

欲法乎先王之所爲，以承乎先王之所底，周王訪其臣然也。夫先王之道，隨在而有着也，於此法之，亦焉往而不得其底哉？成王延訪群臣之意如此。蓋以先王之治本於道，先王之道見於行。吾於多難則未堪，而求道則未合，必何如而可乎？誠以皇考常蒞之以出治者，廷也。一上一下，正百官者以此，御萬幾者以此。亦於此而繼之，于以仰希其成憲之所在。謨訓功烈，識其大也；禮樂文章，識其小也。紹之，弗得弗措焉。皇考常居之以正始者，家也。一陟一降，端本者以此，善則者以此。亦於此而繼之，于以近守其懿範
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “Succeeding to the throne and preserving its achievements depend entirely upon reverence, and King Cheng’s learning owed much to this. This essay flows abundantly, and its concluding argument is especially clear and complete.”

Associate Examiner Sun, Instructor, comments: “For elegance of writing, this essay alone stands out. Its learning is devoted to practical substance.”

Examiner Hua, Acting Director, comments: “Straightforward and sound; worthy of selection.”

Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary, comments: “The wording is apt and the meaning fully expressed.”

Desiring to emulate what the former king had done, and thereby carry forward what the former king had achieved: such was the purpose of the king of Zhou in consulting his ministers. The Way of the former king has manifestations everywhere. If one models oneself upon it here, wherever one goes, how could one fail to attain what he attained? Such was King Cheng’s intention in summoning his assembled ministers for consultation. For the former king’s government was rooted in the Way, and his Way was manifest in his actions. “I cannot yet bear these many difficulties, and in seeking the Way I have not yet accorded with it. What must I do to succeed?”

Indeed, the place where my august deceased father regularly presided to administer government was the court. In every movement, ascending or descending, it was here that he set the hundred officials right, and here that he managed the myriad affairs of state. Here, too, I shall succeed him, looking upward in hope of discerning his established rules. In his counsels, instructions, accomplishments, and achievements, I shall recognize their greater aspects; in rites, music, and cultural forms, I shall recognize their lesser aspects. I shall carry them forward, and will not desist until I succeed. The place where my august deceased father regularly dwelt to set beginnings right was the household. In every movement, ascending or descending, it was here that he rectified the root, and here that he perfected the standards. Here, too, I shall succeed him, closely preserving his admirable example…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之所貽几席觴豆求其志也定省起居述其事
也紹之弗能弗措焉將見循前人之迹或可以
得前人之休拱穆清而正位凝命法之所在即
休之所在也庶幾賴之以保吾之所未安優游
者或以享而泮奐者或可期九重無震驚之虞
亦吾克艱之一助耳不然身且不保成業可得
而守乎亶聰明而垂憲貽謀法之所存即休之
所存也庶幾賴之以啓吾之所未明不聰者或
以擴而緝熈者或可至萬幾無叢脞之患亦吾
===
造哲之一資耳不然則身且不明盛治可得而
致乎夫成王纘緒之圖如此其切此所以道無
不合而克光前烈也歟大抵守成之君未有不
得其祖宗之法而可以善其治者也成王繼序
不忘乎心猶訪于臣而不自是於是羣臣進以
敬之之戒而事天事親之道備矣噫君臣一心
創守一道此所以就文武之業崇大化之本歟
春秋
楚子蔡侯次于厥貉〔文公十年〕公會宋公
punctuated:
之所貽，几席觴豆，求其志也；定省起居，述其事也。紹之弗能弗措焉。將見循前人之迹，或可以得前人之休。拱穆清而正位凝命，法之所在，即休之所在也。庶幾賴之以保吾之所未安，優游者或以享，而泮奐者或可期，九重無震驚之虞，亦吾克艱之一助耳。不然，身且不保，成業可得而守乎？亶聰明而垂憲貽謀，法之所存，即休之所存也。庶幾賴之以啓吾之所未明，不聰者或以擴，而緝熈者或可至，萬幾無叢脞之患，亦吾造哲之一資耳。不然，則身且不明，盛治可得而致乎？夫成王纘緒之圖如此其切，此所以道無不合，而克光前烈也歟！大抵守成之君，未有不得其祖宗之法而可以善其治者也。成王繼序，不忘乎心，猶訪于臣而不自是，於是羣臣進以敬之之戒，而事天事親之道備矣。噫！君臣一心，創守一道，此所以就文武之業，崇大化之本歟！

春秋

楚子、蔡侯次于厥貉。〔文公十年〕公會宋公
translation_en:
…what he has bequeathed: through his tables and mats, cups and vessels, I seek his intentions; through attending him evening and morning and caring for his daily needs, I carry on his practices. Until I can continue them, I shall not desist. By following my predecessor’s footsteps, I may thus obtain my predecessor’s blessings. With hands folded in the august serenity of court, he established his rightful position and secured the Mandate; where his exemplary ways lie, there too lie his blessings. I may hope to rely on them to secure what is not yet secure for me. Ease may become mine to enjoy, and expansive contentment may be hoped for. Within the ninefold palace walls there will be no fear of alarm: this, too, will help me meet my difficulties. Otherwise, if I cannot even preserve myself, how could I preserve the legacy already established? Truly discerning and enlightened, he handed down standards and bequeathed plans; where his exemplary ways abide, there too abide his blessings. I may hope to rely on them to illuminate what I do not yet understand. Where my understanding falls short, it may be enlarged, and continuous illumination may be attained. The myriad affairs of government will suffer no disorder through preoccupation with petty details: this, too, will be a resource in my attainment of wisdom. Otherwise, if I myself lack understanding, how could I bring about flourishing government?

So earnest was King Cheng’s resolve to continue the succession! Was this not why he accorded with the Way in every respect and could bring lustre to his predecessors’ achievements? In general, no ruler preserving an established legacy has ever governed well without grasping the exemplary ways of his ancestors. King Cheng succeeded to the throne and kept this constantly in his heart, yet still consulted his ministers rather than assuming himself right. His ministers accordingly offered the admonition to be reverent, and thus the Way of serving Heaven and serving one’s parents was complete. Ah! Ruler and ministers shared one heart; founding and preserving a dynasty followed one Way. Was this not how they fulfilled the undertaking of Kings Wen and Wu and exalted the foundation of great moral transformation?

Spring and Autumn Annals

The Viscount of Chu and the Marquis of Cai encamped at Juehe. 〔Tenth year of Duke Wen〕 The Duke met with the Duke of Song…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯晉趙盾癸酉
同盟于新城〔文公十有四年〕
謝紘
同考試官教諭陳批聖人予奪晉楚之意無
非以謹君臣之義耳此作能發之而辭義嚴正自
是關繫世教文字未可以場屋之士目之
考試官署郎中華批謹嚴有法
考試官給事中陸批得傳意
夷惡逞而與國從春秋以大義奪之伯信講而
===
諸侯協春秋以大義予之夫君臣之義春秋之
所謹也得不于晉楚之行事而予奪以見意哉
且楚之行事猶夫晉耳而春秋毎奪之者何吾
觀其筆削於厥貉之舉而知之蓋楚以蠻夷而
竊王號其負犯義之罪大矣今焉穆也將逞志
於北方因按兵而脅宋是舉也藏禍心以憑諸
夏也而陳鄭與宋從之蓋迫於禍難弗獲巳耳
若蔡無他虞乃輕焉服役得非樂於異類之從
耶噫四夷雖大不過曰子王法所在夫誰敢不
punctuated:
陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯、晉趙盾，癸酉，同盟于新城〔文公十有四年〕。
謝紘。
同考試官教諭陳批：聖人予奪晉楚之意，無非以謹君臣之義耳。此作能發之，而辭義嚴正，自是關繫世教文字，未可以場屋之士目之。
考試官署郎中華批：謹嚴有法。
考試官給事中陸批：得傳意。
夷惡逞而與國從，《春秋》以大義奪之；伯信講而諸侯協，《春秋》以大義予之。夫君臣之義，《春秋》之所謹也，得不于晉楚之行事而予奪以見意哉？且楚之行事猶夫晉耳，而《春秋》毎奪之者何？吾觀其筆削於厥貉之舉而知之。蓋楚以蠻夷而竊王號，其負犯義之罪大矣。今焉穆也，將逞志於北方，因按兵而脅宋。是舉也，藏禍心以憑諸夏也，而陳鄭與宋從之，蓋迫於禍難，弗獲巳耳。若蔡無他虞，乃輕焉服役，得非樂於異類之從耶？噫！四夷雖大，不過曰子。王法所在，夫誰敢不
translation_en:
…the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, and Zhao Dun of Jin; on the guiyou day, they together concluded a covenant at Xincheng. 〔The fourteenth year of Duke Wen.〕
Xie Hong.
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: The Sage’s intention in approving or censuring Jin and Chu was simply to uphold strictly the proper relationship between ruler and minister. This composition brings that intention to light, and its language and reasoning are rigorous and upright. It is assuredly a piece of writing that bears upon the moral instruction of the age; its author cannot be regarded merely as a candidate in the examination hall.
Comment by Examiner Hua, Acting Director: Careful and rigorous, with sound method.
Comment by Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary: It captures the meaning of the Commentary.
When a barbarian pursued his wicked designs and allied states followed him, the Spring and Autumn Annals censured them according to the great principles of righteousness; when a hegemon established good faith and the feudal lords acted in concord, the Spring and Autumn Annals approved them according to those same principles. The proper relationship between ruler and minister is what the Spring and Autumn Annals guards strictly. How could it fail to express its intent by approving or censuring the deeds of Jin and Chu?
Now, Chu’s deeds were much like Jin’s; why, then, does the Spring and Autumn Annals repeatedly censure Chu? By examining what it includes and omits in recording the affair at Juehe, I understand the reason. Chu, a barbarian state, usurped the title of king: grave indeed was its guilt in violating righteousness. Now Mu, its ruler, intended to carry out his ambitions in the north, and accordingly halted his troops to intimidate Song. In this undertaking he harbored a malicious purpose, seeking to overawe the states of the central realm. Chen, Zheng, and Song followed him, presumably because the threat of calamity left them no alternative. But Cai, facing no other danger, rashly submitted to his service. Was this not to follow an alien people willingly?
Alas! However great the barbarians of the four quarters might be, their rulers were entitled to be called no more than viscounts. Where royal law holds sway, who would dare fail to…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
嚴楚也實亂之而蔡人則甘心爲之羽翼是僭
王之惡楚爲首而蔡亦其從也苟自此而或逞
其志使禍及宗周君臣之義其與存者幾何春
秋以尊周爲本者不能無懼乎此故削三國而
書蔡侯以罪之奪從楚之蔡所以奪僭王之楚
也若晉之行事猶夫楚耳而春秋每予之者何
吾觀其致意於新城之盟而知之盖晉自文襄
已主夏盟其著仗義之略久矣今焉趙盾倡爲
外楚之謀因講服貳之信是盟也抑強夷以安
===
周室也而陳鄭與宋在焉盖出於同欲非強之
矣雖蔡不預盟而决於從楚亦何害于衆志之
同耶噫周德雖衰天命未改王室之憂其誰能
弗恤晉也實念之而諸侯則恊心爲之股肱是
尊王之舉晉爲主而諸國其輔也苟繼此而益
堅其從使威伸強楚君臣之義不尚亦有賴哉
春秋以大義率人者不能不謹乎此故特書同
盟以善之予從晉之諸侯所以予尊王之晉也
其進退抑揚皆非苟然者夫豈有所私於其間
punctuated:
嚴？楚也實亂之，而蔡人則甘心爲之羽翼。是僭王之惡，楚爲首，而蔡亦其從也。苟自此而或逞其志，使禍及宗周，君臣之義，其與存者幾何？春秋以尊周爲本者，不能無懼乎此，故削三國而書蔡侯以罪之。奪從楚之蔡，所以奪僭王之楚也。
若晉之行事猶夫楚耳，而春秋每予之者何？吾觀其致意於新城之盟而知之。盖晉自文襄已主夏盟，其著仗義之略久矣。今焉趙盾倡爲外楚之謀，因講服貳之信。是盟也，抑強夷以安周室也。而陳鄭與宋在焉，盖出於同欲，非強之矣。雖蔡不預盟，而决於從楚，亦何害于衆志之同耶？噫！周德雖衰，天命未改，王室之憂，其誰能弗恤？晉也實念之，而諸侯則恊心爲之股肱。是尊王之舉，晉爲主，而諸國其輔也。苟繼此而益堅其從，使威伸強楚，君臣之義，不尚亦有賴哉？春秋以大義率人者，不能不謹乎此，故特書同盟以善之。予從晉之諸侯，所以予尊王之晉也。其進退抑揚，皆非苟然者，夫豈有所私於其間？
translation_en:
…be strict? It was Chu that disrupted this order, while the people of Cai willingly served as its wings. In the wrongdoing of usurping the royal title, Chu was the ringleader, and Cai its accomplice. If, from this point, Chu were allowed to fulfill its ambitions and bring disaster upon the ancestral house of Zhou, how much of the proper relationship between ruler and subject would remain? The Spring and Autumn Annals, which takes honoring Zhou as its foundation, could not but fear this. Thus it omits the three states and records the Lord of Cai, thereby condemning him. Its censure of Cai for following Chu is a means of censuring Chu for usurping the royal title.
Yet if Jin’s actions were much like Chu’s, why does the Spring and Autumn Annals repeatedly approve of Jin? I understand this by examining the significance it attaches to the covenant at Xincheng. Since the time of Dukes Wen and Xiang, Jin had presided over the covenants of the Xia states, and had long demonstrated its policy of upholding righteousness. Now Zhao Dun proposed a plan to exclude Chu and accordingly sought to establish pledges of loyalty among those wavering in their allegiance. This covenant was intended to restrain a powerful barbarian state and secure the royal house of Zhou. Chen, Zheng, and Song participated because they shared this desire, not because they were compelled. Although Cai did not join the covenant and was resolved to follow Chu, how could that detract from the unity of purpose among the others? Alas! Though Zhou’s virtue had declined, Heaven’s mandate had not changed. Who could fail to show concern for the troubles of the royal house? Jin indeed kept them in mind, and the regional lords joined together to serve as its limbs. In this undertaking to honor the king, Jin took the lead, and the other states assisted it. If they thereafter became still firmer in their allegiance, allowing Jin’s authority to prevail over powerful Chu, would not the proper relationship between ruler and subject still have something on which to depend? The Spring and Autumn Annals, which guides people by the great principles of righteousness, could not but take care over this. Thus it specifically records that they “covenanted together,” thereby commending them. Its approval of the regional lords who followed Jin is a means of approving Jin for honoring the king. Its advancement and demotion, censure and praise, are never arbitrary. How could there be any partiality in them?

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
抑當是時動天下屬諸侯有大感焉列國若
罔聞知而盟好是講悖矣又况主之者晉卿而
其君不預也春秋何善乎是而與之夫中國不
振旅而蠻夷入伐是盟也猶有憂思防患之意
焉且其事關於君臣夷夏之際春秋有不得不
予之者矣嗚呼其衰世之意耶
齊人伐我北鄙〔僖公二十有六年〕楚公子
貞帥師伐鄭〔襄公八年〕
羅洪
===
同考試官教諭陳批斐然之文奇氣溢發而
敘事且極詳備錄此以警世之學春秋而忽傳註
者
考試官署郎中華批詳贍
考試官給事中陸批不失題旨
稱王命以卻敵賢臣修辭之功背伯信以從夷
大夫失職之罪此展禽之卻齊所以能安其國
而子駟之從楚卒於不免其身也觀春秋所書
而得失見矣嘗夫莒衞請平而我僖因背齊以
punctuated:
抑當是時，動天下、屬諸侯，有大感焉。列國若罔聞知，而盟好是講，悖矣。又况主之者晉卿，而其君不預也，春秋何善乎是而與之？夫中國不振旅，而蠻夷入伐，是盟也，猶有憂思防患之意焉。且其事關於君臣夷夏之際，春秋有不得不予之者矣。嗚呼，其衰世之意耶！

齊人伐我北鄙〔僖公二十有六年〕楚公子貞帥師伐鄭〔襄公八年〕
羅洪

同考試官教諭陳批：斐然之文，奇氣溢發，而敘事且極詳備。錄此以警世之學春秋而忽傳註者。
考試官署郎中華批：詳贍。
考試官給事中陸批：不失題旨。

稱王命以卻敵，賢臣修辭之功；背伯信以從夷，大夫失職之罪。此展禽之卻齊所以能安其國，而子駟之從楚卒於不免其身也。觀春秋所書，而得失見矣。嘗夫莒衞請平，而我僖因背齊以
translation_en:
…Yet at that time there was a great cause for grief that stirred all under Heaven and bound the feudal lords together. For the various states to act as though they had heard and knew nothing, and merely concern themselves with alliances and friendly relations, was perverse. Moreover, the presiding figure was a minister of Jin, while his ruler took no part. What did the Spring and Autumn Annals find good in this, that it should approve it? Now, the central states had not mobilized their armies, while the barbarians had invaded. This alliance still expressed concern and an intention to guard against calamity. Furthermore, the affair touched upon the distinctions between ruler and minister, and between barbarians and the Xia states: the Spring and Autumn Annals could not but accord it approval. Alas! Was this its intent in an age of decline?

“The men of Qi attacked our northern border region.” 〔Twenty-sixth year of Duke Xi〕 “Prince Zhen of Chu led an army to attack Zheng.” 〔Eighth year of Duke Xiang〕
Luo Hong

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “An elegant composition, overflowing with extraordinary vigor; its account of events is also exceptionally detailed and complete. It is included here to admonish those of our time who study the Spring and Autumn Annals but neglect its commentaries and annotations.”
Comment by Examiner Hua, Acting Bureau Director: “Detailed and ample.”
Comment by Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary: “Keeps to the purport of the topic.”

To invoke the king’s command to repel an enemy is the achievement of a worthy minister in crafting his words; to betray faith with the hegemon and follow the barbarians is the offense of a grand master who fails in his duty. This is why Zhan Qin, in repelling Qi, was able to secure his state, whereas Zisi, in following Chu, ultimately could not save himself. By examining what the Spring and Autumn Annals records, their successes and failures become apparent. Once [?], Ju and Wei sought peace, and our Duke Xi consequently turned his back on Qi in order to…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
從之一盟于洮再盟于向而齊人逞忿之兵至
矣爲魯者苟如臧孫之謀不以義服而徒以賂
免其何恥如之幸而栁下惠有辭以應敵而展
喜實將犒師之禮於是乎稱先王之命以對之
不曰股肱周室之盟載書猶在則曰糾合諸侯
之舉舊職未忘果爾其言未終而齊師遂退當
是之時室如縣罄野無青草魯幾無以爲國微
惠也誰安之從容應對以抑強暴之鋒偃息笑
談而紓危亡之禍辭之有益蓋如此傳曰不有
===
君子其能國乎斯之謂矣後此仲尼相魯秉禮
而化強齊以惠方之殆庶幾哉當夫晉楚爭鄭
而鄭人復侵蔡以怒之既敗其兵又獲其將而
楚人問罪之師至矣爲鄭者能如子展之謀堅
守老楚而杖信待晉其誰曰不可夫何公孫騑
決謀以向楚而諸卿共執牛耳之盟於是乎背
五會之信以從之晉君方明不能事也而親我
無成楚師將歸弗能待也而鄙我是欲果爾爲
盟未久而晉師又至自是之後犧牲玉帛待於
punctuated:
從之，一盟于洮，再盟于向，而齊人逞忿之兵至矣。爲魯者苟如臧孫之謀，不以義服而徒以賂免，其何恥如之！幸而栁下惠有辭以應敵，而展喜實將犒師之禮，於是乎稱先王之命以對之。不曰「股肱周室之盟，載書猶在」，則曰「糾合諸侯之舉，舊職未忘」。果爾，其言未終，而齊師遂退。當是之時，室如縣罄，野無青草，魯幾無以爲國。微惠也，誰安之？從容應對以抑強暴之鋒，偃息笑談而紓危亡之禍，辭之有益蓋如此。傳曰：「不有君子，其能國乎？」斯之謂矣。後此仲尼相魯，秉禮而化強齊，以惠方之，殆庶幾哉！

當夫晉楚爭鄭，而鄭人復侵蔡以怒之，既敗其兵，又獲其將，而楚人問罪之師至矣。爲鄭者能如子展之謀，堅守老楚，而杖信待晉，其誰曰不可？夫何公孫騑決謀以向楚，而諸卿共執牛耳之盟，於是乎背五會之信以從之！晉君方明，不能事也，而親我無成；楚師將歸，弗能待也，而鄙我是欲。果爾，爲盟未久，而晉師又至。自是之後，犧牲玉帛待於
translation_en:
…to follow them, making one covenant at Tao and another at Xiang; then the army of Qi arrived to vent its anger. Had those governing Lu followed Zangsun’s plan, seeking deliverance merely through bribes instead of winning submission through righteousness, what could have been more shameful? Fortunately, Liuxia Hui devised words with which to answer the enemy, and Zhan Xi actually carried out the ceremonial presentation of provisions to its army. He thereupon invoked the former kings’ commands in his reply.
