On the one hand, he declared, “The written covenant pledging support to the royal house of Zhou still exists”; on the other, “The old duty of bringing the regional lords together has not been forgotten.” Sure enough, before he had finished speaking, the army of Qi withdrew. At that time, households were as empty as suspended chime stones, and there was no green grass in the fields: Lu could scarcely sustain itself as a state. Without Hui, who could have secured its peace? By replying with composure, he blunted the assault of a powerful aggressor; with relaxed conversation and laughter, he relieved the danger of destruction. Such is the benefit that words can bring. The Commentary says, “Without gentlemen, could a state remain a state?” This is what it means. Later, Zhongni served as chief minister of Lu and, by upholding ritual propriety, transformed powerful Qi. Measured against him, Hui surely came close!

When Jin and Chu were contending for Zheng, the people of Zheng again invaded Cai, provoking Chu’s anger. They defeated Cai’s troops and captured its commander, whereupon Chu’s punitive army arrived. Had those governing Zheng followed Zizhan’s plan, holding firm to wear down Chu and relying upon good faith while awaiting Jin, who could have said this was unacceptable? Why, then, did Gongsun Fei decide upon turning toward Chu, with all the ministers joining in a covenant sealed by holding the ox’s ear, thus abandoning the good faith pledged at five meetings in order to follow Chu? The ruler of Jin was then enlightened, yet they could not serve him, claiming that his friendship with them had achieved nothing; Chu’s army was about to withdraw, yet they could not wait, although Chu desired to reduce them to a border dependency. Sure enough, not long after the covenant was concluded, Jin’s army arrived in turn. From that time onward, sacrificial animals, jade, and silk were kept ready at …

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
二竟鄭幾不免於亡則騑也實爲之忍陪貳之
尊而甘心市井之行忘政本之重而終遺社稷
之憂謀之不臧孰甚焉詩曰誰生厲階至今爲
梗斯之謂矣後此子產相鄭馳詞以當晋楚以
騑視之不有愧哉蓋未幾有西宮之難騑與二
卿死焉君子謂斯人之宜及此久矣春秋削其
大夫所以示當官失職者之戒也抑又有可深
慨者夫以展季之賢魯國賴之以安而終不見
用雖臧孫之竊位蔽賢而魯僖亦不能無責夫
===
若公孫騑之謀所謂一言喪邦者顧其盟與否
皆二三臣主之而君不與知焉此何爲者哉然
則春秋所書不惟人臣謀國任事之鑒亦人君
聽言用人之法也
禮記
故人情者聖王之田也脩禮以耕之陳義
以種之講學以耨之本仁以聚之播樂
以安之故禮也者義之實也協諸義而
協則禮雖先王未之有可以義起也義
punctuated:
二竟，鄭幾不免於亡，則騑也實爲之。忍陪貳之尊，而甘心市井之行；忘政本之重，而終遺社稷之憂。謀之不臧，孰甚焉？詩曰：「誰生厲階，至今爲梗。」斯之謂矣。後此子產相鄭，馳詞以當晋楚，以騑視之，不有愧哉？蓋未幾有西宮之難，騑與二卿死焉。君子謂斯人之宜及此久矣。春秋削其大夫，所以示當官失職者之戒也。抑又有可深慨者：夫以展季之賢，魯國賴之以安，而終不見用，雖臧孫之竊位蔽賢，而魯僖亦不能無責。夫若公孫騑之謀，所謂一言喪邦者，顧其盟與否，皆二三臣主之，而君不與知焉，此何爲者哉？然則春秋所書，不惟人臣謀國任事之鑒，亦人君聽言用人之法也。

禮記

故人情者，聖王之田也。脩禮以耕之，陳義以種之，講學以耨之，本仁以聚之，播樂以安之。故禮也者，義之實也。協諸義而協，則禮雖先王未之有，可以義起也。義
translation_en:
…at the two borders, and Zheng narrowly escaped destruction. It was Fei who had brought this about. He could bear to debase the dignity of his position as deputy to the ruler and willingly adopt the conduct of the marketplace; he forgot the importance of the foundations of government and ultimately left the state beset with troubles. What could surpass the wickedness of his counsel? The Book of Odes says: “Who first gave rise to these steps toward disaster, which remain an obstruction even now?” This is precisely what it means. Later, Zichan served as chief minister of Zheng and dispatched diplomatic communications to deal with Jin and Chu. Measured against him, would Fei not have been ashamed? Before long, the calamity at the Western Palace occurred, and Fei and two other ministers died there. The gentleman observes that this man had long deserved such an end. The Spring and Autumn Annals omits his designation as a grand master, thereby warning those who hold office yet fail in their duties.

There is, moreover, something here that calls for profound lament. Worthy as Zhan Ji was, and although Lu depended upon him for its security, he was never given employment. Although Zangsun usurped his position and concealed a worthy man’s merits, Duke Xi of Lu cannot escape blame either. As for Gongsun Fei’s counsel, it exemplifies the saying that a single utterance can ruin a state. Yet the decision whether to enter the covenant was entirely controlled by two or three ministers, while the ruler had no part in knowing about it. What sort of conduct was this? Thus, what the Spring and Autumn Annals records serves not only as a mirror for ministers who plan for the state and undertake its affairs, but also as a rule for rulers in heeding counsel and employing men.

Book of Rites

Thus, human feelings are the field of the sage king. He cultivates ritual propriety to plough it, sets forth righteousness to sow it, expounds learning to weed it, takes benevolence as his foundation to gather its harvest, and spreads music to bring it peace. Thus, ritual propriety is the concrete realization of righteousness. If a rite is measured against righteousness and accords with it, then, even if the former kings never possessed that rite, it may be instituted on the basis of righteousness. Righteousness…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
者藝之分仁之節也協於藝講於仁得
之者強仁者義之本也順之體也得之
者尊
徐建
同考試官學正凌批聖王治情以禮義仁爲
急而講學播樂非從事於三者之外此作識見真
到詞意貫通以十爲廣明相須之義尤根本註疏
成說以發集說所未備其殆究心經學者高薦允
宜
===
考試官署郎中華批亦可與言禮矣
考試官給事中陸批縝審
記者敘聖王脩道以治情必深明其道有相須
之義也夫聖王治情之道亦多矣序不可紊而
義實相須此所以盡善而無弊歟記禮運者若
曰農人耕種耨穫以治田聖王脩道以治人情
是人情乃聖王之田也而治之何如夫禮者人
情之防範可以濯舊習正持循也則品節于開
導之初猶農夫舉趾于載耕之候然特習其事
punctuated:
者，藝之分，仁之節也。協於藝，講於仁，得之者強。仁者，義之本也，順之體也，得之者尊。
徐建。
同考試官學正凌批：「聖王治情，以禮義仁爲急，而講學播樂，非從事於三者之外。此作識見真到，詞意貫通，以十爲廣，明相須之義，尤根本註疏成說，以發集說所未備。其殆究心經學者，高薦允宜。」
考試官署郎中華批：「亦可與言禮矣。」
考試官給事中陸批：「縝審。」
記者敘聖王脩道以治情，必深明其道有相須之義也。夫聖王治情之道亦多矣，序不可紊，而義實相須，此所以盡善而無弊歟？記禮運者若曰：農人耕種耨穫以治田，聖王脩道以治人情，是人情乃聖王之田也。而治之何如？夫禮者，人情之防範，可以濯舊習、正持循也，則品節于開導之初，猶農夫舉趾于載耕之候，然特習其事
translation_en:
…is the differentiation of the arts and the regulation of benevolence. When brought into accord with the arts and examined in relation to benevolence, those who attain it become strong. Benevolence is the root of righteousness and the embodiment of accord; those who attain it are honored.

Xu Jian.

Comment by Associate Examiner Ling, School Instructor: “In governing human feelings, the sage kings gave priority to ritual, righteousness, and benevolence. Expounding learning and spreading music were not activities outside these three. This composition displays truly penetrating insight, and its language and meaning are coherent throughout. It takes ‘ten’ as an expansion [?], elucidating their mutual dependence. In particular, it draws on established interpretations in the commentaries and subcommentaries to develop what the Collected Explanations leaves incomplete. Its author is surely someone who has devoted himself to the study of the Classics. A high recommendation is fully appropriate.”

Comment by Examiner Hua, Acting Director: “Here too is someone with whom one may discuss ritual.”

Comment by Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary: “Meticulous and discerning.”

In describing how the sage kings cultivated the Way to govern human feelings, the recorder must have understood profoundly the mutual dependence inherent in that Way. The sage kings indeed had many methods for governing feelings. Their sequence must not be confused, yet in principle they depend upon one another. Is this not why they were wholly good and free of defects? The author of the ‘Evolution of Ritual’ chapter seems to say: Farmers manage their fields by plowing, sowing, weeding, and harvesting; the sage kings cultivate the Way to govern human feelings. Thus human feelings are the sage kings’ fields. How, then, do they govern them? Ritual provides safeguards and bounds for human feelings: it can wash away old habits and rectify what people observe and follow. Establishing distinctions and regulations at the outset of instruction is therefore like the farmer setting foot to work when the plowing season begins. Yet this is only practicing the acts themselves…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
夫義者事之宜也必陳義以示其裁制之方便
善端滋長如播種而有生夫種之斯耨之矣於
此有非義之義不能擇而去之也則講學以明
之去非存是而義於是乎精焉然特明諸心耳
仁者心之德也必本仁以要其合一之歸使心
德渾全如旣耨而有穫夫穫之斯得之矣於此
而強仁利仁未遽至於安之也則播樂以養之
詠歌舞蹈而仁於是乎熟焉夫治情之道如此
然亦未始不相須也以禮言之視權度之推移
===
而經制由之以定非義之實乎若有事合於義
而在所當爲則禮雖未有固可以義而創爲之
制矣禮之義如此其廣也不觀諸義乎義也者
爲藝之分限而協合其事宜爲仁之品節而量
度其隆殺且得義者強足以有執也義之義如
此其博也又不觀諸仁乎仁也者以全德則爲
斯義之本以大用則爲百順之質且得仁者尊
足以長人也夫禮義仁之相須如此學也者明
此者也樂也者安此者也盡始終條理之功階
punctuated:
夫義者，事之宜也，必陳義以示其裁制之方便，善端滋長，如播種而有生。夫種之斯耨之矣。於此有非義之義，不能擇而去之也，則講學以明之，去非存是，而義於是乎精焉。然特明諸心耳。仁者，心之德也，必本仁以要其合一之歸，使心德渾全，如旣耨而有穫。夫穫之斯得之矣。於此而強仁、利仁，未遽至於安之也，則播樂以養之，詠歌舞蹈，而仁於是乎熟焉。夫治情之道如此，然亦未始不相須也。
以禮言之，視權度之推移，而經制由之以定，非義之實乎？若有事合於義，而在所當爲，則禮雖未有，固可以義而創爲之制矣。禮之義如此其廣也。不觀諸義乎？義也者，爲藝之分限，而協合其事宜；爲仁之品節，而量度其隆殺。且得義者，強足以有執也。義之義如此其博也。又不觀諸仁乎？仁也者，以全德則爲斯義之本，以大用則爲百順之質。且得仁者，尊足以長人也。夫禮義仁之相須如此，學也者明此者也，樂也者安此者也。盡始終條理之功，階
translation_en:
Righteousness is what is fitting in affairs. One must set forth righteousness to show the appropriate means of judging and regulating them, so that the beginnings of goodness flourish, like seeds that sprout after sowing. Once one has sown, one must weed. If, at this point, there are forms of supposed righteousness that are not truly righteous, and one cannot distinguish and remove them, one must elucidate them through study and discussion. By eliminating what is wrong and preserving what is right, righteousness is refined. Yet this is merely to understand it in the mind. Benevolence is the virtue of the mind. One must take benevolence as the foundation and seek the ultimate unity of all these practices, making the mind’s virtue complete and undivided, like reaping a harvest after weeding. Once one has harvested, one has secured the yield. If, at this point, one practices benevolence through effort or for its benefits, without yet being at ease in it, one must cultivate it through the performance of music. Through chanting, singing, and dancing, benevolence becomes fully mature. Such is the way of ordering human feelings; yet its elements invariably depend upon one another.
To speak of ritual: its established regulations are determined in accordance with shifting judgments and standards. Is this not the actual working of righteousness? If an affair accords with righteousness and ought to be undertaken, then, even if ritual has no existing provision for it, one may certainly create a regulation on the basis of righteousness. So broad is the significance of ritual. Should we not examine righteousness? Righteousness establishes the bounds of the arts, bringing their practice into accord with what is fitting; it provides the gradations and measures of benevolence, determining where its expression should be greater or lesser. Moreover, one who attains righteousness has sufficient strength to hold firmly to a principle. So extensive is the significance of righteousness. Should we not also examine benevolence? As complete virtue, benevolence is the root of this righteousness; in its great functioning, it is the substance of every form of harmonious accord. Moreover, one who attains benevolence possesses sufficient dignity to lead others. Such is the mutual dependence of ritual, righteousness, and benevolence. Learning makes these things clear; music enables one to be at ease in them. Fully accomplishing the work of ordering them from beginning to end, ascending by stages [?] …

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有曲暢旁通之妙則情無不治而禮制行矣其
斯以為君人之大柄歟大抵禮者一定不易而
人情則曲折萬殊制禮本以治情也故必酌諸
義之權度藝之分量仁之支節以觀其會通然
後可以言禮雖三代因革與天地不磨者惟此
義之實耳若體信達順則仁之用塞乎兩間也
噫禮一也脩之則情其性矣廢之則性其情矣
是故先王慎其所以治情者
樂則安安則久久則天天則神
===
同考試官學正凌 批 樂音和平中正故致此
以治心而感化之妙如此此作妙會是意而天神
久安四字句句親切非有得於樂而窮神知化者
不能
考試官署郎中華 批 此樂化章中精粹語而
學者苦於無註子獨發揮明白且神字處與人異
是之取爾
考試官給事中陸 批 語和而莊
banxin: 應天郷試録 四十八 許來學
punctuated:
有曲暢旁通之妙，則情無不治而禮制行矣。其斯以為君人之大柄歟？大抵禮者，一定不易，而人情則曲折萬殊。制禮本以治情也，故必酌諸義之權度、藝之分量、仁之支節，以觀其會通，然後可以言禮。雖三代因革，與天地不磨者，惟此義之實耳。若體信達順，則仁之用塞乎兩間也。噫！禮一也，脩之則情其性矣，廢之則性其情矣。是故先王慎其所以治情者。
樂則安，安則久，久則天，天則神。
同考試官學正凌批：樂音和平中正，故致此以治心，而感化之妙如此。此作妙會是意，而天、神、久、安四字，句句親切。非有得於樂而窮神知化者不能。
考試官署郎中華批：此樂化章中精粹語，而學者苦於無註。子獨發揮明白，且神字處與人異，是之取爾。
考試官給事中陸批：語和而莊。
translation_en:
…there is the subtle capacity to develop every particular fully and comprehend its connections in all directions; then every feeling is brought into order, and the institutions of ritual operate. Is this not the great instrument by which a ruler governs his people? Broadly speaking, ritual is fixed and unchanging, whereas human feelings take countless intricate forms. Ritual was instituted precisely to regulate feelings. Thus one must weigh the standards of righteousness, the measured limits of the arts, and the articulations of benevolence, observing how they converge and interconnect; only then can one speak of ritual. Despite the continuities and changes of the Three Dynasties, what endures undiminished alongside Heaven and Earth is simply the substance of this righteousness. As for embodying trustworthiness and attaining harmonious compliance, these are the workings of benevolence filling the space between Heaven and Earth. Ah! Ritual is one and the same: cultivate it, and feelings conform to one's nature; abandon it, and one's nature conforms to feelings. Thus the former kings were careful about the means by which they regulated feelings.
Music brings repose; repose brings endurance; endurance brings accord with Heaven; accord with Heaven brings spiritual efficacy.
Associate Examiner Ling, Instructor, comments: Musical sounds are harmonious, balanced, centered, and correct. Thus, by bringing these qualities to bear upon the regulation of the mind, music achieves such subtle powers of influence and transformation. This composition wonderfully grasps that meaning, and every sentence treats the four terms—Heaven, spiritual efficacy, endurance, and repose—with precision. This could only have been achieved by someone who has gained an understanding of music, fathomed spiritual efficacy, and understood transformation.
Examiner Hua, Acting Director, comments: These are quintessential words from the chapter on music's transforming power, but students struggle because they lack commentary. You alone have expounded them clearly; moreover, your treatment of the word “spiritual” differs from that of others. It is for this that I select your work.
Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary, comments: The language is harmonious yet dignified.

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
善豫於中而馴致其妙此樂之治心然也甚矣
樂之入人深也旣豫於中則有所得矣而安久
天神之妙有不馴致者哉且君子所貴乎樂者
無他正以治其心耳誠於和平中正之音以致
則易直子諒之心以生其不有所樂乎蓋善端
萌動悅意自爾其流通有義理以養其心也道
腴深味至趣悠然其自適有和粹以平其性也
夫心每患於不安爲其未能樂也旣樂矣則豈
弟之美優柔厭飫而外物無以撓其眞性分之
===
懿涵泳從容而非僻無以奪其守一何如其安
乎夫心每難於持久爲其未能安也旣安矣則
心與理一確乎貞固不以始終而或違德惟日
新卓乎堅定不以先後而或間又何如其久乎
持之以久不但已也充養渾化而朕兆不萌于
見聞存主純熟而機緘不涉於形迹即吾心固
有之天而得乎渾然自成之妙矣非天而何旣
至于天不徒然也無聲無臭而淵乎幾微之黙
運無方無體而闋乎流動之不拘即吾心神明
punctuated: 善豫於中而馴致其妙，此樂之治心然也。甚矣，樂之入人深也！旣豫於中，則有所得矣，而安、久、天、神之妙，有不馴致者哉？且君子所貴乎樂者，無他，正以治其心耳。誠於和平中正之音以致，則易直子諒之心以生，其不有所樂乎？蓋善端萌動，悅意自爾，其流通有義理以養其心也；道腴深味，至趣悠然，其自適有和粹以平其性也。夫心每患於不安，爲其未能樂也。旣樂矣，則豈弟之美，優柔厭飫，而外物無以撓其眞；性分之懿，涵泳從容，而非僻無以奪其守。一何如其安乎！夫心每難於持久，爲其未能安也。旣安矣，則心與理一，確乎貞固，不以始終而或違；德惟日新，卓乎堅定，不以先後而或間。又何如其久乎！持之以久，不但已也。充養渾化，而朕兆不萌于見聞；存主純熟，而機緘不涉於形迹。即吾心固有之天，而得乎渾然自成之妙矣，非天而何？旣至于天，不徒然也。無聲無臭，而淵乎幾微之黙運；無方無體，而闋乎流動之不拘。即吾心神明
translation_en: …goodness brings inward delight, and its wondrous effects are gradually attained: this is what music accomplishes in ordering the heart. How profoundly music enters into people! Once there is inward delight, something has been attained; how could the wondrous states of tranquillity, endurance, Heaven, and spiritual efficacy fail to follow gradually? Moreover, the gentleman values music for no other reason than that it orders his heart. When harmonious, peaceful, balanced, and correct sounds are truly brought to bear, a heart that is easy, upright, loving, and trustworthy arises. Would he not find joy in this? As the beginnings of goodness stir, delight arises of itself; in their free circulation, moral principles nourish his heart. As he deeply savors the richness of the Way, its highest pleasures unfold at leisure; in this contentment, harmony and purity bring his nature into balance. The heart often suffers from a lack of tranquillity because it has not yet attained joy. Once it has attained joy, it gently rests in and fully savors the beauty of kindliness and ease, so that external things cannot disturb its genuineness; it leisurely immerses itself in the excellence inherent in its nature, so that perversity and waywardness cannot dislodge what it holds fast. How tranquil it is! The heart often finds endurance difficult because it has not yet attained tranquillity. Once it is tranquil, the heart is one with principle, steadfast and firm, never departing from it from beginning to end; its virtue is renewed daily, outstandingly resolute, never interrupted from first to last. How enduring it is! Sustaining this endurance does not merely stop there. Through full nourishment and thorough transformation, no incipient signs emerge within sight or hearing; through complete mastery of preserving the heart and maintaining its guiding purpose, its inner workings leave no outward traces. Thus one realizes the Heaven inherent in one’s own heart and attains the wonder of spontaneous, integral completion. What could this be but Heaven? Having reached Heaven, this is no empty attainment. Soundless and odorless, it is profound in the silent operation of its subtlest impulses; without fixed location or form, it is complete [?] in the unrestricted freedom of its flow. Thus, the spiritual luminosity of one’s own heart…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之奧而入于變化莫測之中矣非神而何夫曰
樂曰安曰久人道之所由至也曰天曰神天德
之所由達也一致樂以治心而其妙如此君子
之於樂也而可斯須去身哉抑此論君子治心
之學至爲精切雖禮順樂和表裏交養而養於
中者實爲之主故以禮治身不過嚴威而止樂
之治心則至于天且神即子思之致中孟子之
大化也要之聖人作樂之本端在于此故曰致
禮樂之道舉而措之天下無難矣
===
第貳場
論
治天下者審所上
顧四科
同考試官教諭毛批筆勢滔滔波瀾千里而
自有曲折往復之妙學者得之文體當爲一變
同考試官教諭吳批此題作者類以陳言綴
緝成文是篇立意迥别而詞足以發之故錄
同考試官教諭宋批文氣秀發信爲佳作
punctuated:
之奧，而入于變化莫測之中矣，非神而何？夫曰樂、曰安、曰久，人道之所由至也；曰天、曰神，天德之所由達也。一致樂以治心，而其妙如此，君子之於樂也，而可斯須去身哉？抑此論君子治心之學，至爲精切。雖禮順樂和，表裏交養，而養於中者實爲之主。故以禮治身，不過嚴威而止；樂之治心，則至于天且神，即子思之致中、孟子之大化也。要之，聖人作樂之本端在于此，故曰：「致禮樂之道，舉而措之天下無難矣。」

第貳場

論

治天下者審所上

顧四科

同考試官教諭毛批：筆勢滔滔，波瀾千里，而自有曲折往復之妙。學者得之，文體當爲一變。

同考試官教諭吳批：此題作者類以陳言綴緝成文，是篇立意迥别，而詞足以發之，故錄。

同考試官教諭宋批：文氣秀發，信爲佳作。
translation_en:
…the depths of my own mind’s spiritual illumination, entering into transformations beyond all fathoming. What could this be but the spiritual? Joy, repose, and enduring constancy are the stages through which the human way reaches fulfillment; Heaven and the spiritual are the stages through which heavenly virtue finds full expression. Once music is brought to its fullest realization in governing the mind, its wondrous effects are such as these. How, then, could the gentleman let music depart from him even for a moment? Indeed, this discussion of the gentleman’s cultivation of the mind is supremely precise and pertinent. Although ritual brings order and music brings harmony, nurturing the outer and inner together, nurturing what is within is truly the governing element. Thus, governing the person through ritual goes no further than solemn dignity; governing the mind through music reaches Heaven and even the spiritual. This is precisely Zisi’s attainment of equilibrium and Mencius’s greatness that transforms. In essence, herein lies the fundamental purpose for which the sages created music. Hence it is said: “Bring the way of ritual and music to its fullest realization, and there will be no difficulty in applying it throughout the world.”

Second Session

Discourse

“Those Who Govern All under Heaven Must Scrutinize What They Esteem”

Gu Sike 顧四科

Comment by Associate Examiner Mao, Instructor: The force of the writing flows in an inexhaustible torrent, its waves rolling a thousand li; yet it possesses its own subtle artistry of turns and returns. If students grasp this, their prose style should undergo a transformation.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: Those who write on this topic generally stitch together stock expressions to form an essay. This piece is markedly different in conception, and its language adequately develops that conception. For this reason it has been included.

Comment by Associate Examiner Song, Instructor: The vitality of the prose unfolds with elegance. It is truly an excellent work.

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官署郎中華批清美圓健機軸自別
考試官給事中陸批脫去近時浮靡之習是
亦能審所上者
君子所以先天下者亦惟有定志而已天
下之俗未始不自夫在上者為之也是故
必有所上焉以先之者然而古之為治者
其術亦甚不同也有先之以禮者矣有先
之以刑者矣是二者其志不同故所上不
同而俗之美惡因之此無他存乎審不審
之間而已故夫治天下者莫先於定其志
志定則所上無不審而天下之治幾矣嘗
觀賈誼之論治有所謂審取舍者而匡衡
告元帝亦曰治天下者審所上彼衡之言
亦誼之遺說與夫二子者以為刑罰之不
如禮誼法令之不如教化而思以是易天
下也其意亦美矣雖然天下之治則莫先
於人主之有定志而二子者之論未之及
也刑罰之不如禮誼也法令之不如教化
punctuated:
考試官署郎中華批：清美圓健，機軸自別。
考試官給事中陸批：脫去近時浮靡之習，是亦能審所上者。
君子所以先天下者，亦惟有定志而已。天下之俗，未始不自夫在上者為之也。是故必有所上焉以先之者。然而古之為治者，其術亦甚不同也。有先之以禮者矣，有先之以刑者矣。是二者，其志不同，故所上不同，而俗之美惡因之。此無他，存乎審不審之間而已。故夫治天下者，莫先於定其志。志定，則所上無不審，而天下之治幾矣。嘗觀賈誼之論治，有所謂審取舍者，而匡衡告元帝亦曰：「治天下者審所上。」彼衡之言，亦誼之遺說與？夫二子者，以為刑罰之不如禮誼，法令之不如教化，而思以是易天下也。其意亦美矣。雖然，天下之治，則莫先於人主之有定志，而二子者之論未之及也。刑罰之不如禮誼也，法令之不如教化
translation_en:
Examiner Hua, Acting Bureau Director, comments: “Pure and elegant, rounded and vigorous; its conception is distinctive.”
Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary, comments: “It casts off the superficial and ornate habits of recent times. This author, too, can discern what should be esteemed.”
What enables the gentleman to lead the world is simply a settled purpose. The customs of the world have never failed to take their shape from those above. Thus there must be something they esteem by which to lead the people. Yet the methods by which the ancients governed differed greatly. Some led through ritual propriety; others led through punishments. These two differed in purpose, and therefore in what they esteemed; the goodness or badness of customs followed accordingly. This has no other cause: it rests simply on whether or not they exercise discernment. Thus, for one who governs the world, nothing takes precedence over settling his purpose. Once his purpose is settled, he will exercise discernment in all that he esteems, and the world will be close to good order.
I have observed that Jia Yi, in discussing government, spoke of exercising discernment in what one adopts and rejects. Kuang Heng likewise told Emperor Yuan: “One who governs the world must discern what should be esteemed.” Was Heng’s statement also a teaching handed down from Yi? These two men considered punishments inferior to ritual propriety and righteousness, and laws and ordinances inferior to moral instruction and transformation; they hoped thereby to change the world. Their intention was indeed admirable. Nevertheless, in bringing order to the world, nothing takes precedence over the ruler’s having a settled purpose, and the arguments of these two men did not reach this point. That punishments are inferior to ritual propriety and righteousness, and laws and ordinances inferior to moral instruction and transformation …

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
也世主亦知之矣然不能勉於此而顧安
於彼者何也彼其志不先定則見之弗明
而行之有弗力故也是故其道非難知而
難擇非難擇而難守能擇能守可以言審
所上矣而非有定志者其孰知之今夫法
之所用易見而禮之所為難知也人主之
能無惑焉者鮮矣苟擬議之間稍有不當
將有不勝其弊者故必辨之明而斷之决
曉然見其若黑白之相去也而後從之夫
===
是之謂能擇天下固有知所上者也勉於
一時而不能持之終身其心初向於道而
異說入焉則有盡棄其所為以從之者此
尤君子之所慎焉而不敢忽也執此之政
堅如金石持此之令信如四時吾之所上
在是則舉天下無以加之夫是之謂能守
能擇而後得所審能守而後所審者不易
所審者不易夫然後推而行之則教化之
流由内及外動之而和綏之而安民日遷
punctuated: 也，世主亦知之矣。然不能勉於此，而顧安於彼者，何也？彼其志不先定，則見之弗明，而行之有弗力故也。是故其道非難知而難擇，非難擇而難守。能擇能守，可以言審所上矣，而非有定志者，其孰知之？今夫法之所用易見，而禮之所為難知也。人主之能無惑焉者鮮矣。苟擬議之間稍有不當，將有不勝其弊者。故必辨之明，而斷之决，曉然見其若黑白之相去也，而後從之。夫是之謂能擇。天下固有知所上者也，勉於一時，而不能持之終身；其心初向於道，而異說入焉，則有盡棄其所為以從之者。此尤君子之所慎焉，而不敢忽也。執此之政，堅如金石；持此之令，信如四時。吾之所上在是，則舉天下無以加之。夫是之謂能守。能擇而後得所審，能守而後所審者不易。所審者不易，夫然後推而行之，則教化之流，由内及外，動之而和，綏之而安，民日遷
translation_en: …The rulers of the age know this too. Yet why can they not exert themselves in pursuing the one, but instead rest content with the other? It is because, unless their resolve is first settled, they cannot perceive clearly or act with sufficient vigor. Thus the difficulty lies not in knowing the Way but in choosing it, and not in choosing it but in holding fast to it. Only when one can both choose and hold fast may one speak of carefully discerning what to esteem. Yet who can understand this without settled resolve? Now, the effects of applying laws are readily seen, whereas what ritual accomplishes is difficult to discern. Few rulers can remain free from confusion on this point. If, in their deliberations, they make even a slight error of judgment, the resulting harm may prove more than they can overcome. They must therefore distinguish clearly and decide resolutely, seeing the difference as plainly as that between black and white, before following their chosen course. This is what is meant by being able to choose. There are certainly those in the world who know what to esteem, yet exert themselves only for a time and cannot sustain it throughout their lives. Their minds initially turn toward the Way, but when divergent teachings enter, some wholly abandon what they have been doing to follow them. This is precisely what the gentleman guards against with particular care, never daring to neglect it. In carrying out this governance, be firm as metal and stone; in upholding these commands, be dependable as the four seasons. If what I esteem lies here, nothing in all the world can surpass it. This is what is meant by being able to hold fast. Only through being able to choose does one arrive at a considered judgment; only through being able to hold fast does that judgment remain unchanged. Once that judgment remains unchanged, one may extend it into practice. Then the influence of moral instruction flows from within to without: stir the people, and they become harmonious; soothe them, and they become peaceful. Day by day the people are transformed…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之言治則舍是而曰有定志云者何哉夫
未有不定其志而能正其心者吾之言固
董子意也學不足以知此而謂有二焉者
是未足與言審所上也
同前
姜良翰
同考試官教諭徐批士子類用匡衡語而重
疊排比之是卷筆老意新而步驟衝逸眞妙於文
哉
===
同考試官教諭鄭批場中作論記者固多率
掇拾腐說誇多鬭靡此卷獨能會題意於言外理
到而句亦工也
同考試官學正孫批此作波瀾疊壓而源委
不紊讀之惟恐其盡是宜錄出
考試官署郎中華批詞氣充贍而亦不失程
文之矩度
考試官給事中陸批有議論有操縱他作鮮
及
punctuated:
之言治，則舍是而曰有定志云者，何哉？夫未有不定其志而能正其心者，吾之言固董子意也。學不足以知此，而謂有二焉者，是未足與言審所上也。

同前。
姜良翰。

同考試官教諭徐批：士子類用匡衡語，而重疊排比之。是卷筆老意新，而步驟衝逸，眞妙於文哉！

同考試官教諭鄭批：場中作論記者固多，率掇拾腐說，誇多鬭靡。此卷獨能會題意於言外，理到而句亦工也。

同考試官學正孫批：此作波瀾疊壓，而源委不紊，讀之惟恐其盡，是宜錄出。

考試官署郎中華批：詞氣充贍，而亦不失程文之矩度。

考試官給事中陸批：有議論，有操縱，他作鮮及。
translation_en:
…in speaking of governance, why abandon this and speak instead of having a settled resolve? No one has ever been able to rectify his mind without first settling his resolve. My words certainly convey Master Dong’s meaning. Those whose learning is insufficient to understand this, and who claim that these are two different things, are not yet fit to discuss discerning what one should esteem.

Same as the preceding topic.
Jiang Lianghan.

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: Candidates generally use Kuang Heng’s words, piling them up in parallel constructions. This paper displays a seasoned pen and fresh ideas, and its movement is vigorous and untrammeled. Truly, it is masterful writing!

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: There are certainly many who write discourses and accounts [?] in the examination hall, but most merely gather stale explanations, boasting of their profusion and competing in ornate excess. This paper alone grasps the meaning of the topic beyond its wording. Its reasoning reaches the heart of the matter, and its sentences are finely crafted.

Comment by Associate Examiner Sun, Director of Studies: This composition’s waves surge one upon another, yet its course from source to end remains orderly. Reading it, one fears only that it will end. It deserves to be included in the record.

Comment by Examiner Hua, Acting Director: Its language and rhetorical force are ample and rich, yet it remains within the standards of a model answer.

Comment by Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary: It offers substantive argument and skillful control of its development. Few other compositions can match it.

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
過慮之直以天下之治不可以法病道道
固萬世無弊而紛紜膠轕以變更乎天下
者皆法也觀其變神其幾其預待乎天下
後世者審矣故夏之尚忠也忠弊而商救
之以質質弊而周則以文救之皆通於道
而不離於法善其道於不窮者也雖然後
世之徒法也久矣清靜而黃老之刻核而
申韓之執一實以御百虛而權謀功利之
玆數者恒足以奔走天下之人而聖人則
===
育於仁陶於禮成於義而終不肯以彼易
此彼以厲吾恬以和彼以速吾安以鈍計
功程效而吾則疎宜乎後世之君深信彼
之有成而不吾尚也夫吾之治一道也非
徒法也彼雖不吾信而吾將見彼之日窮
矣此非神於幾達於變者孰能察識於心
術之微而審之也哉審之無異術也是其
所是必其非天下之公是也非其所非必
其非天下之公非也非非而是是者求之
punctuated:
過慮之，直以天下之治不可以法病道。道固萬世無弊，而紛紜膠轕以變更乎天下者，皆法也。觀其變，神其幾，其預待乎天下後世者審矣。故夏之尚忠也，忠弊而商救之以質；質弊而周則以文救之。皆通於道而不離於法，善其道於不窮者也。

雖然，後世之徒法也久矣。清靜而黃老之，刻核而申韓之，執一實以御百虛而權謀功利之。玆數者恒足以奔走天下之人，而聖人則育於仁，陶於禮，成於義，而終不肯以彼易此。彼以厲，吾恬以和；彼以速，吾安以鈍。計功程效，而吾則疎。宜乎後世之君深信彼之有成，而不吾尚也。夫吾之治，一道也，非徒法也。彼雖不吾信，而吾將見彼之日窮矣。此非神於幾、達於變者，孰能察識於心術之微而審之也哉？

審之無異術也。是其所是，必其非天下之公是也；非其所非，必其非天下之公非也。非非而是是者，求之
translation_en:
…having pondered it excessively [?], simply because governing All under Heaven must not allow administrative methods to impair the Way. The Way assuredly remains free of defects through ten thousand generations; what becomes tangled and confused, bringing changes to All under Heaven, consists entirely of administrative methods. By observing changes and apprehending their incipient signs with unfathomable insight, one makes discerning provision for All under Heaven and later generations. Thus, the Xia prized loyalty; when loyalty developed defects, the Shang remedied them with simplicity. When simplicity developed defects, the Zhou remedied them with cultural refinement. All comprehended the Way without departing from administrative methods, thereby making good use of their Way without exhausting its possibilities.

Nevertheless, later generations have long relied on administrative methods alone. They pursue purity and stillness in the manner of Huang-Lao, harsh scrutiny in the manner of Shen Buhai and Han Fei, or strategic manipulation and the pursuit of achievement and advantage, holding to a single actuality to control a hundred empty appearances. These approaches are always sufficient to make the people of All under Heaven hasten to follow them. The sage, however, nurtures through benevolence, molds through ritual propriety, and brings to completion through righteousness, steadfastly refusing to exchange these for those approaches. They employ severity; I remain tranquil through harmony. They employ speed; I rest content with slowness. When achievements are calculated and results assessed, I fall short. Little wonder that rulers of later generations firmly believe those approaches will succeed and do not esteem mine. My governance rests wholly on the Way, not merely on administrative methods. Though they do not trust me, I shall see their approaches become increasingly exhausted. Unless one possesses unfathomable insight into incipient signs and comprehends change, who can discern the subtleties of the workings of the mind and judge them accurately?

There is no special technique for making this judgment. To approve what they approve is necessarily not the common judgment of what is right throughout All under Heaven [?]; to condemn what they condemn is necessarily not the common judgment of what is wrong throughout All under Heaven [?]. To condemn what is wrong and approve what is right, one seeks it …

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
吾心之公也求之道也而非徒法也吾計
已定吾術已明諒其非而去之原其是而
從之由是見微於泰以防天下之過也由
是起教於否以約天下之趨也由是觀變
於賁以成天下之文也明物采設典則天
下之化成而民情樂彼之清靜無爲者吾
弗尚之矣慎感孚妙鼓舞天下之風清而
習俗淳彼之綜核名實者吾弗尚之矣不
識不知與天下相安於仁義禮樂之歸彼
===
之執實以御虛如權謀術數之類皆吾所
見棄者也吾又何求然則吾之所尚者皆
道也而非徒法也苟不此之審而與天下
日逐逐于赦令刑罰之末則雖強焉以必
之而天下不從是何也不從其所治而從
其治之所先也且刑者仁之薄也令者禮
之衰也赦者義之竭也秪見其民日殘而
俗日壞矣雖日赦而求其治不可得也古
之聖人未嘗一日不審所尚以爲天下先
punctuated: 吾心之公也，求之道也，而非徒法也。吾計已定，吾術已明，諒其非而去之，原其是而從之。由是見微於泰，以防天下之過也；由是起教於否，以約天下之趨也；由是觀變於賁，以成天下之文也。明物采，設典則，天下之化成而民情樂，彼之清靜無爲者，吾弗尚之矣。慎感孚，妙鼓舞，天下之風清而習俗淳，彼之綜核名實者，吾弗尚之矣。不識不知，與天下相安於仁義禮樂之歸，彼之執實以御虛，如權謀術數之類，皆吾所見棄者也。吾又何求？然則吾之所尚者皆道也，而非徒法也。苟不此之審，而與天下日逐逐于赦令刑罰之末，則雖強焉以必之，而天下不從。是何也？不從其所治，而從其治之所先也。且刑者，仁之薄也；令者，禮之衰也；赦者，義之竭也。秪見其民日殘而俗日壞矣，雖日赦而求其治，不可得也。古之聖人未嘗一日不審所尚，以爲天下先。
translation_en:
…in the impartiality of my own heart; I seek it in the Way, not merely in methods. My plans are settled, and my approach is clear. I ascertain what is wrong and discard it; I investigate what is right and follow it. Thus, by discerning the subtle signs in Tai (Peace), I guard against excesses in the realm; by initiating instruction in Pi (Obstruction), I restrain the tendencies of the realm; and by observing change in Bi (Adornment), I bring the realm’s cultural refinement to completion. I clarify the distinctions marked by ceremonial objects and colors and establish canonical standards. The realm’s moral transformation is accomplished, and the people are content: I no longer esteem their doctrine of quietude and nonaction. I attend carefully to inspiring trust and exercise a subtle power to rouse the people. The realm’s moral climate becomes pure and its customs sincere: I no longer esteem their practice of comprehensively checking names against actual performance. Without conscious knowledge or contrivance, I dwell at peace with all under Heaven in a shared commitment to benevolence, righteousness, ritual, and music. Their practice of grasping the concrete to control the intangible—such things as expedient schemes and manipulative techniques—is entirely rejected by me. What more need I seek?

Thus, what I esteem is entirely the Way, not merely methods. If one does not scrutinize this, but instead daily busies oneself and the realm with such secondary matters as pardons, ordinances, and punishments, then, even if one forcefully insists upon compliance, the realm will not follow. Why is this? People follow not what the ruler seeks to regulate, but what he puts first in governing. Punishment is benevolence grown thin; ordinances are ritual in decline; pardons are righteousness exhausted. One will see only the people increasingly harmed and customs increasingly corrupted. Even if one grants pardons every day in pursuit of good government, it cannot be attained. The sages of antiquity never let a single day pass without scrutinizing what they esteemed, thereby setting an example for all under Heaven.

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
對此致治之本也是作莊整得體讀之使人興起
同考試官學正孫批辭氣恭謹寫出希文忠
愛至情宜錄以
獻
考試官署郎中華批典重不浮寓意懇切
考試官給事中陸批得宋人告君之意
慶曆三年某月某日伏蒙
開天章閣引輔臣入對者伏以
道隆交際鴻猷益懋于泰來義重彌綸
清問式勤於晉接當
萬幾之少暇誠千載之一時表著聳觀縉紳
動色臣仲淹誠歡誠抃稽首頓首竊惟元
首得股肱而弘化宰輔贊天子以經邦二
典都俞濬開心學三謨翼慎面從一
家人父子之相親敦左右臣鄰之大義但
道隨時降而分與堂高坐論風衰恩覃造
膝疇咨日懈獻匪格心補過漢庭願毋違
于紫闥論思唐閣制旋廢乎正牙尋常僅
punctuated:
對此，致治之本也。是作莊整得體，讀之使人興起。
同考試官學正孫批：辭氣恭謹，寫出希文忠愛至情，宜錄以獻。
考試官署郎中華批：典重不浮，寓意懇切。
考試官給事中陸批：得宋人告君之意。
慶曆三年某月某日，伏蒙開天章閣，引輔臣入對者。伏以道隆交際，鴻猷益懋于泰來；義重彌綸，清問式勤於晉接。當萬幾之少暇，誠千載之一時。表著聳觀，縉紳動色。臣仲淹誠歡誠抃，稽首頓首。竊惟元首得股肱而弘化，宰輔贊天子以經邦。二典都俞，濬開心學；三謨翼慎，面從一家人父子之相親，敦左右臣鄰之大義。但道隨時降，而分與堂高。坐論風衰，恩覃造膝；疇咨日懈，獻匪格心補過。漢庭願毋違于紫闥，論思唐閣，制旋廢乎正牙。尋常僅
translation_en:
…Responding to this is the foundation of good government. This composition is dignified, orderly, and fitting; reading it inspires the reader.
Associate Examiner Sun, Instructor, comments: “Its language and tone are respectful and circumspect, expressing Xiwen’s deepest feelings of loyalty and devotion. It merits being copied out and presented to the throne.”
Examiner Hua, Acting Bureau Director, comments: “Classically dignified and substantial, without frivolity; its underlying intent is earnest.”
Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary, comments: “It captures the spirit in which men of the Song addressed their sovereign.”
On a certain day of a certain month in the third year of Qingli [1043], we humbly received the favor of Your Majesty’s opening Tianzhang Pavilion and summoning the chief ministers to an audience.
I humbly submit: when the Way flourishes through intercourse between ruler and ministers, grand designs advance still further as prosperity arrives; when comprehensive ordering is esteemed as a duty, enlightened inquiries are diligently pursued in audiences. Amid a brief respite from the myriad affairs of government, this is truly an occasion encountered once in a thousand years. Its conspicuous manifestation has stirred all who behold it, and the assembled officials are visibly moved. Your servant Zhongyan, truly joyful and truly exultant, bows his head to the ground and kowtows.
I humbly reflect that the sovereign obtains ministers as his arms and legs and thereby extends his transforming influence; chief ministers assist the Son of Heaven in governing the realm. The exchanges of assent recorded in the Two Canons profoundly opened up the learning of the mind; the reverent caution of the Three Counsels [was joined to] the intimacy of father and son within a single household [?], strengthening the great moral bond between a ruler and the ministers at his side. Yet the Way declined with the passage of time, while distinctions of rank rose as high as the audience hall. The practice of sitting together to discuss government weakened, and intimate audiences depended upon the extension of imperial favor; consultation grew daily more remiss, and what was offered failed to rectify the ruler’s mind and remedy his faults [?]. At the Han court, there was the wish that remonstrance should not be thwarted at the palace gates [?]; deliberation in the Tang pavilion was an institution soon abandoned in favor of formal court audiences [?]. On ordinary occasions, there was merely …

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
止趨班臨御多從暇日延英五刻便殿無
時或假借而強從或背議而少直徒沿故
事適侈彌文茲蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
聖功天監
神道民懷言路一開攬機權而獨運仁聲四
訖歛智勇以無為謂
三聖經綸久布昭回之象而百年禮樂當調未
解之弦不有盡言曷殫至理弘開
===
秘閣廣佇論思尚手攜面命之風求苦口沃
心之助蓋禮意極其周至而
寵渥無復有加者也臣仲淹夙夜先憂致身
是願再三陳列多口茲憎方甘盡瘁於邊
防忽荷
深知于巷遇適當通變宜民之際可無補偏
救敝之陳言出心聲情因義激內外本末
其凡一十餘條興革後先冀采萬分之一
私切惓惓自許敢謂鑿鑿可行伏願
punctuated:
止趨班，臨御多從暇日。延英五刻，便殿無時，或假借而強從，或背議而少直，徒沿故事，適侈彌文。茲蓋伏遇

〇〇〇〇

聖功天監，神道民懷。言路一開，攬機權而獨運；仁聲四訖，歛智勇以無為。謂三聖經綸，久布昭回之象，而百年禮樂，當調未解之弦。不有盡言，曷殫至理？弘開秘閣，廣佇論思，尚手攜面命之風，求苦口沃心之助。蓋禮意極其周至，而寵渥無復有加者也。

臣仲淹夙夜先憂，致身是願。再三陳列，多口茲憎。方甘盡瘁於邊防，忽荷深知于巷遇。適當通變宜民之際，可無補偏救敝之陳？言出心聲，情因義激。內外本末，其凡一十餘條；興革後先，冀采萬分之一。私切惓惓自許，敢謂鑿鑿可行？伏願
translation_en:
…amounted only to taking their places in court ranks, and imperial audiences were mostly held in moments of leisure. Audiences at Yanying lasted five quarter-hours, while those in the side hall had no fixed time. Some received indulgence and reluctantly complied; others criticized behind the throne’s back but offered little frank counsel. They merely followed established precedents, serving only to multiply elaborate formalities.

Now, we have reverently encountered Your Majesty [four circle marks in the text]: Heaven beholds your sagely achievements, and the people cherish your divine Way. Once the channels of counsel were opened, you took command of the crucial powers and exercised them alone; your reputation for benevolence reached the four quarters, while you restrained the exercise of cleverness and martial prowess, governing through nonaction. You consider that the ordering labors of the three sage sovereigns have long displayed the pattern of celestial radiance, yet the rites and music of a hundred years require retuning of strings not yet loosened. Without fully candid speech, how could the utmost principles be exhaustively explored? You have opened wide the Palace Library and eagerly awaited deliberation and reflection. You esteem the practice of taking ministers by the hand and instructing them face to face, seeking the aid of bitter words that refresh the heart. Your courteous consideration has indeed reached the utmost fullness, and no further addition could be made to your generous favor.

Your servant Zhongyan, anxious before others day and night, desires only to devote himself to service. Having repeatedly set forth my views, I have incurred resentment for speaking too much. Just as I was willingly exhausting myself in frontier defense, I unexpectedly received your profound recognition upon an encounter in a lane [?]. At this very time, when institutions must be adapted to benefit the people, could I fail to submit proposals to correct imbalances and remedy abuses? My words give voice to my heart; my feelings are stirred by righteousness. Concerning affairs within and without, fundamentals and details, there are somewhat more than ten proposals in all. As to what should be instituted or abolished, and what should come first or later, I hope that even one ten-thousandth may be adopted. Privately, I venture to credit myself with earnest devotion; how could I dare claim that my proposals are assuredly practicable? I humbly wish…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
式供用之度宏綱大體粲然具列條貫品
式纖悉不遺維持保愛之意無所不至而
節制防範之道亦未嘗不行乎其間恩法
並施仁義兼得真足以傳之萬世而無弊
矣百六十年
聖子
神孫守爲家法
朝廷隆敦叙之恩
諸藩膺忠謹之福自三代以還未有若是之
===
盛也執事乃以爲猶有所未安者殆弗然
乎藉今有之而愚以爲
皇祖之訓典具在
聖孝之繼述方隆舉而行之亦甚易爾夫祿賜
不贍誠有可慮者愚以爲莫若訓之以儉
必也示撙節之方以去其靡習且於歲時
之給無所稽滯而屬之疎者則間施不時
之恩如古所謂以脤膰親兄弟之國者可
也或者患其不繼則曰是何不繼也
punctuated: 式供用之度，宏綱大體，粲然具列；條貫品式，纖悉不遺。維持保愛之意，無所不至，而節制防範之道，亦未嘗不行乎其間。恩法並施，仁義兼得，真足以傳之萬世而無弊矣。百六十年，聖子神孫守爲家法，朝廷隆敦叙之恩，諸藩膺忠謹之福。自三代以還，未有若是之盛也。執事乃以爲猶有所未安者，殆弗然乎？藉今有之，而愚以爲皇祖之訓典具在，聖孝之繼述方隆，舉而行之，亦甚易爾。夫祿賜不贍，誠有可慮者。愚以爲莫若訓之以儉，必也示撙節之方，以去其靡習；且於歲時之給，無所稽滯，而屬之疎者，則間施不時之恩，如古所謂以脤膰親兄弟之國者，可也。或者患其不繼，則曰：「是何不繼也？」
translation_en:
…the prescribed measures for provision and expenditure [?]. The broad principles and general framework are clearly and fully set out; the detailed regulations and prescribed forms omit nothing, however minute. The intention to sustain, protect, and cherish them extends to every concern, while methods of restraint and precaution likewise operate throughout. Favor and law are applied together, and benevolence and righteousness are both realized. These arrangements can truly be handed down through ten thousand generations without ill effects. For one hundred and sixty years, sagely sons and divine grandsons have maintained them as the rules of the imperial house. The court has lavished its favor in fostering affection and proper order among imperial kinsmen, and the various princely houses have enjoyed the blessings of loyalty and circumspection. Since the Three Dynasties, there has never been such flourishing. Yet you, sir, suggest that there are still grounds for unease. Surely that is not so? Even supposing such grounds now exist, I humbly believe that the Imperial Ancestor’s instructions and statutes remain fully available, and that His Majesty’s filial devotion to continuing and carrying forward his predecessor’s work is now flourishing. To take up and implement those instructions would therefore be very easy.

As for inadequate stipends and grants, this is indeed a legitimate concern. I humbly believe that nothing would be better than instructing the princes in frugality. They must be shown ways to economize, so as to eliminate their extravagant habits. Moreover, their regular annual and seasonal provisions should suffer no delays. Those more distantly related should occasionally receive extraordinary favors, following the ancient practice described as using sacrificial meat to foster close relations with the states of royal brothers. This would be appropriate. Some may worry that such provision cannot be sustained; to them I would say: “Why should it not be sustained?”

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
踐其實其爲敎也必始諸下學而著述獨
盛于前古極吾心之大用折百氏之異同
所謂集大成者是矣夫濂洛獨啓心傳於
詞章口耳盛行之餘而朱子乃救流弊於
馳心空渺之始一則予欲無言之旨一則
刪述垂憲之意也嗚呼朱子之用心若此
其慮後世也遠矣愚獨怪夫今之學者滯
章句以溺其心而無或進于道也豈朱子
之爲是敎也將徒博而已乎夫亦擴我聰
===
明之實耳今之學者或涉獵章句或綴緝
詞章佔畢而言性命道德之不離于口肆
筆而書習爲竒僻甚至不能以句則曰學
云學云而不知身心性情爲何物由朱子
觀之其異于俗學也者幾希豈顏子之所
謂博乎無惑乎其不知約也夫學之爲道
未有不知要而能博者亦未有不博而能
逕約者故曰耳目之官不思而蔽於物心
之官則思思則得之博必資於耳目而耳
punctuated:
踐其實。其爲敎也，必始諸下學，而著述獨盛于前古，極吾心之大用，折百氏之異同，所謂集大成者是矣。夫濂洛獨啓心傳於詞章口耳盛行之餘，而朱子乃救流弊於馳心空渺之始，一則「予欲無言」之旨，一則刪述垂憲之意也。嗚呼！朱子之用心若此，其慮後世也遠矣。愚獨怪夫今之學者，滯章句以溺其心，而無或進于道也。豈朱子之爲是敎也，將徒博而已乎？夫亦擴我聰明之實耳。

今之學者，或涉獵章句，或綴緝詞章，佔畢而言，性命道德之不離于口；肆筆而書，習爲竒僻，甚至不能以句，則曰「學云學云」，而不知身心性情爲何物。由朱子觀之，其異于俗學也者幾希！豈顏子之所謂博乎？無惑乎其不知約也！夫學之爲道，未有不知要而能博者，亦未有不博而能逕約者。故曰：「耳目之官不思而蔽於物，心之官則思，思則得之。」博必資於耳目，而耳
translation_en:
…put its substance into practice. His teaching necessarily began with elementary learning, yet his writings surpassed those of earlier ages in their abundance, fully developing the great capacities of our minds and adjudicating the agreements and differences among the various schools. This is what is meant by bringing together the great achievements of the past. The masters of Lian and Luo alone opened the way to the transmission of the mind after literary composition and learning confined to the mouth and ears had become prevalent; Master Zhu then remedied the ensuing abuses just as minds began to stray into empty abstractions. The former embodied the purport of “I wish to say nothing”; the latter, the intention of editing and transmitting texts to leave enduring models. Alas! Such was Master Zhu’s purpose, and so far-reaching was his concern for later generations. I, in my ignorance, marvel particularly at today’s scholars: they become mired in textual divisions and explanations, submerging their minds in them, without ever advancing toward the Way. Could Master Zhu have established this teaching merely to promote breadth of learning? Its purpose was also to enlarge our actual powers of perception and understanding.

Today’s scholars either browse textual divisions and explanations or piece together literary compositions. Poring over texts and discoursing upon them, they never cease talking of human nature, destiny, the Way, and virtue. When they wield their brushes to write, they habitually strive for the strange and obscure, sometimes even failing to form sentences [?]. Yet they keep saying “learning, learning,” without knowing what the body, mind, nature, and feelings are. Viewed from Master Zhu’s standpoint, how little they differ from vulgar learning! Can this be what Master Yan meant by breadth of learning? No wonder they do not understand how to grasp its essentials! In the pursuit of learning, no one has ever attained breadth without understanding what is essential; nor has anyone proceeded directly to the essentials without breadth. Hence it is said: “The faculties of the ears and eyes do not think and are obscured by things. The faculty of the mind thinks; through thinking, it attains understanding.” Breadth of learning must draw upon the ears and eyes, while the ears…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
耳目則役于心心固萬理咸具也其所謂蔽
者有二查滓以渾淆於有生之初邪僞以
汙壞於旣長之後不知省察慎獨而溺心
章句譬諸目翳交蔽坐于寶藏之中不自
知其所有也其必讀書以破愚以格物窮
理使吾心之蔽光明四達萬理畢見而不
可勝用夫然後謂之博耳程子曰聖賢千
言萬語欲人將已放之心約之使反復入
身來朱子亦以居敬窮理互相發爲讀書
===
之要夫亦求博于吾心之智則今之學者
之弊亦庶乎其可救矣或者乃曰盍亦以
子靜之學救之乎夫子靜專尊德性而先
立乎其大者自是高明獨得之學有子靜
之資斯可矣惟恐不善學者後致知而先
行事將必至廢書而不讀則識見不充蘊
蓄不大無復經綸大經焉而理學之功用
狹矣夫子靜之學一也善學者則進于高
明不善學者則馳于空渺存乎人之自識
punctuated:
耳目則役于心，心固萬理咸具也。其所謂蔽者有二：查滓以渾淆於有生之初，邪僞以汙壞於旣長之後。不知省察慎獨，而溺心章句，譬諸目翳交蔽，坐于寶藏之中，不自知其所有也。其必讀書以破愚，以格物窮理，使吾心之蔽光明四達，萬理畢見，而不可勝用，夫然後謂之博耳。程子曰：「聖賢千言萬語，欲人將已放之心約之，使反復入身來。」朱子亦以居敬窮理互相發爲讀書之要。夫亦求博于吾心之智，則今之學者之弊亦庶乎其可救矣。
或者乃曰：「盍亦以子靜之學救之乎？」夫子靜專尊德性，而先立乎其大者，自是高明獨得之學。有子靜之資，斯可矣。惟恐不善學者，後致知而先行事，將必至廢書而不讀，則識見不充，蘊蓄不大，無復經綸大經焉，而理學之功用狹矣。夫子靜之學一也，善學者則進于高明，不善學者則馳于空渺，存乎人之自識
translation_en:
…The ears and eyes, in turn, serve the mind, which inherently contains all principles. What are called its obstructions are of two kinds: dregs that cloud it at the beginning of life, and perversity and falsehood that defile it after one has grown up. To immerse one’s mind in textual exposition without knowing how to examine oneself and remain watchful when alone is like having one’s eyes covered by obscuring films: one sits amid a storehouse of treasures without knowing what one possesses. One must read books to dispel ignorance, investigate things, and fathom principles, so that the obstructions in one’s mind [are removed?], its light reaches everywhere, and all principles become manifest, inexhaustible in their application. Only then can this be called breadth of learning. Master Cheng said: “The thousands upon thousands of words spoken by sages and worthies seek to have people gather in the mind that has strayed and bring it back within themselves.” Master Zhu likewise regarded maintaining reverent attentiveness and fathoming principles, each bringing out the other, as essential to reading. If we seek breadth in the knowing capacity of our own minds, there may yet be hope of remedying the failings of today’s learners.
Someone then asks: “Why not remedy them through the learning of Zijing?” Zijing’s learning concentrates on honoring moral nature and first establishing the greater part of oneself. It is indeed a lofty and enlightened learning attained through personal insight. For someone with Zijing’s endowments, it is practicable. The concern is that those who do not learn well will put extending knowledge last and acting first, eventually abandoning books and ceasing to read. Their understanding will then be incomplete and their accumulated learning meager; they will no longer be able to order the great guiding principles, and the practical efficacy of the learning of principle will be narrowed. Zijing’s learning is one and the same: those who learn it well advance toward loftiness and illumination, while those who learn it poorly race off into empty vagueness. It depends upon each person’s own discernment…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而非所以示人也教人者亦曰讀書窮理
求博于吾心之智而反之約也約之維何
仁人心也顏子自視聽言動以至不違亦
約諸仁耳約而未至于仁仁而或在或亡
不足以言約也其博也以智而其約也以
仁何往而非心學哉愚故曰求諸內而已
矣要其所歸而已矣
第四問
俞介
===
同考試官教諭毛批識見高遠愛國憂民之
念溢於言表經世之學也
同考試官教諭吳批推原東南之患起於賦
重最為有見而末三弊之說尤甚警切所謂豪傑
之士非耶
同考試官教諭宋批東南之地財賦所仰給
關係匪細是策于致弊之由補弊之法歷歷條答
無遺非平日究心于時務者諒不及此讀之令人
起敬
punctuated:
而非所以示人也。教人者亦曰：讀書窮理，求博于吾心之智，而反之約也。約之維何？仁，人心也。顏子自視聽言動，以至不違，亦約諸仁耳。約而未至于仁，仁而或在或亡，不足以言約也。其博也以智，而其約也以仁，何往而非心學哉？愚故曰：求諸內而已矣，要其所歸而已矣。

第四問
俞介

同考試官教諭毛批：識見高遠，愛國憂民之念溢於言表，經世之學也。

同考試官教諭吳批：推原東南之患起於賦重，最為有見，而末三弊之說尤甚警切，所謂豪傑之士非耶？

同考試官教諭宋批：東南之地，財賦所仰給，關係匪細。是策于致弊之由、補弊之法，歷歷條答無遺。非平日究心于時務者，諒不及此。讀之令人起敬。
translation_en:
…and is not a method for instructing others. Those who teach others likewise say: read books and investigate principles, seek breadth in the knowledge of one's own mind, and bring it back to its essentials. What constitutes this concentration on essentials? Benevolence is the human mind. From his seeing, hearing, speaking, and acting to his never departing from benevolence, Master Yan likewise did no more than concentrate upon benevolence. If this concentration has not attained benevolence, or if benevolence is now present and now absent, one cannot speak of having grasped the essentials. Breadth is achieved through wisdom, and concentration through benevolence: where, then, is this not the learning of the mind? Thus I humbly say: seek within, that is all; grasp the ultimate end of this learning, that is all.

Fourth Question
Yu Jie 俞介

Comment by Associate Examiner Mao, Instructor: His understanding is lofty and far-reaching. His concern for the country and its people overflows beyond his words. This is learning directed toward ordering the world.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: Tracing the troubles of the southeast to their origin in heavy taxation shows exceptional insight. His discussion of the three abuses at the end is especially compelling and pointed. Is he not what is called a man of outstanding ability?

Comment by Associate Examiner Song, Instructor: The southeast is the region upon which fiscal revenues depend; its importance is no small matter. This policy essay answers point by point, clearly and without omission, concerning both the causes of the abuses and the methods of remedying them. Surely someone who had not regularly devoted his attention to current affairs could not attain this. Reading it inspires respect.

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官署郎中華批東南利病夫人能言之
未有善處如是者所謂識時務者子其人耶
考試官給事中陸批議論切中時弊而規畫
皆有定見當路者得是說而推行之吳浙之民其
有瘳乎
古所謂豪傑之士必其能通於世務者也
執事之意蓋以是望諸生而愚也豈其人
哉雖然天下之事非愚所知而東南之利
病則習聞之矣執事之問及之愚其容默
===
乎夫東南之地自晉宋以來蓋已日趨於
富庶非復往時厥田下下之舊已若今嘉
湖與蘇松諸郡民力勤而物產盛則財賦
因之加多固也然嘗考前代賦額皆莫有
重於今者雖
國初猶不至是也蓋自永樂以後漕運既遠
且凡雜征汎賦一切取給于其中而加耗
日重至于今日極矣洪武開創之初軍國
之用甚廣然猶屢下蠲租之
punctuated:
考試官署郎中華批：東南利病，夫人能言之，未有善處如是者。所謂識時務者，子其人耶？

考試官給事中陸批：議論切中時弊，而規畫皆有定見。當路者得是說而推行之，吳浙之民其有瘳乎？

古所謂豪傑之士，必其能通於世務者也。執事之意，蓋以是望諸生，而愚也豈其人哉？雖然，天下之事非愚所知，而東南之利病則習聞之矣。執事之問及之，愚其容默乎？夫東南之地，自晉宋以來，蓋已日趨於富庶，非復往時厥田下下之舊已。若今嘉湖與蘇松諸郡，民力勤而物產盛，則財賦因之加多，固也。然嘗考前代賦額，皆莫有重於今者，雖國初猶不至是也。蓋自永樂以後，漕運既遠，且凡雜征汎賦，一切取給于其中，而加耗日重，至于今日極矣。洪武開創之初，軍國之用甚廣，然猶屢下蠲租之
translation_en:
Examiner Hua, Acting Director, comments: “Anyone can speak of the advantages and afflictions of the southeast, but no one has dealt with them as well as this. Are you the very person meant by the expression ‘one who understands the affairs of the times’?”

Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary, comments: “The argument strikes directly at the abuses of the times, and the proposed measures all rest on firm judgments. If those in authority obtained this account and put it into practice, might the people of Wu and Zhejiang find relief?”

Those whom the ancients called outstanding men were necessarily men thoroughly versed in worldly affairs. Your intention, honored examiners, is surely to hold this expectation for us candidates; yet how could someone as unworthy as I be such a man? Nevertheless, although the affairs of the realm lie beyond my knowledge, I have often heard about the advantages and afflictions of the southeast. Since your question touches upon them, how could I remain silent?

Since the Jin and Song dynasties, the southeast has steadily grown wealthy and populous; it is no longer as it was in ancient times, when “its fields were of the lowest grade.” In such prefectures as Jiaxing, Huzhou, Suzhou, and Songjiang today, the people work diligently and production is abundant, so it is natural that tax revenues should increase accordingly. Yet when I examine the tax quotas of previous dynasties, none were heavier than those of today. Even at the founding of our dynasty, they had not reached this level. Since the Yongle reign, the grain tribute has had to travel far, while all manner of miscellaneous levies and taxes have also been drawn from this region. Surcharges for wastage have grown heavier by the day, reaching their extreme today. At the founding of the dynasty in the early Hongwu reign, military and state expenditures were very great, yet repeated orders were still issued for the remission of land taxes…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
詔宣德間亦甞降
旨減蘇郡賦額至七十餘萬石當其時民未甚
病也矧疲弊如今而可無以寛之哉夫賦
額一定誠有未可輕議者彼舊逋之積能
捐以予民如洪武之
詔額外之入能稍為節省如宣德之
旨奚獨不可乎雖然
聖天子賢公卿在上苟有意於養民而本末之
政兼舉其久也雖一定之賦亦安知其終
===
不可減哉蓋今日為東南之患者固難縷
數而其原皆起於賦重苟於此有以處之
則其他如執事所憂者固可以漸而去也
夫昔之民長鄉賦者督其賦之入而已今
則厨傳饋遺百需萃焉重以貪吏侵牟豪
強逋負歲運則利歸於姦民交兌則力屈
於悍卒誠舉是數者悉去之且使長民者
無徒以威虐加之而有體悉愛護之意則
亦庶幾其有瘳乎輸納之費在於懲有司
punctuated:
詔。宣德間亦甞降旨，減蘇郡賦額至七十餘萬石。當其時，民未甚病也，矧疲弊如今，而可無以寛之哉？夫賦額一定，誠有未可輕議者。彼舊逋之積，能捐以予民，如洪武之詔；額外之入，能稍為節省，如宣德之旨，奚獨不可乎？雖然，聖天子、賢公卿在上，苟有意於養民，而本末之政兼舉，其久也，雖一定之賦，亦安知其終不可減哉？蓋今日為東南之患者，固難縷數，而其原皆起於賦重。苟於此有以處之，則其他如執事所憂者，固可以漸而去也。
夫昔之民長鄉賦者，督其賦之入而已。今則厨傳、饋遺，百需萃焉，重以貪吏侵牟、豪強逋負。歲運則利歸於姦民，交兌則力屈於悍卒。誠舉是數者悉去之，且使長民者無徒以威虐加之，而有體悉愛護之意，則亦庶幾其有瘳乎？輸納之費，在於懲有司
translation_en:
…edicts. During the Xuande reign, too, an imperial command was issued reducing the tax quota of Suzhou Prefecture by more than seven hundred thousand shi of grain. At that time the people were not yet suffering severely. How much more exhausted and impoverished they are today: can they be left without relief? Once a tax quota has been fixed, there are indeed reasons why it cannot lightly be reconsidered. Yet why should accumulated arrears not be remitted for the people's benefit, as under the Hongwu edict, and collections beyond the quota somewhat curtailed, as under the Xuande command? Nevertheless, with a sage Son of Heaven and worthy high ministers above, if they intend to nourish the people and pursue measures addressing both fundamentals and particulars, who can know that, in time, even the established tax quota might not ultimately be reduced? The afflictions troubling the southeast today are indeed too numerous to enumerate, but all originate in heavy taxation. If this can be dealt with, the other problems that concern you, sir, can certainly be eliminated gradually.
In former times, commoners placed in charge of village tax collection merely supervised the payment of taxes. Today, expenses for official hospitality and transport, gifts, and a hundred other demands converge upon them, compounded by the exactions of corrupt officials and the arrears of powerful local families. In the annual grain transport, the profits go to unscrupulous commoners; when the grain is handed over, their strength is exhausted in dealing with overbearing soldiers. If all these abuses were truly eliminated, and those who govern the people were made to show understanding and care rather than merely subjecting them to intimidation and cruelty, might there not be some prospect of recovery? As for the costs of delivering and paying taxes, the remedy lies in curbing the responsible officials…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之苛刻絶胥吏之旁縁而事渉
中禁又能不以宫府有所異同俾外廷得制
其出入則或可省矣徭役之制舉十年之
力而盡於一時既非所堪而九等之數奸
人又得上下其手必也計里而受役論丁
以出庸舉周文襄之舊法而復之乎田賦
之則自巧歴者所不能筭而以喻愚氓難
矣今欲計其所入之數而均之於田使較
若畫一足以杜詭射之弊而豪貴不便自
===
非主計之臣誠心經理無爲身謀而
廟堂之上剛斷不惑未易行也民多轉徙而荒
蕪未闢賦役不均之所致耳而其間亦不
能無所欺蔽固有冒其名而享膏腴之利
有其實而蒙督責之擾者今必先覈其真
僞然後盡蠲舊逋與之更始而於願耕之
民厚加優恤庶乎有開墾之漸而釋公私
之累矣水利之不修則主其事者憚於任
怨而弗躬親之耳誠得果敢有爲者任之
punctuated: 之苛刻，絶胥吏之旁縁，而事渉中禁，又能不以宫府有所異同，俾外廷得制其出入，則或可省矣。徭役之制，舉十年之力而盡於一時，既非所堪，而九等之數，奸人又得上下其手。必也計里而受役，論丁以出庸，舉周文襄之舊法而復之乎？田賦之則，自巧歴者所不能筭，而以喻愚氓難矣。今欲計其所入之數而均之於田，使較若畫一，足以杜詭射之弊，而豪貴不便。自非主計之臣誠心經理，無爲身謀，而廟堂之上剛斷不惑，未易行也。民多轉徙而荒蕪未闢，賦役不均之所致耳。而其間亦不能無所欺蔽，固有冒其名而享膏腴之利、有其實而蒙督責之擾者。今必先覈其真僞，然後盡蠲舊逋，與之更始，而於願耕之民厚加優恤，庶乎有開墾之漸，而釋公私之累矣。水利之不修，則主其事者憚於任怨，而弗躬親之耳。誠得果敢有爲者任之，
translation_en:
…the harsh exactions of the responsible officials, and eliminating the clerks’ opportunities for incidental extortion. Where matters involve the inner palace, if palace and government can be treated alike, and the outer court allowed to regulate its receipts and disbursements, these expenses might be reduced.

Under the corvée system, ten years’ labor is exhausted at a single stroke—already more than people can bear—and unscrupulous men can also manipulate the nine grades of assessment. Surely service should be assigned according to the village units, and payments in lieu of service assessed according to the adult males, restoring the old methods of Zhou Wenxiang?

The land-tax rates are beyond even a skilled calculator’s ability to reckon; explaining them to unlettered commoners is therefore difficult. The present aim is to calculate the revenue required and apportion it evenly over the land, making the assessment clear and uniform enough to prevent fraudulent tax evasion. Yet this would disadvantage the powerful and wealthy. Unless the ministers responsible for fiscal affairs administer the matter sincerely, without scheming for their own benefit, and those at court act firmly and decisively without wavering, it will not be easy to implement.

That many people migrate and wasteland remains unreclaimed is simply the result of unequal taxes and labor obligations. Yet deception and concealment also inevitably occur: some falsely claim that status while enjoying the profits of fertile land, whereas others whose circumstances genuinely warrant it suffer the harassment of demands and reprimands. Now it is essential first to verify which cases are genuine and which false, then remit all old arrears and allow the people a fresh start. Generous concessions and assistance should be given to those willing to cultivate the land. Reclamation might thus gradually proceed, relieving burdens on both the government and the people.

The failure to maintain waterworks is simply because those responsible fear incurring resentment and do not attend to the work personally. If truly resolute and capable men could be found and entrusted with it…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
按圖籍以尋源委之迹懲豪猾以復陂堰
之利嚴脩築以固隄防之設時疏濬以續
已成之功且無與水爭尺寸而多爲之委
以瀦瀉之又何旱潦涸溢之足患哉夫是
數者皆方今迫切之憂有志者所欲亟圖
而終莫能遂則有故矣吏之不肖者監司
容養而不問曰惜其出於科目也愛其善
於承迎也是故吏得以肆于民上而無忌
此一弊也昔之主計大臣任之久者至二
===
十餘年而郡縣親民之吏亦七八年五六
年而後遷也今也歲歲易之彼雖賢者亦
不暇行其志矣此一弊也在上者求治甚
切也然吏之奉行者取具文移而無實是
以
詔書每下詞意懇惻士民欣欣而姦胥老吏已
相與竊笑之彼知其文雖美而其實終無
所成耳此一弊也使此三弊而不去則雖
有良法莫爲之經理求民之息肩終不可
punctuated:
按圖籍以尋源委之迹，懲豪猾以復陂堰之利，嚴脩築以固隄防之設，時疏濬以續已成之功，且無與水爭尺寸，而多爲之委以瀦瀉之，又何旱潦涸溢之足患哉？夫是數者，皆方今迫切之憂，有志者所欲亟圖而終莫能遂，則有故矣。
吏之不肖者，監司容養而不問，曰：「惜其出於科目也，愛其善於承迎也。」是故吏得以肆于民上而無忌，此一弊也。昔之主計大臣，任之久者至二十餘年，而郡縣親民之吏亦七八年、五六年而後遷也。今也歲歲易之，彼雖賢者，亦不暇行其志矣，此一弊也。在上者求治甚切也，然吏之奉行者取具文移而無實。是以詔書每下，詞意懇惻，士民欣欣，而姦胥老吏已相與竊笑之。彼知其文雖美，而其實終無所成耳，此一弊也。使此三弊而不去，則雖有良法，莫爲之經理，求民之息肩終不可
translation_en:
…consult maps and registers to trace the waterways from their sources to their outlets; punish powerful wrongdoers to restore the benefits of ponds and weirs; rigorously oversee construction and repair to strengthen dikes and embankments; and dredge periodically to sustain what has already been achieved. Moreover, do not contend with the water over every inch of land, but provide ample outlets for it, allowing it to collect and drain away. What need then be feared from drought or excessive rain, from waterways drying up or overflowing? These matters are all pressing concerns today. Those with resolve wish to address them urgently, yet ultimately cannot accomplish their aims. There are reasons for this.
Provincial surveillance officials tolerate and shield unworthy local officials without calling them to account, saying, “We cherish them because they came through the examinations; we value their skill at accommodating our wishes.” Thus local officials can behave without restraint toward the people, fearing nothing. This is one abuse. In former times, the ministers in charge of state finances sometimes held office for more than twenty years, while prefectural and county officials directly responsible for the people likewise served seven or eight years, or five or six, before being transferred. Now they are replaced every year. Even worthy men have no time to carry out their intentions. This is another abuse. Those above are most earnest in seeking good government, but the officials charged with implementation merely produce the requisite official correspondence, without substantive action. Thus, whenever an imperial edict is issued, its language and intent are earnest and compassionate, and scholars and commoners rejoice; yet corrupt clerks and veteran functionaries are already laughing about it among themselves. They know that, however fine its wording, nothing will ultimately be accomplished in practice. This is another abuse. If these three abuses are not eliminated, then even sound policies will have no one to administer them, and securing relief for the people from their burdens will ultimately be impossible…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
得矣夫當積蠹大壞之餘而欲求經常簡
易之說不先從其要者圖之雖一日百變
法豈有益哉執事苟不以愚言爲迂妄而
有取焉豈惟東南雖推之天下可也
第五問
謝紘
同考試官敎諭陳批馬政國之大事固儒者
所當究心也士子所對殊爲踈略晩得此策條答
敷暢考據詳明而議論鑿鑿讀之令人忘倦吾知
===
斯人行且空冀北之羣矣
考試官署郎中華批此策救弊窮源而得其
處之之要他日有位亦何施而不可
考試官給事中陸批馬政策詳贍且以東南
之士而能具知西北之利害亦難得矣
馬政之不善未有甚於今日者也在民有
無窮之害而於國無纖毫之益當是時雖
吾
祖宗之舊法有不能盡行者矣乃欲議及於周
punctuated:
得矣。夫當積蠹大壞之餘，而欲求經常簡易之說，不先從其要者圖之，雖一日百變法，豈有益哉？執事苟不以愚言爲迂妄而有取焉，豈惟東南，雖推之天下可也。

第五問
謝紘

同考試官敎諭陳批：馬政，國之大事，固儒者所當究心也。士子所對，殊爲踈略。晩得此策，條答敷暢，考據詳明，而議論鑿鑿，讀之令人忘倦。吾知斯人行且空冀北之羣矣。

考試官署郎中華批：此策救弊窮源，而得其處之之要。他日有位，亦何施而不可？

考試官給事中陸批：馬政策詳贍，且以東南之士而能具知西北之利害，亦難得矣。

馬政之不善，未有甚於今日者也。在民有無窮之害，而於國無纖毫之益。當是時，雖吾祖宗之舊法，有不能盡行者矣。乃欲議及於周
translation_en:
…be attained. Amid the devastation wrought by long-accumulated abuses, if we seek a regular, enduring, simple, and practicable approach without first addressing the essentials, what benefit would there be even in changing the laws a hundred times a day? If you, sir, do not regard my foolish words as impractical and presumptuous, but find something worth adopting in them, they could be applied not merely to the southeast but throughout the realm.

Fifth Question
Xie Hong

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: Horse administration is a great affair of state, and certainly deserves the earnest attention of Confucian scholars. The candidates’ responses were particularly sketchy. Late in the process I obtained this policy essay: its answers to the individual points are fully and fluently developed, its supporting evidence detailed and clear, and its arguments convincing. Reading it makes one forget fatigue. I know that this man will soon leave the herds of northern Ji empty—that is, he will outshine all his peers, like a superior horse among the celebrated horses of that region.

Comment by Examiner Hua, Acting Bureau Director: This policy essay traces abuses to their source in seeking remedies and grasps the essentials of dealing with them. When its author holds office in the future, what undertaking could be beyond him?

Comment by Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary: This policy essay on horse administration is detailed and comprehensive. Moreover, for a scholar from the southeast to possess such thorough knowledge of the advantages and disadvantages of conditions in the northwest is a rare accomplishment.

Never has horse administration been worse than it is today. It causes endless harm to the people while bringing not the slightest benefit to the state. At such a time, even some of the established laws of our imperial ancestors cannot be fully implemented. Yet to wish to extend the discussion to the Zhou…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
官之政難矣哉雖然有治人無治法法之
立也不能保其無弊變而通之亦存乎人
焉爾矣甞讀周禮而知周公留意於馬政
之切也掌邦政者以司馬名之蓋示戎事
之莫急於此而其屬則有校人掌王六馬
有廋人掌十二閑趣馬齊其節巫馬治其
疾馬質平其賈牧師掌其地圉師主其教
圉人供其役設官多而立法詳若是聖人
之所重者亦可識矣至其取之於民則以
===
六千四百井之地而出馬百乗積而數之
誠若不可勝計而視後世則已省矣矧自
其井牧之法行而上下之間聯絡通貫國
有大事不待徵發之勞而無弗具集事已
兵休則渙然復故而已亦何病於擾哉由
周而來言馬政者凡幾變矣牧之官者典
守怠而侵牟起則病於國牧之民者亡失
多而輸納困則妨於民而
本朝實兼受其弊在今日則耗散窘迫之勢
punctuated: 官之政，難矣哉！雖然，有治人，無治法。法之立也，不能保其無弊；變而通之，亦存乎人焉爾矣。甞讀《周禮》，而知周公留意於馬政之切也。掌邦政者，以司馬名之，蓋示戎事之莫急於此。而其屬則有校人掌王六馬，有廋人掌十二閑，趣馬齊其節，巫馬治其疾，馬質平其賈，牧師掌其地，圉師主其教，圉人供其役。設官多而立法詳若是，聖人之所重者亦可識矣。至其取之於民，則以六千四百井之地而出馬百乗。積而數之，誠若不可勝計，而視後世則已省矣。矧自其井牧之法行，而上下之間聯絡通貫，國有大事，不待徵發之勞而無弗具集；事已兵休，則渙然復故而已，亦何病於擾哉？由周而來，言馬政者凡幾變矣！牧之官者，典守怠而侵牟起，則病於國；牧之民者，亡失多而輸納困，則妨於民。而本朝實兼受其弊，在今日則耗散窘迫之勢
translation_en:
…the institutions of the Offices of Zhou: how difficult it is to discuss them! Nevertheless, there are people who bring about good government, but no laws that do so of themselves. When laws are established, there is no assurance that they will remain free of abuses; adapting them so that they continue to work likewise depends upon people alone. I have read the Rites of Zhou and thereby learned how earnestly the Duke of Zhou attended to horse administration. The official responsible for the government of the realm was named Minister of War (sima, literally “director of horses”), indicating that nothing in military affairs was more urgent than this. Among his subordinates, the Director of Horses (jiaoren) managed the king’s six classes of horses; the Stable Master (souren) managed the twelve stables; the Horse Trainer (quma) regulated their routines; the Horse Veterinarian (wuma) treated their illnesses; the Horse Appraiser (mazhi) ensured fair prices for them; the Pasture Master (mushi) managed their grazing grounds; the Chief Groom (yushi) directed their training; and the Grooms (yuren) performed the necessary labor. With so many offices established and such detailed regulations laid down, we can recognize what the sage regarded as important.
As for what was required from the people, land comprising 6,400 jing, or well-field units, supplied horses for a hundred chariots. Added together and counted, their number would indeed seem beyond reckoning; yet compared with later ages, the burden was already light. Moreover, once the system of well-fields and pasturage was in operation, higher and lower levels were interconnected throughout. When the state faced a major undertaking, everything was assembled in readiness without the trouble of levying and mobilizing resources. Once the undertaking was over and the troops stood down, all dispersed and simply returned to their former condition. What suffering could such disturbances cause?
Since the Zhou, how many changes horse administration has undergone! When horses were raised by officials, their custodians grew negligent and embezzlement arose, harming the state. When horses were raised by the people, losses were numerous and delivery obligations burdensome, harming the people. Our dynasty has in fact suffered both kinds of abuse. Today, the depletion of resources and the pressure of straitened circumstances…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
極矣誠宜亟處而不容巳者以民牧之法
言之則宋熙寧保馬之舊也然牧必計丁
不問其願否不貰其他役則其害視宋益
甚矣矧孳生有供給之繁倒失有陪納之
費其所養且多羸劣無益戎行河洛齊魯
兩畿之民日困而
國家曾未得其利也為今之計亦惟優恤貧
弱蠲其積逋令民當出馬者輪直有差而
不復歲課其駒之入至於畿内之寄養孳
生者則官自牧之而不以煩民可矣近時
丘文莊公常論此欲即里社為廄舍寓官
牧於民養是或一說然愚恐其如昔人社
倉之制終貽擾民之害此或未易行耳以
招易之法言之亦宋熙寧茶馬之遺也然
名曰差發如田之有賦如身之有庸則國
體視彼為尊矣自金牌之制廢而私易行
給蕃之茶偽而官市沮故所得大抵駑下
徒費豢養洮河西寧三衛之卒苦之而邊
punctuated:
極矣，誠宜亟處而不容巳者。以民牧之法言之，則宋熙寧保馬之舊也。然牧必計丁，不問其願否，不貰其他役，則其害視宋益甚矣。矧孳生有供給之繁，倒失有陪納之費，其所養且多羸劣，無益戎行。河洛齊魯兩畿之民日困，而國家曾未得其利也。為今之計，亦惟優恤貧弱，蠲其積逋，令民當出馬者輪直有差，而不復歲課其駒之入。至於畿内之寄養孳生者，則官自牧之，而不以煩民可矣。近時丘文莊公常論此，欲即里社為廄舍，寓官牧於民養，是或一說。然愚恐其如昔人社倉之制，終貽擾民之害，此或未易行耳。
以招易之法言之，亦宋熙寧茶馬之遺也。然名曰差發，如田之有賦，如身之有庸，則國體視彼為尊矣。自金牌之制廢而私易行，給蕃之茶偽而官市沮，故所得大抵駑下，徒費豢養。洮河西寧三衛之卒苦之，而邊
translation_en:
…has reached an extreme; this truly calls for urgent action that admits of no delay. As for the system of having the people rear horses, it follows the horse-guarantee system of the Song dynasty’s Xining era. Yet horse-rearing obligations are assessed by the number of adult males, without regard to their willingness and without exemption from other services. Its harm is therefore even greater than under the Song. Moreover, breeding entails burdensome provisioning, while deaths and losses entail the expense of compensation. Most of the horses raised are weak and inferior, of no benefit to the army. The people of He, Luo, Qi, Lu, and the two metropolitan regions grow poorer by the day, yet the state has never obtained the benefit.
The only course now is to give generous relief to the poor and weak, remit their accumulated arrears, and have those obliged to supply horses take turns according to a graded schedule, without continuing to demand an annual delivery of their foals. As for horses entrusted to households for rearing and breeding within the metropolitan region, the authorities should rear them themselves, without burdening the people. Recently, Lord Qiu Wenzhuang discussed this, proposing to establish stables in village communities and incorporate official horse-rearing into household rearing. This is one possible proposal. Yet I fear that, like the community granary system of earlier times, it would ultimately bring the harm of harassment upon the people. It may therefore be difficult to implement.
As for the system of procuring horses through trade, this too is a legacy of the tea-for-horses system of the Song dynasty’s Xining era. Yet it is designated an obligatory levy, like the tax on land or the service obligation on an individual, and thus accords the state greater dignity than did the Song arrangement. Since the gold-token system was abolished, private trading has flourished; the tea supplied to the non-Han peoples has been adulterated, and official trade has been obstructed. Consequently, most horses obtained are inferior, merely wasting resources on their upkeep. The soldiers of the three guards of Taozhou, Hezhou, and Xining suffer from this, while the frontier…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
方非全賴其用也為今之計亦惟嚴設屯
戍以遏私販令茶之輸官者每篦皆精而
仍復往年招商之舊至於諸邊之奏乞開
中者則弗徇其請而專以易馬可矣近時
李文正公甞論此欲增馬直以啗羣胡捐
微利以收竒駿是誠良策然愚則以為我
聖祖差發之設實寓制戎之機此所當先復耳
抑馬政有可議者惟牧於官為善而執事
之問未之及也今欲振而起之則有二說
===
焉得其地也得其人也夫燕薊之地馬之
所生而秦隴汧渭之間有唐人監牧之迹
今草塲侵没寓曠土多汙萊矣能覈實以
歸官則芻牧何患乎無資廐寺之官牧政
所寄而撫諭巡察之職又督率作興之機
今選用滅裂而更代者不常矣能精擇而
久任則綱紀何患乎不舉如是則可以復
祖宗之政而侵據有罰倒失有罰尅減盗易者
有罰凡可以為馬之害無不去也可以行
punctuated:
方非全賴其用也。為今之計，亦惟嚴設屯戍以遏私販，令茶之輸官者每篦皆精，而仍復往年招商之舊。至於諸邊之奏乞開中者，則弗徇其請，而專以易馬可矣。近時李文正公甞論此，欲增馬直以啗羣胡，捐微利以收竒駿，是誠良策。然愚則以為我聖祖差發之設，實寓制戎之機，此所當先復耳。
抑馬政有可議者，惟牧於官為善，而執事之問未之及也。今欲振而起之，則有二說焉：得其地也，得其人也。夫燕薊之地，馬之所生，而秦隴汧渭之間，有唐人監牧之迹。今草塲侵没，寓曠土多汙萊矣。能覈實以歸官，則芻牧何患乎無資？廐寺之官，牧政所寄，而撫諭巡察之職，又督率作興之機。今選用滅裂，而更代者不常矣。能精擇而久任，則綱紀何患乎不舉？如是，則可以復祖宗之政，而侵據有罰，倒失有罰，尅減盗易者有罰，凡可以為馬之害，無不去也。可以行
translation_en:
…the frontier does not depend entirely on their service. The present course should simply be to establish strict garrison controls to stop illicit trading, ensure that every basket [?] of tea delivered to the authorities is of fine quality, and restore the former practice of recruiting merchants. As for memorials from the various frontier regions requesting that merchants be allowed to obtain tea through the delivery of supplies, their requests should not be granted; the tea should be reserved exclusively for exchange for horses. Recently, Lord Li Wenzheng discussed this, proposing to raise the price paid for horses to entice the various Hu peoples, sacrificing a small profit to acquire exceptional steeds. This is indeed a sound policy. Yet in my humble view, our sagely founding emperor’s institution of requisitions embodied a means of controlling the Rong peoples. This is what should first be restored.
There is, however, another point concerning horse administration worth discussing: the best approach is to rear horses under official management, but your question has not addressed it. To revive this system now requires two things: obtaining suitable land and obtaining suitable men. The lands of Yan and Ji produce horses, while between Qin, Long, Qian, and Wei there remain traces of the Tang dynasty’s state horse pastures. Today the grazing grounds have been encroached upon and lost, and extensive vacant lands [?] have largely become overgrown wasteland. If these holdings can be investigated and restored to official possession, why worry that fodder and pasture will lack resources? The officials of the Court of the Imperial Stud are entrusted with administering horse breeding, while the duties of admonition and inspection provide the means to supervise and revitalize it. Today appointments are made carelessly, and replacements occur irregularly. If men can be carefully selected and retained in office for long terms, why worry that discipline and order will not be maintained? In this way, the administration of our imperial ancestors can be restored: there will be penalties for encroachment and unauthorized occupation, penalties for deaths and losses, and penalties for those who make illicit deductions, steal, or substitute horses. Everything that might harm the horses will be eliminated. It will be possible to implement…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
周官之政而攻駒有法講馭有法游牝去
特者有法凡可以為馬之利者無不興也
亦何必襲宋人之弊法以重困吾民哉雖
然得其地易得其人難是二者之輕重亦
可知也故曰存乎人焉爾矣
punctuated: 周官之政，而攻駒有法，講馭有法，游牝去特者有法，凡可以為馬之利者，無不興也。亦何必襲宋人之弊法，以重困吾民哉！雖然，得其地易，得其人難，是二者之輕重亦可知也。故曰：存乎人焉爾矣。
translation_en: …the administration prescribed in the Offices of Zhou: there would be proper methods for castrating colts, for training in driving, and for turning mares out to breed and removing stallions. Every measure beneficial to horses would be put into effect. Why, then, must we follow the defective methods of the Song and thereby further burden our people? Nevertheless, obtaining suitable land is easy; obtaining suitable men is difficult. The relative importance of these two can thus be understood. Hence I say: it depends upon the men, and that is all.

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄後序
我
高皇帝立國之明年即建學弘化
又明年
詔開科取士俾士各專一經以効
用諸所科條盡刷漢唐以來
苟簡之規而敺之古將以成
===
全才也是以百六十年于茲
涵育既久人文鬯達昌大衍
溢之才相望于海內顧各省
校文專限學職而議其不便
者亦久矣恭遇
皇上釐敝更化百度咸貞時惟戊
子鄉試爰稽故事分
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄後序

我高皇帝立國之明年，即建學弘化。又明年，詔開科取士，俾士各專一經以効用。諸所科條，盡刷漢唐以來苟簡之規，而敺之古，將以成全才也。是以百六十年于茲，涵育既久，人文鬯達，昌大衍溢之才相望于海內。顧各省校文專限學職，而議其不便者亦久矣。恭遇皇上釐敝更化，百度咸貞。時惟戊子鄉試，爰稽故事，分
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

In the year after founding the dynasty, our Emperor Gao established schools to extend moral transformation. In the following year, he decreed the opening of examinations to recruit scholars, requiring each to specialize in one Classic so that he could render service. All the regulations swept away the makeshift practices inherited from the Han and Tang dynasties and directed scholars toward antiquity, with the aim of developing fully rounded talent. Thus, over the 160 years down to the present, prolonged cultivation has brought literary culture to full expression, and men of abundant and expansive talent have appeared throughout the realm in succession. Yet the assessment of examination essays in each province was restricted exclusively to educational officials, and the disadvantages of this arrangement had long been debated.

We have reverently witnessed His Majesty remedy abuses and renew governance, setting all institutions in proper order. At the time of the Provincial Examination in the wuzi year [1528], precedents were accordingly consulted, and separately …

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
遣廷臣爲各省考試官錄士之
文率尚平實爾雅思得醇篤
眞材以資化理乃六月丁卯
上方精白載嘗以承休慶而臣粲
臣鑰寔受
命典試浙中深以謭劣弗稱是𢗅
至則合諸事事者鎖院試之
===
三而防檢經理加密矣因得
一省多士之文而熟觀之淵
乎理之奧也浩乎政之藏也
蔚乎氣之光也文運道化風
行海流顧茲藩亦極盛也已
竊嘗論之理精矣貴得也政
達矣貴純也文盛矣貴不窮
punctuated: 遣廷臣爲各省考試官，錄士之文率尚平實爾雅，思得醇篤眞材，以資化理。乃六月丁卯，上方精白載嘗，以承休慶，而臣粲、臣鑰寔受命典試浙中，深以謭劣弗稱是𢗅。至則合諸事事者，鎖院試之三，而防檢經理加密矣。因得一省多士之文而熟觀之：淵乎，理之奧也；浩乎，政之藏也；蔚乎，氣之光也。文運道化，風行海流，顧茲藩亦極盛也已。竊嘗論之：理精矣，貴得也；政達矣，貴純也；文盛矣，貴不窮
translation_en:
…dispatched court officials to serve as Examiners in the various provinces. In selecting candidates’ compositions, they generally prized plain substance and refined correctness, seeking genuine talent of integrity and sincerity to assist moral transformation and governance. On the dingmao day of the sixth month, His Majesty was then, with utmost purity of purpose, performing the seasonal offering [?] to receive auspicious blessings. Your servants Can and Yue duly received the command to preside over the examination in Zhejiang, deeply concerned [?] that our limited abilities were unequal to the charge. Upon arrival, we assembled all those responsible for the work, entered the sealed examination compound, and conducted the examination in three sessions. Precautions, inspections, and administrative arrangements were made still more rigorous.

We thus obtained the compositions of the many candidates of the entire province and examined them closely. How profound their exploration of principle’s mysteries! How vast their store of knowledge of government! How splendid the radiance of their vital force! Literary flourishing and the transforming influence of the Way spread like wind and flowed like the sea. This province, indeed, had attained the height of prosperity.

I have ventured to reflect upon this: when understanding of principle is refined, what matters is truly grasping it; when knowledge of government is comprehensive, what matters is its purity; when literary expression flourishes, what matters is that it remain inexhaustible…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
則通通則一不專則不信不
達而無所於得百物匱而六
學窮矣故示之以弗兼寔引
而深之以俟其通耳若或施
之有政而弗果於用畏且遷
焉弗周于用窒且踣焉則六
經一筌蹄耳矣而亦何貴於
===
專哉我
皇祖首詔作成之意殆不若是也
夫豈獨作成之意有在我
皇上今日
側席之懷亦夫人所可測而知
也諸士子獲登兹選幾於專
以精矣博以達矣其將守之
punctuated: 則通，通則一。不專則不信，不達而無所於得，百物匱而六學窮矣。故示之以弗兼，寔引而深之，以俟其通耳。若或施之有政而弗果於用，畏且遷焉；弗周于用，窒且踣焉，則六經一筌蹄耳矣，而亦何貴於專哉！我皇祖首詔作成之意，殆不若是也。夫豈獨作成之意有在？我皇上今日側席之懷，亦夫人所可測而知也。諸士子獲登兹選，幾於專以精矣，博以達矣，其將守之
translation_en: …then understanding becomes comprehensive; when comprehensive, it becomes unified. Without specialization, one lacks assured understanding; without comprehensive understanding, one gains nothing. Knowledge of the myriad things is impoverished, and learning in the six disciplines reaches an impasse. Thus, instructing students not to undertake everything at once is in fact a means of guiding them into deeper study, awaiting their eventual comprehensive understanding. If, however, when applying their learning to government, they lack resolve in putting it to use, they will become fearful and waver; if they cannot apply it comprehensively, they will become obstructed and stumble. Then the Six Classics are merely fish traps and rabbit snares—means to an end. What value, then, is there in specialization? Such can hardly have been the intention of our imperial ancestor when he first decreed the cultivation of talent. Yet it is not only his intention to cultivate talent that has a deeper purpose. Our present emperor’s eagerness to receive worthy men—sitting with a place beside him left vacant—is likewise something everyone can discern and understand. You scholars who have succeeded in this selection have come close to achieving refinement through specialization and comprehensive understanding through breadth of learning. Will you hold fast to this…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
終身而弗畏弗遷矣乎其將
局於一藝而弗利弗安矣乎
今之登玆選者固他日致用
之地也敢於試事告竣因以
諗之
承德郎兵部武庫清吏司署
郎中事主事華鑰謹序
punctuated:
終身而弗畏弗遷矣乎？其將局於一藝而弗利弗安矣乎？今之登玆選者，固他日致用之地也。敢於試事告竣，因以諗之。
承德郎、兵部武庫清吏司署郎中事主事華鑰謹序。
translation_en:
…throughout their lives, without fear or wavering? Or will they confine themselves to a single field of learning, finding neither advantage nor ease in it? Selection in this examination today is indeed the foundation for putting their abilities to use in the future. As the examination proceedings draw to a close, I venture to offer them these words of counsel.
Preface respectfully written by Hua Yue 華鑰, Gentleman for Receiving Virtue and Secretary acting as Director of the Bureau of Armories in the Ministry of War.

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄序
嘉靖戊子秋八月浙江鄉試
給事中臣粲郎中臣鑰寔奉
命主之臣粲竊惟浙江古揚州之
境而今之首藩也粤自我
皇祖起南服定金陵遂下浙東西
諸郡方
===
國家草創日不暇給而崇禮樂
考文章搢紳先生出入風議
訢訢如也其間二三耆碩參
侍帷幄者大抵皆自浙起以
博學贍辭潤色鴻業於是
皇明之號令典法炳焉與三代同
風而浙之文遂先天下粲不
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄序

嘉靖戊子秋八月，浙江鄉試，給事中臣粲、郎中臣鑰寔奉命主之。臣粲竊惟浙江，古揚州之境，而今之首藩也。粤自我皇祖起南服，定金陵，遂下浙東西諸郡。方國家草創，日不暇給，而崇禮樂，考文章，搢紳先生出入風議，訢訢如也。其間二三耆碩參侍帷幄者，大抵皆自浙起，以博學贍辭潤色鴻業。於是皇明之號令典法，炳焉與三代同風，而浙之文遂先天下。粲不
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination
