In the eighth month of autumn in the wuzi year of Jiajing [1528], your servants Can, Supervising Secretary, and Yue, Bureau Director, duly received the imperial command to preside over the Zhejiang Provincial Examination. Your servant Can humbly considers that Zhejiang lay within the territory of ancient Yangzhou and is now foremost among the provinces. When our imperial ancestor arose in the southern lands and established his capital at Jinling, he proceeded to conquer the prefectures of eastern and western Zhejiang. At that time, the dynasty was newly founded, and each day scarcely afforded time to meet its pressing needs. Yet rites and music were honored, and literary compositions examined. Learned gentlemen of official standing came and went, offering counsel in a spirit of cheerful harmony. Among them, the few venerable scholars who attended the sovereign in his inner councils had, for the most part, risen from Zhejiang. With their broad learning and ample eloquence, they lent lustre to the grand imperial enterprise. Thus the august Ming’s proclamations, commands, institutions, and laws shone forth in the same spirit as those of the Three Dynasties, and Zhejiang’s literary achievement consequently took precedence throughout the realm. I, Can, do not …

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有若陸贄者司考校而韓愈
輩出焉天下至于今稱之然
愈嘗自言其當時程試之文
以爲讀之使人忸怩而已耳
其信然乎抑有激而云爾也
夫唐之文初亦失之靡矣自
愈出然後一振之以復于古
===
彼所謂豪傑之士者非邪而
其始也微贄孰能知而取之
我
國家稽古立法以經術造士百
六十年治敎熈洽文亦日趨
于盛學士大夫操筆伸紙類
能達其所欲言者顧藻飾有
punctuated:
有若陸贄者司考校，而韓愈輩出焉，天下至于今稱之。然愈嘗自言其當時程試之文，以爲讀之使人忸怩而已耳。其信然乎？抑有激而云爾也？夫唐之文，初亦失之靡矣，自愈出，然後一振之以復于古。彼所謂豪傑之士者非邪？而其始也，微贄，孰能知而取之？

我國家稽古立法，以經術造士，百六十年，治敎熈洽，文亦日趨于盛。學士大夫操筆伸紙，類能達其所欲言者。顧藻飾有
translation_en:
There was Lu Zhi 陸贄, who presided over the examinations, from which Han Yu 韓愈 and others emerged; the world praises him to this day. Yet Han Yu once said of his own examination writings at the time that reading them merely made one blush with embarrassment. Was this truly so? Or did some provocation lead him to say it? Tang prose, too, initially erred toward florid extravagance. Only after Han Yu emerged was it reinvigorated and restored to the ancient models. Was he not one of those called men of outstanding talent? Yet at the outset, had it not been for Lu Zhi, who could have recognized and selected him?

Our dynasty has examined antiquity to establish its institutions and nurtured scholars through classical learning. For one hundred and sixty years, governance and moral instruction have flourished in harmony, while literary composition has daily grown more accomplished. Scholars and officials take up their brushes and spread out their paper, and generally can express what they wish to say. Yet, of ornate embellishment there is …

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
餘而朴茂忠實之意視前輩
若少衰焉當是時其亦有豪
傑者出而振之而司考校者
亦能知而取之乎
聖天子方篤意敎化屢詔所司選
師儒嚴條約將責士以有本
之學而非直曰文云者故屬
===
者之舉雖有司存而特
簡近臣涖之意嚮所在昭然可識
士於是時有弗自奮也者非
夫也况若浙之嘗以文先天
下者哉將必有異才焉如愈
者卓然出其間乎得若人以
稱塞
punctuated:
餘，而朴茂忠實之意視前輩若少衰焉。當是時，其亦有豪傑者出而振之，而司考校者亦能知而取之乎？
聖天子方篤意敎化，屢詔所司選師儒、嚴條約，將責士以有本之學，而非直曰文云者。故屬者之舉，雖有司存，而特簡近臣涖之，意嚮所在，昭然可識。士於是時有弗自奮也者，非夫也。况若浙之嘗以文先天下者哉！將必有異才焉，如愈者卓然出其間乎？得若人以稱塞
translation_en:
…in excess, while the spirit of simplicity, substance, loyalty, and sincerity seems somewhat diminished compared with that of earlier generations. At such a time, will outstanding men emerge to revive it, and will those charged with examining candidates be able to recognize and select them?
The sagely Son of Heaven is now deeply committed to moral instruction. He has repeatedly commanded the responsible officials to select learned teachers and enforce regulations strictly, intending to require of scholars learning with a sound foundation, rather than mere literary accomplishment. Thus, for the recent examination, although the regular officials were in place, he specially selected ministers close to him to oversee it. The direction of his intentions is plain to see. A scholar who fails to exert himself at such a time is no true man. How much more must this apply to Zhejiang, which has previously led the realm in literary accomplishment! Will there surely be an exceptional talent, someone like Yu, who emerges conspicuously from their midst? To obtain such a man, and thereby answer and fulfill…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
明詔則司考校者之責任亦無負
矣而愧無贄之明弗能識也
抑所謂公無私者或庶幾焉
爾矣是舉也同考試則學正
孫鰲凌雲教諭鄭子充徐逵
宋大本唐佐吳畀陳岳林汝
永毛鳳監臨則巡按監察御
===
史張問行申飭藩臬百務具
舉提調則左布政使潘旦右
布政使劉節監試則按察使
桑溥副使傅鑰遴士以試則
提學副使萬潮協贊于外則
監察御史王化工部主事郭
秉聰南京戶部主事王銳參
punctuated:
明詔，則司考校者之責任亦無負矣。而愧無贄之明，弗能識也。抑所謂公無私者，或庶幾焉爾矣。
是舉也，同考試則學正孫鰲、凌雲，教諭鄭子充、徐逵、宋大本、唐佐、吳畀、陳岳、林汝永、毛鳳；監臨則巡按監察御史張問行，申飭藩臬，百務具舉；提調則左布政使潘旦、右布政使劉節；監試則按察使桑溥、副使傅鑰；遴士以試則提學副使萬潮；協贊于外則監察御史王化、工部主事郭秉聰、南京戶部主事王銳、參
translation_en:
…the illustrious imperial edict, then those charged with examining and assessing the candidates will also have fulfilled their responsibility. Yet I am ashamed that I lack Zhi’s discernment and cannot recognize such men. Still, I may perhaps come close to what is called being fair and free of private bias.
For this examination, the Associate Examiners were Sun Ao and Ling Yun, instructors in prefectural schools, and Zheng Zichong, Xu Kui, Song Daben, Tang Zuo, Wu Bi, Chen Yue, Lin Ruyong, and Mao Feng, instructors in county schools. The Supervising Official was Zhang Wenxing, Regional Inspector, who issued admonitory instructions to the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions, ensuring that all duties were carried out. The Proctors were Pan Dan, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Liu Jie, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner. Those overseeing the examination were Sang Pu, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and Fu Yue, Surveillance Vice Commissioner. Wan Chao, Surveillance Vice Commissioner for Education, selected the candidates to sit the examination. Those providing assistance outside the examination compound were Wang Hua, Investigating Censor; Guo Bingcong, Secretary in the Ministry of Works; Wang Rui, Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; and the Assistant…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
政胡纘宗葉寛朱裳叅議萬
廷彩龐浩副使党以平何鰲
汪金僉事孫元巴思明梁世
驃江良材都指揮僉事張浩
李節士就試者二千八百有
奇預選者九十人刻其文之
優者二十一篇合諸執事姓
名爲錄以
獻粲序之
從仕郎工科給事中陸粲謹
序
punctuated:
政胡纘宗、葉寛、朱裳，叅議萬廷彩、龐浩，副使党以平、何鰲、汪金，僉事孫元、巴思明、梁世驃、江良材，都指揮僉事張浩、李節。士就試者二千八百有奇，預選者九十人。刻其文之優者二十一篇，合諸執事姓名爲錄，以獻。粲序之。
從仕郎、工科給事中陸粲謹序。
translation_en:
…Administration Vice Commissioners Hu Zuanzong, Ye Kuan, and Zhu Shang; Administration Assistant Commissioners Wan Tingcai and Pang Hao; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Dang Yiping, He Ao, and Wang Jin; Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Sun Yuan, Ba Siming, Liang Shibiao, and Jiang Liangcai; and Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Zhang Hao and Li Jie.
More than 2,800 candidates sat the examination, and ninety were selected. Twenty-one of their finest essays were engraved for printing and combined with the names of the officials involved to form a record for presentation to the throne. I, Can, have written its preface.
Respectfully prefaced by Lu Can, Gentleman for Attendant Service and Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Works.

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
福建福州府長樂縣儒學教諭唐佐〔一夔廣西臨桂縣人丙子貢士〕
廣東廣州府番禺縣儒學教諭吳畀〔汝畏福建龍溪縣人壬午貢士〕
福建福州府懷安縣儒學教諭陳岳〔舜咨廣東海陽縣人丙子貢士〕
直隸大名府南樂縣儒學教諭林滚〔若脩福建莆田縣人壬午貢士〕
直隸鳳陽府懷遠縣儒學教諭毛鳳〔伯鳴廣西桂林中衛籍湖廣益陽縣人壬午貢士〕
印卷官
浙江等處承宣布政使司經歷司經歷賈鋼〔世用萬全都司龍門衛人監生〕
浙江等處提刑按察司經歷司經歷于重〔邦信遼東廣寧前屯衛人監生〕
收掌試卷官
===
兩浙都轉運鹽使司運使吳瓚〔廷灇直隸休寧縣人戊辰進士〕
湖州府知府萬雲鵬〔圖南直隸鹽城縣人甲戌進士〕
受卷官
杭州府知府陳力〔以相四川內江縣人甲戌進士〕
寧波府推官王守〔履約直隸吳縣人丙戌進士〕

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
復則不妄矣故受之以无妄
書
人心惟危道心惟微惟精惟一允執厥中
朝夕納誨以輔台德
王省惟歲卿士惟月師尹惟日
受王嘉師監于茲祥刑
詩
葛之覃兮施于中谷維葉莫莫是刈是濩
爲絺爲綌服之無斁
===
宜爾室家樂爾妻帑是究是圖亶其然乎
追琢其章金玉其相勉勉我王綱紀四方
紹庭上下陟降厥家休矣皇考以保明其
身
春秋
公會齊侯于防〔隱公九年〕
楚子蔡侯次于厥貉〔文公十年〕公會宋公
陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯晉趙盾癸酉
同盟于新城〔文公十有四年〕
punctuated:
復則不妄矣，故受之以无妄。

書
人心惟危，道心惟微，惟精惟一，允執厥中。
朝夕納誨，以輔台德。
王省惟歲，卿士惟月，師尹惟日。
受王嘉師，監于茲祥刑。

詩
葛之覃兮，施于中谷，維葉莫莫。是刈是濩，爲絺爲綌，服之無斁。
宜爾室家，樂爾妻帑。是究是圖，亶其然乎？
追琢其章，金玉其相。勉勉我王，綱紀四方。
紹庭上下，陟降厥家。休矣皇考，以保明其身。

春秋
公會齊侯于防〔隱公九年〕。
楚子、蔡侯次于厥貉〔文公十年〕。公會宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯、晉趙盾，癸酉，同盟于新城〔文公十有四年〕。
translation_en:
…When there is a return, there is no falsity; therefore it is followed by Without Falsehood (Wuwang).

Book of Documents
The human mind is precarious; the mind of the Way is subtle. Be discerning and single-minded, and sincerely hold fast to the mean.
Morning and evening, offer admonitions to assist my virtue.
The king examines affairs by the year, the ministers by the month, and the heads of offices by the day.
You who have charge of the king’s good people, take these beneficent punishments as your guide.

Book of Odes
The kudzu vines spread out into the midst of the valley, their leaves luxuriant. They are cut and boiled, made into fine and coarse cloth, and worn without weariness.
Bring harmony to your household and joy to your wife and children. Examine this and consider it: is it truly so?
Carved and polished is his pattern; gold and jade are his substance. Diligently our king orders and regulates the four quarters.
He continues the ancestral ways in his court, above and below; he ascends and descends within his house. Glorious is his august deceased father, who thereby protects and brings lustre to his person.

Spring and Autumn Annals
The duke met the Marquis of Qi at Fang. 〔Ninth year of Duke Yin.〕
The Viscount of Chu and the Marquis of Cai encamped at Juehe. 〔Tenth year of Duke Wen.〕 The duke met the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, and Zhao Dun of Jin. On the guiyou day, they jointly concluded a covenant at Xincheng. 〔Fourteenth year of Duke Wen.〕

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
擬漢令郡國舉孝廉詔元光元年
擬唐以孫伏伽為治書侍御史誥武德元
年
擬宋開天章閣引輔臣入對參知政事范
仲淹謝表慶曆三年
判語五條
上言大臣德政
檢踏災傷田糧
禁止師巫邪術
===
關防內使出入
失時不修隄防
第參場
策五道
問古之有國家者必封建宗親以藩王室
我
太祖高皇帝肇創大業廣樹
親藩布列天下磐石之宗萬世永賴旣又親
作
punctuated:
擬漢令郡國舉孝廉詔，元光元年。
擬唐以孫伏伽為治書侍御史誥，武德元年。
擬宋開天章閣引輔臣入對參知政事范仲淹謝表，慶曆三年。

判語五條：
上言大臣德政。
檢踏災傷田糧。
禁止師巫邪術。
關防內使出入。
失時不修隄防。

第參場
策五道

問：古之有國家者，必封建宗親以藩王室。我太祖高皇帝肇創大業，廣樹親藩，布列天下，磐石之宗，萬世永賴。旣又親作
translation_en:
Draft an edict of the Han ordering the commanderies and kingdoms to recommend men distinguished for filial devotion and integrity (xiaolian). First year of Yuanguang (134 BCE).
Draft a proclamation of the Tang appointing Sun Fujia as Censor for Legal Affairs. First year of Wude (618).
Draft a memorial of thanks by Fan Zhongyan, Vice Administrator of the Council of State, upon the Song emperor’s opening the Tianzhang Pavilion and summoning his chief ministers for an audience. Third year of Qingli (1043).

Five legal judgments:
Reporting to the throne on the virtuous administration of high officials.
Inspecting disaster-stricken farmland and its grain-tax assessment.
Prohibiting the heterodox arts of ritual masters and spirit mediums.
Controlling the entry and exit of palace eunuchs.
Failing to repair dikes in the proper season.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: Those who ruled states in antiquity invariably enfeoffed members of their own lineage to serve as bulwarks of the royal house. Our Emperor Taizu Gao, when founding his great enterprise, established princely fiefs for his kinsmen far and wide, distributing them throughout the realm. His lineage, firm as a massive rock, would remain a support for ten thousand generations. He subsequently also personally composed…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
祖訓以貽
東宫及
諸王使世守焉數傳之後本支益昌敦睦之
風内外隆洽所以恪遵
訓典者至矣自今觀之猶竊有未安於心者夫
歲禄時賜禮秩有定矣然支庶日蕃而
勢將不贍何以處之而使無戚戚具爾
之心樂善好禮賢名有聞矣然稍踰檢
制者亦未嘗無也何以道之而使有卓
===
爾不羣之行抑又有異焉者親賢並用
故事也今連姻
帝胄則仕者不得通籍京朝内外均勞常法
也今備位藩僚則終身無遷轉之望果
皇祖之訓則然乎抑别有據乎是皆關繫政體
之大者願一言之將轉
聞焉以為
當宁法
祖睦親之助
punctuated: 《祖訓》以貽東宫及諸王，使世守焉。數傳之後，本支益昌，敦睦之風内外隆洽，所以恪遵訓典者至矣。自今觀之，猶竊有未安於心者。夫歲禄時賜，禮秩有定矣，然支庶日蕃，而勢將不贍，何以處之，而使無戚戚具爾之心？樂善好禮，賢名有聞矣，然稍踰檢制者亦未嘗無也，何以道之，而使有卓爾不羣之行？抑又有異焉者：親賢並用，故事也，今連姻帝胄，則仕者不得通籍京朝；内外均勞，常法也，今備位藩僚，則終身無遷轉之望。果皇祖之訓則然乎？抑别有據乎？是皆關繫政體之大者，願一言之，將轉聞焉，以為當宁法祖睦親之助。
translation_en:
… the Ancestral Instructions (Zuxun), to be bequeathed to the Crown Prince and the princes, for them to observe generation after generation. After several generations, the principal and collateral branches have flourished ever more abundantly, and a spirit of familial affection and harmony has spread fully within and beyond the court. Their reverent observance of these instructions has been exemplary. Yet, viewed from the present, there remain matters about which we privately feel uneasy.

Annual stipends and occasional grants have fixed scales prescribed by ritual and rank. Yet the collateral descendants grow more numerous daily, and resources will inevitably become insufficient. How should this be managed so that these brothers and kinsmen harbor no feelings of distress? They delight in goodness and cherish ritual propriety, and their worthy reputations are widely known. Nevertheless, there have also been some who somewhat overstep the restraints and regulations. How should they be guided so that their conduct becomes outstanding and exceptional?

There are, moreover, other anomalies. Employing both imperial relatives and worthy men is established precedent; yet nowadays, when someone becomes related by marriage to imperial descendants, those holding office may not be enrolled for service at the capital court. Sharing the burdens of service between the capital and the provinces is the regular rule; yet nowadays, those appointed to the staff of a princely establishment have no prospect of transfer or promotion throughout their lives. Do the instructions of the imperial ancestor truly prescribe this, or is there some other authority for it? These are all major matters concerning the structure of governance. We ask you to address them, so that your words may be transmitted to the throne and help the reigning emperor follow his ancestor’s example and maintain harmony with his imperial kin.

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
問廉恥者士人之美節風俗者天下之大
事也古昔人知自重行已有恥而習以
相安此豈一朝一夕之故哉秦漢而下
士多隨世以就功名守義者少尚通者
多其間明君賢輔間嘗崇獎高潔以激
厲一時如不拜諫議遇以故人不受右
相待爲賓友固辭諫官特加待制安於
靜退乞賜甄擢私書不至京師召復御
史問訊不及政府薦充館職若此者可
===
歷數其人歟我
國家所以造士道民者率由禮義廉恥而又
風勸養厲于其間宜乎道德可一風俗
可同也夫何習俗尚未盡美而士風亦
未盡淳恬退者固多冒進者猶或間有
其故何歟恭遇
皇上聖資高明動稽堯舜力欲挽回隆古之盛
茲固首務也歷考前聞或謂退讓不可
以刑罰使或謂莫若倡清議于天下或
punctuated: 問：廉恥者，士人之美節；風俗者，天下之大事也。古昔人知自重，行已有恥，而習以相安，此豈一朝一夕之故哉？秦漢而下，士多隨世以就功名，守義者少，尚通者多。其間明君賢輔，間嘗崇獎高潔，以激厲一時。如不拜諫議，遇以故人；不受右相，待爲賓友；固辭諫官，特加待制；安於靜退，乞賜甄擢；私書不至京師，召復御史；問訊不及政府，薦充館職。若此者，可歷數其人歟？我國家所以造士道民者，率由禮義廉恥，而又風勸養厲于其間，宜乎道德可一，風俗可同也。夫何習俗尚未盡美，而士風亦未盡淳？恬退者固多，冒進者猶或間有，其故何歟？恭遇皇上聖資高明，動稽堯舜，力欲挽回隆古之盛，茲固首務也。歷考前聞，或謂退讓不可以刑罰使，或謂莫若倡清議于天下，或
translation_en:
Question: Integrity and a sense of shame are admirable virtues in scholars; customs and mores are matters of great consequence to the realm. In antiquity, people knew to respect themselves and had a sense of shame in their conduct; through habitual practice, they lived together at ease. Could this have come about in a single morning or evening? From the Qin and Han onward, scholars mostly followed the times in pursuit of achievement and renown. Few upheld righteousness; many prized advancement. During this period, enlightened rulers and worthy ministers sometimes honored and rewarded men of lofty integrity, thereby inspiring their contemporaries. For example, one declined appointment as Grand Master of Remonstrance and was treated as an old friend; another refused appointment as Right Chief Councilor and was treated as an honored guest and friend; another firmly declined a remonstrance post and was specially granted the title of Auxiliary Academician; another was content in quiet retirement, and a request was made that he be selected for promotion; another sent no private letters to the capital and was recalled to serve again as Investigating Censor; another sent no greetings or inquiries to the chief councilors and was recommended for a post in a literary institute. Can you enumerate these men individually?

Our dynasty cultivates scholars and guides the people consistently through ritual propriety, righteousness, integrity, and a sense of shame, further encouraging, nurturing, and inspiring them in these pursuits. Surely moral principles should thereby be unified and customs brought into accord. Why, then, are prevailing customs still less than wholly admirable, and the ethos of scholars still less than wholly pure? Although many are content to remain in retirement, some still seek advancement presumptuously. What is the reason?

We reverently live under His Majesty, whose sagely endowments are lofty and enlightened, who takes Yao and Shun as his models in every action, and who strives to restore the flourishing age of high antiquity. This is certainly a foremost concern. Examining the teachings handed down from the past, we find that some say modest yielding cannot be imposed through punishments; others say nothing is better than promoting upright public judgment throughout the realm; others …

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
謂崇靜退以率之或謂妙求人物參錯
立朝之數說者施之于今何者爲當抑
别有其本乎願相與一論之
問孔門學者以德行言語政事文學並稱
而獨稱顏子爲好學曰不遷怒不貳過
夷考之其過與怒無聞焉顏子嘗曰夫
子博我以文約我以禮亦不見其所謂
文也然則顏子所好果何學歟自是千
有餘年獨宋儒有曰學顏子之所學曰
===
顏子示不違如愚之學於後世曰顏子
之學與今之學異觀其道之所傳有天
資出人造養深遠者有探索本原洞見
道體者有默坐澄心體認天理者而皆
不涉於言語文字之間豈即所謂顏子
之學歟厥後朱子繼出乃取聖賢之遺
言遺旨發明精蘊自有經傳以來著述
之盛一人而已其書一出天下家傳而
人誦之學者曉然趨道之至正誠所謂
punctuated:
謂崇靜退以率之，或謂妙求人物，參錯立朝之數說者，施之于今，何者爲當？抑别有其本乎？願相與一論之。

問：孔門學者以德行、言語、政事、文學並稱，而獨稱顏子爲好學，曰：「不遷怒，不貳過。」夷考之，其過與怒無聞焉。顏子嘗曰：「夫子博我以文，約我以禮。」亦不見其所謂文也。然則顏子所好果何學歟？自是千有餘年，獨宋儒有曰：「學顏子之所學。」曰：「顏子示不違如愚之學於後世。」曰：「顏子之學與今之學異。」觀其道之所傳，有天資出人、造養深遠者，有探索本原、洞見道體者，有默坐澄心、體認天理者，而皆不涉於言語文字之間，豈即所謂顏子之學歟？厥後朱子繼出，乃取聖賢之遺言遺旨，發明精蘊。自有經傳以來，著述之盛，一人而已。其書一出，天下家傳而人誦之，學者曉然趨道之至正，誠所謂
translation_en:
…say that those who are composed and retiring should be honored to lead others by example; others say that outstanding men should be discerningly sought out and placed together in varied positions at court. Of these several proposals, which would be appropriate to put into practice today? Or is there some other fundamental basis? We invite you to discuss this together.

Question: The disciples of Confucius were celebrated alike for virtuous conduct, speech, government service, and literary learning. Yet Yanzi alone was praised as loving learning, with the words: “He did not transfer his anger to others, nor repeat a fault.” On careful examination, however, we hear nothing of his faults or anger. Yanzi once said: “The Master broadens me through cultural learning and restrains me through ritual.” Yet here too we do not see what this cultural learning actually was. What learning, then, did Yanzi truly love? For more than a thousand years thereafter, it was only among the Song Confucians that someone said, “Learn what Yanzi learned”; another said, “Yanzi showed later generations the learning of one who did not contradict his teacher and seemed foolish”; and another said, “Yanzi’s learning differs from the learning of today.” Looking at those through whom this Way was transmitted, some possessed exceptional natural gifts and attained profound cultivation; some investigated the fundamental source and perceived the substance of the Way with penetrating insight; and some sat silently, clearing their minds and apprehending heavenly principle. Yet all of these proceeded without involvement in speech or writing. Was this, then, what is called Yanzi’s learning? Subsequently, Zhuzi emerged and took up the words and underlying intentions bequeathed by the sages and worthies, elucidating their subtle depths. Since the inception of the classics and their commentaries, he alone has achieved such a wealth of writings. Once his books appeared, households throughout the realm passed them down and people recited them. Learners clearly understood how to advance toward the utmost rectitude of the Way. This truly is what is called…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
家何以捄之徵斂無經而輸納之費動
至數倍何以省之徭役有常期矣而輕
重失均何以平之田賦有定額矣而詭
射之弊至不可勝窮何以釐之民多轉
徙而荒蕪未闢又遺其稅以為公私之
累何以處之水利有專官而旱潦不免
於涸溢何以拯之當是時欲求經常簡
易之法可以弭斯患者非豪傑之士誰
與議此故願諸君之極言之也
===
問記稱問國之富數馬以對馬之所繫亦
重矣考之周禮大司馬之屬有校人以
掌王六馬有廋人以掌十二閑又有趣
馬巫馬馬質牧師圉師圉人之類夫一
事而設官之多如此無乃失之冗與至
其取之民者自丘甸以上積而數之至
於一同之地出戎馬百乘亦不為不多
矣不識當時國有征役何以能弗擾而
事集與抑其法亦可用於今日否與今
punctuated:
家，何以捄之？徵斂無經，而輸納之費動至數倍，何以省之？徭役有常期矣，而輕重失均，何以平之？田賦有定額矣，而詭射之弊至不可勝窮，何以釐之？民多轉徙，而荒蕪未闢，又遺其稅以為公私之累，何以處之？水利有專官，而旱潦不免於涸溢，何以拯之？當是時，欲求經常簡易之法，可以弭斯患者，非豪傑之士，誰與議此？故願諸君之極言之也。

問：記稱：「問國之富，數馬以對。」馬之所繫亦重矣。考之《周禮》，大司馬之屬有校人，以掌王六馬；有廋人，以掌十二閑；又有趣馬、巫馬、馬質、牧師、圉師、圉人之類。夫一事而設官之多如此，無乃失之冗與？至其取之民者，自丘甸以上，積而數之，至於一同之地，出戎馬百乘，亦不為不多矣。不識當時國有征役，何以能弗擾而事集與？抑其法亦可用於今日否與？今
translation_en:
…households: how can they be rescued? Tax exactions follow no regular rules, and the costs of delivering payments often amount to several times the sum due: how can these costs be reduced? Corvée service has its prescribed terms, yet the burdens are uneven: how can they be equalized? Land taxes have fixed quotas, yet fraudulent devices for evading liability are virtually inexhaustible: how can these abuses be rectified? Many people have migrated, leaving land waste and unreclaimed, while their unpaid taxes remain a burden on both public authorities and private households: how should this be handled? Water management has officials specifically responsible for it, yet droughts and excessive rains still cause waterways to dry up or overflow: how can relief be provided? At such a time, if we seek regular, simple, and practicable methods to eliminate these troubles, with whom could we discuss them but men of outstanding ability? We therefore hope that you gentlemen will express your views fully.

Question: The Record of Rites states: “When asked about a state's wealth, one answers by counting its horses.” Horses thus bear on matters of considerable importance. Examining the Rites of Zhou, we find among the subordinates of the Minister of War (da sima) a Director of Horses (xiaoren), responsible for the king's six categories of horses; a Stable Master (souren [?]), responsible for the twelve stables; and also such officers as Horse Trainers (quma), Horse Shamans (wuma), Horse Appraisers (mazhi), Pasture Masters (mushi), Chief Grooms (yushi), and Grooms (yuren). With so many offices established for a single undertaking, was there not an excess of personnel? As for what was levied from the people, reckoning cumulatively from the territorial units called qiu and dian upward, a territory of one tong supplied warhorses for a hundred chariots. This, too, was no small number. We wonder how, when the state undertook military expeditions in those days, its business could be accomplished without disturbing the people. Could those methods also be applied today? Now…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
國馬所出內則計丁以牧之民間外則用茶
以易之蕃夷是法也亦嘗襲前代之舊
與夫飼牧之民日困而孳畜不聞其蕃
息差發之制不行而招易所得未必皆
良也馬政之弊至今日極矣茲欲舉二
者之法一振起之使上不病國下不妨
民而馬皆足用若何而可諸生其必有
以處此矣
punctuated: 國馬所出，內則計丁以牧之民間，外則用茶以易之蕃夷。是法也，亦嘗襲前代之舊與？夫飼牧之民日困，而孳畜不聞其蕃息；差發之制不行，而招易所得未必皆良也。馬政之弊，至今日極矣。茲欲舉二者之法，一振起之，使上不病國，下不妨民，而馬皆足用，若何而可？諸生其必有以處此矣。
translation_en: …as for the sources of the state's horses, domestically, adult males are counted to apportion responsibility for rearing them among the common people; externally, tea is used to obtain them in exchange from non-Chinese peoples. Did these methods likewise follow practices inherited from earlier dynasties? The people who feed and tend the horses grow more impoverished by the day, yet we hear of no increase in the breeding stock. The system of requisitions is not being implemented, while the horses obtained by soliciting trade are not necessarily all good. The failings of horse administration have now reached their extreme. If we wish to take these two methods and reinvigorate them together, so that they neither burden the state above nor hinder the people's livelihoods below, and so that the horses are sufficient for use, how can this be accomplished? You candidates surely have a way to address this.

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
禮云禮云玉帛云乎哉樂云樂云鍾鼓云
乎哉
周如底
同考試官教諭唐批聖人語意含蓄深遠非
達禮樂者未易識是作默會成文詞理俱到其達
者乎
同考試官教諭林批題本正大作者頃尚華
===
藻而於夫子當時本意頓反失之是篇明白典雅
詞若近簡而讀之自有一倡三嘆之妙殆有意於
變浮靡之習者與
考試官署郎中華批詞明潔而意甚足當是
作者
考試官給事中陸批簡明可取
聖人論禮樂不專於末以見其本之有在也甚
矣禮樂之有本也玉帛鍾鼓特其末耳曾足以
盡之乎且夫禮樂之在天下不可一日無顧人
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

「禮云禮云，玉帛云乎哉？樂云樂云，鍾鼓云乎哉？」

周如底

同考試官教諭唐批：「聖人語意含蓄深遠，非達禮樂者未易識。是作默會成文，詞理俱到，其達者乎！」

同考試官教諭林批：「題本正大，作者頃尚華藻，而於夫子當時本意頓反失之。是篇明白典雅，詞若近簡，而讀之自有一倡三嘆之妙，殆有意於變浮靡之習者與！」

考試官署郎中華批：「詞明潔而意甚足，當是作者。」

考試官給事中陸批：「簡明可取。」

聖人論禮樂，不專於末，以見其本之有在也。甚矣，禮樂之有本也！玉帛鍾鼓，特其末耳，曾足以盡之乎？且夫禮樂之在天下，不可一日無，顧人
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“Ritual, ritual—is it merely jade and silk of which we speak? Music, music—is it merely bells and drums of which we speak?”

Zhou Rudi

Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: “The sage’s meaning is implicit and profound; anyone without a thorough understanding of ritual and music cannot readily comprehend it. This composition apprehends that meaning intuitively and gives it written form. Both its language and its reasoning fully attain their aims. Surely its author possesses such understanding!”

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “The topic is fundamentally upright and grand. Writers have lately prized ornate language, thereby entirely losing sight of the Master’s original intention. This essay is clear, classically elegant, and refined. Its language may seem rather plain, yet reading it affords the subtle pleasure of ‘one voice singing and three responding.’ Perhaps the author intends to reform the prevailing habit of superficial extravagance!”

Comment by Examiner Hua, Acting Bureau Director: “The language is clear and clean, and the meaning amply expressed. This is surely an accomplished writer.”

Comment by Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary: “Concise and clear; worthy of selection.”

In discussing ritual and music, the sage does not dwell exclusively on their outward details, thereby showing that their foundation lies elsewhere. How profound is the foundation of ritual and music! Jade and silk, bells and drums, are merely their outward details. Could these possibly encompass them in their entirety? Moreover, the world cannot do without ritual and music for even a single day; yet people…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有終身由之而不知者矣自夫斯人之相際也
而有禮以節之禮云禮云孰不曰玉帛而已乎
夫禮行於文飾玉帛固不可無也然方其物之
未將必有所以爲之先者彼圭璧之錯陳玄黃
之稠疊皆其具耳禮果專在是乎蓋禮非文飾
之謂也有無體之禮矣自夫斯人之相與也而
有樂以洽之樂云樂云孰不曰鍾鼓而已乎夫
樂寓於聲音鍾鼓固不可無也然方其聲之未
著必有所以爲之主者彼節奏之抑揚音律之
===
高下特其文耳樂果專在是乎蓋樂非聲音之
謂也有無聲之樂矣要之玉帛不足以言禮敬
而將之斯禮之成也鍾鼓不足以言樂和而發
之斯樂之成也從事於禮樂者惡可遺其本而
惟末之是務哉聖人言此所以警當世者切矣
抑斯言卽易所謂道器之說耳禮樂之原出於
天地而其道則具於人心玉帛鍾鼓皆器也器
由道而立道以器而彰二者相須以成而先後
本末之間則自有等矣夫子所云雖一時有警
punctuated: 有終身由之而不知者矣。自夫斯人之相際也，而有禮以節之。禮云禮云，孰不曰玉帛而已乎？夫禮行於文飾，玉帛固不可無也。然方其物之未將，必有所以爲之先者。彼圭璧之錯陳，玄黃之稠疊，皆其具耳。禮果專在是乎？蓋禮非文飾之謂也，有無體之禮矣。自夫斯人之相與也，而有樂以洽之。樂云樂云，孰不曰鍾鼓而已乎？夫樂寓於聲音，鍾鼓固不可無也。然方其聲之未著，必有所以爲之主者。彼節奏之抑揚，音律之高下，特其文耳。樂果專在是乎？蓋樂非聲音之謂也，有無聲之樂矣。要之，玉帛不足以言禮，敬而將之，斯禮之成也；鍾鼓不足以言樂，和而發之，斯樂之成也。從事於禮樂者，惡可遺其本而惟末之是務哉？聖人言此，所以警當世者切矣。抑斯言卽《易》所謂道器之說耳。禮樂之原出於天地，而其道則具於人心。玉帛鍾鼓皆器也。器由道而立，道以器而彰。二者相須以成，而先後本末之間則自有等矣。夫子所云，雖一時有警
translation_en: …there are those who follow them throughout their lives without understanding them. As people interact with one another, ritual provides regulation. “Ritual, ritual!” Who does not say that it consists merely of jade and silk? Ritual is indeed enacted through ceremonial adornment, and jade and silk certainly cannot be dispensed with. Yet before these objects are presented, there must be something that precedes them. The jade tablets and discs arrayed together, the dark and yellow silks piled in abundance—all these are merely its implements. Does ritual truly consist exclusively in these things? Ritual does not mean ceremonial adornment: there is ritual without bodily form. As people associate with one another, music brings them into harmony. “Music, music!” Who does not say that it consists merely of bells and drums? Music indeed resides in sounds, and bells and drums certainly cannot be dispensed with. Yet before the sounds become audible, there must be something that governs them. The rise and fall of rhythms and the high and low pitches are merely its outward embellishment. Does music truly consist exclusively in these things? Music does not mean sounds: there is music without sound. In essence, jade and silk are insufficient to define ritual; presenting them with reverence brings ritual to fulfillment. Bells and drums are insufficient to define music; sounding them in harmony brings music to fulfillment. How can those engaged in ritual and music neglect their root and attend solely to their branches? In saying this, the Sage offered an urgent admonition to his age. Moreover, these words express precisely the teaching concerning the Way and concrete implements found in the Book of Changes. Ritual and music originate in Heaven and Earth, while their Way is fully present in the human heart. Jade, silk, bells, and drums are all concrete implements. Implements are established through the Way, and the Way is made manifest through implements. The two depend upon each other for their fulfillment, yet there is an inherent ordering between what comes first and what follows, between root and branch. Although what the Master said was an admonition prompted by the circumstances of his time…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之言而聖人制作之本意宜不外此故欲知禮
樂之情者必先明於道器之說而後可
唯天下至誠為能經綸天下之大經立天
下之大本知天地之化育夫焉有所倚
肫肫其仁淵淵其淵浩浩其天
姜良翰
同考試官教諭徐批至誠功用自然之妙學
者類能言之然體認不精支離可厭是義詞理俱
到非平日用心於内者不能作
===
同考試官教諭鄭批一破卓有定見講中以
誠字發明精蘊讀之令人豁然
同考試官學正孫批題本難作諸卷非泛則
畧惟此篇體認親切而氣象舂容即文可以知人矣
考試官署郎中華批說理精密
考試官給事中陸批自是理趣文字
中庸極言至誠之道必贊其道之至也夫道之
所以為至者一誠而已中庸極言以贊之聖人
之道之極致豈復有餘蘊哉且均是人也而有
punctuated:
之言，而聖人制作之本意，宜不外此。故欲知禮樂之情者，必先明於道器之說而後可。
「唯天下至誠，為能經綸天下之大經，立天下之大本，知天地之化育，夫焉有所倚？肫肫其仁，淵淵其淵，浩浩其天。」
姜良翰
同考試官教諭徐批：至誠功用自然之妙，學者類能言之，然體認不精，支離可厭。是義詞理俱到，非平日用心於内者不能作。
同考試官教諭鄭批：一破卓有定見，講中以誠字發明精蘊，讀之令人豁然。
同考試官學正孫批：題本難作，諸卷非泛則畧，惟此篇體認親切，而氣象舂容，即文可以知人矣。
考試官署郎中華批：說理精密。
考試官給事中陸批：自是理趣文字。
中庸極言至誠之道，必贊其道之至也。夫道之所以為至者，一誠而已。中庸極言以贊之，聖人之道之極致，豈復有餘蘊哉？且均是人也，而有
translation_en:
…words of admonition, yet the original intention behind the sage’s institutions surely does not extend beyond this. Thus, anyone wishing to understand the true nature of rites and music must first comprehend the relationship between the Way and concrete instruments.

“Only one possessed of utmost sincerity under Heaven can order the great constant relationships of the world, establish its great foundation, and understand the transforming and nourishing processes of Heaven and Earth. On what, then, would he depend? How earnest his benevolence, how unfathomable his depth, how vast his Heaven!”

Jiang Lianghan

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: Students can generally speak of the wondrous spontaneity of the workings of utmost sincerity. Yet their understanding is imprecise, and their fragmented explanations are tiresome. In this essay, both expression and reasoning are fully realized. Only someone habitually devoted to inward cultivation could have written it.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: The opening interpretation displays a remarkably firm grasp. In the exposition, the word “sincerity” elucidates the profound meaning; reading it brings sudden clarity.

Comment by Associate Examiner Sun, Instructor: This topic is inherently difficult to write on. The other essays are either vague or cursory. This essay alone shows an intimate understanding, while its manner is ample and unhurried. From the writing itself one can know the man.

Comment by Examiner Hua, Acting Director: The exposition of principle is precise and meticulous.

Comment by Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary: This is indeed writing imbued with the savor of principle.

When the Doctrine of the Mean speaks fully of the Way of utmost sincerity, it necessarily extols that Way’s perfection. What makes the Way perfect is sincerity alone. The Doctrine of the Mean speaks fully to extol it: could any aspect of the supreme perfection of the sage’s Way remain undisclosed? Moreover, all are equally human, yet there are…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
所謂至誠者焉渾乎賦予之真而天德無不實
湛乎純一之體而天下莫能加是故天下有大
經焉人倫是也則隨其分而比其類各盡夫當
然之實所謂惟聖盡倫而天下後世之法於是
乎在矣天下有大本焉人性是也則得於天者
全於己無一毫私偽之雜所謂惟聖盡性而千
變萬化之道胥此焉出矣且化育著于兩間至
神妙也則斯理之中涵一天命之於穆而於所
謂發見流行之實與之黙契而弗違焉凡若此
===
者蓋其無妄盡天下之理極誠一天下之動不
假於思勉而亦無事乎心力夫豈有所倚著于
物而後能哉是以自其盡倫者言之五品之間
藹然至恩之篤純乎其純而情意之懇到是即
仁而已矣而無或間焉者也自其盡性者言之
一中之立允為眾理之源淵乎其淵而靜深之
無際是即淵而已矣而無或二焉者也自其知
化者言之神明不測一太極本然之妙而浩浩
乎其廣大是即所謂天焉又非特如之而已也
punctuated: 所謂至誠者焉，渾乎賦予之真，而天德無不實；湛乎純一之體，而天下莫能加。是故天下有大經焉，人倫是也，則隨其分而比其類，各盡夫當然之實，所謂惟聖盡倫，而天下後世之法於是乎在矣。天下有大本焉，人性是也，則得於天者全於己，無一毫私偽之雜，所謂惟聖盡性，而千變萬化之道胥此焉出矣。且化育著于兩間，至神妙也，則斯理之中涵一天命之於穆，而於所謂發見流行之實，與之黙契而弗違焉。凡若此者，蓋其無妄盡天下之理，極誠一天下之動，不假於思勉，而亦無事乎心力，夫豈有所倚著于物而後能哉？是以自其盡倫者言之，五品之間，藹然至恩之篤，純乎其純，而情意之懇到，是即仁而已矣，而無或間焉者也。自其盡性者言之，一中之立，允為眾理之源，淵乎其淵，而靜深之無際，是即淵而已矣，而無或二焉者也。自其知化者言之，神明不測，一太極本然之妙，而浩浩乎其廣大，是即所謂天焉，又非特如之而已也。
translation_en:
…those who are called utterly sincere: wholly integrated with the genuineness bestowed upon them, they possess Heaven’s virtue in all its reality; profound in their pure and undivided constitution, they cannot be surpassed by anyone under Heaven. Thus, the world has its great constant relationships—the human relationships. Following their respective distinctions and ordering them by their kinds, the utterly sincere fully realize what each properly requires. This is what is meant by saying that only the sage fulfills the human relationships; herein lies the model for all under Heaven and for later generations. The world has its great foundation—human nature. What the utterly sincere receive from Heaven is preserved whole within themselves, without the slightest admixture of selfishness or falsity. This is what is meant by saying that only the sage fully realizes human nature; from this issue the ways of the thousand changes and myriad transformations. Moreover, the transforming and nourishing activity manifest between Heaven and Earth is supremely numinous and wondrous. Within this principle is contained the profound mystery of Heaven’s mandate, and the utterly sincere accord silently and without deviation with the reality of its manifestation and circulation.

All this is because, free of falsity, they fully comprehend the principles of all under Heaven and, consummate in sincerity, unify all its movements. They do not depend upon deliberation or exertion, nor need they expend mental effort. How could they achieve this only by relying upon external things? Thus, speaking of their fulfillment of the human relationships, among the five relationships there abounds the deepest loving kindness: pure in its purity, with feelings and intentions utterly earnest. This is simply benevolence, admitting no interruption. Speaking of their full realization of human nature, the establishment of the single Mean is indeed the source of all principles: deep in its depth, with stillness and profundity without limit. This is simply unfathomable depth, admitting no duality. Speaking of their understanding of transformation, their numinous intelligence is beyond fathoming, wholly the inherent wonder of the Supreme Ultimate, vast in its breadth and greatness. This is what is called Heaven itself, rather than merely resembling it.

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
上下一致徹性命之精微道器相安妙身心之
神化而天下至誠之功用斯其至矣借曰有所
倚而能之固不若是其至也吁其斯以為天道
歟大抵人之一心萬善咸備盛德大業皆由此
出至誠之道亦惟有是心而已是心也人病弗
求耳擴而充之人皆可以為堯舜復而執之君
子之所以不可及也要其所入亦自下學為己
立心之始求之故曰惟慎獨可以行王道
夫道一而已矣成覸謂齊景公曰彼丈夫
===
也我丈夫也吾何畏彼哉顏淵曰舜何
人也予何人也有為者亦若是公明儀
曰文王我師也周公豈欺我哉
謝紘
同考試官教諭陳批能發孟子道性善之旨
而氣昌辭達殆究心於性學而有得者
考試官署郎中華批峻整可誦
考試官給事中陸批得孟子語意
大賢論道無二致而引言以明之所以發性善
punctuated:
上下一致，徹性命之精微；道器相安，妙身心之神化，而天下至誠之功用斯其至矣。借曰有所倚而能之，固不若是其至也。吁！其斯以為天道歟？大抵人之一心，萬善咸備，盛德大業皆由此出。至誠之道，亦惟有是心而已。是心也，人病弗求耳。擴而充之，人皆可以為堯舜；復而執之，君子之所以不可及也。要其所入，亦自下學為己立心之始求之。故曰：「惟慎獨可以行王道。」

夫道一而已矣。成覸謂齊景公曰：「彼丈夫也，我丈夫也，吾何畏彼哉？」顏淵曰：「舜何人也？予何人也？有為者亦若是。」公明儀曰：「文王我師也，周公豈欺我哉？」

謝紘

同考試官教諭陳批：「能發孟子道性善之旨，而氣昌辭達，殆究心於性學而有得者。」

考試官署郎中華批：「峻整可誦。」

考試官給事中陸批：「得孟子語意。」

大賢論道無二致，而引言以明之，所以發性善
translation_en:
…Above and below are united, penetrating the subtleties of human nature and Heaven’s mandate; the Way and concrete things accord with one another, bringing the spiritual transformation of body and mind to its marvelous fulfillment. Here the efficacy of the utmost sincerity under Heaven reaches its culmination. Suppose one could accomplish this only by relying on something else: surely it could not reach such perfection. Ah! Is this what constitutes the Way of Heaven? In general, the human mind contains every goodness; abundant virtue and great achievements all issue from it. The way of utmost sincerity consists simply in this mind. The trouble is only that people fail to seek it. By expanding and fully developing it, everyone can become a Yao or a Shun; by recovering it and holding fast to it, the gentleman becomes impossible to match. As for the point of entry, one must seek it at the very beginning: learning from ordinary affairs and establishing one’s resolve for one’s own moral cultivation. Thus it is said: “Only through vigilance when alone can one practice the Kingly Way.”

“The Way is one, and that is all. Cheng Jian said to Duke Jing of Qi: ‘He is a man, and I too am a man. Why should I fear him?’ Yan Yuan said: ‘What sort of person was Shun? What sort of person am I? Whoever makes the effort can likewise become such a person.’ Gongming Yi said: ‘King Wen is my teacher. How could the Duke of Zhou have deceived me?’”

Xie Hong 謝紘

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “He is able to bring out the purport of Mencius’s teaching on the goodness of human nature, with vigorous spirit and fluent expression. He seems to be someone who has devoted himself to the study of human nature and attained insight into it.”

Comment by Examiner Hua, Acting Bureau Director: “Rigorous and well ordered; worthy of recitation.”

Comment by Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary: “He grasps the meaning of Mencius’s words.”

The great worthy’s discussion of the Way admits of no divergent principles; he quotes these sayings to make it clear, thereby bringing out the goodness of human nature…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
師聖賢而已尚何他說之可求乎抑孟子性善
之云豈獨爲世子告哉實以示天下後世也自
道學不明而儒者之言性往往失之君子以爲
欲知性之本善求諸心而已方其寂然不動之
中善且未形而惡有所謂惡又惡有所謂善惡
混與三品者哉夫心與性亦有異乎曰非異也
語有之曰心之神明是謂性
易
是故君子所居而安者易之序也所樂而
===
玩者爻之辭也是故君子居則觀其象
而玩其辭動則觀其變而玩其占是以
自天祐之吉无不利
俞介
同考試官教諭毛批詞理明瑩機軸自別場
中如此作者絕少
同考試官教諭吳批題本明白正大作者紛
紜令人厭觀認理精切措詞渾雅無踰此篇而一
結尤有發明其深於易者乎
punctuated:
師聖賢而已，尚何他說之可求乎？抑孟子性善之云，豈獨爲世子告哉？實以示天下後世也。自道學不明，而儒者之言性往往失之。君子以爲欲知性之本善，求諸心而已。方其寂然不動之中，善且未形，而惡有所謂惡？又惡有所謂善惡混與三品者哉？夫心與性亦有異乎？曰：非異也。語有之曰：「心之神明，是謂性。」
易
「是故君子所居而安者，易之序也；所樂而玩者，爻之辭也。是故君子居則觀其象而玩其辭，動則觀其變而玩其占。是以自天祐之，吉无不利。」
俞介
同考試官教諭毛批：「詞理明瑩，機軸自別，場中如此作者絕少。」
同考試官教諭吳批：「題本明白正大，作者紛紜，令人厭觀。認理精切，措詞渾雅，無踰此篇，而一結尤有發明。其深於易者乎？」
translation_en:
…merely taking the sages and worthies as teachers. What other doctrine need one seek? Moreover, when Mengzi spoke of human nature as good, was he addressing only the heir apparent? In truth, he was instructing all under Heaven and generations to come. Since the Learning of the Way ceased to be clearly understood, Confucian scholars have often erred in their accounts of human nature. The gentleman holds that to understand the original goodness of human nature, one need only seek it in the mind. While the mind is still and unmoving, even goodness has yet to take form: where, then, could there be what is called evil? And where could there be a mixture of good and evil, or the three grades of human nature? Are the mind and human nature, then, different? The answer is: they are not different. As the saying goes, “The mind’s numinous intelligence is what is called human nature.”
Book of Changes
“Thus, what the gentleman rests in and finds peace in is the sequence of the Changes; what he delights in and ponders is the wording of its lines. Thus, when at rest, the gentleman contemplates its images and ponders its statements; when acting, he contemplates its changes and ponders its prognostications. Hence, ‘Heaven itself blesses him: good fortune, with nothing unfavorable.’”
Yu Jie
Comment by Associate Examiner Mao, Instructor: “The language and reasoning are lucid and luminous, and the organizing conception is distinctive. Authors of this caliber are exceedingly rare in the examination hall.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: “The topic itself is clear, straightforward, and upright, yet writers make such a tangle of it that reading their work becomes tiresome. In precise and penetrating understanding of the principles, and in rounded and elegant expression, nothing surpasses this essay. Its conclusion is especially illuminating. Is its author not someone profoundly versed in the Changes?”

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭宋批所居而安說多不一是一義順題平寫自覺明備子之所養可知矣
考試官署郎中華批善體貼
考試官給事中陸批是善言易者
大傳即君子得易之妙著君子學易之益甚矣
君子之有得乎易也然非動靜兼致其學亦孰
從而得之哉且易既作於聖人則象變辭占之
已具而天下之理盡之矣非君子不能學也何
則君子以言以動順適乎隨時變易之天而無
===
所困所居何其安也蓋易有事理當然之序昭
著於卦爻而君子為能得之時有萬變一陰陽
消息之流通也事或殊途一剛柔盈虛之運用
也泰然從容於自足孰非易之序乎心領神會
沉潛於得意忘言之表而不可遠所樂何其深
也蓋易有吉凶悔吝之辭發揮於諸爻而君子
為能玩之精蘊之所發有以研其旨趣也隱顯
之所之有以極其幾微也悠然涵泳于不厭孰
非爻之辭乎是蓋隨在有得乎易矣然非學何
punctuated:
同考試官教諭宋批：所居而安，說多不一，是一義。順題平寫，自覺明備，子之所養可知矣。
考試官署郎中華批：善體貼。
考試官給事中陸批：是善言易者。
大傳即君子得易之妙，著君子學易之益。甚矣，君子之有得乎易也！然非動靜兼致其學，亦孰從而得之哉？且易既作於聖人，則象變辭占之已具，而天下之理盡之矣，非君子不能學也。何則？君子以言以動，順適乎隨時變易之天，而無所困，所居何其安也！蓋易有事理當然之序，昭著於卦爻，而君子為能得之。時有萬變，一陰陽消息之流通也；事或殊途，一剛柔盈虛之運用也。泰然從容於自足，孰非易之序乎？心領神會，沉潛於得意忘言之表，而不可遠，所樂何其深也！蓋易有吉凶悔吝之辭，發揮於諸爻，而君子為能玩之。精蘊之所發，有以研其旨趣也；隱顯之所之，有以極其幾微也。悠然涵泳于不厭，孰非爻之辭乎？是蓋隨在有得乎易矣，然非學何
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Song, Instructor: There are many differing explanations of “that in which he abides and finds repose”; this is one interpretation. Following the topic and expounding it straightforwardly, the essay comes across as clear and complete. From it one can discern what you have cultivated within yourself.
Comment by Examiner Hua, Acting Director: An adept grasp of the meaning.
Comment by Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary: Here is someone who speaks well about the Book of Changes.
The Great Commentary brings out the benefits of the gentleman’s study of the Book of Changes by considering the subtle understanding he gains from it. Profound indeed is what the gentleman gains from the Changes! Yet unless he pursues his learning fully in both activity and stillness, how could he attain it? Once the Changes had been composed by the sages, its images, transformations, statements, and prognostications were all complete, encompassing all the principles of the world. Only the gentleman can learn from it. Why is this? In speech and action, the gentleman accords with Heaven, which changes and transforms with the times, and encounters no impediment. How securely he rests in what he abides in!
For the Changes contains the proper order of affairs and their principles, clearly displayed in the hexagrams and their lines, and the gentleman can apprehend it. Though circumstances undergo myriad changes, these are all the circulation of yin and yang as they wane and wax. Though affairs may follow different paths, these are all the operation of the firm and yielding, fullness and emptiness. At ease and unhurried in his own sufficiency, what does he experience that is not the order of the Changes? Apprehending it in his heart and comprehending it in spirit, he immerses himself beyond the realm where one grasps the meaning and forgets the words, yet cannot depart from it. How profound is his delight!
For the Changes contains statements concerning good fortune, misfortune, remorse, and humiliation, expounded in its various lines, and the gentleman can ponder them. Where their subtle import emerges, he has the means to investigate their purport; where the hidden and manifest tend, he has the means to fathom their finest incipient signs. Contemplating them at leisure, immersing himself without weariness, what does he encounter that is not the statements of the lines? Thus, wherever he finds himself, he gains understanding from the Changes. Yet without learning, how …

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
以致之也哉是以君子時乎靜焉尚象以觀其
形容而尤玩味乎所繫之辭先事而說諸心也
時乎動焉尚變以觀其變化而尤精審乎所值
之占臨事而研諸慮也靜知所學則靜與天俱
動知所學則動與吉會若或相之在在有資深
逢原之益矣何所往而不利哉若或祐之隨處
有引伸觸類之妙矣何所適而不宜哉夫君子
學易之事如此其資於易者深矣人亦何憚而
不學乎大抵學易之道不外乎安分窮理二者
===
而已君子所樂而玩玩其理也所居而安安其
分也安分則窮理愈精窮理則安分愈固此君
子終身之心學也若不進於此而徒牽滯于辭
變象占之間則亦藝焉而已其諸異乎君子之
學歟
復則不妄矣故受之以无妄
翁溥
同考試官教諭毛批此題似易實難場中多
為所窘是篇平平寫出若不經意且明白沖淡必
punctuated:
以致之也哉？是以君子時乎靜焉，尚象以觀其形容，而尤玩味乎所繫之辭，先事而說諸心也；時乎動焉，尚變以觀其變化，而尤精審乎所值之占，臨事而研諸慮也。靜知所學，則靜與天俱；動知所學，則動與吉會。若或相之，在在有資深逢原之益矣，何所往而不利哉？若或祐之，隨處有引伸觸類之妙矣，何所適而不宜哉？夫君子學《易》之事如此，其資於《易》者深矣，人亦何憚而不學乎？大抵學《易》之道，不外乎安分、窮理二者而已。君子所樂而玩，玩其理也；所居而安，安其分也。安分則窮理愈精，窮理則安分愈固。此君子終身之心學也。若不進於此，而徒牽滯于辭、變、象、占之間，則亦藝焉而已，其諸異乎君子之學歟？
復則不妄矣，故受之以无妄。
翁溥
同考試官教諭毛批：此題似易實難，場中多為所窘。是篇平平寫出，若不經意，且明白沖淡，必
translation_en:
…how could one attain it? Thus, when the gentleman is still, he esteems the images in order to observe their forms and appearances, and especially savors the statements attached to them, finding delight in his heart before affairs arise. When he acts, he esteems the changes in order to observe their transformations, and especially scrutinizes the prognostication he encounters, examining it in his deliberations as he faces affairs. If, in stillness, he knows what to study, his stillness accords with Heaven; if, in action, he knows what to study, his actions meet with good fortune. As though someone were assisting him, everywhere he gains the benefit of drawing deeply upon his resources and encountering their source: wherever he goes, how could he fail to benefit? As though someone were protecting him, everywhere he enjoys the subtle power of extending his understanding and drawing inferences by analogy: wherever he turns, how could he fail to find what is fitting? Such is the gentleman’s study of the Book of Changes, and profound indeed is the sustenance he draws from it. Why should anyone shrink from studying it?
Broadly speaking, the way of studying the Book of Changes consists simply of two things: resting content in one’s allotted station and investigating principle to the utmost. What the gentleman delights in and ponders is its principle; what he abides in and finds peace in is his allotted station. Resting content in one’s station makes the investigation of principle ever more exact; investigating principle makes one’s contentment with one’s station ever more secure. This is the gentleman’s lifelong learning of the mind. If one fails to advance to this, but merely becomes entangled in statements, changes, images, and prognostications, it amounts only to a technical skill. Surely this differs from the gentleman’s learning?
“Once there is Return, there is no falseness; therefore it is followed by Without Falseness.”
Weng Pu
Comment by Associate Examiner Mao, Instructor: This topic seems easy but is actually difficult; many in the examination hall were stymied by it. This essay unfolds in an even manner, seemingly without effort; moreover, it is clear, restrained, and unadorned. Its author must…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
深於理學者故錄
同考試官教諭吳批說理文字至此亦精矣
高薦何忝
同考試官教諭宋批心學之妙極難形容是
篇酌量不苟舂容有條愈讀而愈有味
考試官署郎中華批易義當如是作
考試官給事中陸批說復與无妄處明白
觀實理所以得于心知无妄所以次于復夫人
心有主則實亦復其理而已矣序卦之義以之
===
宣聖人發明以示人也歟且理在人心本無不
實自夫物欲交蔽理斯失焉而妄即乘之矣謂
之曰復則善端著于介然之頃有以收其放而
存其良天理於是乎復全也全體呈于本心之
明有以啓其端而致其養天眞於是乎復反也
夫理欲相爲消長而誠僞不容並立天理旣還
則復者漸以實而私欲自爾其潜消將馴致于
至誠無息之域矣而尚何妄之存哉天眞内涵
則實者漸以充而德性自爾其完固將日進于
punctuated:
深於理學者，故錄。
同考試官教諭吳批：說理文字至此亦精矣，高薦何忝！
同考試官教諭宋批：心學之妙極難形容，是篇酌量不苟，舂容有條，愈讀而愈有味。
考試官署郎中華批：易義當如是作。
考試官給事中陸批：說復與无妄處明白。
觀實理所以得于心，知无妄所以次于復。夫人心有主，則實亦復其理而已矣。序卦之義以之宣，聖人發明以示人也歟？且理在人心，本無不實。自夫物欲交蔽，理斯失焉，而妄即乘之矣。謂之曰復，則善端著于介然之頃，有以收其放而存其良，天理於是乎復全也；全體呈于本心之明，有以啓其端而致其養，天眞於是乎復反也。夫理欲相爲消長，而誠僞不容並立。天理旣還，則復者漸以實，而私欲自爾其潜消，將馴致于至誠無息之域矣，而尚何妄之存哉？天眞内涵，則實者漸以充，而德性自爾其完固，將日進于
translation_en:
…one deeply versed in the learning of principle; hence its inclusion.
Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: Writing that explains principle has here attained refinement indeed. How could a high recommendation be undeserved?
Associate Examiner Song, Instructor, comments: The subtleties of the learning of the mind are extremely difficult to describe. This essay weighs its words carefully, without carelessness; it is unhurried and orderly. The more one reads it, the richer its meaning becomes.
Examiner Hua, Acting Bureau Director, comments: Essays on the meaning of the Book of Changes should be written like this.
Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary, comments: The passages explaining Return and Freedom from Falsehood are clear.
By examining how genuine principle is apprehended in the mind, one understands why Freedom from Falsehood (Wuwang) follows Return (Fu). When the human mind has a governing center, its genuineness consists simply in recovering its principle. Through this, the meaning of the Sequence of the Hexagrams is made manifest. Is this what the sage elucidated to instruct others?
Now principle within the human mind is originally entirely genuine. Once material desires combine to obscure it, principle is lost, and falsehood immediately takes advantage of this. What is called Return means that the beginnings of goodness become apparent in a fleeting instant: one can gather back the wandering mind and preserve its goodness, and heavenly principle thereby becomes whole again. Its entire substance appears in the illumination of the original mind: one can bring forth its beginnings and nurture it fully, and innate genuineness thereby returns.
Principle and desire wax and wane at one another’s expense, while sincerity and falsity cannot coexist. Once heavenly principle has returned, what is recovered gradually becomes genuine, and selfish desires naturally fade away. One will gradually reach the realm of utmost sincerity without interruption. What falsehood could still remain? When innate genuineness is held within, what is genuine gradually becomes abundant, and one’s moral nature naturally becomes complete and firm. One will advance daily toward…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
純一無僞之地矣而亦何妄之有哉夫人心之
機如此是以聖人之序卦也於復之後必以无
妄次之蓋復有復善之義而无妄有實理自然
之義一先後之相承而斷乎其不可易一次第
之相因而確乎其不容紊存乎易者猶夫存乎
人者也聖人序卦之意夫豈苟焉者哉大抵理
之在人心者未嘗息而君子之學莫有先于復
者復則不妄至于无妄則誠矣誠則止矣復者
賢人之事无妄則聖人之道也若理雖粗復而
===
有未純已雖粗克而有未盡皆非君子自止之
地也故雖以顏子之不遠復幾于聖矣而夫子
猶曰未見其止也學易者審諸
書
人心惟危道心惟微惟精惟一允執厥中
錢應揚
同考試官教諭唐批帝王授受心法最所難
言此作認理明白詞亦鬯達錄之
同考試官教諭林批體認精切詞理明瑩足
punctuated:
純一無僞之地矣，而亦何妄之有哉？夫人心之機如此，是以聖人之序卦也，於復之後必以无妄次之。蓋復有復善之義，而无妄有實理自然之義。一先後之相承，而斷乎其不可易；一次第之相因，而確乎其不容紊。存乎易者，猶夫存乎人者也。聖人序卦之意，夫豈苟焉者哉？大抵理之在人心者未嘗息，而君子之學莫有先于復者。復則不妄，至于无妄則誠矣，誠則止矣。復者賢人之事，无妄則聖人之道也。若理雖粗復而有未純，已雖粗克而有未盡，皆非君子自止之地也。故雖以顏子之不遠復，幾于聖矣，而夫子猶曰：「未見其止也。」學易者審諸。
書
人心惟危，道心惟微，惟精惟一，允執厥中。
錢應揚
同考試官教諭唐批：帝王授受心法，最所難言。此作認理明白，詞亦鬯達，錄之。
同考試官教諭林批：體認精切，詞理明瑩，足
translation_en:
…the state of pure unity without falsity; what falsehood could there still be? Such is the working of the human mind. Thus, when the sage arranged the hexagrams, he necessarily placed Without Falsehood (Wuwang) after Return (Fu). Return signifies returning to goodness, while Without Falsehood signifies the natural operation of genuine principle. Their succession is decidedly unalterable; their sequential relationship is assuredly not to be disordered. What obtains in the Changes is like what obtains in human beings. Could the sage’s intention in arranging the hexagrams have been arbitrary?
In general, principle in the human mind has never ceased to operate, and in the gentleman’s learning nothing takes precedence over returning. Returning dispels falsehood; reaching Without Falsehood is sincerity, and sincerity is the point at which to rest. Returning is the work of the worthy; Without Falsehood is the Way of the sage. If principle has been roughly restored but is not yet pure, or the self has been roughly overcome but not yet completely [the transcription reads 已, apparently for 己], neither is a state in which the gentleman may allow himself to rest. Thus, although Master Yan’s returning before going far astray brought him close to sagehood, Confucius still said: “I have never seen him stop.” Let those who study the Changes examine this carefully.
Book of Documents
“The human mind is precarious; the mind of the Way is subtle. Be discerning, be single-minded, and truly hold fast to the Mean.”
Qian Yingyang
Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: “The methods of cultivating the mind transmitted from one emperor or king to another are exceptionally difficult to discuss. This composition understands principle clearly, and its language is also fluent and expressive. Include it in the record.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Its understanding is precise and penetrating; its language and reasoning are lucid and clear, sufficient to…”

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
善言心學者
考試官署郎中華批講危微精一處似有得
者
考試官給事中陸批文有典則
觀聖君治法之傳一心學之要也蓋天下無心
外之治也即一心而察以守之則執中之要在
是矣帝舜命禹攝位而傳以治心之法如此且
治道不外乎中執中必本於心心一也自其發
於形氣者謂之人心人心雖未入於邪惡而牽
===
引之機已動易私而難公也何危如之自其發
於義理者謂之道心道心雖根於天性而發見
之端始萌難明而易昧也何微如之二者雜於
方寸之間而無以治之則危者愈危微者愈微
矣必也自其一念之所從起者而察之極其精
使凡感於外而動於中者不雜於形氣之私也
旣精矣必也因吾之所已明者而守之極其固
使凡萌於中而漸以著者一純乎義理之正也
夫然則人心已收孰非道心道心所擴孰非中
punctuated:
善言心學者。
考試官署郎中華批：講危微精一處，似有得者。
考試官給事中陸批：文有典則。
觀聖君治法之傳，一心學之要也。蓋天下無心外之治也，即一心而察以守之，則執中之要在是矣。帝舜命禹攝位，而傳以治心之法如此。且治道不外乎中，執中必本於心。心一也，自其發於形氣者謂之人心。人心雖未入於邪惡，而牽引之機已動，易私而難公也，何危如之！自其發於義理者謂之道心。道心雖根於天性，而發見之端始萌，難明而易昧也，何微如之！二者雜於方寸之間，而無以治之，則危者愈危，微者愈微矣。必也自其一念之所從起者而察之，極其精，使凡感於外而動於中者，不雜於形氣之私也。旣精矣，必也因吾之所已明者而守之，極其固，使凡萌於中而漸以著者，一純乎義理之正也。夫然，則人心已收，孰非道心？道心所擴，孰非中
translation_en:
…one who speaks well of the learning of the mind.

Examiner Hua, Acting Bureau Director, comments: “His discussion of perilousness, subtlety, refinement, and single-mindedness seems to show genuine understanding.”

Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary, comments: “The composition follows classical standards.”

Consider the sage ruler’s transmission of the method of government: it consists entirely in the essentials of learning concerning the mind. For there is no governing the realm apart from the mind. By examining this single mind and preserving it, one finds the essential means of holding fast to the Mean. When Emperor Shun commanded Yu to act in his place on the throne, it was thus that he transmitted the method of governing the mind. Moreover, the way of government does not go beyond the Mean, and holding fast to the Mean must be rooted in the mind. The mind is one. Insofar as it issues from bodily form and vital energy, it is called the human mind. Although the human mind has not yet fallen into perversity and evil, the impulses that draw it astray have already stirred: it readily becomes selfish and finds it difficult to be impartial. What could be more perilous? Insofar as it issues from moral principle, it is called the mind of the Way. Although the mind of the Way is rooted in our Heaven-given nature, the first signs of its manifestation are only beginning to sprout: it is difficult to discern and easily obscured. What could be subtler? These two intermingle within the heart. Without a means of governing them, the perilous becomes ever more perilous, and the subtle ever subtler.

One must examine the source from which each thought arises with the utmost refinement, so that whatever is stirred within by external stimuli is unmixed with the selfishness of bodily form and vital energy. Having achieved refinement, one must then hold with the utmost firmness to what one has already understood, so that whatever sprouts within and gradually becomes manifest accords wholly and purely with the rectitude of moral principle. When this is so, once the human mind has been brought under control, what in it is not the mind of the Way? Wherever the mind of the Way extends, what is not the Mean …

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
道由一心之動靜以至萬變之酬酢而自無過
不及之差自一身之云爲以至萬幾之裁决而
皆至當不易之理謂之允執厥中蓋信乎其能
執中而天下之治皆從此出矣舜之命禹何其
言約而義盡也哉抑是道也乃舜所親受於堯
者唐虞之治所以精純粹美而非後世所能及
端在於此自秦漢以下心學不傳而千載不得
蒙至治之澤良以人君不知用力於此耳欲學
堯舜者其可以他求哉然學之之要一言以蔽
===
之曰敬而已
王省惟歲卿士惟月師尹惟日
周如底
同考試官教諭唐批題本正大作者爲五氣
五事休咎得失等語所困往往纏繞可厭詞不費
而意足獨見此篇
同考試官教諭林批措詞命意自是精確箕
子告武王之旨正如此
考試官署郎中華批冲淡中有餘味
punctuated:
道。由一心之動靜，以至萬變之酬酢，而自無過不及之差；自一身之云爲，以至萬幾之裁决，而皆至當不易之理，謂之允執厥中。蓋信乎其能執中，而天下之治皆從此出矣。舜之命禹，何其言約而義盡也哉！抑是道也，乃舜所親受於堯者。唐虞之治，所以精純粹美，而非後世所能及，端在於此。自秦漢以下，心學不傳，而千載不得蒙至治之澤，良以人君不知用力於此耳。欲學堯舜者，其可以他求哉？然學之之要，一言以蔽之，曰敬而已。

王省惟歲，卿士惟月，師尹惟日。
周如底。

同考試官教諭唐批：題本正大，作者爲五氣、五事、休咎、得失等語所困，往往纏繞可厭。詞不費而意足，獨見此篇。

同考試官教諭林批：措詞命意，自是精確。箕子告武王之旨，正如此。

考試官署郎中華批：冲淡中有餘味。
translation_en:
…the Way of the Mean. From the activity and stillness of a single mind to its responses to myriad changes, there will naturally be no error of excess or deficiency; from one’s own words and deeds to decisions on the countless affairs of government, all will accord with principles that are supremely fitting and unalterable. This is what is meant by “truly holding fast to the Mean.” For when one can indeed hold fast to the Mean, all good government throughout the realm proceeds from this. How concise were Shun’s words in charging Yu, yet how exhaustive their meaning! Moreover, this Way was what Shun himself received from Yao. Precisely herein lies the reason why the government of Tang and Yu was so refined, pure, and excellent that later ages could not equal it. From the Qin and Han onward, the learning of the mind was no longer transmitted, and for a thousand years people could not enjoy the blessings of perfect government. This was truly because rulers did not know to apply themselves to this alone. Could those who wish to emulate Yao and Shun seek elsewhere? Yet the essential point of learning, summed up in a single word, is simply reverence.

“The king examines the year; the high ministers, the month; the various officials, the day.”
By Zhou Rudi 周如底.

Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: “The topic itself is upright and substantial. Writers become constrained by such expressions as the five climatic influences, the five affairs, favorable and unfavorable signs, and successes and failures; their discussions often become tediously entangled. Only in this essay do we find economy of language together with fullness of meaning.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “The wording and the conception are indeed precise. This is exactly the purport of Jizi’s counsel to King Wu.”

Comment by Examiner Hua, Acting Director: “Within its unassuming simplicity there is a lingering savor.”

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官給事中陸批整潔
君子敘庶徵之當省者一視其分之尊卑而已
夫庶徵之休咎因天以驗於人者也然則君臣
之分不同而其所省能弗異乎箕子衍庶徵之
疇以告武王及此謂夫天人相與之際亦甚可
畏矣彼王統卿士而卿士統乎師尹猶夫歲之
統月而月之統日也故五事有得失而庶徵之
休咎應之其所當省者則各有等焉莫尊於王
而所省則其係於一歲之利害者也蓋王者統
===
御萬國而綱紀四方凡歲功之虧全在君德之
修否自當容心於其大者矣王省不於歲而何
其次則有卿士焉輔佐之任攸歸而調燮之功
有賴然其位稍卑而所統者則有限矣故順天
行以考其職業者獨於一月之利害所係耳是
雖未擬於王者而亦非無所當省也所謂卿士
惟月者以此其次則有師尹焉分理之務既衆
而奉順之責惟均然其職愈降而所及者益無
幾矣故因時變以驗其修爲者獨於一日之利
punctuated:
考試官給事中陸批：整潔。

君子敘庶徵之當省者，一視其分之尊卑而已。夫庶徵之休咎，因天以驗於人者也。然則君臣之分不同，而其所省能弗異乎？箕子衍庶徵之疇以告武王，及此，謂夫天人相與之際，亦甚可畏矣。彼王統卿士，而卿士統乎師尹，猶夫歲之統月，而月之統日也。故五事有得失，而庶徵之休咎應之，其所當省者則各有等焉。莫尊於王，而所省則其係於一歲之利害者也。蓋王者統御萬國而綱紀四方，凡歲功之虧全，在君德之修否，自當容心於其大者矣。王省不於歲而何？其次則有卿士焉，輔佐之任攸歸，而調燮之功有賴。然其位稍卑，而所統者則有限矣。故順天行以考其職業者，獨於一月之利害所係耳。是雖未擬於王者，而亦非無所當省也。所謂卿士惟月者以此。其次則有師尹焉，分理之務既衆，而奉順之責惟均。然其職愈降，而所及者益無幾矣。故因時變以驗其修爲者，獨於一日之利
translation_en:
Examiner Lu, Supervising Secretary, comments: “Orderly and polished.”

In setting out which of the various signs merit scrutiny, the gentleman attends solely to the relative rank of each person’s station.

The auspicious and inauspicious manifestations of the various signs provide, through Heaven, a means of testing human conduct. Since the stations of ruler and ministers differ, can what they scrutinize fail to differ as well? When Jizi elaborated the category of the various signs to instruct King Wu, he reached this point and declared that the interaction between Heaven and humanity was indeed greatly to be feared. The king presides over the high ministers, and the high ministers preside over the administrative officers, just as the year encompasses the months and the month encompasses the days. Thus, successes and failures in the Five Affairs elicit corresponding auspicious and inauspicious signs; what each ought to scrutinize accordingly varies with rank.

None is more exalted than the king, and what he scrutinizes concerns the benefits and harms of an entire year. For the king rules the myriad states and orders the four quarters. Whether the year’s achievements fall short or reach completion depends upon whether the ruler cultivates his virtue. Naturally, he should direct his attention to matters of the greatest scope. If the king does not scrutinize the year, what should he scrutinize?

Next come the high ministers. They bear the responsibility of assisting the ruler, and the work of harmonizing the cosmic forces depends upon them. Yet their position is somewhat lower, and the scope of their authority is limited. Thus, in following Heaven’s movements to assess the performance of their duties, they attend only to what bears upon the benefits and harms of a single month. Although they do not stand on a level with the king, they too have matters that they ought to scrutinize. This is the meaning of the saying, “The high ministers attend to the month.”

Next come the administrative officers. Their separate administrative tasks are numerous, and they share equally the responsibility of obedient service. Yet their offices are lower still, and the reach of their authority is even more restricted. Thus, in using changes in seasonal conditions to test their cultivation and conduct, they attend only to what bears upon the benefits of a single day…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
害所係耳是雖未同於卿士而亦自有所當省
也所謂師尹惟日者以此其尊者省之大而要
非曰略也其卑者省之小而詳非曰繁也即人
事之當爲以準天時之序有自然而不容紊者
矣抑所謂省之云者夫豈必徧求於歲日月之
間哉亦視其有所關係者云爾然大小之分雖
殊而警懼之心則一孰謂王者於月日之徵畧
而不問卿士師尹於歲之徵避而不省耶有國
家者必上下交修以免夫咎徵之及然後協於
===
箕子衍疇之旨
詩
追琢其章金玉其相勉勉我王綱紀四方
姜良翰
同考試官敎諭徐批是題最難措詞晩得此
卷殆不可以塲屋文字目之
同考試官敎諭鄭批於追琢金玉處盡去陳
言綱紀只就勉勉上見而文王當時維持世道之
心溢出言表真得詩人詠歌聖德之意
punctuated:
害所係耳。是雖未同於卿士，而亦自有所當省也。所謂「師尹惟日」者以此。其尊者省之大而要，非曰略也；其卑者省之小而詳，非曰繁也。即人事之當爲，以準天時之序，有自然而不容紊者矣。抑所謂省之云者，夫豈必徧求於歲日月之間哉？亦視其有所關係者云爾。然大小之分雖殊，而警懼之心則一。孰謂王者於月日之徵畧而不問，卿士師尹於歲之徵避而不省耶？有國家者必上下交修，以免夫咎徵之及，然後協於箕子衍疇之旨。
詩
「追琢其章，金玉其相。勉勉我王，綱紀四方。」
姜良翰
同考試官敎諭徐批：「是題最難措詞，晩得此卷，殆不可以塲屋文字目之。」
同考試官敎諭鄭批：「於追琢金玉處盡去陳言，綱紀只就勉勉上見，而文王當時維持世道之心溢出言表，真得詩人詠歌聖德之意。」
translation_en:
…the harm involved in a single day. Although this differs from the responsibilities of the high ministers, these officials likewise have matters they ought to examine. This is why it is said, “The various officials attend to the day.” Those of higher rank examine matters broad in scope and essential in character; this does not mean that they are cursory. Those of lower rank examine smaller matters in detail; this does not mean that they are overly elaborate. Aligning what ought to be done in human affairs with the sequence of Heaven’s seasons follows a natural order that permits no confusion. Yet does this “examination” necessarily mean searching exhaustively through the year, the day, and the month? It means only attending to what bears upon one’s responsibilities. Although the distinction between greater and lesser responsibilities differs, the spirit of vigilance and apprehension is the same. Who could say that the king neglects the signs appearing in months and days without inquiry, or that the high ministers and various officials evade the signs appearing over the year without examining them? Those who govern a state must cultivate their conduct together, above and below, to avert the advent of ominous signs. Only then will they accord with Jizi’s intent in expounding the categories of the Great Plan.
Book of Odes
“Carved and polished is his refinement; gold and jade are his substance. Diligent, diligent is our king, ordering the four quarters.”
Jiang Lianghan
Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: “This topic is exceptionally difficult to put into words. I obtained this script late in the process; it can scarcely be regarded as merely examination writing.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “In treating ‘carved and polished’ and ‘gold and jade,’ he dispenses entirely with stock expressions. He brings out ‘ordering’ solely through ‘diligent, diligent,’ while King Wen’s concern at that time for sustaining the moral order of the world overflows beyond the words themselves. He has truly grasped the poet’s intention in singing the praises of sage virtue.”

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同考試官學正孫批士子既以勉勉講德而
於綱紀又以政治言之殊戾傳意此篇詞不繁而
意已獨至宜錄之以式來學
考試官署郎中華批得旨
考試官給事中陸批醇雅
詩人興聖德之純繫人心之至夫惟德可以繫
天下之心也聖人之德純而不已則所以綱紀
四方者不已至耶此亦以詠歌文王之德也且
百工之事攻金曰追攻玉曰琢文非追琢猶夫
===
文耳而非美之至也惟追之琢之以致其飾焉
則雕刻之功既極而天下之文無以尚之矣質
非金玉猶夫質耳而非美之至也惟以金以玉
而為之地焉則純瑩得之天成而天下之質不
足言矣夫物且然況我周王之德乎我周王以
視民如傷之心持遹求厥寧之志一誠貫徹於
終始而勤勞之匪懈一敬緝熙於無息而日昃
之不遑雖未嘗有所勉也而人見之若勉勉不
已者焉勉勉如此則蘊之而為天德徵之而為
punctuated:
同考試官學正孫批：士子既以勉勉講德，而於綱紀又以政治言之，殊戾傳意。此篇詞不繁而意已獨至，宜錄之以式來學。
考試官署郎中華批：得旨。
考試官給事中陸批：醇雅。
詩人興聖德之純、繫人心之至。夫惟德可以繫天下之心也。聖人之德純而不已，則所以綱紀四方者，不已至耶？此亦以詠歌文王之德也。且百工之事，攻金曰追，攻玉曰琢。文非追琢，猶夫文耳，而非美之至也。惟追之琢之，以致其飾焉，則雕刻之功既極，而天下之文無以尚之矣。質非金玉，猶夫質耳，而非美之至也。惟以金以玉而為之地焉，則純瑩得之天成，而天下之質不足言矣。夫物且然，況我周王之德乎？我周王以視民如傷之心，持遹求厥寧之志。一誠貫徹於終始，而勤勞之匪懈；一敬緝熙於無息，而日昃之不遑。雖未嘗有所勉也，而人見之若勉勉不已者焉。勉勉如此，則蘊之而為天德，徵之而為
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Sun, an Instructor, comments: Candidates explain “unceasing diligence” in terms of virtue, but then discuss “ordering and regulating” in terms of government, sharply contradicting the meaning of the commentary. This essay, though sparing in words, is uniquely penetrating in meaning. It should be recorded as a model for future students.
Examiner Hua, Acting Bureau Director, comments: It grasps the purport.
Examiner Lu, a Supervising Secretary, comments: Pure and elegant.
The poet uses an evocative comparison to express the purity of sagely virtue and its consummate power to bind human hearts. Only virtue can bind the hearts of all under Heaven. When the sage’s virtue is pure and unceasing, is not the means by which he orders and regulates the four quarters supremely effective? This, too, serves to sing the praises of King Wen’s virtue. Now, among the work of the various artisans, working metal is called chasing, and working jade is called carving. Without chasing and carving, ornament remains mere ornament, falling short of the utmost beauty. Only when it is chased and carved to bring its adornment to perfection does the workmanship reach its utmost, so that no ornament in the world can surpass it. If its substance is neither gold nor jade, it remains mere substance, falling short of the utmost beauty. Only when gold and jade serve as its material foundation does it possess a purity and brilliance bestowed by nature, beside which other substances in the world scarcely merit mention. If this is so even of objects, how much more so of the virtue of our king of Zhou!
Our king of Zhou, with a heart that regarded the people as though they were wounded, maintained his resolve to seek their peace. A single sincerity ran through all his actions from beginning to end, and he labored without slackening; a single reverence shone ever more brightly without interruption, and even when the sun declined he had no leisure. Though he never needed to force himself, people saw him as one who exerted himself diligently without cease. With diligence such as this, what he held within constituted the virtue of Heaven, and what he manifested outwardly constituted…

title: 嘉靖七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
王道天下雖大也精神志向與吾而相攝由人
心觀之祇自覺其有所屬焉而莫知其然也億
兆雖衆也心神意氣與吾而相關由斯民觀之
祇日見其有所統焉而莫知為之者也謂之曰
綱紀四方信乎文王之德繫於人心而歸附趨
向之勢自有所不容已矣抑禹思天下有溺者
由己溺之也稷思天下有飢者由己飢之也文
王當殷道之衰天下之憔悴於虐政也甚矣勉

punctuated:
王道。天下雖大也，精神志向與吾而相攝；由人心觀之，祇自覺其有所屬焉，而莫知其然也。億兆雖衆也，心神意氣與吾而相關；由斯民觀之，祇日見其有所統焉，而莫知為之者也。謂之曰「綱紀四方」，信乎文王之德繫於人心，而歸附趨向之勢自有所不容已矣。抑禹思天下有溺者，由己溺之也；稷思天下有飢者，由己飢之也。文王當殷道之衰，天下之憔悴於虐政也甚矣。勉勉之心，固有不容自已者。故位不在文王，而天命人心在焉。蓋一念憂勤，王業勃然興矣。雖然，文王豈有心於是哉？為人臣，止於敬，是亦勉勉之心也。
紹庭上下，陟降厥家。休矣皇考，以保明其身。
符驗
同考試官教諭徐批：成王繼述之志，實在於道，而延訪羣臣，其意甚至。此篇寫出，句句親切，直是作者。
translation_en:
…the kingly Way. Vast though the realm is, its spirit and aspirations are bound together with mine. Viewed from the people's hearts, they simply feel that they have someone to whom they belong, without knowing why this is so. Numerous though the countless multitudes are, their hearts, spirits, intentions, and energies are connected with mine. Viewed from the people's perspective, each day they simply find themselves united under a guiding authority, without knowing who brings this about. This is called “ordering and binding together the four quarters.” Truly, King Wen's virtue held the people's hearts, and their movement toward allegiance and submission was naturally irresistible.
Moreover, Yu thought that whenever anyone in the realm drowned, it was as though he himself had drowned that person; Ji thought that whenever anyone in the realm went hungry, it was as though he himself had caused that hunger. King Wen lived during the decline of Yin's rule, when the realm suffered grievously under oppressive government. His unremitting concern was therefore something he could not restrain. Thus, although King Wen did not occupy the royal throne, Heaven's Mandate and the people's hearts rested with him. From a single impulse of anxious diligence, the royal enterprise sprang vigorously into being. Yet did King Wen deliberately aim at this? As a minister, he rested in reverence: this, too, was an expression of his unremitting concern.
“Continue the ancestral ways above and below, ascending and descending within that house. Glorious is the august deceased father, thereby protecting and illuminating his person.”
Fu Yan 符驗
Comment by Associate Examiner Xu 徐, Instructor: King Cheng's resolve to continue and carry forward his predecessor's work truly rested upon the Way; his purpose in inviting and consulting his ministers was most earnest. This essay brings that purpose out, every sentence closely expressing it. Here indeed is an accomplished writer.
